### Alpha compositing modes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#alpha-compositing-modes "Link to this heading")
This section describes the Porter-Duff blend modes in Kanzi. The Porter-Duff blend modes were defined by Thomas Porter and Tom Duff in their 1984 paper [Compositing Digital Images](https://graphics.pixar.com/library/Compositing/paper.pdf).
Use the Porter-Duff blend modes for alpha compositing. The Porter-Duff blend modes combine two layers based on the alpha channels of those layers. If the target framebuffer does not have alpha channel, or the alpha value is constant 1, many of the alpha compositing modes can produce unintuitive but correct results. For example, the Source Out mode produces the same result as the Clear blend mode.
When you use alpha compositing, make sure that the alpha channel of the render target is suitable for alpha compositing. For example:
  * Use a parent node which you composite by enabling the Node 2D > Force Composition property. This way you render the nodes to a cleared render target.
  * If the window surface is translucent, use the Clear blend mode to clear the target framebuffer.


By default Kanzi composites nodes using the Alpha: Premultiplied mode, which corresponds to the Porter-Duff **Source Over** mode.
In Kanzi to achieve the behavior of the Porter-Duff **Destination** or **Source** mode, in the destination or source node disable the Node > Visibility property.
Each description includes:
  * The equations that Kanzi uses to compute the result color (Cout) and alpha (αout) of the composition of the source (src) and destination (dst).
  * Visualization of how the blend mode operates on overlapping source and destination images with opaque (left) or partially transparent (right) content:

  
|   |   | Opaque  | Partially transparent  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|   | Destination (dst)  |  ![../../_images/red-r255-g0-b64.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/red-r255-g0-b64.png)  |  ![../../_images/red-r255-g0-b64-0.7opacity.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/red-r255-g0-b64-0.7opacity.png)  |  
|   | Source (src)  |  ![../../_images/blue-r32-g64-b255.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blue-r32-g64-b255.png)  |  ![../../_images/blue-r32-g64-b255-0.7opacity.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blue-r32-g64-b255-0.7opacity.png)  |  
#### Opaque[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#opaque "Link to this heading")  
|  Replaces the destination pixels with the source pixels. This mode is equivalent to the Porter-Duff **Source** mode. Cout=Csrcαout=αsrc  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-opaque.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-opaque.png)  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-opaque-alpha.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-opaque-alpha.png)  |

content:
#### Clear[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#clear "Link to this heading")  
|  Sets the destination pixels to transparent black. Cout=0αout=0  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-clear.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-clear.png)  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-clear.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-clear.png)  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
#### Exclusive Or[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#exclusive-or "Link to this heading")  
|  Draws the non-overlapping source and destination pixels. In the overlapping source and destination pixels reduces the source alpha by the inverse of the destination alpha, and the destination alpha by the inverse of the source alpha, then merges the pixels. Cout=(1−αdst)∗Csrc+(1−αsrc)∗Cdstαout=(1−αdst)∗αsrc+(1−αsrc)∗αdst  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-exclusive-or.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-exclusive-or.png)  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-exclusive-or-alpha.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-exclusive-or-alpha.png)  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
#### Source Atop[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#source-atop "Link to this heading")  
|  Discards those source pixels that do not cover destination pixels, and draws the rest of the source pixels over destination pixels. Cout=αdst∗Csrc+(1−αsrc)∗Cdstαout=αdst  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-source-atop.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-source-atop.png)  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-source-atop-alpha.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-source-atop-alpha.png)  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
#### Source In[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#source-in "Link to this heading")  
|  Draws those source pixels that cover destination pixels, and discards all destination pixels. Cout=αdst∗Csrcαout=αdst∗αsrc  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-source-in.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-source-in.png)  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-source-in-alpha.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-source-in-alpha.png)  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
#### Source Out[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#source-out "Link to this heading")  
|  Draws the source pixels with alpha reduced by the inverse of the destination alpha, and discards all destination pixels. Cout=(1−αdst)∗Csrcαout=(1−αdst)∗αsrc  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-source-out.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-source-out.png)  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-source-out-alpha.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-source-out-alpha.png)  |

content:
#### Destination Atop[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#destination-atop "Link to this heading")  
|  Discards those destination pixels that are not covered by source pixels, and draws the rest of the destination pixels over source pixels. Cout=αsrc∗Cdst+(1−αdst)∗Csrcαout=αsrc  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-destination-atop.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-destination-atop.png)  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-destination-atop-alpha.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-destination-atop-alpha.png)  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
#### Destination In[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#destination-in "Link to this heading")  
|  Draws only those destination pixels that intersect with the source pixels, and discards all source pixels. You can use this blend mode to implement a mask effect. See [Using alpha compositing to create a mask effect](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#using-alpha-compositing-to-create-a-mask-effect). Cout=αsrc∗Cdstαout=αsrc∗αdst  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-destination-in.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-destination-in.png)  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-destination-in-alpha.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-destination-in-alpha.png)  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
#### Destination Out[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#destination-out "Link to this heading")  
|  Draws the destination pixels with alpha reduced by the inverse of the source alpha, and discards all source pixels. You can use this blend mode to implement an inverse mask effect. Cout=(1−αsrc)∗Cdstαout=(1−αsrc)∗αdst  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-destination-out.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-destination-out.png)  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-destination-out-alpha.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-destination-out-alpha.png)  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
#### Destination Over[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#destination-over "Link to this heading")  
|  Draws the destination pixels over the source pixels. Cout=(1−αdst)∗Csrc+Cdstαout=(1−αdst)∗αsrc+αdst  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-destination-over.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-destination-over.png)  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-destination-over-alpha.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-destination-over-alpha.png)  |

### Advanced color blending modes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#advanced-color-blending-modes "Link to this heading")
This section describes the advanced color blending modes in Kanzi. When using OpenGL or OpenGL ES, these modes require the `GL_KHR_blend_equation_advanced` and `GL_KHR_blend_equation_advanced_coherent` extensions. When using Vulkan these modes require the `VK_EXT_blend_operation_advanced` extension.
Each description includes:
  * The equation that Kanzi uses to compute the result color (Cout) of the composition of the source (src) and destination (dst).
All advanced color blending modes use this equation to compute the result alpha:
αout=αsrc+(1−αsrc)∗αdst
  * Visualization of how the blend mode operates on these overlapping source and destination images:

  
|   | Destination (dst)  |  ![../../_images/advanced-blend-modes-destination.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/advanced-blend-modes-destination.png)  |  ![../../_images/advanced-blend-modes-destination.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/advanced-blend-modes-destination.png)  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
|   | Source (src)  |  ![../../_images/advanced-blend-modes-source-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/advanced-blend-modes-source-color.png)  |  ![../../_images/advanced-blend-modes-source-bw.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/advanced-blend-modes-source-bw.png)  |  
#### Multiply (advanced khr)[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#multiply-advanced-khr "Link to this heading")  
|  Multiplies the source and destination, resulting in a darker color. This mode is otherwise similar to the [Multiply](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#multiply) mode, but it handles alpha in the same way as the [Screen](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#screen) mode. Cout=Cdst∗Csrc  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-multiply-advanced-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-multiply-advanced-color.png)  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-multiply-advanced-bw.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-multiply-advanced-bw.png)  |  
| --- | --- | --- |

content:
#### Overlay[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#overlay "Link to this heading")  
| Combines the [Multiply](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#multiply) and [Screen](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#screen) modes. Where the destination is light, the source becomes lighter, and where the destination is dark, the source becomes darker. This mode preserves the highlights and shadows in the destination.  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-overlay-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-overlay-color.png)  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-overlay-bw.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-overlay-bw.png)  |

Cout={2∗Csrc∗Cdstif Cdst<=0.51−2∗(1−Csrc)∗(1−Cdst)otherwise
#### Darken[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#darken "Link to this heading")  
|  Compares the colors of the destination and source and selects the darker one. Cout=min(Cdst,Csrc)  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-darken-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-darken-color.png)  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-darken-bw.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-darken-bw.png)  |

#### Lighten[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#lighten "Link to this heading")  
|  Compares the colors of the destination and source and selects the lighter one. Cout=max(Cdst,Csrc)  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-lighten-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-lighten-color.png)  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-lighten-bw.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-lighten-bw.png)  |

#### Color Burn[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#color-burn "Link to this heading")  
|  Darkens the destination to reflect the color of the source, producing a result with higher contrast, saturated mid-tones, and reduced highlights. White source color produces no change. content:
#### Color Dodge[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#color-dodge "Link to this heading")  
|  Lightens the destination to reflect the color of the source, producing a result with lower contrast, saturated mid-tones, and blown highlights. Black source color produces no change. This mode is the opposite of the Color Burn mode.  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-color-dodge-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-color-dodge-color.png)  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-color-dodge-bw.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-color-dodge-bw.png)  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
Cout={0if Cdst<=0min(1,Cdst1−Csrc)if Cdst>0 and Csrc<11if Cdst<0 and Csrc>=1
#### Hard Light[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#hard-light "Link to this heading")  
|  Multiplies or screens the colors:
  * A source color lighter than 50% gray lightens the destination as if screening it.
  * A source color darker than 50% gray darkens the destination as if multiplying it.

Black source color produces black and white source color produces white.  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-hard-light-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-hard-light-color.png)  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-hard-light-bw.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-hard-light-bw.png)  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
Cout={2∗Csrc∗Cdstif Csrc<=0.51−2∗(1−Csrc)∗(1−Cdst)otherwise
#### Soft Light[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#soft-light "Link to this heading")  
|  Darkens or lightens the colors:
  * A source color lighter than 50% gray lightens the destination as if dodging it.
  * A source color darker than 50% gray darkens the destination as if burning it.

The result is softer than with the [Overlay](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#overlay) mode. Black or white source color produces a distinctly darker or lighter result, but not pure black or white.  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-soft-light-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-soft-light-color.png)  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-soft-light-bw.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-soft-light-bw.png)  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
Cout={Cdst−(1−2∗Csrc)∗Cdst∗(1−Cdst)if Csrc<=0.5Cdst+(2∗Csrc−1)∗Cdst∗((16∗Cdst−12)∗Cdst+3)if Csrc>0.5 and Cdst<=0.25Cdst+(2∗Csrc−1)∗(Cdst−Cdst)if Csrc>0.5 and Cdst>0.25

content:
#### Difference[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#difference "Link to this heading")  
|  Subtracts either the source color from the destination color or the other way around, depending on which one is brighter. White source color inverts the destination color. Black source color produces no change. Cout=abs(Cdst−Csrc)  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-difference-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-difference-color.png)  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-difference-bw.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-difference-bw.png)  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
#### Exclusion[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#exclusion "Link to this heading")  
|  Creates an effect that is similar to Difference but lower in contrast. White source color inverts the destination color. Black source color produces no change. Cout=Csrc+Cdst−2∗Csrc∗Cdst  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-exclusion-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-exclusion-color.png)  |  ![../../_images/blend-mode-exclusion-bw.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-exclusion-bw.png)  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
#### HSL Hue[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#hsl-hue "Link to this heading")  
|  Uses:

## Using color blending to create an overlay[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#using-color-blending-to-create-an-overlay "Link to this heading")
You can use color blending to create a partially transparent overlay that is darker or lighter than its backdrop.
[![../../_images/multiply-overlay-with-content.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/multiply-overlay-with-content.png)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/multiply-overlay-with-content.png) [![../../_images/screen-overlay-with-content.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/screen-overlay-with-content.png)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/screen-overlay-with-content.png)
To create an overlay to which you can apply post-processing effects, use effects. For example, you can use multiple effects to create the frosted glass effect. See [Effects for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/2d-effects.html) and [Using multiple effects](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/multiple-effects.html).
To use color blending to create an overlay:
  1. In the Prefabs create the prefab that you use as the root of the overlay.
For example, create an Empty Node 2D prefab, name it Notification, and add the Notification prefab to an Activity. This way you see the content of the prefab in the Preview when the Activity is activated.
![../../_images/notification-in-prefabs.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/notification-in-prefabs.png)
  2. In the Prefabs select the prefab that you created or the Activity to which you added the prefab, and in the Properties set the size and positioning of the overlay.
![../../_images/notification-size.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/notification-size.png)
  3. To draw the background of the overlay, in the prefab that you use as the root of the overlay create an Empty Node 2D node and in the Properties add and set:
     * Foreground Brush to the color brush that you want to use to set the color of the overlay
     * Material > Blend Mode to:
       * Multiply to create an overlay that is darker than its backdrop
The [Multiply](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#multiply) blend mode multiplies the source (overlay) and destination (backdrop) pixels.
       * Screen to create an overlay that is lighter than its backdrop
The [Screen](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#screen) blend mode adds the source (overlay) and destination (backdrop) pixels and subtracts from the result the product of the source and destination.
![../../_images/notification-overlay-in-prefabs.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/notification-overlay-in-prefabs.png) ![../../_images/set-blend-mode-multiply.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-blend-mode-multiply.png) ![../../_images/multiply-applied.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/multiply-applied.png)

metadata.title: Blending and compositing 2D nodes (Part 15/19)
metadata.breadcrumb: Working with … > 2D content > Blending and compositing 2D nodes

content:
4. Add to the root of the overlay prefab the content that you want to show on top of the overlay.
![../../_images/notification-content-in-prefabs.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/notification-content-in-prefabs.png) ![../../_images/multiply-overlay-with-content.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/multiply-overlay-with-content.png)
  5. (Optional) To create fade-out and fade-in transitions for the overlay, use a state manager where in the state that does not show the overlay:
     * In the overlay background node set the Brush Color of the Foreground Brush:
       * If your overlay background uses the Multiply blend mode, set the Brush Color to white.
When you multiply a color with white, that color does not change.
![../../_images/white-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/white-brush.png)
       * If your overlay background uses the Screen blend mode, set the Brush Color to transparent black.
When you screen a color with transparent black, that color does not change.
![../../_images/transparent-black-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/transparent-black-brush.png)
     * In the node that contains the content that you want to show on top of the overlay, set the Node > Opacity property to 0.
You cannot adjust the opacity of the overlay prefab or the overlay background with the Node > Opacity property, because adjusting that property in a node causes Kanzi to composite that node. For the same reason you cannot assign a 2D effect to the overlay. For example, if your overlay background uses the Multiply blend mode and Kanzi composites the overlay prefab, Kanzi applies the Multiply blend mode against an empty composition render target, resulting in a fully transparent overlay.
![../../_images/blend-mode-multiply-overlay.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-mode-multiply-overlay.gif)

## Using alpha compositing to create a mask effect[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#using-alpha-compositing-to-create-a-mask-effect "Link to this heading")
You can use alpha compositing to implement a simple mask effect.
[![../../_images/mask-completed.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-completed.png)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-completed.png)
To create a more versatile mask effect, use the Mask Effect 2D effect. See [Using the Mask Effect 2D effect](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/mask-effect-2d.html).
To use alpha compositing to create a mask effect:
  1. Create a 2D node that you use to host both the content, which you want to mask, and the mask.
For example, in the Prefabs create an Empty Node 2D prefab and add it to an Activity. This way you see the content of the prefab in the Preview when the Activity is activated.
![../../_images/masked-content-in-prefabs.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/masked-content-in-prefabs.png)
  2. In the node that you created, create:
    1. The content that you want to mask.
![../../_images/content-to-mask-in-prefabs.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/content-to-mask-in-prefabs.png) ![../../_images/content-to-mask.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/content-to-mask.png)
    2. The node that you use as the mask.
For example, create an Image node and in the Properties add and set:
       * Image to the texture that you want to use as the mask
       * Horizontal Alignment and Vertical Alignment to Stretch
![../../_images/mask-node-in-prefabs.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-node-in-prefabs.png) ![../../_images/mask-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-properties.png) ![../../_images/mask-node-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-node-in-preview.png)
  3. Select the node that you use as the mask, in the Properties add the Material > Blend Mode property, and set it to Destination In.
The [Destination In](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#destination-in) mode draws those pixels of the content that intersect with the mask, using the alpha channel of the mask.
Tip
To create an inverse mask effect, use the [Destination Out](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html#destination-out) mode.
![../../_images/blend-more-destination-in.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blend-more-destination-in.png) ![../../_images/mask-applied-without-composition.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-applied-without-composition.png)
  4. Select the node that hosts both the content and the mask, in the Properties add the Node 2D > Force Composition property, and enable it.
This way you set Kanzi to composite the node and render its content to a cleared render target.

## How Kanzi applies 2D effects[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/2d-effects.html#how-k-applies-2d-effects "Link to this heading")
Kanzi applies 2D effects to the visual shape of the content in a node and its descendant nodes.
![../../_images/effect-node.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/effect-node.png) ![../../_images/parent-children-effect-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/parent-children-effect-preview.png)
When you want to apply an effect to a node but not to its descendant nodes, place the descendant nodes in a sibling node of the node to which you apply the effect. Position that sibling node in the node tree below the node to which you apply the effect. Make sure that the sibling nodes are of the same size, layout, transformation, and opacity.
![../../_images/effect-node-2.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/effect-node-2.png) ![../../_images/parent-only-effect-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/parent-only-effect-preview.png)
## Effects and layout[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/2d-effects.html#effects-and-layout "Link to this heading")
When you use effects, keep in mind that:
  * Kanzi does not take effects into account when calculating layout. When your design does not allow an effect to exceed the layout bounds, make sure that there is enough space in the layout for that effect.
For example, in a layout that contains a Text Block 2D node where you apply a drop shadow, in that Text Block 2D node ensure sufficient space for the shadow by setting the Horizontal Margin and Vertical Margin properties.
![../../_images/shadow-margin.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/shadow-margin.png)
  * When Kanzi applies an effect to a 2D node, it composites that node and clips its descendant nodes to the node bounds, regardless of the value of the Clip Children property. This happens because the size of the render target texture matches the size of the node.


## Impact of effects on application performance[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/2d-effects.html#impact-of-effects-on-application-performance "Link to this heading")
For every instance of an effect Kanzi requests the composition manager to provide a temporary composition target. Kanzi composition manager reuses temporary composition targets if they are compatible in size and parameters.
The final performance of an application that uses effects depends on:
  * The amount of allocated memory, and therefore the bandwidth required to render the UI of the application
  * The number of draw calls
  * The number of render target or texture switches


To find the most efficient way of using effects, test the performance of your application with these approaches:
  * Apply a separate effect to each UI element to minimize the area.
  * Apply an effect to a group of UI elements that cover a larger area.

## Applying anti-aliasing[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/2d-effects.html#applying-anti-aliasing "Link to this heading")
When you apply an effect to a 2D node, Kanzi renders that node to a composition target. By default, Kanzi does not apply anti-aliasing to the child nodes of a composited node. For example, when you rotate these nodes, their edges can look jaggy.
![../../_images/node-tree-flow-layout.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-flow-layout.png) ![../../_images/preview-no-msaa.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-no-msaa.png)
To apply multisample anti-aliasing:
  1. In the Node Tree or Prefabs, select the node to which you apply the effect.
  2. In the Properties, add the Render Target > Multisample Level property and set it to the number of anti-aliasing samples that you want to use.
See the documentation of the device on which you want to run your Kanzi application for supported values, because the number of anti-aliasing samples depends on the device. If you set the Multisample Level property to a value that your device does not support, Kanzi Engine clamps the value to the largest value supported by the device driver.
![../../_images/properties-multisample-level.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-multisample-level.png) ![../../_images/preview-4x-msaa.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-4x-msaa.png)

## Creating a blur effect for a 2D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/blur-effect-2d.html#creating-a-blur-effect-for-a-2d-node "Link to this heading")
To create a blur effect for a 2D node:
  1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Effects and select Blur Effect 2D.
![../../_images/create-blur-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-blur-effect-2d.png)
  2. In the Node Tree or Prefabs create a 2D node to which you want to apply the blur effect.
![../../_images/image-in-node-tree.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/image-in-node-tree.png) ![../../_images/image-in-preview1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/image-in-preview1.png)
  3. From the Library > Effects > 2D Effects drag the Blur Effect 2D effect to the Node Tree or Prefabs and drop it on the 2D node to which you want to apply the blur effect.
This way you set in that 2D node the Effect Prefab property to the Blur Effect 2D effect.
![../../_images/drag-blur-effect-to-node.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/drag-blur-effect-to-node.png) ![../../_images/blur-effect-prefab-set.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blur-effect-prefab-set.png)
  4. In the Library select the Blur Effect 2D effect and in the Properties add and set the Blur Effect 2D properties.
![../../_images/blur-effect-2d-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blur-effect-2d-properties.png) ![../../_images/blur-effect-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blur-effect-in-preview.png)  
|    
Blur Radius sets the amount of blur by defining the radius of the circular area of pixels that blend into each other. The default radius is 8 pixels. This property also determines the distance in pixels that the blur expands the render area at the node borders unless you enable the Masked Blur property.  |  ![../../_images/blur-radius.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blur-radius.gif)  |  
| --- | --- |  
|    
Blur Quality sets the visual quality of the blur. Lower quality uses less computing and memory resources.  |  ![../../_images/blur-quality.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blur-quality.gif)  |  
|    
Masked Blur sets whether to blur only the pixels whose alpha channel value is not zero. When you enable this property, the blur does not spread to fully transparent pixels and the edges of the content stay sharp.  |  ![../../_images/masked-blur.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/masked-blur.gif)  |

## Customizing an instance of a blur effect[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/blur-effect-2d.html#customizing-an-instance-of-a-blur-effect "Link to this heading")
When you edit the properties of an effect in the Library > Effects, you change the appearance of that effect for all nodes that use it. You can customize each effect instance by overriding the effect property values. For example:
  * When you create a Shadow Effect 2D effect, you can vary the softness of the shadow in different instances of that effect.
  * When you create a Mask Effect 2D effect, you can vary the size of the mask in different instances of that effect.
  * When you create a Blur Effect 2D effect, you can vary the amount of blur in different instances of that effect.
  * When you create an Outline Effect 2D effect, you can vary the color of the outline in different instances of that effect.

content:
To customize an instance of an effect:
  1. Create an effect and set a node to use it.
For example, create a Shadow Effect 2D effect and set an Image node to use it. See [Creating a shadow effect for a 2D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/shadow-effect-2d.html#creating-a-shadow-effect-for-a-2d-node).
![../../_images/effect-prefab-property-set.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/effect-prefab-property-set.png) ![../../_images/image-in-preview-w-shadow.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/image-in-preview-w-shadow.png)
  2. Customize a property in the effect:
    1. In the Library, select the effect that you created. In the Properties, next to the property that you want to customize, click ![image-publish-property](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/enable-editing-of-this-property.png).
Kanzi Studio creates from that property a custom property, adds it to the root of the effect prefab, and creates a `##Template` binding to the property in the 2D effect.
For example, click ![image-publish-property](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/enable-editing-of-this-property.png) next to Shadow Blur Radius property. Kanzi Studio creates a custom Shadow Blur Radius property, adds it to the root effect prefab, and creates in the Shadow Effect 2D effect prefab a `##Template` binding to the custom Shadow Blur Radius property.
![../../_images/properties-publish-shadow-blur-radius.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-publish-shadow-blur-radius.png) ![../../_images/properties-shadow-blur-radius-template-binding.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-shadow-blur-radius-template-binding.png)
    2. In the Node Tree or Prefabs, select the 2D node that uses the effect that you created. In the Properties, click ![image-add-property](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-property.png) next to the property that you customized and set the value of the property.
Kanzi Studio adds to the 2D node a To Source binding which pushes the value of that property to the effect instance made available through the `Node2D.Effect` property of the node.
You can set multiple 2D nodes to use the same effect and in each 2D node, you can add and set the property to have different values.
For example, in the Properties, add the Shadow Effect 2D Properties > ShadowEffect2D.BlurRadius property and use it to adjust the softness of the shadow only in the Image node.
![../../_images/properties-shadow-effect-2d-blur-radius.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-shadow-effect-2d-blur-radius.png) ![../../_images/preview-shadow-effect-2d-blur-radius.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-shadow-effect-2d-blur-radius.png)
  3. (Optional) Repeat the previous step for each effect property that you want to customize.
Tip
When you want to remove from a node a property and its To Source binding, right-click that property and select Remove Property And Binding.

## Creating a mask effect for a 2D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/mask-effect-2d.html#creating-a-mask-effect-for-a-2d-node "Link to this heading")
To create a mask effect for a 2D node:
  1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Effects and select Mask Effect 2D.
![../../_images/create-mask-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-mask-effect-2d.png)
  2. In the Node Tree or Prefabs create a 2D node to which you want to apply the mask effect.
![../../_images/image-in-node-tree.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/image-in-node-tree.png) ![../../_images/image-in-preview1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/image-in-preview1.png)
  3. From the Library > Effects > 2D Effects drag the Mask Effect 2D effect to the Node Tree or Prefabs and drop it on the 2D node to which you want to apply the mask effect.
This way you set in that 2D node the Effect Prefab property to the Mask Effect 2D effect.
![../../_images/drag-mask-effect-to-node.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/drag-mask-effect-to-node.png) ![../../_images/mask-effect-prefab-set.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-effect-prefab-set.png)
  4. In the Library select the Mask Effect 2D effect and in the Properties add and set the Mask Effect 2D properties.
![../../_images/mask-effect-2d-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-effect-2d-properties.png) ![../../_images/mask-effect-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-effect-in-preview.png)  
|    
Mask Texture sets the texture that you want to use as the mask. To use the mask effect, you must set this property.  |  ![../../_images/mask-texture.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-texture.gif)  |  
| --- | --- |  
|    
Mask Width sets the width of the mask. By default the width of the mask is the width of the texture that you set as the Mask Texture.  |  ![../../_images/mask-width.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-width.gif)  |  
|    
Mask Height sets the height of the mask. By default the height of the mask is the height of the texture that you set as the Mask Texture.  |  ![../../_images/mask-height.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-height.gif)  |  
|    
Mask Horizontal Alignment sets the horizontal alignment of the mask:
     * Left aligns the left edge of the mask with the left edge of the node. This is the default value.
     * Right aligns the right edge of the mask with the right edge of the node.
     * Center aligns the mask horizontally to the center of the node.
     * Stretch stretches the mask horizontally to fit the node from the left edge to the right edge.
 |  ![../../_images/mask-horizontal-alignment.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-horizontal-alignment.gif)  |  
|    
Mask Vertical Alignment sets the vertical alignment of the mask:
     * Top aligns the top edge of the mask with the top edge of the node. This is the default value.

content:
|  ![../../_images/mask-horizontal-alignment.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-horizontal-alignment.gif)  |  
|    
Mask Vertical Alignment sets the vertical alignment of the mask:
     * Top aligns the top edge of the mask with the top edge of the node. This is the default value.
     * Bottom aligns the bottom edge of the mask with the bottom edge of the node.
     * Center aligns the mask vertically to the center of the node.
     * Stretch stretches the mask vertically to fit the node from the top edge to the bottom edge.
 |  ![../../_images/mask-vertical-alignment.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-vertical-alignment.gif)  |  
|    
Mask Offset sets the mask offset along the x and y axes. Kanzi applies this property after the Mask Stretch, Mask Horizontal Alignment, Mask Vertical Alignment, and Mask Scale properties.  |  ![../../_images/mask-offset.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-offset.gif)  |  
|    
Mask Scale sets the factor by which to scale the mask. Kanzi applies this property after the Mask Stretch, Mask Horizontal Alignment, and Mask Vertical Alignment properties.  |  ![../../_images/mask-scale.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-scale.gif)  |  
|    
Use Screen Space sets whether to layout the mask relative to the screen. By default Kanzi layouts a mask relative to the node that uses the mask effect.  |  ![../../_images/mask-screen-space.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-screen-space.gif)  |  
|    
Mask Stretch sets the stretch mode of the mask:
     * None does not stretch the mask.
     * Fill stretches the mask so that it fills the node.
     * Uniform stretches the mask using uniform scaling to fill the node in either vertical or horizontal direction, whichever requires smaller scale.
     * Uniform To Fill stretches the mask using uniform scaling to fill the node in either vertical or horizontal direction, whichever requires larger scale.
     * Repeat does not stretch the mask, but allows the mask to repeat outside of its area based on the value of the Wrap Mode property in the texture that you set as the Mask Texture.
 |  ![../../_images/mask-stretch.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-stretch.gif)  |  
|    
Mask Channel sets the channel in the Mask Texture that you want to use as input for the mask:
     * Alpha uses the alpha channel from the texture. This is the default value.
     * Red uses the red color channel from the texture.
     * Green uses the green color channel from the texture.
     * Blue uses the blue color channel from the texture.
     * Luminance uses the luminance value calculated from the red, green, and blue color channels.
 |  ![../../_images/mask-channel.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-channel.gif)  |  
|

|    
Invert Mask sets whether to invert the mask so that transparent areas in the mask become opaque and the other way around.  |  ![../../_images/invert-mask.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/invert-mask.gif)  |

     * To disable the mask effect, use the value 0.
 |  ![../../_images/mask-strength.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-strength.gif)  |

## Creating an outline color effect[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/outline-effect-2d.html#creating-an-outline-color-effect "Link to this heading")
To create an outline color effect:
  1. In the Library, press `Alt` and right-click Effects and select Outline Effect 2D.
![../../_images/create-outline-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-outline-effect-2d.png)
  2. In the Node Tree or Prefabs, create a 2D node to which you want to apply the outline effect.
![../../_images/text-block-2d-in-node-tree.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-block-2d-in-node-tree.png) ![../../_images/text-block-2d-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-block-2d-in-preview.png)
  3. From the Library > Effects > 2D Effects, drag the Outline Effect 2D effect to the 2D node to which you want to apply the outline effect.
This way you set in that 2D node the Effect Prefab property to the Outline Effect 2D effect.
Kanzi applies to the visual shape of the content in the 2D node an outline that is black and four pixels wide.
![../../_images/drag-outline-effect-to-node.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/drag-outline-effect-to-node.png) ![../../_images/outline-effect-prefab-set.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/outline-effect-prefab-set.png) ![../../_images/outline-effect-default-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/outline-effect-default-preview.png)
  4. In the Library, select the Outline Effect 2D effect. In the Properties, use these properties to set the appearance of the outline:
     * Outline Blend Mode sets the blend mode that Kanzi uses to render the outline.
     * Outline Width sets the thickness of the outline in pixels.
     * Outline Color sets the color of the outline.
     * Outline Softness sets the length of a gradient, relative to the width of the outline, that softens the outline.
![../../_images/outline-color-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/outline-color-properties.png) ![../../_images/outline-color-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/outline-color-in-preview.png)

metadata.title: Using theOutline Effect 2Deffect (Part 2/7)

content:
## Creating a textured outline[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/outline-effect-2d.html#creating-a-textured-outline "Link to this heading")
You can apply a one-dimensional texture to an outline that you create with the Outline Effect 2D effect. For example, you can use a texture to add multiple strokes to text.
To create a textured outline:
  1. Create an outline effect for a 2D node. See [Creating an outline color effect](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/outline-effect-2d.html#creating-an-outline-color-effect).
![../../_images/outline-effect-prefab-set.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/outline-effect-prefab-set.png) ![../../_images/outline-effect-default-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/outline-effect-default-preview.png)
  2. In the Library, select the Outline Effect 2D effect. In the Properties, add and set:
     * Outline Width to the thickness in pixels that you want for the outline.
     * Outline Color to the color with which you want to modulate the color values in the outline texture.
To apply the colors in the outline texture as they are, set Outline Color to white.
     * Outline Texture to the texture that you want to apply to the outline.
Kanzi applies to the outline only the top row of pixels from this texture. The leftmost pixel in the texture maps to the innermost part of the outline and the rightmost pixel to the outmost part of the outline. Kanzi scales the width of the texture to the width of the outline.
For example, in the Outline Texture dropdown select + Import Image and import this image:
![../../_images/outline-texture-grays.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/outline-texture-grays.png)
![../../_images/outline-textured-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/outline-textured-properties.png) ![../../_images/outline-textured-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/outline-textured-in-preview.png)
  3. (Optional) To position and scale the texture along the outline, in the Properties, add and set these Outline Effect 2D properties:
     * Outline Texture Offset sets the relative start position at which Kanzi starts to sample the texture.
For example, to start the outline with the middle gray shade in the example texture, set Outline Texture Offset to 0.33.
     * Outline Texture Tiling sets the value by which Kanzi scales the outline texture.
For example, to create an outline that shows the texture twice, set Outline Texture Tiling to 2.
![../../_images/outline-repeated-texture-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/outline-repeated-texture-properties.png)
Tip
When you want a texture to repeat to cover the outline, in the Library > Materials and Textures > Textures, select that texture, and in the Properties, set Wrap Mode to Repeat.

  1. Create an effect and set a node to use it.
For example, create a Shadow Effect 2D effect and set an Image node to use it. See [Creating a shadow effect for a 2D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/shadow-effect-2d.html#creating-a-shadow-effect-for-a-2d-node).
![../../_images/effect-prefab-property-set.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/effect-prefab-property-set.png) ![../../_images/image-in-preview-w-shadow.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/image-in-preview-w-shadow.png)
  2. Customize a property in the effect:
    1. In the Library, select the effect that you created. In the Properties, next to the property that you want to customize, click ![image-publish-property](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/enable-editing-of-this-property.png).
Kanzi Studio creates from that property a custom property, adds it to the root of the effect prefab, and creates a `##Template` binding to the property in the 2D effect.
For example, click ![image-publish-property](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/enable-editing-of-this-property.png) next to Shadow Blur Radius property. Kanzi Studio creates a custom Shadow Blur Radius property, adds it to the root effect prefab, and creates in the Shadow Effect 2D effect prefab a `##Template` binding to the custom Shadow Blur Radius property.
![../../_images/properties-publish-shadow-blur-radius.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-publish-shadow-blur-radius.png) ![../../_images/properties-shadow-blur-radius-template-binding.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-shadow-blur-radius-template-binding.png)
    2. In the Node Tree or Prefabs, select the 2D node that uses the effect that you created. In the Properties, click ![image-add-property](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-property.png) next to the property that you customized and set the value of the property.
Kanzi Studio adds to the 2D node a To Source binding which pushes the value of that property to the effect instance made available through the `Node2D.Effect` property of the node.
You can set multiple 2D nodes to use the same effect and in each 2D node, you can add and set the property to have different values.
For example, in the Properties, add the Shadow Effect 2D Properties > ShadowEffect2D.BlurRadius property and use it to adjust the softness of the shadow only in the Image node.
![../../_images/properties-shadow-effect-2d-blur-radius.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-shadow-effect-2d-blur-radius.png) ![../../_images/preview-shadow-effect-2d-blur-radius.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-shadow-effect-2d-blur-radius.png)
  3. (Optional) Repeat the previous step for each effect property that you want to customize.
Tip
When you want to remove from a node a property and its To Source binding, right-click that property and select Remove Property And Binding.

To create a shadow effect for a 2D node:
  1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Effects and select Shadow Effect 2D.
![../../_images/create-shadow-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-shadow-effect-2d.png)
  2. In the Node Tree or Prefabs create a 2D node to which you want to apply the shadow effect.
![../../_images/image-in-node-tree.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/image-in-node-tree.png) ![../../_images/image-in-preview1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/image-in-preview1.png)
  3. From the Library > Effects > 2D Effects drag the Shadow Effect 2D effect to the Node Tree or Prefabs and drop it on the 2D node to which you want to apply the shadow effect.
This way you set in that 2D node the Effect Prefab property to the Shadow Effect 2D effect.
Kanzi applies to the visual shape of the content in the 2D node a partially transparent black drop shadow directed at a 45-degree angle relative to the positive x axis.
![../../_images/drag-effect-to-node.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/drag-effect-to-node.png) ![../../_images/effect-prefab-property-set.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/effect-prefab-property-set.png) ![../../_images/image-in-preview-w-shadow.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/image-in-preview-w-shadow.png)
  4. To adjust the appearance of the shadow, in the Library select the Shadow Effect 2D effect and in the Properties add and set the Shadow Effect 2D properties.
![../../_images/shadow-effect-2d-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/shadow-effect-2d-properties.png) ![../../_images/shadow-effect-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/shadow-effect-in-preview.png)  
|    
Shadow Blend Mode sets the blend mode that Kanzi uses to render the shadow. The default is Alpha: Premultiplied. For example, use the Multiply (advanced khr) blend mode to create a more realistic shadow. See [Blending and compositing 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/blending-2d-nodes.html).  |    
 |  
| --- | --- |  
|    
Shadow Blur Radius sets the softness of the shadow by defining the distance in pixels that the shadow blur extends outward from each edge of the shadow. The higher the value, the blurrier the shadow is. The default radius is 8 pixels.  |  ![../../_images/shadow-blur-radius.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/shadow-blur-radius.gif)  |  
|    
Shadow Type sets the type of the shadow:
     * Drop Shadow appears behind or below an object. This is the default.
     * Inner Shadow appears inside an object.
 |  ![../../_images/shadow-type.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/shadow-type.gif)  |

## Customizing an instance of a shadow effect[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/shadow-effect-2d.html#customizing-an-instance-of-a-shadow-effect "Link to this heading")
When you edit the properties of an effect in the Library > Effects, you change the appearance of that effect for all nodes that use it. You can customize each effect instance by overriding the effect property values. For example:
  * When you create a Shadow Effect 2D effect, you can vary the softness of the shadow in different instances of that effect.
  * When you create a Mask Effect 2D effect, you can vary the size of the mask in different instances of that effect.
  * When you create a Blur Effect 2D effect, you can vary the amount of blur in different instances of that effect.
  * When you create an Outline Effect 2D effect, you can vary the color of the outline in different instances of that effect.

## Applying multiple effects to a 2D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/multiple-effects.html#applying-multiple-effects-to-a-2d-node "Link to this heading")
To apply multiple effects to a 2D node:
  1. In the Library, press `Alt` and right-click Effects and select Effect Stack 2D.
![../../_images/library-create-effect-stack-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/library-create-effect-stack-2d.png)
  2. In the Node Tree or Prefabs, create a 2D node to which you want to apply multiple effects.
![../../_images/text-block-2d-in-node-tree.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-block-2d-in-node-tree.png) ![../../_images/preview-text-block-2d-start.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-text-block-2d-start.png)
  3. In the Properties, add the Effect Prefab property and set it to the Effect Stack 2D.
This way, you assign the effect prefab to the node so that you can follow the creation of the effects in the Preview.
![../../_images/properties-text-block-2d-effect-prefab.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-text-block-2d-effect-prefab.png)
  4. In the Library in the Effect Stack 2D effect prefab, create the effects that you want to apply to the 2D node.
Kanzi applies the effects to the content of the node in the order that the effects appear in the Effect Stack 2D, from top to bottom.
For example, create:
    1. Outline Effect 2D effect. See [Using the Outline Effect 2D effect](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/outline-effect-2d.html).
![../../_images/library-effect-stack-outline.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/library-effect-stack-outline.png) ![../../_images/preview-effect-stack-outline.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-effect-stack-outline.png)
    2. Shadow Effect 2D effect. See [Using the Shadow Effect 2D effect](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/shadow-effect-2d.html).
![../../_images/library-effect-stack-shadow.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/library-effect-stack-shadow.png) ![../../_images/preview-multi-effect-layered.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-multi-effect-layered.png)
  5. (Optional) To control how Kanzi applies the effects in a stack, in an effect, add the Effect Stack 2D > Effect Stacking Mode property and set it to:
     * Chained to use as input for the effect the output of the previous effect.
For example, this way, when you apply the Shadow Effect 2D after the Outline Effect 2D, you apply the shadow also to the outline. By default, the outline is not included in the shadow.
     * Layered to use as input for the effect the output of the previous chained effect.
This is the default mode for the Shadow Effect 2D and Outline Effect 2D effects.
The Effect Stacking Mode property has no impact on the Mask Effect 2D and Blur Effect 2D effects, which always use the Chained mode.

## Using the Default Effect Stack 2D preset[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/multiple-effects.html#using-the-default-effect-stack-2d-preset "Link to this heading")
To help you get started with the Effect Stack 2D, Kanzi Studio comes with the Default Effect Stack 2D preset.
To use the Default Effect Stack 2D preset:
  1. In the Library, press `Alt` and right-click Effects and select Default Effect Stack 2D.
![../../_images/library-create-default-effect-stack-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/library-create-default-effect-stack-2d.png)
Kanzi Studio creates in the Library > Effects > 2D Effects an Effect Stack 2D effect prefab named Default Effect Stack 2D and inside it:
     * Mask Effect 2D effect named Mask
     * Shadow Effect 2D effect named Shadow
     * Outline Effect 2D effect named Outline
     * Blur Effect 2D effect named Blur
The most common properties of each effect have bindings to the Default Effect Stack 2D. This way you can set each effect in the Default Effect Stack 2D.
![../../_images/library-default-effect-stack-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/library-default-effect-stack-2d.png) ![../../_images/properties-default-effect-stack-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-default-effect-stack-2d.png)
  2. In the Node Tree or Prefabs, create a 2D node to which you want to apply multiple effects.
![../../_images/node-tree-image.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-image.png) ![../../_images/preview-image.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-image.png)
  3. In the Properties, add the Effect Prefab property and set it to the Default Effect Stack 2D.
By default, the Default Effect Stack 2D preset applies the default Shadow Effect 2D effect. All other effects in the Default Effect Stack 2D are disabled.
When you set a node to use the Default Effect Stack 2D, Kanzi Studio adds to that node the properties that you can use to set the blur, mask, outline, and shadow effects in the Default Effect Stack 2D.
![../../_images/properties-image-effect-prefab-default-stack.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-image-effect-prefab-default-stack.png) ![../../_images/preview-default-effect-stack-initial.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-default-effect-stack-initial.png)
  4. In the Properties, add and set the Effect Stack properties.
For example, add and set:
     * Mask Enabled to enabled
     * Mask Texture to the texture that you want to use as the mask
     * Outline Enabled to enabled
     * Outline Color to the color that you want to use for the outline
     * Shadow Distance to 20
![../../_images/image-properties-default-stack-configured.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/image-properties-default-stack-configured.png) ![../../_images/preview-default-effect-stack-configured.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-default-effect-stack-configured.png)

## Creating a frosted glass effect[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/multiple-effects.html#creating-a-frosted-glass-effect "Link to this heading")
In this procedure, you use the Effect Stack 2D effect prefab with the Blur Effect 2D, Mask Effect 2D, and Shadow Effect 2D effects to create a frosted glass effect.
![../../_images/frosted-glass-with-content.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/frosted-glass-with-content.png)
To create a frosted glass effect:
  1. Create the background for the frosted glass effect:
    1. Create the nodes that you want to use as the background of the frosted glass.
For example, in the Node Tree, create an Image node and name it Background. In the Properties, add and set:
       * Image to a texture that shows an image that you want to use as the backdrop of the frosted glass effect.
       * Horizontal Alignment and Vertical Alignment to Stretch
       * Content Stretch to Uniform to fill
![../../_images/background-in-node-tree.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/background-in-node-tree.png) ![../../_images/background-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/background-properties.png)
    2. In the Library, press `Alt` and right-click Materials and Textures, select Render Target Texture, and name it Background Render Target. In the Properties, set the Width and Height properties to at least the width and height of the background that you created in the previous step.
If the size of the background is fixed, you can enable the Automatic setting. This way, you set the render target texture to the size of the node that uses this texture.
![../../_images/create-render-target-texture1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-render-target-texture1.png) ![../../_images/background-render-target-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/background-render-target-properties.png)
    3. In the Node Tree, select the node that shows the background of the frosted glass. In the Properties, add the Render Target > Render Target property and set it to Background Render Target.
This way, you set Kanzi to render the background both to the screen and to the Background Render Target render target texture. You use the Background Render Target render target texture later in this procedure to render a part of the background in the node that shows the frosted glass.
![../../_images/background-render-target.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/background-render-target.png)
    4. In the Node Tree, press `Alt` and right-click the node that shows the background of the frosted glass and select Alias.
Kanzi Studio creates in the resource dictionary of the Screen node an alias that points to the background node. You use this alias later in this procedure to access the background node in a binding.

metadata.title: Using multiple effects (Part 6/15)

For example, set it to 32.

You set the blur effect to blur only those pixels in the node whose alpha channel value is not zero. This way, you prevent the blur from spreading to fully transparent pixels and the edges of the content stay sharp.

    6. In the Library > Effects > 2D Effects, press `Alt` and right-click Frosted Glass Effect and select Shadow Effect 2D.
This way, you add a drop shadow to the frosted glass.
The Shadow Effect 2D by default applies to the visual shape of the content in a 2D node a partially transparent black drop shadow directed at a 45-degree angle relative to the positive x axis.

## Adding a 2D UI control to a 3D scene[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/2D-nodes-in-3D-scene.html#adding-a-2d-ui-control-to-a-3d-scene "Link to this heading")
In this procedure, you use the Viewport 3D node to add a 2D color picker to a 3D scene.
![../../_images/preview-viewport-3d-complete.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-viewport-3d-complete.gif)
To add a 2D UI control to a 3D scene:
  1. In the Prefabs, create a 2D prefab that contains the 2D nodes that you want to add to a 3D scene.
For example, create a color picker with a slider. See [Creating a color picker with a slider](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/sliders/using-sliders.html#creating-a-color-picker-with-a-slider).
![../../_images/prefabs-color-picker.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/prefabs-color-picker.png) ![../../_images/preview-color-wheel-prefab.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-color-wheel-prefab.png)
  2. In the Node Tree or Prefabs, create a 3D scene to which you want to add 2D nodes.
For example, use the Car from the Factory Content.
See [Using the Factory Content assets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/using-the-factory-content-assets.html).
![../../_images/preview-fc-car.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-fc-car.png)
  3. In the Node Tree or Prefabs, press `Alt` and right-click the 3D node to which you want to add 2D nodes and select Viewport 3D.
For example, create a Viewport 3D node in the Prefabs > CarScene > RootNode node.
![../../_images/prefabs-create-viewport-3d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/prefabs-create-viewport-3d.png) ![../../_images/prefabs-viewport-3d-color-picker.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/prefabs-viewport-3d-color-picker.png)
  4. Select the Viewport 3D node and in the Properties, add and set:
     * Prefab Template property to the 2D prefab whose content you want to add to the 3D scene.
For example, select the Color Picker prefab.
Kanzi first renders the content of the prefab to a texture, and then renders that texture on a 3D plane.
     * Render Transformation or Layout Transformation to position and orient the 2D prefab in the 3D scene.
For example, add the Render Transformation property and set:
       * Rotation X property field to -90
       * Rotation Y property field to 90
       * Translation Y property field to 0.1
This way you position the 2D prefab just above the floor under the car.
![../../_images/properties-prefab-template-and-transform.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-prefab-template-and-transform.png) ![../../_images/preview-color-picker-initial.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-color-picker-initial.png)
  5. To set the size of the 2D content in the 3D scene, in the Properties, add and set:
     * 2D to 3D Projection Scale to the scaling factor that you want to use to project the 2D content to the 3D space.

Use the Perspective Transformation property to create a 3D perspective effect for 2D nodes. With the Layout Transformation Rotation property field you can rotate a node only in the 2D space, around the z axis. With the Perspective Transformation Rotation X, Y, and Z property fields you can rotate a 2D node around all three axes, creating a 3D perspective effect.
The Perspective Transformation property transforms the node after it applies the layout pass, but before it renders the node.
To create a 3D perspective effect for a 2D node:
  1. In the Node Tree create or select a 2D node for which you want to create a 3D perspective effect. For example, create an Image node.
![../../_images/image-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/image-in-project.png) ![../../_images/image-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/image-in-preview.png)
  2. In the Properties add the Perspective Transformation property.
![../../_images/add-perspective-transformation-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-perspective-transformation-property.png)
  3. In the Properties in the Perspective Transformation property set:
     * Rotation X to the number of degrees you want to rotate the node around the x axis.
     * Rotation Y to the number of degrees you want to rotate the node around the y axis.
     * Rotation Z to the number of degrees you want to rotate the node around the z axis.
For example, set the Perspective Transformation Rotation Y property field to 45 to rotate the image 45 degrees around the y axis.
![../../_images/perspective-transformation-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/perspective-transformation-properties.png) ![../../_images/image-perspective-y-rotated-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/image-perspective-y-rotated-in-preview.png)
  4. (Optional) In the Properties add the Render Transformation Origin property and set:

4. (Optional) In the Properties add the Render Transformation Origin property and set:
     * X to the percentage of the node width you want to set the origin on the x axis
     * Y to the percentage of the node height you want to set the origin on the y axis
In Kanzi by default the origin of all 2D nodes is in the upper left corner of the node. You use the Render Transformation Origin property to set the origin of the node.
For example, if you set the Perspective Transformation property to rotate the node around the y axis, to make the node rotate around its horizontal center point set the Render Transformation Origin X property field to 0,5.

To apply custom rendering to a 2D node, use the Composition Brush property to compose the node on the screen with a Material Brush, and enable the Force Composition property.
To apply custom rendering to a 2D node:

For example, to create a material that converts color to grayscale:

    2. In the Library > Materials and Textures > Material Types, expand the material type that you created. Double-click the Vertex Shader to open it in the Shader Source Editor, replace the existing shader code with this code, and save the shader.

```
#version 310 es

in vec3 kzPosition;
in vec2 kzTextureCoordinate0;
uniform highp mat4 kzProjectionCameraWorldMatrix;

out mediump vec2 vTexCoord;

void main()
{
    precision mediump float;
    vTexCoord = kzTextureCoordinate0;
    gl_Position = kzProjectionCameraWorldMatrix * vec4(kzPosition.xyz, 1.0);
}

```

To improve the performance of your application, you can cache the rendering of 2D nodes that become static after a certain point or change only seldom. Use this method to speed up the rendering of complex nodes.
When you enable caching for a 2D node, that node generates a cache image for itself, renders itself to it, and for future frames uses this generated cache image instead of rendering itself again.
You can:
  * Set Kanzi to update the render cache automatically when needed. See [Using automatic render cache updates](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/caching-2d-nodes.html#using-automatic-render-cache-updates).
  * Control the render cache updates manually. See [Controlling render cache updates manually](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/caching-2d-nodes.html#controlling-render-cache-updates-manually).


To cache the rendering of 3D content, configure the caching in the parent Viewport 2D node of the Scene node that contains the 3D content that you want to cache.
Because caching consumes GPU memory, it is by default disabled. When caching is disabled for a node, Kanzi renders that node normally and frees all resources associated with the render cache.

content:
## Using automatic render cache updates[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/caching-2d-nodes.html#using-automatic-render-cache-updates "Link to this heading")
Use automatic render cache updates for complex nodes that are expensive to render and whose rendering does not change often. You can set Kanzi to cache a 2D node and automatically update the render cache when the rendering of that node or its descendant nodes changes and the cache image no longer correctly represents that node. For example, when the size or shape of a node change.
Tip
When you want to enable automatic cache updates for a complex node whose rendering does not change often but that has child nodes whose rendering changes often, move those child nodes to a separate node.
To set Kanzi to update the render cache of a 2D node automatically, in the Node Tree select the node, in the Properties add the Render Target > Caching Mode property, and set it to Automatic.
This way you set Kanzi to cache the node the next time it renders the node and does not detect changes in the rendering of the node or its descendants.
When you enable automatic render cache updates, Kanzi keeps checking for changes to the node or its descendant nodes during rendering:
  * If the nodes are static, Kanzi recreates the cache image or renders the nodes using an existing and still valid cache image.
  * If the rendering of the nodes changes, Kanzi invalidates the cache image and renders the nodes normally without caching.

![../../_images/caching-mode-automatic.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/caching-mode-automatic.png)

metadata.title: Caching 2D nodes (Part 2/3)
metadata.breadcrumb: Working with … > 2D content > Caching 2D nodes

content:
## Controlling render cache updates manually[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/caching-2d-nodes.html#controlling-render-cache-updates-manually "Link to this heading")
When you know exactly when the render cache of a 2D node needs updating, you can control the cache updates manually. You can enable caching for a node and set Kanzi to update the render cache when the node or any of its descendants change. For example, use the Set Property action or a binding to invalidate the render cache that you want Kanzi to update.
To control the render cache updates manually:
  1. In the Node Tree select the node that you want to cache, in the Properties add the Render Target > Caching Mode property, and set it to Enabled.
This way you set Kanzi to cache the node the next time it renders that node, and to keep rendering the node from the cache until you invalidate the cache.
If Kanzi already cached the node, it does not automatically update the cache.
![../../_images/caching-mode-enabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/caching-mode-enabled.png)
  2. To set Kanzi to update the render cache, invalidate the render cache by disabling the Cache Valid property in the node whose render cache you want to update.
Set the cache invalidation to happen when you know that the node or any of its descendants change and you want Kanzi to update the render cache the next time it renders that node.
For example, in a trigger that sets the node to change, create a Set Property action that disables the Cache Valid property.
Note
Invalidating the render cache does not free any resources allocated by the node.
To free the resources associated with the render cache, set the Caching Mode property to Disabled.

## How Kanzi applies 2D effects[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/2d-effects.html#how-k-applies-2d-effects "Link to this heading")
Kanzi applies 2D effects to the visual shape of the content in a node and its descendant nodes.
![../../_images/effect-node.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/effect-node.png) ![../../_images/parent-children-effect-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/parent-children-effect-preview.png)
When you want to apply an effect to a node but not to its descendant nodes, place the descendant nodes in a sibling node of the node to which you apply the effect. Position that sibling node in the node tree below the node to which you apply the effect. Make sure that the sibling nodes are of the same size, layout, transformation, and opacity.
![../../_images/effect-node-2.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/effect-node-2.png) ![../../_images/parent-only-effect-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/parent-only-effect-preview.png)
## Effects and layout[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/2d-effects.html#effects-and-layout "Link to this heading")
When you use effects, keep in mind that:
  * Kanzi does not take effects into account when calculating layout. When your design does not allow an effect to exceed the layout bounds, make sure that there is enough space in the layout for that effect.
For example, in a layout that contains a Text Block 2D node where you apply a drop shadow, in that Text Block 2D node ensure sufficient space for the shadow by setting the Horizontal Margin and Vertical Margin properties.
![../../_images/shadow-margin.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/shadow-margin.png)
  * When Kanzi applies an effect to a 2D node, it composites that node and clips its descendant nodes to the node bounds, regardless of the value of the Clip Children property. This happens because the size of the render target texture matches the size of the node.


## Impact of effects on application performance[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/2d-effects.html#impact-of-effects-on-application-performance "Link to this heading")
For every instance of an effect Kanzi requests the composition manager to provide a temporary composition target. Kanzi composition manager reuses temporary composition targets if they are compatible in size and parameters.
The final performance of an application that uses effects depends on:
  * The amount of allocated memory, and therefore the bandwidth required to render the UI of the application
  * The number of draw calls
  * The number of render target or texture switches


To find the most efficient way of using effects, test the performance of your application with these approaches:
  * Apply a separate effect to each UI element to minimize the area.
  * Apply an effect to a group of UI elements that cover a larger area.

content:
## Applying anti-aliasing[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/2d-effects.html#applying-anti-aliasing "Link to this heading")
When you apply an effect to a 2D node, Kanzi renders that node to a composition target. By default, Kanzi does not apply anti-aliasing to the child nodes of a composited node. For example, when you rotate these nodes, their edges can look jaggy.
![../../_images/node-tree-flow-layout.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-flow-layout.png) ![../../_images/preview-no-msaa.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-no-msaa.png)
To apply multisample anti-aliasing:
  1. In the Node Tree or Prefabs, select the node to which you apply the effect.
  2. In the Properties, add the Render Target > Multisample Level property and set it to the number of anti-aliasing samples that you want to use.
See the documentation of the device on which you want to run your Kanzi application for supported values, because the number of anti-aliasing samples depends on the device. If you set the Multisample Level property to a value that your device does not support, Kanzi Engine clamps the value to the largest value supported by the device driver.
