## GPU resources[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#gpu-resources "Link to this heading")
### HandleGPUResources[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#handlegpuresources "Link to this heading")
You can set how your Kanzi application handles in the paused state (`MainLoopState::Paused[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11119.html#ae35554056f5fa4e74b1d5d5921bf8ea4ae99180abf47a8b3a856e0bcb2656990a)`) the GPU resources that are not stored in a kzb file.  
| In `application.cfg`  | `HandleGPUResources = handling`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.handleGPUResources = handling`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `handling`  |  The way to handle GPU resources in the paused state. To do nothing (default value on all platforms except Android):
  * In `application.cfg` use `none`.
  * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `ApplicationProperties::HandleGPUResources::NoHandling[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11374.html#af88b724d0e6d13456a45ddf2a4afe910a9066d42e3bd95606b9294d74c176629f)`.

To invalidate the GPU resources (default value on Android):
  * In `application.cfg` use `invalidate`.
  * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `ApplicationProperties::HandleGPUResources::Invalidate[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11374.html#af88b724d0e6d13456a45ddf2a4afe910a07fd9d526a0330e197fb396ebc3349ba)`.

To destroy the GPU resources:
  * In `application.cfg` use `destroy`.
  * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `ApplicationProperties::HandleGPUResources::Destroy[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11374.html#af88b724d0e6d13456a45ddf2a4afe910a10cdebab75c28d3535e4c5f9a8283ceb)`.

 |  
| --- | --- |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Invalidates the GPU resources.
HandleGPUResources = invalidate

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
| `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` example  |  
```

## QNX system logger (slogger2)[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#qnx-system-logger-slogger2 "Link to this heading")
On QNX you can use the QNX system logger (slogger2) to write log messages. When you redirect log messages to slogger2, your Kanzi application continues writing the log messages to the default logger.
A Kanzi application does not use the default slogger2 buffer, which allows you to use `slog2_set_default_buffer`. Kanzi provides slogger2 that supports logging to only one slogger2 buffer. When slogger2 stops logging, Kanzi calls `slog2_reset`. To change this behavior, see: [Cleaning up after slogger2](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/logging/logging.html#cleaning-up-after-slogger2).
Keep in mind that slogger2 initializes after Kanzi reads the configuration for your Kanzi application. For this reason the slogger2 logs do not contain the log messages before that time.
To use slogger2, you can either:
  * Configure slogger2 in the `application.cfg` or `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`.
  * Provide a custom slogger2 buffer to the Kanzi logger. See [customSlog2Buffer](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#customslog2buffer).


### QnxEnableSlogger2[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#qnxenableslogger2 "Link to this heading")
Before you can use slogger2 with your Kanzi application, you must enable it.  
| In `application.cfg`  | `QnxEnableSlogger2 = value`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.slog2Config.enabled = value`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `true`  | Enable slogger2.  |  
| --- | --- |  
| `false`  | Disable slogger2. Default value.  |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Enable logging to slogger2.
QnxEnableSlogger2 = true

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
| `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` example  |  
```
// Enable logging to slogger2.
configuration.slog2Config.enabled = true;

```
Copy to clipboard  |

### QnxSlogger2VerbosityLevel[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#qnxslogger2verbositylevel "Link to this heading")
You can set which log messages you want slogger2 to log. The Kanzi application configuration verbosity levels map to the slogger2 log verbosity levels.

| Values  |   
 | `Slog2Shutdown`  | Maps to the slogger2 level `SLOG2_SHUTDOWN`.  |  
| --- | --- |  
| `Slog2Critical`  | Maps to the slogger2 level `SLOG2_CRITICAL`.  |  
| `Slog2Error`  | Maps to the slogger2 level `SLOG2_ERROR`.  |  
| `Slog2Warning`  | Maps to the slogger2 level `SLOG2_WARNING`.  |  
| `Slog2Notice`  | Maps to the slogger2 level `SLOG2_NOTICE`.  |  
| `Slog2Info`  | Maps to the slogger2 level `SLOG2_INFO`.  |  
| `Slog2Debug1`  | Maps to the slogger2 level `SLOG2_DEBUG1`.  |

### QnxSlogger2MaxRetries[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#qnxslogger2maxretries "Link to this heading")
On QNX versions 7.0.4 and newer you can limit the amount of times slogger2 retries to obtain a buffer.
When you set this limit and slogger2 reaches it, Kanzi drops the log message and increases the dropped message count. You can see the number of dropped messages in the slogger2 logs in the next non-dropped log entry of the variable `code` written before the log message.  
| In `application.cfg`  | `QnxSlogger2MaxRetries = value`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.slog2Config.maxRetries = value`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `value`  | uint32_t value that sets the limit. By default a Kanzi application sets this to `Slog2UnlimitedRetries` (`UINT32_MAX`). This means that the number of retries is not limited.  |  
| --- | --- |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Set the retry limit to 10 retries.
QnxSlogger2MaxRetries = 10

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
| `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` example  |  
```
// Set the retry limit to 10 retries.
configuration.slog2Config.maxRetries = 10;

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
### pageCount[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#pagecount "Link to this heading")
You can set the multiple of 4KB pages that the QNX logger acquires for the internal slogger2 buffer.  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.slog2Config.pageCount = value`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Values  |   
 | `value`  | Integer value for the number of pages to allocate for the slogger2 buffer. The default is 8.  |  
| --- | --- |  
 |  
| `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` example  |  
```
// For example, when you set the slogger2 verbosity level to
// SLOG2_ERROR slogger2 writes to log less frequently
// (low rate logging), and by decreasing the page count
// you can increase the logging pace.
configuration.slog2Config.pageCount = 1;

```

### customSlog2Buffer[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#customslog2buffer "Link to this heading")
Kanzi enables you to register a custom slogger2 buffer and pass it to a Kanzi application. Your Kanzi application then uses the buffer to write logs. For example, you can register a custom slogger2 buffer when you want to give the buffer a custom name or if you want to set any of the properties from the `slog2_buffer_set_config_t` structure passed to `slog2_register`. See [QNX system logger (slogger2)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/logging/logging.html#qnx-system-logger-slogger2).

## Graphics library[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#graphics-library "Link to this heading")
On the Windows operating system you can select whether you want to use OpenGL ES, OpenGL, or Vulkan in the `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` function, in the `application.cfg`, or using the command line arguments, if your target supports command line arguments.
On the command line use:
  * `--gles` or `--opengles` to use OpenGL ES
  * `--gl` or `--opengl` to use OpenGL
  * `--vk` or `--vulkan` to use Vulkan
  * `--egl` to use EGL
  * `--wgl` to use WGL
  * `--glx` to use GLX

  
| In `application.cfg`  |  `SurfaceClientAPI = clientApi` `GraphicsContextAPI = contextApi`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  |  `configuration.defaultSurfaceProperties.clientAPI = clientApi;` `configuration.defaultSurfaceProperties.contextAPI = contextApi;`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `clientApi`  |  To use OpenGL ES:
  * In `application.cfg` use `gles` or `opengles`.
  * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `SurfaceClientAPI::OpenGLES[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11119.html#a6559e617448fb7945ea688c318ec43a6af4b7db07e13ba92157b1b7d961abfaae)`.

To use OpenGL:
  * In `application.cfg` use `gl` or `opengl`.
  * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `SurfaceClientAPI::OpenGL[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11119.html#a6559e617448fb7945ea688c318ec43a6a760716b590ee7c0adc25f434f577d8be)`.

To use Vulkan:
  * In `application.cfg` use `vk` or `vulkan`.
  * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `SurfaceClientAPI::Vulkan[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11119.html#a6559e617448fb7945ea688c318ec43a6a38625270231b647116c80bcbc4f9d1d8)`.

 |  
| --- | --- |  
| `contextApi`  |  To use WGL:
  * In `application.cfg` use `wgl`.
  * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `GraphicsContextAPI::WGL[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11119.html#a6f5c2a73db0b2d1b65db9b192a451013aef3c7326c5c23cc9c408d29410352b67)`.

metadata.breadcrumb: Working with … > Application > Application configuration reference

content:
To use EGL:

  * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `GraphicsContextAPI::EGL[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11119.html#a6f5c2a73db0b2d1b65db9b192a451013ab1e1fe0cc927dbeae22dc1839e01bb20)`.

### GraphicsStatisticEnabled[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#graphicsstatisticenabled "Link to this heading")
You can enable the statistics layer for the Kanzi graphics library of your application. The statistics layer is always enabled in the debug mode, regardless of the configuration. The statistics layer shows the information about the Kanzi graphics objects in the Performance HUD. See [Showing the performance measurement graphs in the Performance HUD](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/performance-profiling/profiling-kanzi-engine.html#showing-performance-measurement-graphs).

 |

# Enables the statistics layer for the Kanzi graphics library.

```

## Surface properties[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#surface-properties "Link to this heading")
Surface properties control the properties of the hardware-accelerated graphics surface onto which Kanzi renders. They control the relation between image quality and rendering speed.
The surface properties that you set are considered requests to be matched by the graphics system of the target hardware. Whether a given request is considered an upper bound, a lower bound, or an exact value, is platform-dependent.
To get the platform-dependent default values of surface properties, call `kzsSurfaceGetDefaultProperties()`.

### Color format[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#color-format "Link to this heading")
You can set the sizes of the RGB color channels and the alpha channel in bits.  
| In `application.cfg`  |  `SurfaceBitsRed = red` `SurfaceBitsGreen = green` `SurfaceBitsBlue = blue` `SurfaceBitsAlpha = alpha`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  |  `configuration.defaultSurfaceProperties.bitsColorR = red;` `configuration.defaultSurfaceProperties.bitsColorG = green;` `configuration.defaultSurfaceProperties.bitsColorB = blue;` `configuration.defaultSurfaceProperties.bitsAlpha = alpha;`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `red`  | Size of the red color channel in bits.  |  
| --- | --- |  
| `green`  | Size of the green color channel in bits.  |  
| `blue`  | Size of the blue color channel in bits.  |  
| `alpha`  | Size of the alpha channel in bits.  |  
The default size of each channel is 8 bits.
To let the platform choose the value, use `"unspecified"`.
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Set the sizes of the color and alpha channels for a typical
# high-speed rendering application.
SurfaceBitsRed = 5
SurfaceBitsGreen = 6
SurfaceBitsBlue = 5
SurfaceBitsAlpha = 0

```

# Let the platform choose the sizes of the color and alpha channels.

SurfaceBitsGreen = "unspecified"
SurfaceBitsBlue = "unspecified"
SurfaceBitsAlpha = "unspecified"

```

```

configuration.defaultSurfaceProperties.bitsColorG = 6;

configuration.defaultSurfaceProperties.bitsAlpha = 0;

```
Copy to clipboard To let the platform choose the color and alpha channel sizes:

configuration.systemConfiguration[ConfigurationKeyDefaultSurfaceBitsGreen] = "unspecified";

### SurfaceColorSpace[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#surfacecolorspace "Link to this heading")
You can enable the initialization of OpenGL for the hardware that displays your Kanzi application.  
| In `application.cfg`  | `SurfaceColorSpace = colorSpace`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.defaultSurfaceProperties.colorSpace = colorSpace;`  |  
| On the command line  | `-surface-color-space=colorSpace`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `colorSpace`  |  Enables the initialization of OpenGL for the hardware that displays the application.
  * To use the sRGB color space:
    * In `application.cfg` use `"srgb"`.
    * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `SurfaceColorSpace::sRGB[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11119.html#aea49f8797d15f7dc3cade46e372cc469a9ed33d9be17d174aeb4393a989586ed9)`.
    * On the command line use `srgb`.
Use this option when your application uses the linear color workflow, where Kanzi performs operations on color values in linear color space. The linear color workflow requires:
    * OpenGL extension GL_EXT_sRGB
    * EGL version 1.5 or later, or EGL version 1.4 with the EGL_KHR_gl_colorspace extension
When you use the sRGB color space, Kanzi expects that in the Kanzi Studio project properties the Color Workflow property is set to Linear. See [Using the linear color workflow](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html#using-the-linear-color-workflow).
  * To use an unspecified color space:
    * In `application.cfg` use `"standard"`.
    * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `SurfaceColorSpace::Standard[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11119.html#aea49f8797d15f7dc3cade46e372cc469aeb6d8ae6f20283755b339c0dc273988b)`.
    * On the command line use `standard`.
This is the default. Use this option when your application uses the standard color workflow, where Kanzi performs operations on color values in the nonlinear gamma color space. When you use an unspecified color space, Kanzi expects that in the Kanzi Studio project properties the Color Workflow property is set to Standard (default value). See [Using the standard color workflow](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html#using-the-standard-color-workflow).
  * To pass the shader output directly to the graphics surface:
    * In `application.cfg` use `"passthrough"`.

When you use a custom color space, Kanzi expects that in the Kanzi Studio project properties the Color Workflow property is set to Linear.

### SwapBehavior[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#swapbehavior "Link to this heading")
You can set whether to swap or copy buffers during buffer swap.  
| In `application.cfg`  | `SwapBehavior = swap`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.defaultSurfaceProperties.swapBehaviorCopy = swap;`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `swap`  |  Sets whether to swap or copy buffers during buffer swap. To let Kanzi automatically select whether to copy or swap the buffers, in `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `SwapBehavior::Unspecified[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11119.html#a75613725197ccf3a1355558404dac0bfa6fcdc090caeade09d0efd6253932b6f5)`. This is the default value. To copy the buffers:
  * In `application.cfg` use `"copy"`.
  * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `SwapBehavior::Copy[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11119.html#a75613725197ccf3a1355558404dac0bfa5fb63579fc981698f97d55bfecb213ea)`.

To swap the buffers:
  * In `application.cfg` use `"exchange"`.
  * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `SwapBehavior::Exchange[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11119.html#a75613725197ccf3a1355558404dac0bfa992374d8e2e24f17bebc50a6e57becd6)`.

 |  
| --- | --- |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Copy buffers during buffer swap.
SwapBehavior = "copy"

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
| `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` example  |  
```
// Copy buffers during buffer swap.
configuration.defaultSurfaceProperties.swapBehaviorCopy = SwapBehavior::Copy;

```
Copy to clipboard  |

### PresentMode[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#presentmode "Link to this heading")
You can set the surface present mode. Not all platforms support this setting.  
| In `application.cfg`  | `PresentMode = mode`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.defaultSurfaceProperties.presentMode = mode;`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `mode`  |  Sets the surface present mode.
  * To queue and swap buffers in the order given during the VBLANK interval.
    * In `application.cfg` use `fifo`. Default value.
    * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `platform::PresentMode::FIFO[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11143.html#a71ba3f36085d689cba3be2ae864530d8ac589858dbe1d06c46544266ae4cd2c6f)`. Default value.
  * To swap buffers at any time. Tearing can occur.
    * In `application.cfg` use `immediate`.
    * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `platform::PresentMode::Immediate[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11143.html#a71ba3f36085d689cba3be2ae864530d8a43f6615bbb2c40a5306ff804094420b1)`.
  * To set `FIFORelaxed` mode. Similar to FIFO, but if no image is available, the next image is immediate. This option prefers tearing over showing a stale image.
    * In `application.cfg` use `fiforelaxed`.
    * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `platform::PresentMode::FIFORelaxed[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11143.html#a71ba3f36085d689cba3be2ae864530d8adaf9234613f238288f3bc5482274e555)`.
  * To set `Mailbox` mode. Similar to FIFO, but only a single surface is in the queue. If the second surface is prepared before the next VBLANK, replaces the surface.
    * In `application.cfg` use `mailbox`.
    * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `platform::PresentMode::Mailbox[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11143.html#a71ba3f36085d689cba3be2ae864530d8a2dcff8c037093c5d3552ad532e603f9f)`.

 |  
| --- | --- |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Swap buffers at any time.
PresentMode = immediate

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
| `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` example  |  
```
// Swap buffers at any time.
configuration.defaultSurfaceProperties.presentMode = kanzi::platform::PresentMode::Immediate;

### EGLIMGContextPriority[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#eglimgcontextpriority "Link to this heading")
You can create an EGL IMG context with a priority hint. By default, Kanzi lets the platform choose the priority.  
| In `application.cfg`  | `EGLIMGContextPriority = priority`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.defaultSurfaceProperties.priority = priority;`  |  
| On the command line  | `-egl-img-context-priority=priority`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `priority`  |  Enables the creation of an EGL IMG context with a priority hint. By default, Kanzi lets the platform choose the priority. To set low priority:
  * In `application.cfg` use `"low"`.
  * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `EGLIMGContextPriority::Low[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11119.html#ab90f37a14217a735d13d1c1f2a455cafa28d0edd045e05cf5af64e35ae0c4c6ef)`.
  * On the command line use `low`.

To set medium priority:
  * In `application.cfg` use `"medium"`.
  * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `EGLIMGContextPriority::Medium[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11119.html#ab90f37a14217a735d13d1c1f2a455cafa87f8a6ab85c9ced3702b4ea641ad4bb5)`.
  * On the command line use `medium`.

To set high priority:
  * In `application.cfg` use `"high"`.
  * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `EGLIMGContextPriority::High[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11119.html#ab90f37a14217a735d13d1c1f2a455cafa655d20c1ca69519ca647684edbb2db35)`.
  * On the command line use `high`.

 |  
| --- | --- |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Set the EGL IMG context priority to high.
EGLIMGContextPriority = "high"

```
Copy to clipboard 
```
# Let the platform choose the EGL IMG context priority.
EGLIMGContextPriority = "unspecified"

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
| `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` example  |  
```
// Set the EGL IMG context priority to high.
configuration.defaultSurfaceProperties.priority = EGLIMGContextPriority::High;

```
Copy to clipboard To let the platform choose the EGL IMG context priority:

## Application window position and size[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#application-window-position-and-size "Link to this heading")
You can set the position of your Kanzi application on the screen relative to the upper-left corner of the screen and the size of the application window in pixels. The default size of the window is 640x480 pixels and center of the device screen.
To make the application window fixed size, resizable, fullscreen, or without borders, see [WindowStyle](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#windowstyle).
To set the default display where the application window appears, see [DefaultDisplayIndex](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#defaultdisplayindex).  
| In `application.cfg`  |  `WindowX = positionX` `WindowY = positionY` `WindowWidth = width` `WindowHeight = height` `WindowOrder = order`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  |  `configuration.defaultWindowProperties.x = positionX;` `configuration.defaultWindowProperties.y = positionY;` `configuration.defaultWindowProperties.width = width;` `configuration.defaultWindowProperties.height = height;` `configuration.defaultWindowProperties.order = order;` `configuration.systemConfiguration[ConfigurationKeyDefaultWindowX] = "positionX";` `configuration.systemConfiguration[ConfigurationKeyDefaultWindowY] = "positionY";` `configuration.systemConfiguration[ConfigurationKeyDefaultWindowWidth] = "width";` `configuration.systemConfiguration[ConfigurationKeyDefaultWindowHeight] = "height";` `configuration.systemConfiguration[ConfigurationKeyDefaultWindowOrder] = "order";`  |  
| Value  |   
 | `positionX`  | Horizontal position of the top-left corner of the application window from the top-left corner of the screen in pixels. Use 0 to position the window to the left of the device screen.  |  
| --- | --- |  
| `positionY`  | Vertical position of the top-left corner of the application window from the top-left corner of the screen in pixels. Use 0 to position the window to the top of the device screen.  |  
| `width`  | Window width in pixels.  |  
| `height`  | Window height in pixels.  |

metadata.title: Application configuration reference (Part 51/88)
metadata.breadcrumb: Working with … > Application > Application configuration reference

content:
| `positionY`  | Vertical position of the top-left corner of the application window from the top-left corner of the screen in pixels. Use 0 to position the window to the top of the device screen.  |  
| `width`  | Window width in pixels.  |  
| `height`  | Window height in pixels.  |  
| `order`  | Z-order of the application window in decimal or hexadecimal format. You can use this parameter to arrange Kanzi applications when you run more than one application at the same time. The values for this parameter depend on your target platform. By default Kanzi sets the value to `NativeWindowProperties::WindowPositionSpecifiers::WindowPositionUnspecified[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a17702.html#a0e1f8acdb1bc88695ef8f9215df4712fa3c29aca834d1ca97b59ccafd4b11e855)`, which does not set order.  |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Sets the width to 1280 and height to 720 pixels and place it 100 pixels
# from the top and 1 pixel from the left side of the device screen.
WindowWidth = 1280
WindowHeight = 720
WindowX = 100
WindowY = 1

### Preferred Vulkan GPU[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#preferred-vulkan-gpu "Link to this heading")
You can set the GPU type to favor when the Kanzi Vulkan backend selects a device to use, where more than one GPU is available. By default Kanzi uses the first enumerated GPU.  
| In `application.cfg`  | `PreferredGPU = value`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.preferredGPU = gfx::GpuSelectionType::value`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `value`  |  Maps to the Vulkan backend GPU selection criteria:
  * To map to `First`, selecting the first enumerated GPU, often controlled by a control panel application. Default Value.
    * In `application.cfg`, use `first`.
    * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`, use `gfx::GpuSelectionType::First[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11052.html#gga373266e6248b16a1937a866589a43feda7fb55ed0b7a30342ba6da306428cae04)`.
  * To map to `LargestMemory`, favoring the GPU with the most memory available.
    * In `application.cfg`, use `largestmemory`.
    * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`, use `gfx::GpuSelectionType::LargestMemory[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11052.html#gga373266e6248b16a1937a866589a43feda7fcc6ae01473ff9641f68598a723fe1f)`.
  * To map to `Discrete`, favoring discrete GPU devices. The device is typically a separate processor connected to the host.
    * In `application.cfg`, use `discrete`.
    * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`, use `gfx::GpuSelectionType::Discrete[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11052.html#gga373266e6248b16a1937a866589a43feda4984667940802dedc139aa7a430a6553)`.
  * To map to `Integrated`, favoring integrated GPU devices. The device is typically one embedded in or tightly coupled with the host.
    * In `application.cfg`, use `integrated`.
    * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`, use `gfx::GpuSelectionType::Integrated[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11052.html#gga373266e6248b16a1937a866589a43feda92d909e2ae45ed6c55a55088f1d46394)`.
  * To map to `CPU`, favoring CPU-based graphics devices. The device is typically running on the same processor as the host.
    * In `application.cfg`, use `cpu`.

metadata.breadcrumb: Working with … > Application > Application configuration reference

## QNX context type selection[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#qnx-context-type-selection "Link to this heading")
On QNX, you can set the context type that you want your Kanzi application to use. In `application.cfg` and on the command line you can set only one context type. To set more than one context type, set it in the `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`.  
| In `application.cfg`  | `QnxContextType = contextType`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.defaultDesktopProperties.contextFlags = contextType | contextType | contextType...;`  |  
| On the command line  | `-qnx-context-type=contextType`  |  
| Value  |   
 | `contextType`  |  Type of the QNX context that you want your Kanzi application to use. Default value is `SCREEN_APPLICATION_CONTEXT`. You can set your application to use these contexts:
  * `SCREEN_APPLICATION_CONTEXT`
  * `SCREEN_WINDOW_MANAGER_CONTEXT`
  * `SCREEN_INPUT_PROVIDER_CONTEXT`
  * `SCREEN_POWER_MANAGER_CONTEXT`
  * `SCREEN_DISPLAY_MANAGER_CONTEXT`
  * `SCREEN_INPUT_MANAGER_CONTEXT`
  * `SCREEN_BUFFER_PROVIDER_CONTEXT`

 |  
| --- | --- |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Sets Kanzi to use the SCREEN_DISPLAY_MANAGER_CONTEXT context type.
QnxContextType = SCREEN_DISPLAY_MANAGER_CONTEXT

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
| `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` example  |  
```
// Sets Kanzi to use the SCREEN_WINDOW_MANAGER_CONTEXT and SCREEN_INPUT_PROVIDER_CONTEXT context types.
configuration.defaultDesktopProperties.contextFlags = SCREEN_WINDOW_MANAGER_CONTEXT | SCREEN_INPUT_PROVIDER_CONTEXT;

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
| Command line example  |  Sets Kanzi to use the SCREEN_DISPLAY_MANAGER_CONTEXT context type. 
```
-qnx-context-type=SCREEN_DISPLAY_MANAGER_CONTEXT

```
Copy to clipboard  |

### WindowStyle[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#windowstyle "Link to this heading")
You can set the style of your Kanzi application window. Besides the default window with a border that users can resize, you can set your Kanzi application to launch in a window without a border, in a window of fixed size, and in a window that occupies the entire device screen.
To set the position and size of the application window, see [Application window position and size](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#application-window-position-and-size).  
| In `application.cfg`  | `WindowStyle = "style"`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.defaultWindowProperties.style = style;`  |  
| Value  |   
 | `style`  |  To set a window without borders or any other decorations that users cannot resize:
  * In `application.cfg` use `borderless`.
  * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `window_properties.hpp::KzsWindowStyle::KZS_WINDOW_STYLE_BORDERLESS[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a09749.html#a77f290cf91d478624555ab40691bdd8ca67386a29891e44bc781180e164263f85)`.

To set a window that users cannot resize:
  * In `application.cfg` use `fixed`.
  * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `window_properties.hpp::KzsWindowStyle::KZS_WINDOW_STYLE_FIXED[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a09749.html#a77f290cf91d478624555ab40691bdd8ca723979abfe6fd4310c8ecace66b92869)`.

To set a window that occupies the whole device screen:
  * In `application.cfg` use `fullscreen`.
  * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `window_properties.hpp::KzsWindowStyle::KZS_WINDOW_STYLE_FULL_SCREEN[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a09749.html#a77f290cf91d478624555ab40691bdd8ca85e273d16ae845564920eae16c39b135)`.

To set a window that users can resize:
  * In `application.cfg` use `resizable`.
  * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `window_properties.hpp::KzsWindowStyle::KZS_WINDOW_STYLE_RESIZABLE[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a09749.html#a77f290cf91d478624555ab40691bdd8ca7a1b9137f58ee9f14bf59d7b36809190)`.

### DefaultDisplayIndex[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#defaultdisplayindex "Link to this heading")
When you run your Kanzi application in full-screen mode on a system with more than one display, you can set the default display where your Kanzi application window appears.
To make the application window fullscreen, see [WindowStyle](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#windowstyle).
You can use this configuration option only on platforms where Kanzi owns the output window. This is not the case on Android. On Android, to launch your Android Activity on a particular display set the intent option with `setLaunchDisplayId(id)` or use `adb` with the `--display` argument. See <https://source.android.com/docs/core/display/multi_display/activity-launch>.  
| In `application.cfg`  | `DefaultDisplayIndex = index`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.defaultWindowProperties.defaultDisplayIndex = index;`  |  
| Value  |   
 | `index`  | Index number of the display. Default value is 0.  |  
| --- | --- |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Sets the second display as the default display for the full-screen application window.
DefaultDisplayIndex = 1

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
| `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` example  |  
```
// Sets the second display as the default display for the full-screen application window.
configuration.defaultWindowProperties.defaultDisplayIndex = 1;

```
Copy to clipboard  |

content:
### WindowBufferCount[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#windowbuffercount "Link to this heading")
If the windowing system of your target device supports setting the number of window buffers, you can set the number of native window buffers that your Kanzi application window uses. For example, Renesas window manager and QNX Screen support the setting of the number of window buffers.  
| In `application.cfg`  | `WindowBufferCount = value`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.defaultWindowProperties.bufferCount = value;`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `value`  | The number of native window buffers used by the Kanzi application window. The default value is 0 and sets Kanzi to use the default value provided by the native windowing system of the target device.  |  
| --- | --- |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Set the number of native window buffers used by the Kanzi application window to 3.
WindowBufferCount = 3

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
| `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` example  |  
```
// Set the number of native window buffers used by the Kanzi application window to 3.
configuration.defaultWindowProperties.bufferCount = 3;

```
Copy to clipboard  |

metadata.title: Application configuration reference (Part 64/88)
metadata.breadcrumb: Working with … > Application > Application configuration reference

content:
### QnxWindowBufferCount[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#qnxwindowbuffercount "Link to this heading")
Sets the number of native window buffers that your Kanzi application window uses on QNX platform. To ensure compatibility, if you do not set this configuration option explicitly, Kanzi uses the value from the [WindowBufferCount](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#windowbuffercount) configuration option.  
| In `application.cfg`  | `QnxWindowBufferCount = value`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.systemConfiguration[ConfigurationKeyQnxWindowBufferCount] = value;`  |  
| Values  |

### GroupName[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#groupname "Link to this heading")
On platforms with windowing systems that use the window group name, such as QNX, you can set the group name for the application window group. When you run multiple Kanzi applications, in each Kanzi application set a unique name for the window group.  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.defaultWindowProperties.groupName = "value";`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Values  |   
 | `value`  | The name of the Kanzi application window group.  |  
| --- | --- |  
 |  
| `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` example  |  
```
// Set the Kanzi application window group name to Cluster.
configuration.defaultWindowProperties.groupName = "Cluster";

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
### QnxPipelineID[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#qnxpipelineid "Link to this heading")
You can set the QNX Screen pipeline ID for your Kanzi application window. A graphics pipeline ID is an identifier that refers to the hardware layering that is specific to your target device.
When you set the pipeline ID, your Kanzi application sets that ID using the underlying system functions. By default a Kanzi application does not set the pipeline ID.
If you set the pipeline ID, make sure that the pipeline order of your target device and the z-ordering of the application windows make sense together. You can set the z-order of a Kanzi application window using the `WindowOrder` setting. See [Application window position and size](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#application-window-position-and-size).  
| In `application.cfg`  | `QnxPipelineID = value`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| On the command line  | `-qnx-pipeline-id=value`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `value`  |  Integer value that contains the QNX Screen pipeline ID. By default a Kanzi application does not set the pipeline ID. The value that you set on the command line takes priority over the value that you set in `application.cfg`.  |  
| --- | --- |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Sets the QNX Screen pipeline ID to 1.
QnxPipelineID = 1

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
| Command line example  |  Sets the QNX Screen pipeline ID to 1. 
```
-qnx-pipeline-id=1

```
Copy to clipboard  |

### QnxWindowSelfLayout[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#qnxwindowselflayout "Link to this heading")
On QNX platforms, enables self layout mode of the QNX Screen property for the Kanzi application window. When enabled, in your application you can control window properties that are otherwise managed by the QNX window manager.  
| In `application.cfg`  | `QnxWindowSelfLayout = value`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.systemConfiguration[ConfigurationKeyDefaultQnxWindowSelfLayout] = value;`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `value`  | 
  * `1` - Enables self layout so that you can control layout properties. When enabled, you can set the window properties as listed under the `SCREEN_PROPERTY_SELF_LAYOUT` at [QNX Screen property types](https://www.qnx.com/developers/docs/7.1/index.html#com.qnx.doc.screen/topic/screen_8h_1Screen_Property_Types.html).
  * `0` - Disables self layout so that the window manager controls properties. Default value.

 |  
| --- | --- |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Enables self layout for this QNX window.
QnxWindowSelfLayout = 1

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
| `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` example  |  
```
// Enables self layout for this QNX window.
configuration.systemConfiguration[ConfigurationKeyDefaultQnxWindowSelfLayout] = "1";

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
| Command line example  |  Enables self layout for this QNX window. 
```
-qnx-window-self-layout=1

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
### QnxUsageFlags[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#qnxusageflags "Link to this heading")
For a Kanzi application window you can programmatically set the usage flags for the QNX Screen property. Screen usage flags enable you to constrain the allocated QNX window buffers.  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  |  
```
m_applicationProperties.defaultWindowProperties.usageFlags = usageFlags;

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Values  |   
 | `usageFlags`  | For available values, see [QNX Screen usage flags](https://www.qnx.com/developers/docs/7.0.0//////index.html#com.qnx.doc.screen/topic/screen_8h_1Screen_Usage_Flag_Types.html).  |  
| --- | --- |  
 |  
| `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` example  |  
```
// To use the OpenGL ES 3.X to render the QNX window buffer.
m_applicationProperties.defaultWindowProperties.usageFlags = SCREEN_USAGE_OPENGL_ES3;

```

### EGLGraphicsFormatID[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#eglgraphicsformatid "Link to this heading")
You can set the EGL graphics format ID for your Kanzi application. EGL graphics format ID is an identifier that refers to an EGL configuration for a Kanzi application that runs on EGL-supported platforms. Use the command line to list EGL configurations available for your Kanzi application.
Keep in mind that when you set the EGL graphics format ID, you override the EGL graphics format settings.
You can set the EGL format ID for these EGL graphics outputs:
  * Android WS
  * Emscripten
  * Wayland
  * X11

  
| In `application.cfg`  | `EGLGraphicsFormatID = value`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| On the command line  |  `-egl-graphics-format-id=value` `-enum-egl-configs`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `value`  |  Integer value that contains the EGL graphics format ID. By default, a Kanzi application does not set the EGL graphics format ID. The value that you set on the command line takes priority over the value that you set in `application.cfg`.  |  
| --- | --- |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Sets the EGL graphics format ID to 1.
EGLGraphicsFormatID = 1

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
| Command line example  |  Sets the EGL graphics format ID to 1. 
```
-egl-graphics-format-id=1

```
Copy to clipboard Lists EGL configurations available for the application. 
```
-enum-egl-configs

```

### EGLContextClientVersion[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#eglcontextclientversion "Link to this heading")
You can set the EGL context client version for these EGL graphics outputs:
  * Android WS
  * Emscripten
  * Wayland
  * QNX
  * X11

  
| In `application.cfg`  | `EGLContextClientVersion = value`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.systemConfiguration[ConfigurationKeyEGLContextClientVersion] = value;`  |  
| On the command line  | `-egl-context-client-version=value`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `value`  |  The EGL context client version that Kanzi tries to use:
  * To use the highest available ES version, use `automatic` (`EGLContextClientSelection::Automatic[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11119.html#a0d7efdfc2cd89a292b364dff3bef9f26a086247a9b57fde6eefee2a0c4752242d)`). Default value.
  * The use explicitly unspecified version, use `unspecified` (`EGLContextClientSelection::Unspecified[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11119.html#a0d7efdfc2cd89a292b364dff3bef9f26a6fcdc090caeade09d0efd6253932b6f5)`).
  * The use a specific ES version, use `es1`, `es2`, or `es3` (`EGLContextClientSelection[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11119.html#a0d7efdfc2cd89a292b364dff3bef9f26)`).

 |  
| --- | --- |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Sets Kanzi to use ES2 context client version.
EGLContextClientVersion = es2

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
| `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` example  |  
```

configuration.systemConfiguration[ConfigurationKeyEGLContextClientVersion] = "es2";

```

```

## Input handling[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#input-handling "Link to this heading")
You can define how your application handles touch and pointer input. When you run your application on a device, you can set whether the application reacts to the pointer of the device, uses a touch screen, or both. You can also set the transformation matrix of the input event coordinates.
A Kanzi application handles input by default. To disable input handling in your application, override the `Application::setScreenOverride()` function with an empty implementation. See [Disabling input handling](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/application-configuration.html#disabling-input-handling).
### InputTransform[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#inputtransform "Link to this heading")
You can set the transformation matrix of the input event coordinates. This transformation only affects input event coordinates, not the orientation of the Kanzi application screen. For example, use this to rotate the touch screen in relation to your application screen.  
| In `application.cfg`  | `InputTransform = transformation`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.defaultEventSourceProperties.transformation = transformation;`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `transformation`  | Transformation matrix of the touch screen.  |  
| --- | --- |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Rotate a touch screen sized 1280x720 pixels by 180 degrees.
InputTransform = -1, 0, 0, 0, -1, 0, 1280, 720, 1

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
| `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` example  |  
```
// Rotate a touch screen sized 1280x720 pixels by 180 degrees.
configuration.defaultEventSourceProperties.transformation = Matrix3x3::createTranslation(1280.0f, 720.0f) * Matrix3x3::createRotationInDegrees(180.0f);

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
The examples use this equation to calculate the transformation matrix:
[10128001720001]∗[cos(π)−sin(π)0sin(π)cos(π)0001]=[−1012800−1720001]

### InputTranslation[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#inputtranslation "Link to this heading")
You can set how Kanzi translates pointer and touch events.  
| In `application.cfg`  | `InputTranslation = translation`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.defaultEventSourceProperties.translation = translation;`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `translation`  |  Translation of pointer and touch events. To not apply any translation:
  * In `application.cfg` use `none`. Default value.
  * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `InputTranslation::TranslateNone[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11067.html#ggaa696abf3f6a77f6b8bfa4c97ce6a9feda79704c5c04bb9884eebe159708a90763)`. Default value.

To translate pointer events to touch events:
  * In `application.cfg` use `pointertotouch`.
  * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `InputTranslation::TranslatePointerToTouch[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11067.html#ggaa696abf3f6a77f6b8bfa4c97ce6a9fedaa1fa2b8c7230a7c3b8a6aaed1576ed67)`.

To translate pointer events to touch events, and preserve pointer events:
  * In `application.cfg` use `pointertotouchpreserve`.
  * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `InputTranslation::TranslatePointerToTouchPreserve[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11067.html#ggaa696abf3f6a77f6b8bfa4c97ce6a9feda9b37ba0ca2e3738505198ef30b3bdf4c)`.

To translate touch events to pointer events:
  * In `application.cfg` use `touchtopointer`.
  * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `InputTranslation::TranslateTouchToPointer[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11067.html#ggaa696abf3f6a77f6b8bfa4c97ce6a9feda29d4bbc9b85d3207de2b27968725002a)`.

To translate touch events to pointer events, and preserve touch events:
  * In `application.cfg` use `touchtopointerpreserve`.
  * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `InputTranslation::TranslateTouchToPointerPreserve[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11067.html#ggaa696abf3f6a77f6b8bfa4c97ce6a9feda2c6a93c6f1d214ffe010ed24df7cd71f)`.

 |  
| --- | --- |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Translate pointer events to touch events.
InputTranslation = pointertotouch

## Input event devices on Linux[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#input-event-devices-on-linux "Link to this heading")
You can configure the input event devices that Kanzi listens to on Linux ports where the native windowing system does not provide input device handling.
This way Kanzi can listen to events directly from the input event devices provided by the operating system.
For example, in Vivante fbdev and WSEGL ports you can configure the input event devices that Kanzi listens to. In X11 and Wayland ports the native windowing system handles input devices.
Kanzi by default listens to all input event devices named eventN, where N is an integer, in the `/dev/input` directory.  
| In `application.cfg`  | `InputEventDevice = path`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.defaultEventSourceProperties.inputEventDevice = path;`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `path`  | Full path to one or more input event devices. Separate a list of several paths with a semicolon.  |  
| --- | --- |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Listens to events from one input event device.
InputEventDevice = "/dev/input/event1"

```
Copy to clipboard 
```
# Listens to events from two input event devices.
InputEventDevice = "/dev/input/event0;/dev/input/event1"

```
Copy to clipboard 
```
# Disables listening to events from input event devices.
InputEventDevice = "none"

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
| `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` example  |  
```
// Listens to events from one input event device.
configuration.defaultEventSourceProperties.inputEventDevice = "/dev/input/event1";

```

content:
## Image loading[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#image-loading "Link to this heading")
Kanzi uses third-party image libraries, such as [libpng](http://www.libpng.org/pub/png/libpng.html) and [libjpeg](https://jpegclub.org/reference/), to support different image formats. To make your Kanzi application more secure, you can set limits for Kanzi to use when loading images using these libraries. For example, to prevent the loading of malicious files, you can limit the amount of memory to allocate for each object that Kanzi loads.
### libjpeg[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#libjpeg "Link to this heading")
You can set the maximum amount of memory in bytes to allocate for each JPEG object that Kanzi loads using the [libjpeg](https://jpegclub.org/reference/) image library.  
| In `application.cfg`  | `LibJPEGMaxMemory = bytes`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.imageLoad.libJPEGMaxMemory = bytes;`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `bytes`  |  The maximum number of bytes to allocate for a JPEG object in libjpeg. Kanzi passes this value to the libjpeg `jpeg_memory_mgr::max_memory_to_use` parameter. This value affects only the space used for virtual-array buffers and is not a guaranteed maximum but merely advisory. The default value 0 sets no limit on the amount of memory to allocate.  |  
| --- | --- |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Sets the libjpeg memory allocation limit to 2 MB (2,000,000 bytes).
LibJPEGMaxMemory = 2000000

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
| `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` example  |  
```
// Sets the libjpeg memory allocation limit to 2 MB (2,000,000 bytes).
configuration.imageLoad.libJPEGMaxMemory = 2000000;

```
Copy to clipboard  |

content:
### libpng[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#libpng "Link to this heading")
You can set the maximum number of ancillary chunks in a PNG datastream and the maximum amount of memory in bytes to allocate for a chunk that Kanzi loads using the [libpng](http://www.libpng.org/pub/png/libpng.html) image library.
By default Kanzi uses these limits imposed by libpng:
  * Maximum total of 1000 sPLT, tEXt, iTXt, zTXt, and unknown ancillary chunks.
  * Maximum of 8 megabytes of memory to allocate for a chunk other than IDAT.

  
| In `application.cfg`  |  `LibPNGChunkCacheMax = chunks` `LibPNGChunkMallocMax = bytes`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  |  `configuration.imageLoad.libPNGChunkCacheMax = chunks;` `configuration.imageLoad.libPNGChunkMallocMax = bytes;`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `chunks`  |  The maximum number of ancillary chunks stored by libpng. Kanzi passes this value to the libpng `png_set_chunk_cache_max()` function.  |  
| --- | --- |  
| `bytes`  |  The maximum amount of memory in bytes that a chunk other than IDAT can occupy. Kanzi passes this value to the libpng `png_set_chunk_malloc_max()` function.  |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Sets the libpng limit for the number of ancillary chunks to 500.
LibPNGChunkCacheMax = 500
# Sets the libpng limit for the amount of memory that a chunk
# other than IDAT can occupy to 2 MB (2,000,000 bytes).
LibPNGChunkMallocMax = 2000000

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
| `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` example  |  
```
// Sets the libpng limit for the number of ancillary chunks to 500.
configuration.imageLoad.libPNGChunkCacheMax = 500;
// Sets the libpng limit for the amount of memory that a chunk
// other than IDAT can occupy to 2 MB (2,000,000 bytes).
configuration.imageLoad.libPNGChunkMallocMax = 2000000;

```
Copy to clipboard  |

content:
## Shader binary cache[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#shader-binary-cache "Link to this heading")
On performance-constrained platforms, shader compilations can considerably slow down the application startup and decrease runtime performance. You can use a shader binary cache primed with the set of shaders that your application requires. This way, your application does not have to compile shaders from source at runtime.
See [Using binary shaders](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/shaders/using-binary-shaders.html).
### ShaderBinaryCacheDirectory[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#shaderbinarycachedirectory "Link to this heading")
You can set the directory where you want your Kanzi application to cache shader binaries. At the time of caching, this directory must be writable. For production purposes, you can make the directory read-only. See [ShaderBinaryCacheReadOnly](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#shaderbinarycachereadonly).
To enable the caching of shader binaries, use the [ShaderBinaryCacheEnabled](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#shaderbinarycacheenabled) setting.  
| In `application.cfg`  | `ShaderBinaryCacheDirectory = path`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.shaderBinaryCacheDirectory = path;`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `path`  | The path to the cache directory for shader binaries. You can use an absolute path or a relative path from the working directory of your application.  |  
| --- | --- |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Sets the shader binary cache directory to /tmp/shader-cache/.
ShaderBinaryCacheDirectory = "/tmp/shader-cache/"

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
| `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` example  |  
```
// Sets the shader binary cache directory to /tmp/shader-cache/.
configuration.shaderBinaryCacheDirectory = "/tmp/shader-cache/";

```
Copy to clipboard  |

content:
### ShaderBinaryCacheEnabled[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#shaderbinarycacheenabled "Link to this heading")
You can set your application to cache shader binaries. Use this to optimize Kanzi application performance on platforms where offline shader compilation tools are not available.
The caching of shader binaries requires that Kanzi Studio exports the source code of the shaders to the kzb file. In Kanzi Studio, in the Project > Properties, make sure that the Export Shader Source Code property is enabled. This is the default value.  
| In `application.cfg`  | `ShaderBinaryCacheEnabled = value`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.shaderBinaryCacheEnabled = value;`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `true`  | Cache shader binaries.  |  
| --- | --- |  
| `false`  | Do not cache shader binaries. Default value.  |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Enables the caching of shader binaries.
ShaderBinaryCacheEnabled = true

```

### ShaderBinaryCacheCollisionCheck[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#shaderbinarycachecollisioncheck "Link to this heading")
By default, Kanzi stores in the filename of a cached shader binary only a hash of the shader source code. Kanzi then compares that hash to a hash value derived from the requested shader source. Hash collisions, which are rare but possible, result in the use of the wrong shader.
To guard against hash collisions, you can set your application to store the shader source code and perform a full string comparison to make sure that the shaders are identical. If two shaders produce the same hash value, the application logs a warning.
To save disk space and optimize performance, enable the hash collision checks only during development.  
| In `application.cfg`  | `ShaderBinaryCacheCollisionCheck = value`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.shaderBinaryCacheCollisionCheck = value;`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `true`  |  Check for hash collisions in cached shaders. Use this only during development.  |  
| --- | --- |  
| `false`  | Do not check for hash collisions in cached shaders. Default value.  |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Enables checking for hash collisions in cached shaders.
ShaderBinaryCacheCollisionCheck = true

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
| `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` example  |  
```
// Enables checking for hash collisions in cached shaders.
configuration.shaderBinaryCacheCollisionCheck = true;

```
Copy to clipboard  |

content:
### ShaderBinaryCacheReadOnly[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#shaderbinarycachereadonly "Link to this heading")
By default, Kanzi can write to the shader binary cache. When your application is ready for production, you can make the shader binary cache read-only.  
| In `application.cfg`  | `ShaderBinaryCacheReadOnly = value`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.ShaderBinaryCacheReadOnly = value;`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `true`  |  Make the shader binary cache directory read-only. You can use this when your application is ready for production.  |  
| --- | --- |  
| `false`  | Make the shader binary cache directory writable. Default value.  |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Makes the shader binary cache read-only.
ShaderBinaryCacheReadOnly = true

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
| `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` example  |  
```
// Makes the shader binary cache read-only.
configuration.ShaderBinaryCacheReadOnly = true;

```
Copy to clipboard  |

Kanzi Studio asset packages are collections of ready-made content that you can import to your Kanzi Studio projects. With asset packages, you can create an asset library with content, such as UI components, materials, brushes, styles, and textures.
Use asset packages to make this content available for use in different Kanzi Studio projects or to share the content within your company for all your Kanzi applications. For example, the Factory Content asset packages that come with Kanzi Studio contain such content. See [Factory Content assets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/factory-content.html).
## Adding asset sources[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-packages/asset-packages.html#adding-asset-sources "Link to this heading")
Any directory that contains Kanzi Studio asset packages is an asset source. See [Creating an asset package](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-packages/asset-packages.html#creating-an-asset-package).
To add an asset source to Kanzi Studio:
  1. In the Asset Packages window, click + Add Asset Source.
  2. In the Select Asset Directory dialog, select the directory that you want to add.


After you add an asset source, you see in the Asset Packages window all the items included in the asset packages that are stored in the directory that you added as an asset source.
When you add an asset source to Kanzi Studio, you make that asset source available to all your Kanzi Studio projects.
![../../_images/add-asset-source.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-asset-source.png)

## Using asset packages[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-packages/asset-packages.html#using-asset-packages "Link to this heading")
To use asset packages:
  1. In the Asset Packages window, select an asset source.
![../../_images/myassetsource.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/myassetsource.png)
  2. To import an item from the Asset Packages to your Kanzi Studio project, either:
     * From the Asset Packages window, drag an item to a node in the Node Tree, to the Prefabs, or to the Preview.
     * In the Asset Packages, right-click the item and select Import Asset Package.
For example, drag an item to the Node Tree and drop it on a node. Kanzi Studio adds that item to the Prefabs, and instantiates it as a prefab in the node where you dropped that item.
![../../_images/drag-night-vision-to-node-tree.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/drag-night-vision-to-node-tree.png) ![../../_images/night-vision-in-node-tree-and-prefabs.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/night-vision-in-node-tree-and-prefabs.png)

## Creating an asset package[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-packages/asset-packages.html#creating-an-asset-package "Link to this heading")
To share content with other Kanzi Studio users, you can create your own asset packages. You create an asset package by marking a Kanzi Studio project as an asset package, and by marking in that project all the items that you want to include in that asset package. When a Kanzi Studio user adds as an asset source a directory, which contains an asset package project, they see in the Asset Packages window all the items in that asset package.
To create an asset package:
  1. In Kanzi Studio, in the project from which you want to create an asset package, in the Prefabs and Library, select each item that you want to include in that asset package. In the Properties, add and set:
     * Resources > Export in Asset Package to enabled
     * (Optional) Resources > Custom Asset Thumbnail to the bitmap image that you want to use as a thumbnail for your asset in the Asset Packages window
If you do not set a custom thumbnail, Kanzi Studio generates the thumbnail automatically.
To enable Kanzi Studio to generate thumbnails, make sure that the Preview is running and that Kanzi Studio renders thumbnails. To enable thumbnail rendering, select Edit > User Preferences. In the Advanced tab, enable Render thumbnails.
For example, create from a Viewport 2D node a prefab and mark that prefab to be exported in the asset package.
![../../_images/night-vision-prefab.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/night-vision-prefab.png) ![../../_images/export-in-asset-package.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/export-in-asset-package.png)
  2. In the Kanzi Studio main menu, select Project > Properties. In the Properties, in the Profile category, enable the Is Asset Package property.
![../../_images/is-asset-package.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/is-asset-package.png)
  3. Save the Kanzi Studio project. The project is now a Kanzi Studio asset package.
When a Kanzi Studio user adds as an asset source a directory that contains an asset package project, they see in the Asset Packages window all the items in that asset package. See [Adding asset sources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-packages/asset-packages.html#adding-asset-sources).

The Asset Toolkit contains easy, ready-made components and materials with a similar structure and set of properties, that you can use to create Kanzi applications faster.
Here you can find all the Asset Toolkit content:
  * A high quality placeholder car model that you can use in your prototype application. See [Car](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#car).
  * Materials that you can apply to 3D content in your project. See [Materials](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#materials).
  * Environment Textures that you can use to give perspective to your scene. See [Environments](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#environments).
  * Flipbook and Transition Material types that you can use to present content in your application. See [Material types](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#material-types).
  * Interactive User Interface Components that you can use to receive user input. See [Interactivity Control components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#interactivity-control-components).
  * Radial UI Components that you can show progress in a circular arc. See [Radial UI Components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#radial-ui-components).
  * Simple shapes to use in your application. See [Simple Shape UI Components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#simple-shape-ui-components).
  * Scrollable lists that can present collections of items. See [Scroll list UI Components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#scroll-list-ui-components).
  * Example components that shows ways to combine these assets into more complex, reusable components. See [Examples](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#examples).

## Car[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#car "Link to this heading")
Use the Car to add a car model into your scene.
![../../_images/car-asset1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/car-asset1.png)
To position the car, in the Preview use either the Node tool or the Camera tool. See [Editing your application in the Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/editing-in-the-preview.html) and [Using the Camera node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/cameras/creating-and-using-cameras-for-previews.html).
To set the material for the different parts of the car, you can drag materials from the Assets window to the Car in the Preview window, or on the part of the car in the Node Tree. See [Using the Asset Toolkit assets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/using-the-asset-toolkit-assets.html).
## Materials[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/asset-toolkit.html#materials "Link to this heading")
The Asset Toolkit includes Physically Based Rendering (PBR) materials that you can apply to 3D content in your project.
![../../_images/carpaint-blue.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/carpaint-blue.png)
PBR Carpaint-blue
![../../_images/carpaint-orange.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/carpaint-orange.png)
PBR Carpaint-orange
![../../_images/chrome.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/chrome.png)
PBR Chrome
![../../_images/glass.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/glass.png)
PBR Glass
![../../_images/plastic.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/plastic.png)
PBR Plastic
To learn about using materials from the Asset Toolkit in your Kanzi application, see [Using Asset Toolkit materials in your project](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-toolkit/using-the-asset-toolkit-assets.html#using-at-materials).
