Kanzi Java API implements platform-independent Java proxies for Kanzi classes, providing rich access to the Kanzi functionality in Java and Kotlin. This enables you to create applications that are tightly integrated with the Android APIs.
On Android, you can use the Kanzi Java API directly from the Android UI thread without the need for dispatcher mechanisms. See [Developing with the Kanzi Android framework (droidfw)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/android/droidfw/android-droidfw.html).
This topic provides an overview of the fundamentals of Kanzi Java API. For complete API reference, see [Kanzi Engine Java API reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-java-api/index.html).
## Requirements[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/java/using-java.html#requirements "Link to this heading")
Kanzi Java API requires Java 8 (1.8) or higher.

When you run the Kanzi Command Prompt, it sets these environment variables:  
| Environment variable  | Definition  |  
| --- | --- |  
| `KANZI_HOME`  | Sets the path to the Kanzi workspace.  |  
| `ANDROID_HOME`  | Sets the path to the Android SDK.  |  
| `JAVA_HOME`  | Sets the path to the 64-bit JDK.  |

## Contents of a kzb file[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/kzb-binaries/kzb-files.html#contents-of-a-kzb-file "Link to this heading")
The contents and size of a kzb file depend on your Kanzi Studio project and how you configure the kzb export in Kanzi Studio. The size of the kzb file impacts the time it takes to load your application and the amount of resources that the application uses.
You can reduce the size of a kzb file by excluding unused project items from the kzb export. For example, this way you can keep in a project items that you do not use in your Kanzi application. See [Excluding items from an application](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/cleaning-up-a-project.html#excluding-items-from-an-application).
Kanzi Studio does not export to a kzb file the content of the Description property. The purpose of the property is to store the documentation of project items, which a Kanzi application does not use. See [Documenting a project](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/documenting-a-project.html).
By default, the main kzb file that Kanzi Studio creates from your project contains:  
| Content  | Documentation  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Animations Use animation resources to create keyframe animations.  | [Animations](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/animations/animations.html)  |  
|  Brushes Use Brushes to set the appearance of the foreground and background of 2D nodes. For example, with brushes you can define the color of text in a Text Block 2D node, fill a background of a 2D node with an image pattern, or apply a material effect on 2D content.  | [Using brushes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html)  |  
|  Effects Use effects to apply post-processing effects to 2D nodes.  | [Effects for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/2d-effects.html)  |  
|  Font families Use font families to group fonts in your project.  | [Importing fonts](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing-fonts.html)  |  
|  Localization resources Localization involves creation and use of different resources, such as text, textures, and styles, for locales that you want to support in your application. When you mark localization resources as a locale pack, Kanzi Studio exports the marked resources to a separate kzb file. This way you can reduce the size of the main kzb file and load resources for a locale only when the user uses that locale.  |  [Localization](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/localization/localization.html) [Using locales](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/localization/using-locales.html)  |  
|  Materials Use materials to set the appearance of nodes.  | [Using materials](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/using-materials.html)  |

## Creating a kzb file from a Kanzi Studio project[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/kzb-binaries/using-kzb-binaries.html#creating-a-kzb-file-from-a-ks-project "Link to this heading")
To create a kzb file from a Kanzi Studio project, open your Kanzi Studio project and select File > Export > Export KZB.
![../../_images/export-kzb-binary.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/export-kzb-binary.png)
Kanzi Studio creates in the `<ProjectName>/Application/bin` directory these files:
  * `<project_name>.kzb` contains the content of your project in binary format.
  * `<project_name>.kzb.cfg` contains a list of kzb files. If your Kanzi application includes application code, Kanzi by default configures the C++ application to load the kzb files listed in this file

```
configuration.binaryName = "<project_name>.kzb.cfg"

```
Copy to clipboard
  * (Optional) `<project_name>.kzb.txt` contains a list of paths to project items in the exported kzb file. You can use these paths to access the content of your Kanzi application in the application code.
To set whether you want to export this file, select Edit > User Preferences and in the Advanced tab enable the Create table of contents of kzb file setting.
  * (Optional) `<project_name>.kza` contains your project in XML format.
To create this file, before you export the kzb file select Edit > User Preferences and in the Advanced tab enable the Create XML version (kza) of kzb file setting.


Tip
Kanzi Studio by default names the kzb file `<project_name>.kzb`. You can set the name of the kzb file in the Project > Properties using the Binary File Name property.
![../../_images/project-properties-myproject.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties-myproject.png) ![../../_images/project-binary-file-name-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-binary-file-name-property.png)
Tip
When you want to permanently remove all kzb files exported from a project, select File > Export > Delete Exported Binaries.
Kanzi Studio deletes all exported files from the directory set in the Node Tree > Properties in the Binary Export Directory property. This command deletes all exported files, including those from other projects.
![../../_images/delete-exported-binaries.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/delete-exported-binaries.png)

## Opening a kzb file[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/kzb-binaries/using-kzb-binaries.html#opening-a-kzb-file "Link to this heading")
Kanzi comes with the kzb Player you can use to open kzb files on Windows. For example, open kzb files with the kzb Player to visually inspect the content in kzb files. You can find the kzb Player in the `<KanziInstallation>/Studio/Bin` directory.
To run a Kanzi application on Windows, you need to have Microsoft Visual C++ 2015-2019 Redistributable (x86) installed.
See [Deploying Kanzi applications to Windows](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/deploying-applications/deploying-kanzi-applications-for-windows.html).
To open a kzb file:
  1. In Kanzi Studio main menu, select File > Export > Export KZB.
Kanzi Studio exports the kzb file from your project.
  2. Open the command line in the `<KanziInstallation>/Studio/Bin` directory and run

```
kzb_player_GL_vs2022_Release_DLL.exe "C:\<KanziWorkspace>\Projects\MyProject\Binary\myproject.kzb"

```
Copy to clipboard


## Setting how Kanzi loads a kzb file[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/kzb-binaries/using-kzb-binaries.html#setting-how-k-loads-a-kzb-file "Link to this heading")
The presence of the Screen node in a kzb file determines how Kanzi loads a kzb file.
To set whether Kanzi Studio exports the Screen node to the kzb file of that project, in the Node Tree select the Screen node and in the Properties set the Disable KZB Export property to:
  * Disabled to export the kzb file with the Screen node. This is the default setting. You can start your Kanzi application with a kzb file that has a Screen node. If you load during application runtime a kzb file that contains a Screen node, you replace the Screen node that the application uses.
  * Enabled to export the kzb file without the Screen node. You can load a kzb file without a Screen node only during application runtime, when your Kanzi application already has a Screen node.

![../../_images/export-project-settings-to-kzb.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/export-project-settings-to-kzb.png)

## Universal layout properties[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/layouts.html#universal-layout-properties "Link to this heading")
To position items in your Kanzi applications you can use these transformation types:
  * Layout transformation transforms the item before it applies the layout pass.
  * Render transformation transforms the item after it applies the layout pass, but before it renders the item.


Kanzi applies the render transformation after applying the layout transformation, and does not affect the layout calculations. For example, this allows you to animate nodes within a layout without causing the layout recalculation.
Layout control nodes, such as Stack Layout and Grid Layout nodes, apply their own transformations on all immediate child nodes who in their part define their own layout considering their own child nodes, layout transformations, margins and alignments.
  * Alignment defines the gravity of the layout. For example, set the Horizontal Alignment property to Right to align the node to the right side of its parent layout. By setting alignment properties to Stretch, the node stretches to the dimensions of its parent layout. Use the Content Stretch property to specify how a layout handles its content.
![../../_images/layout-horizontal-alignment.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/layout-horizontal-alignment.gif)
  * Margin enforces the object spacing relative to the border of its parent layout. For example, set the Horizontal Margin property to set the spacing on the left and right sides of the node in relation to its parent layout.
![../../_images/layout-margin.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/layout-margin.gif)
  * Layout properties override the bounding box size of a node. The default layout size is defined by the size of the node based on its bounding box and margins.
![../../_images/layout-override.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/layout-override.gif)


For example, a Stack Layout node set in direction on the x axis places its two child nodes next to each other based on their dimensions (bounding boxes). By using the Layout Width property you can override the width of the bounding box: a value smaller than the size of the node makes the node overlap, and a value larger than the size of the node extends the space between the two nodes.
![../../_images/stack-layout-overlap.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/stack-layout-overlap.gif)
After all the layout tasks are done, Kanzi applies the final transformations from the parent nodes. The RootNode under the Screen node has special rules for its layout if it is a Viewport 2D or an Empty Node 2D. It inherits the defined screen size, unless defined by the layout properties.

In Kanzi there are three types of layouts:  
|  ![../_images/layout-types-content.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/layout-types-content.png)  | Layouts that base the position and size of their child nodes, such as the Flow Layout, Grid Layout, Stack Layout, and Trajectory Layout nodes. For example, these layouts are useful when the amount of content changes dynamically.  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  ![../_images/layout-types-control.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/layout-types-control.png)  | Content controls that show specific content and usually center the content, such as the Image node and Button nodes.  |  
|  ![../_images/layout-types-positioning.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/layout-types-positioning.png)  | Absolute positioning controls that act as containers that group their child nodes, such as the Viewport 2D and Empty Node 2D nodes.  |  
You can use layout nodes to position nodes in relation to the application screen and other nodes. Layout consists of properties alignment, margins and layout size and that you can define either specific to a node or as a general rule imposed on child nodes by specific layout containers.
See [Layout control nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/layouts.html).

## Universal layout properties[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/kanzi-fundamentals/layouts.html#universal-layout-properties "Link to this heading")
To position items in your Kanzi applications you can use these transformation types:
  * Layout transformation transforms the item before it applies the layout pass.
  * Render transformation transforms the item after it applies the layout pass, but before it renders the item.


Kanzi applies the render transformation after applying the layout transformation, and does not affect the layout calculations. For example, this allows you to animate nodes within a layout without causing the layout recalculation.
Layout control nodes, such as Stack Layout and Grid Layout nodes, apply their own transformations on all immediate child nodes who in their part define their own layout considering their own child nodes, layout transformations, margins and alignments.
  * Alignment defines the gravity of the layout. For example, set the Horizontal Alignment property to Right to align the node to the right side of its parent layout. By setting alignment properties to Stretch, the node stretches to the dimensions of its parent layout. Use the Content Stretch property to specify how a layout handles its content.
![../_images/layout-horizontal-alignment.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/layout-horizontal-alignment.gif)
  * Margin enforces the object spacing relative to the border of its parent layout. For example, set the Horizontal Margin property to set the spacing on the left and right sides of the node in relation to its parent layout.
![../_images/layout-margin.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/layout-margin.gif)
  * Layout properties override the bounding box size of a node. The default layout size is defined by the size of the node based on its bounding box and margins.
![../_images/layout-override.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/layout-override.gif)


For example, a Stack Layout node set in direction on the x axis places its two child nodes next to each other based on their dimensions (bounding boxes). By using the Layout Width property you can override the width of the bounding box: a value smaller than the size of the node makes the node overlap, and a value larger than the size of the node extends the space between the two nodes.
![../_images/stack-layout-overlap.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/stack-layout-overlap.gif)
After all the layout tasks are done, Kanzi applies the final transformations from the parent nodes. The RootNode under the Screen node has special rules for its layout if it is a Viewport 2D or an Empty Node 2D. It inherits the defined screen size, unless defined by the layout properties.

Use the Content Layout nodes to present content in a UI control as a single item.
For example, use a Content Layout node to create the layout for a list item or a button with a border, a background, an icon, and a label.
![../../_images/content-layout.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/content-layout.gif)
By default the size of a Content Layout node is determined by the size of its child nodes. A Content Layout node that does not have child nodes by default stretches to take all the available space.
A Content Layout node does not arrange its child nodes. To arrange nodes in a Content Layout node, use another layout control node. See [Layout control nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/layouts.html).
Content Layout allows you to create layouts where:
  * Content of a Content Layout node determines the size of the Content Layout node. See [Creating a Content Layout node that adapts to the size of its content](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-content-layouts.html#creating-content-layout-adapts-to-size).
  * Content of a Content Layout node adapts to the size that you set. See [Creating a Content Layout where content adapts to a fixed size](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-content-layouts.html#creating-content-layout-fixed-size).

## Creating a Content Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-content-layouts.html#creating-a-content-layout-node "Link to this heading")
To create a Content Layout node:
  1. In the Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click the node where you want to create a Content Layout node and select either Content Layout 3D, or Content Layout 2D.
You can create a 3D node only in a 3D node, such as the Scene node, and a 2D node only in a 2D node.
![../../_images/create-content-layout-2d-in-root-page.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-content-layout-2d-in-root-page.png)
  2. In the Node Tree add content to the Content Layout node.
For example, if you created a Content Layout 2D node, create a Text Block 2D node.
Content Layout node does not arrange its child nodes. To arrange nodes in a Content Layout node, use another layout control node. See [Layout control nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/layouts.html).
  3. To add space around the content of the Content Layout node, in the Node Tree select the Content Layout node, and in the Properties add and set the padding properties:
     * Depth Padding to add space in the back and front of the content in a Content Layout 3D node
     * Horizontal Padding to add space on the left and the right sides of the content
     * Vertical Padding to add space on the bottom and the top of the content
![../../_images/content-layout-2d-padding.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/content-layout-2d-padding.png)

## Creating a Content Layout node that adapts to the size of its content[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-content-layouts.html#creating-a-content-layout-node-that-adapts-to-the-size-of-its-content "Link to this heading")
You can use a Content Layout node to create a layout that adapts to the size of its content. In this example, you create the layout of a 2D button with a border, a background, an icon, and a label.
To create a Content Layout node that adapts to the size of its content:
  1. In the Node Tree create a Button 2D node, in the Properties add the Background Brush property, and set it to a brush that you want to use to fill the Button 2D node. See [Adjusting the appearance of 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html).
You fill the Button 2D node with a brush to show the border of the button.
For example, select + Color Brush, name the brush, click ![quick-edit-property](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/quick-edit-properties.png) next to the Background Brush property, and set the color of the color brush.
![../../_images/button-2d-in-root-page.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-2d-in-root-page.png) ![../../_images/button-2d-background-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-2d-background-brush.png)
  2. In the Button 2D node create a Content Layout 2D node, in the Properties add the Background Brush property, and set it to a brush that you want to use to fill the Content Layout 2D node.
The Content Layout 2D node stretches the button to take all the available space.
![../../_images/create-content-layout-2d-in-button-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-content-layout-2d-in-button-2d.png) ![../../_images/content-layout-2d-background-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/content-layout-2d-background-brush.png)
  3. Add content to the Content Layout node.
For example, create a Stack Layout 2D node, and in the Stack Layout 2D node create:
     * Image node and in the Properties add and set:
       * Image to a texture that shows the button icon
       * Vertical Alignment to Center
       * Horizontal Margin property Right property field to add space on the right side of the Image node
     * Text Block 2D node and in the Properties add and set:
       * Text to set the button label
       * Vertical Alignment to Center
The Content Layout 2D node takes the space needed by the content that you add to it.
![../../_images/stack-layout-in-content-layout.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/stack-layout-in-content-layout.png) ![../../_images/image-properties1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/image-properties1.png) ![../../_images/text-block-2d-properties1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-block-2d-properties1.png) ![../../_images/navigation-button-in-preview-initial.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/navigation-button-in-preview-initial.png)

4. In the Node Tree select the Content Layout 2D node and in the Properties add and set:
     * Horizontal Padding and Vertical Padding to set the amount of space between the Content Layout 2D node and its parent node.
This way you set the amount of space between the button borders and content.
     * Horizontal Margin and Vertical Margin to set the thickness of the button border.
![../../_images/content-layout-2d-in-button-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/content-layout-2d-in-button-2d.png) ![../../_images/content-layout-padding-and-margin.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/content-layout-padding-and-margin.png) ![../../_images/navigation-button-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/navigation-button-in-preview.png)

## Creating a Content Layout where content adapts to a fixed size[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-content-layouts.html#creating-a-content-layout-where-content-adapts-to-a-fixed-size "Link to this heading")
You can use a Content Layout node to create a layout where the content adapts to the size that you set. In this example, you create the layout of a fixed-sized 2D button with a border, a background, an icon, and a label.
To create a Content Layout where content adapts to a fixed size:
  1. Create a 2D layout that adapts to the size of its content. See [Creating a Content Layout node that adapts to the size of its content](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-content-layouts.html#creating-content-layout-adapts-to-size).
  2. Set the size of the node that contains a Content Layout 2D node.
For example, in the Node Tree select the Button 2D node, and in the Properties add and set the Layout Width and Layout Height properties.
![../../_images/button-2d-with-content-in-root-page.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-2d-with-content-in-root-page.png) ![../../_images/button-2d-size-set.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-2d-size-set.png) ![../../_images/navigation-button-in-preview-3.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/navigation-button-in-preview-3.png)
  3. In the Node Tree select the Content Layout 2D node and in the Properties add and set:
     * Horizontal Alignment and Vertical Alignment to Stretch
This way you set the Content Layout 2D node to take as much space on the x and y axis as it can.
     * Clip Children to enabled
This way you clip the content of the child nodes of the Content Layout 2D node to fit into the size of the Content Layout 2D node.
![../../_images/content-layout-2d-in-button-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/content-layout-2d-in-button-2d.png) ![../../_images/content-layout-2d-alignment-stretch.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/content-layout-2d-alignment-stretch.png) ![../../_images/navigation-button-in-preview-4.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/navigation-button-in-preview-4.png)
  4. Align the content of the Content Layout node.
For example, in the Node Tree select the Stack Layout 2D node, in the Properties add the Vertical Alignment property, and set it to Center.
![../../_images/stack-layout-in-content-layout.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/stack-layout-in-content-layout.png) ![../../_images/stack-layout-alignment-center.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/stack-layout-alignment-center.png) ![../../_images/navigation-button-in-preview-5.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/navigation-button-in-preview-5.png)

  * You can apply a post-processing effect to a 2D node. See [Effects for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/2d-effects.html).
![../../_images/blur-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blur-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/mask-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/outline-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/outline-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/shadow-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/shadow-effect-2d.png)
  * You can rotate a 2D node around all three axes to create a 3D perspective effect. See [Creating a 3D perspective effect for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/setting-the-perspective.html).
![../../_images/perspective-transformation-visualization.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/perspective-transformation-visualization.png)

Use the Dock Layout nodes to place nodes relative to each other along the sides of a Dock Layout node.
A Dock Layout node arranges its items in a subtractive way: after positioning the first node, the Dock Layout node uses the remaining space to position the next node, and so on. When arranging its child nodes, a Dock Layout node uses its entire size.
You set the side along which you want to place a node in a Dock Layout node with the Side property.
![../../_images/dock-layout.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/dock-layout.gif)
A Dock Layout node arranges its items in a subtractive way: after positioning the first node, the Dock Layout node uses the remaining space to position the next node, and so on. When arranging its child nodes, a Dock Layout node uses its entire size.
Dock Layout nodes determine the position of their child nodes by:
  * The order in which the child nodes appear in the node tree.
  * The value of the Side property in each child node of a Dock Layout node. The Dock Layout node sets each child node to occupy that entire side.
  * The number of the child nodes in a Dock Layout node.

![../../_images/dock-layout-how-it-works.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/dock-layout-how-it-works.gif)

## Creating a Dock Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-dock-layouts.html#creating-a-dock-layout-node "Link to this heading")
To create a Dock Layout node:
  1. In the Node Tree, press `Alt` and right-click the node where you want to create a Dock Layout node and select either Dock Layout 3D, or Dock Layout 2D.
You can create a 3D node only in a 3D node, such as the Scene node, and a 2D node only in a 2D node.
![../../_images/node-tree-create-dock-layout-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-create-dock-layout-2d.png)
  2. In the Node Tree, add child nodes to the layout that you created in the previous step.
For example, if you created a Dock Layout 3D, add several Plane nodes, if you created a Dock Layout 2D, add several Image nodes.
As you add child nodes, the Dock Layout node automatically positions them.
![../../_images/node-tree-dock-layout-images.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-dock-layout-images.png) ![../../_images/preview-dock-layout-images.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-dock-layout-images.png)
  3. In the Node Tree, select all child nodes of the Dock Layout node. In the Properties, add the Dock Layout > Side property and set it to:
     * Left to set the child node to occupy the left part of the Dock Layout node.
     * Right to set the child node to occupy the right part of the Dock Layout node.
     * Top to set the child node to occupy the top part of the Dock Layout node.
     * Bottom to set the child node to occupy the bottom part of the Dock Layout node.
For example, set the Side property for:
     * Image to Top
     * Button to Bottom
     * Temperature-F to Right
     * Condition to Right
     * Temperature-C to Left
![../../_images/dock-layout-add-side-property-to-child-node.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/dock-layout-add-side-property-to-child-node.gif)
  4. (Optional) When you want the last child node in a Dock Layout node to occupy the remaining space of the Dock Layout node, add to the Dock Layout node the Last Item Fill property, and enable it.
  5. (Optional) To clear the area around child nodes in a layout, in the Node Tree select child nodes in the layout, in the Properties click ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/open-add-properties-window.png), and add and set the margin properties:
     * Depth Margin to clear the area in the back and the front of a child node.
     * Horizontal Margin to clear the area on the left and the right sides of a child node.
     * Vertical Margin to clear the area on the bottom and the top of a child node.
![../../_images/dock-layout-add-margin.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/dock-layout-add-margin.gif)

Use the Flow Layout nodes to arrange nodes along a line. When a line runs out of space, the Flow Layout node places its child nodes in a new line.
You can use a Flow Layout node to arrange content in the same way you would arrange it on a page.
![../../_images/flow-layout.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/flow-layout.gif)
Flow Layout node iterates through its child nodes in the order you add them and first arranges items along the line set in the Primary Direction property. When a Flow Layout node runs out of available space in the direction set by the Primary Direction property, it creates a new line along the direction you set in the Secondary Direction property. See [Setting the direction of a Flow Layout node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-flow-layouts.html#setting-direction-of-flow-layout-node).
You can set the direction and the starting point for arranging Flow Layout 3D child nodes on x, y, and z axes, and Flow Layout 2D child nodes on x and y axes.
![../../_images/flow-layout-width-change.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/flow-layout-width-change.gif)

## Creating a Flow Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-flow-layouts.html#creating-a-flow-layout-node "Link to this heading")
To create a Flow Layout node:
  1. In the Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click the node where you want to create a Flow Layout node and select either Flow Layout 3D, or Flow Layout 2D.
You can create a 3D node only in a 3D node, such as the Scene node, and a 2D node only in a 2D node.
![../../_images/node-tree-add-flow-layout-node.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-add-flow-layout-node.png)
Tip
In the Preview select the Flow Layout 2D tool ![flow-layout-2d-tool](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/flow-layout-2d-tool.png) to create a Flow Layout 2D node by clicking and dragging in the Preview.
     * When you create a layout whose width is greater than its height, the direction of the layout is Left to Right.
![../../_images/flow-layout-x-axis.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/flow-layout-x-axis.png) ![../../_images/flow-layout-x-direction.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/flow-layout-x-direction.png)
     * When you create a layout whose height is greater than its width, the direction of the layout is Top to Bottom.
![../../_images/flow-layout-y-axis.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/flow-layout-y-axis.png) ![../../_images/flow-layout-y-direction.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/flow-layout-y-direction.png)
  2. In the Node Tree, add child nodes to the layout that you created in the previous step.
For example, if you created a Flow Layout 3D node, add several Empty Node 3D nodes that contain 3D content. If you created a Flow Layout 2D node, add several Image nodes.
As you add child nodes, the Flow Layout node positions them along the axes defined by the Primary Direction and Secondary Direction properties.
![../../_images/node-tree-add-nodes-in-flow-layout-node.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-add-nodes-in-flow-layout-node.png)
  3. (Optional) To clear the area around child nodes in a layout, in the Node Tree select child nodes in the layout, in the Properties click ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/open-add-properties-window.png), and add and set the margin properties:
     * Depth Margin to clear the area in the back and the front of a child node.
     * Horizontal Margin to clear the area on the left and the right sides of a child node.
     * Vertical Margin to clear the area on the bottom and the top of a child node.
![../../_images/flow-layout-add-margin.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/flow-layout-add-margin.gif)

content:
## Setting the direction of a Flow Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-flow-layouts.html#setting-the-direction-of-a-flow-layout-node "Link to this heading")
For a Flow Layout node you can set both the starting point and the direction in which the Flow Layout node arranges its child nodes.
To set the direction of a Flow Layout node:
  1. Create a Flow Layout node and add child nodes to it. See [Creating a Flow Layout node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-flow-layouts.html#creating-flow-layout-node).
  2. In the Properties set the Flow Layout node direction properties:
     * Primary Direction. This is the direction along which the child nodes are arrange until they reach the limit of the Flow Layout node.
For example, for a Flow Layout node with a Primary Direction set to Left to Right, the limit is set by the Layout Width property. However, if the Primary Direction is set to Near to Far, the limit is set by the Layout Depth property.
![../../_images/flow-layout-changes-accroding-to-layout-depth.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/flow-layout-changes-accroding-to-layout-depth.gif)
     * Secondary Direction. This is the direction along which the child nodes are laid out when the child nodes exceed the limit set by the Primary Direction property.
For example, to set a Flow Layout node where child nodes are first added from the left to right and then from top to bottom, set the Primary Direction property to Left to Right and the Secondary Direction property to Top to Bottom.
Note that in order to make the Flow Layout node go in the direction defined by the Secondary Direction property, you must set the limit for the Primary Direction property.
![../../_images/flow-layout-secondary-direction.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/flow-layout-secondary-direction.gif)
For example, to arrange items in a flow layout according to the rules used in:
     * Left-to-right languages, set properties:
       * Primary Direction to Left to Right
       * Secondary Direction to Top to Bottom
![../../_images/english-text-direction-property-setting.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/english-text-direction-property-setting.png) ![../../_images/english-text-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/english-text-preview.png)
     * Right-to-left languages, set properties:
       * Primary Direction to Right to Left
       * Secondary Direction to Top to Bottom
![../../_images/arabic-text-direction-property-setting.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/arabic-text-direction-property-setting.png) ![../../_images/arabic-text-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/arabic-text-preview.png)
     * Traditional Chinese writing layout, set properties:
       * Primary Direction to Top to Bottom
       * Secondary Direction to Right to Left

## Creating a Grid Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#creating-a-grid-layout-node "Link to this heading")
To create a Grid Layout node:
  1. In the Node Tree, press `Alt` and right-click the node where you want to create a Grid Layout node and select either Grid Layout 2D or Grid Layout 3D.
You can create a 3D node only in a 3D node, such as the Scene node, and a 2D node only in a 2D node.
![../../_images/create-grid-layout-2d-node.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-grid-layout-2d-node.png)
Tip
In the Preview tools, use the Grid Layout 2D tool ![grid-layout-2d-tool](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/grid-layout-2d-tool.png) to click and drag in the Preview to create a Grid Layout 2D node. To scale the columns and rows, click and drag those columns and rows in the Preview.
  2. In the Node Tree, add child nodes to the layout that you created in the previous step.
For example, if you created a Grid Layout 2D node, add several Image nodes, if you created a Grid Layout 3D node, add several Sphere nodes.
As you add child nodes, the Grid Layout node positions them in the grid from the top-left towards the bottom-right corner of the grid. To manually set the position of each child node in the Grid Layout node, in each child node set the Column and Row properties. See [Assigning nodes to cells in a Grid Layout node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#setting-custom-node-and-column).
![../../_images/add-image-nodes.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-image-nodes.png) ![../../_images/image-nodes-in-grid-layout.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/image-nodes-in-grid-layout.png) ![../../_images/image-nodes-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/image-nodes-in-preview.png)

## Setting the direction in which a Grid Layout node arranges its child nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#setting-the-direction-in-which-a-grid-layout-node-arranges-its-child-nodes "Link to this heading")
When you let a Grid Layout node arrange its child nodes automatically, you can set the direction in which that Grid Layout node arranges its child nodes.
To set the direction in which a Grid Layout node arranges its child nodes:
  1. In the Node Tree, select the Grid Layout node for which you want to set the direction.
  2. In the Properties, add and set the Layout Direction property to:
     * Down to make the Grid Layout node first place its child nodes in the first column. When the first column is full, the Grid Layout node starts placing its child nodes in the second column, and so on.
     * Right to make the Grid Layout node first place its child nodes in the first row. When the first row is full, the Grid Layout node starts placing its child nodes in the second row, and so on. This is the default value.
![../../_images/grid-layout-2d-layout-direction-down.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/grid-layout-2d-layout-direction-down.png) ![../../_images/layout-direction-in-preview-images.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/layout-direction-in-preview-images.png)

## Assigning nodes to cells in a Grid Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#assigning-nodes-to-cells-in-a-grid-layout-node "Link to this heading")
You can manually assign each child node to a specific row and column in a Grid Layout node.
To assign nodes to cells in a Grid Layout node:
  1. Create a Grid Layout node and add several child nodes to it. See [Creating a Grid Layout node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#creating-grid-layout-node).
  2. In the Node Tree, select the child nodes of the Grid Layout node. In the Properties, add the Grid Layout > Column and Grid Layout > Row properties.
![../../_images/assign-nodes-to-cells-child-nodes.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/assign-nodes-to-cells-child-nodes.png) ![../../_images/assign-nodes-to-cells-row-column-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/assign-nodes-to-cells-row-column-properties.png)
  3. Use the Column and Row properties to specify a zero-based index of a column and a zero-based index of a row that a node occupies in a Grid Layout node.
For example, to arrange three images in a checkerboard pattern, set:
     * For the second child node: Column to 1, Row to 1.
You assign this node to the second column and second row.
     * For the third child node: Column to 0, Row to 2.
You assign this node to the first column and third row.
![../../_images/layout-custom-row-column-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/layout-custom-row-column-in-preview.png)


Tip
To assign a node to another Grid Layout 2D cell in the Preview:
  1. In the Node Tree, select the node.
  2. Hold down the Ctrl key.
  3. In the Preview, drag the node to the cell where you want to assign it.

![../../_images/preview-assign-node-to-cell.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-assign-node-to-cell.gif)

## Spanning columns and rows in a Grid Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#spanning-columns-and-rows-in-a-grid-layout-node "Link to this heading")
For each cell in a Grid Layout node, you can set the number of columns and rows that cell spans.
To span a cell across columns and rows of a Grid Layout node:
  1. Create a Grid Layout node and add several child nodes to it. See [Creating a Grid Layout node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#creating-grid-layout-node).
![../../_images/span-rows-columns-create-child-nodes.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/span-rows-columns-create-child-nodes.png)
  2. In each child node of the Grid Layout node, add the Grid Layout > Column and Grid Layout > Row properties. See [Assigning nodes to cells in a Grid Layout node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#setting-custom-node-and-column).
A Grid Layout node by default has three columns and three rows. For example, you can arrange the first five child nodes in a Grid Layout on the top row and left column. The sixth child node can occupy the rest of the space. In the child nodes of the Grid Layout node, set these properties:  
| Child node  | Column  | Row  | Layout Width  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| 1  | 0  | 0  | 200  |  
| 2  | 1  | 0  | 200  |  
| 3  | 2  | 0  | 200  |  
| 4  | 0  | 1  | 200  |  
| 5  | 0  | 2  | 200  |  
| 6  | 1  | 1  | 400  |  
A Grid Layout node by default calculates the size of its columns and rows automatically based on the size of the largest child node in that column and row. Here the sixth image, which is larger than the other images, stretches the second column and second row of the Grid Layout node. This leaves gaps in the layout.
![../../_images/span-rows-columns-set-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/span-rows-columns-set-properties.png)
  3. In the Grid Layout node, select a child node that you want to span across multiple columns and rows. In the Properties, add and set the Column Span and Row Span properties to the number of columns and rows you want that cell to span.
The cell spans across columns to its right and across rows downwards.
For example, to set the last image to span two rows and two columns, set the Column Span and Row Span properties to 2.
![../../_images/add-columns-span.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-columns-span.png) ![../../_images/column-and-row-span.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/column-and-row-span.png) ![../../_images/span-rows-columns-result.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/span-rows-columns-result.png)

## Setting how a Grid Layout node calculates the size of its columns and rows[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#setting-how-a-grid-layout-node-calculates-the-size-of-its-columns-and-rows "Link to this heading")
When you create columns and rows in a Grid Layout node, you can set how that Grid Layout node calculates the size of its columns and rows. For example, to distribute content equally in a Grid Layout node, you can use proportional sizes for rows and columns.
To set how Grid Layout node calculates the size of its columns and rows:
  1. Create a Grid Layout node and add several child nodes to it. See [Creating a Grid Layout node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#creating-grid-layout-node).
![../../_images/create-grid-layout-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-grid-layout-2d.png)
  2. In the Properties, set the size of the Grid Layout node by setting its Layout Width and Layout Height properties.
For example, set Layout Width to 500 and Layout Height to 300.
![../../_images/layout-width-and-height.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/layout-width-and-height.png)
  3. Set the values of Columns and Rows properties in the Grid Layout node to:
     * Automatic to let the Grid Layout node automatically calculate the size of its columns and rows based on the size of the largest child node in that column and row.
![../../_images/columns-and-rows-automatic.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/columns-and-rows-automatic.png) ![../../_images/automatic-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/automatic-in-preview.png)
     * Fixed to set the exact size of a column and row, regardless of the size of the child nodes in that column and row.
![../../_images/columns-and-rows-fixed.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/columns-and-rows-fixed.png) ![../../_images/fixed-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/fixed-in-preview.png)
     * Proportional to set the size of a column and row in proportion to the remaining size of other columns and rows that use this same setting, and the size of the entire Grid Layout node.
For example:
       * To equally distribute the content in columns, select Proportional and for each column use the same value.
       * If you have three columns and you want the first one to occupy half of the Grid Layout node width, select Proportional, use value 2 for the first column, and 1 for the other two columns.
![../../_images/columns-and-rows-proportional.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/columns-and-rows-proportional.png) ![../../_images/proportional-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/proportional-in-preview.png)

## Using Grid Layout nodes to create user interfaces for different screen sizes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#using-grid-layout-nodes-to-create-user-interfaces-for-different-screen-sizes "Link to this heading")
You can use Grid Layout nodes to create applications with consistent user interfaces across devices with different screen sizes. A Grid Layout node can distribute its child nodes so that they occupy the same relative amount of space in the application interface, regardless of screen size or device orientation. For example, with a Grid Layout node, you can place the user interface controls in the top-left and bottom-right corners, with strictly defined distances from the edges of the screen.
For a more advanced approach to creating user interfaces for different screen sizes, see [Tutorial: Making applications with dynamic layout](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/dynamic-layout/dynamic-layout.html).
To use Grid Layout nodes to create consistent user interface for different screen sizes:
  1. Create a Grid Layout node and add several child nodes to it. See [Creating a Grid Layout node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#creating-grid-layout-node).
  2. Select the Grid Layout node. In the Properties, set:
     * Columns and Rows to Proportional.
     * Horizontal Alignment and Vertical Alignment to Stretch.
To keep images pixel perfect, instead of setting the Horizontal Alignment and Vertical Alignment properties to Stretch, add the Snap to Pixel property to child nodes whose position changes with the application layout.
![../../_images/columns-and-rows-proportional-default.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/columns-and-rows-proportional-default.png) ![../../_images/alignment-stretch.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/alignment-stretch.png) ![../../_images/horizontal-alignment-strech-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/horizontal-alignment-strech-in-preview.png)
With these settings, you set the Grid Layout node to distribute its content equally across its entire width and height, and set the Grid Layout node to stretch across the entire screen.
  3. In the Node Tree, select the third child in the Grid Layout node. In the Properties, add and set:
     * Column to 2
     * Row to 2
     * Horizontal Alignment to Right
     * Vertical Alignment to Bottom
     * Horizontal Margin property Right property field to 20
     * Vertical Margin property Bottom property field to 20
With these settings, you position the third child node of the Grid Layout node in the third column and third row of the Grid Layout node, and place it 20 pixels from the bottom-right corner of the screen. The third child node in the Grid Layout node stays in that position regardless of the screen size or orientation.

![../../_images/column-and-row-settings.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/column-and-row-settings.png) ![../../_images/third-image-settings.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/third-image-settings.png) ![../../_images/third-image-aligned.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/third-image-aligned.png)

## Setting the appearance of a Grid Layout 2D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html#setting-the-appearance-of-a-grid-layout-2d-node "Link to this heading")
To set the appearance of 2D nodes:
  * You can fill 2D nodes with a solid color, a texture, or a material. See [Adjusting the appearance of 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html).
![../../_images/color-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/color-brush.png) ![../../_images/texture-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-brush.png) ![../../_images/material-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/material-brush.png)
  * You can apply a post-processing effect to a 2D node. See [Effects for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/2d-effects.html).
![../../_images/blur-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blur-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/mask-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/outline-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/outline-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/shadow-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/shadow-effect-2d.png)
  * You can rotate a 2D node around all three axes to create a 3D perspective effect. See [Creating a 3D perspective effect for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/setting-the-perspective.html).
![../../_images/perspective-transformation-visualization.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/perspective-transformation-visualization.png)
  * You can apply custom rendering to 2D nodes to create post-processing effects. See [Applying custom rendering to 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/applying-custom-rendering.html).
![../../_images/texture-grayscale.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-grayscale.png)
  * You can render a 2D node as pixel-perfect. See [Rendering pixel-perfect 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html#rendering-pixel-perfect-2d-nodes).
![../../_images/snap-to-pixel-icon.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/snap-to-pixel-icon.png)

content:
## Creating a Stack Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-stack-layouts.html#creating-a-stack-layout-node "Link to this heading")
To create a Stack Layout node:
  1. In the Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click the node where you want to create a Stack Layout node and select either Stack Layout 3D, or Stack Layout 2D.
You can create a 3D node only in a 3D node, such as the Scene node, and a 2D node only in a 2D node.
![../../_images/node-tree-create-stack-layout-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-create-stack-layout-2d.png)
Tip
In the Preview select the Stack Layout 2D tool ![stack-layout-tool](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/stack-layout-2d-tool.png) to create a Stack Layout 2D node by clicking and dragging in the Preview. The ![stack-tool-arrow](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/stack-tool-arrow.png) above the Stack Layout 2D shows the direction of the layout.
     * When you create a layout whose width is greater than its height, the direction of the layout is on the x axis.
![../../_images/stack-layout-x-axis.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/stack-layout-x-axis.png) ![../../_images/stack-layout-x-direction.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/stack-layout-x-direction.png)
     * When you create a layout whose height is greater than its width, the direction of the layout is on the y axis.
![../../_images/stack-layout-y-axis.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/stack-layout-y-axis.png) ![../../_images/stack-layout-y-direction.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/stack-layout-y-direction.png)
  2. In the Node Tree, add child nodes to the layout that you created in the previous step.
For example, if you created a Stack Layout 3D node, add several Sphere nodes, if you created a Stack Layout 2D node, add several Image nodes.
As you add child nodes, the Stack Layout node positions them along the axis defined by its Direction property.
![../../_images/node-tree-stack-layout-images.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-stack-layout-images.png) ![../../_images/preview-stack-layout-images.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-stack-layout-images.png)
  3. (Optional) In the Properties set the Direction property to the axis long which you want the Stack Layout node to arrange its child nodes.
![../../_images/stack-layout-change-direction.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/stack-layout-change-direction.gif)
  4. (Optional) To clear the area around child nodes in a layout, in the Node Tree select child nodes in the layout, in the Properties click ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/open-add-properties-window.png), and add and set the margin properties:
     * Depth Margin to clear the area in the back and the front of a child node.
     * Horizontal Margin to clear the area on the left and the right sides of a child node.

content:
## Creating a Trajectory Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html#creating-a-trajectory-layout-node "Link to this heading")
To create a Trajectory Layout node:
  1. In the Node Tree, press `Alt` and right-click the node where you want to create a Trajectory Layout node and select either Trajectory Layout 3D, or Trajectory Layout 2D.
![../../_images/node-tree-create-trejectory-layout-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-create-trejectory-layout-2d.png)
You can create a 3D node only in a 3D node, such as the Scene node, and a 2D node only in a 2D node.
Tip
To see the trajectory, in the Preview click ![image-analyze-off](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/analyze-off.png) to enter the Analyze mode, right-click ![image-analyze-on](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/analyze-on.png), and select Debug objects.
![../../_images/visualize-mode-debug-objects.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/visualize-mode-debug-objects.png)
  2. In the Node Tree, add child nodes to the layout that you created in the previous step.
For example, if you created a Trajectory Layout 3D node, add several Sphere nodes. If you created a Trajectory Layout 2D node, add several Image nodes.
![../../_images/node-tree-trajectory-layout-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-trajectory-layout-2d.png)
As you add child nodes, the Trajectory Layout node positions them along the trajectory used by the Trajectory Layout node.
![../../_images/trajectory-layout-element-position.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout-element-position.gif)
  3. (Optional)
Kanzi Studio creates and uses a circle trajectory by default. You can use an angle, arc, circle, ellipse, line, rectangle, spiral, spline, or a trapezoid trajectory. See [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html).
![../../_images/trajectory-layout-types.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout-types.gif)


## Stretching the trajectory to fill the layout[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html#stretching-the-trajectory-to-fill-the-layout "Link to this heading")
By default, the size of the trajectory used by a Trajectory Layout node determines the amount of space that the trajectory occupies in the layout. For example, in a Circle Trajectory, the Radius property determines the size of the trajectory.
To stretch the trajectory to fill the layout:
  1. Select a Trajectory Layout node.
  2. In the Properties, add and enable the Trajectory Layout > Stretch property.

![../../_images/trajectory-layout-stretch.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout-stretch.gif)

## Adjusting the distance between items in a Trajectory Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html#adjusting-the-distance-between-items-in-a-trajectory-layout-node "Link to this heading")
A Trajectory Layout node automatically calculates the distance between its child nodes.
To adjust the distance between the child nodes in a Trajectory Layout node:
  1. Select a Trajectory Layout node.
  2. In the Properties, add and set the Trajectory Layout > Override Distance property.

![../../_images/trajectory-layout-override-distance.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout-override-distance.gif)
## Adjusting the position of items in a Trajectory Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html#adjusting-the-position-of-items-in-a-trajectory-layout-node "Link to this heading")
By default, a Trajectory Layout node arranges its child nodes from the start of the trajectory spline.
To adjust the starting position of the Trajectory Layout node child nodes on the trajectory:
  1. Select a Trajectory Layout node.
  2. In the Properties, add and set the Trajectory Layout > Start Offset property.

![../../_images/trajectory-layout-start-offset.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout-start-offset.gif)

# Using the light nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/lights/using-lights.html#using-the-light-nodes "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use the light nodes to create sources of light for a Scene in your Kanzi application.
Kanzi has these light node types:  
| Directional Light emits light only in one direction and is suitable for modeling the sunlight.  |  ![../../_images/directional-light.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/directional-light.png)  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Point Light emits light from a specific location uniformly to all directions (360 degrees).  |  ![../../_images/point-light.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/point-light.png)  |  
| Spot Light emits light from a specific location towards a specified direction in the shape of a cone.  |  ![../../_images/spot-light.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/spot-light.png)  |  
Lights contain properties that are passed as uniforms to shaders when Kanzi renders 3D nodes. Lights affect only the rendering of nodes that use materials with shaders that use those lights.
In Kanzi, the VertexPhong, FragmentPhong, and PhysicallyBased materials by default support:
  * One directional light
  * Two point lights
  * One spot light


See [Setting the number of lights for a smart material](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/lights/using-lights.html#setting-the-number-of-lights-for-a-smart-material) and [Setting the number of lights for a material type](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/lights/using-lights.html#setting-the-number-of-lights-for-a-material-type).
You can use uniform bindings to control property types of light nodes. See [Controlling light uniforms](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/lights/using-lights.html#controlling-light-uniforms).

content:
## Creating a light node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/lights/using-lights.html#creating-a-light-node "Link to this heading")
To create a light node:
  1. In the Node Tree, press `Alt` and right-click the node where you want to create a light node and select Directional Light, Point Light, or Spot Light.
For example, create a Spot Light.
You can create a light node only in a 3D node, such as the Scene node.
![../../_images/create-spot-light.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-spot-light.png)
  2. In the Preview, use the Node tool ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tool.png) to position the light node.
![../../_images/select-node-tool.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-node-tool.png)
  3. In the Properties, adjust the properties of the light node to create the light suitable for your needs.
For example, to adjust the color of a Spot Light, set the value of the Spot Light Color property.
![../../_images/spot-light-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/spot-light-color.png)

metadata.title: Light nodes (Part 2/10)

content:
## Adjusting the brightness of a light[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/lights/using-lights.html#adjusting-the-brightness-of-a-light "Link to this heading")
To adjust the brightness of a light, set the intensity of the light color.
For example, to set the brightness of a Point Light, set the value of the Point Light Color property Intensity (I) property field.
![../../_images/set-light-intensity.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-light-intensity.png) [![../../_images/sphere-and-point-light.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/sphere-and-point-light.png)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/sphere-and-point-light.png)
Light intensity in Kanzi works similarly to exposure in photography:
  * Increase of intensity by one unit doubles the amount of light.
  * Decrease of intensity by one unit halves the amount of light.


For example, when you change the intensity:
  * From 0 to +2, you quadruple the brightness.
  * From 0 to -3, you decrease the brightness to 1/8.

[![../../_images/intensity-4.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/intensity-4.png)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/intensity-4.png) [![../../_images/intensity-3.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/intensity-3.png)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/intensity-3.png) [![../../_images/intensity-2.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/intensity-2.png)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/intensity-2.png) [![../../_images/intensity-1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/intensity-1.png)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/intensity-1.png) [![../../_images/intensity1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/intensity1.png)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/intensity1.png) [![../../_images/intensity2.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/intensity2.png)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/intensity2.png) [![../../_images/intensity3.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/intensity3.png)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/intensity3.png) [![../../_images/intensity4.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/intensity4.png)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/intensity4.png)
## Turning off a light[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/lights/using-lights.html#turning-off-a-light "Link to this heading")
To turn off a light, select the light node, and in the Properties add and disable the Node > Visible property.
![../../_images/node-visible-disabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-visible-disabled.png)

content:
## Setting the number of lights for a smart material[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/lights/using-lights.html#setting-the-number-of-lights-for-a-smart-material "Link to this heading")
In a material that uses the SmartPhysicallyBased, SmartVertexPhong, or SmartFragmentPhong material type, you can set the type and number of lights that the material can use. See [Using smart materials](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/using-smart-materials.html).
To set the number of lights for a smart material:
  1. In the Library > Materials and Textures > Materials, select a material that uses the SmartPhysicallyBased, SmartVertexPhong, or SmartFragmentPhong material type.
For example, select the SmartPhysicallyBasedMaterial. If your project does not contain that material, in the Library > Materials and Textures press `Alt` and right-click Material Types, and select SmartPhysicallyBased.
![../../_images/library-smart-physically-based-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/library-smart-physically-based-material.png)
  2. In the Properties, add and set any of these Material Properties:
     * Limit Directional Lights to set the number of directional lights
By default, the material supports one directional light.
     * Limit Point Lights to set the number of point lights
By default, the material supports two point lights.
     * Limit Spot Lights to set the number of spot lights
By default, the material supports one spot light.
For example, to set the material to render the first three Point Light nodes in the scene, add the Limit Point Lights property and set it to 3.
If a scene contains more than three point lights, only the first three of them affect the rendering of the nodes that use this material.
![../../_images/properties-limit-point-lights.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-limit-point-lights.png)

metadata.title: Light nodes (Part 4/10)

content:
## Setting the number of lights for a material type[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/lights/using-lights.html#setting-the-number-of-lights-for-a-material-type "Link to this heading")
For a material type, you can set the type and number of lights that the materials based on that material type can use.
To set the number of lights for a material type:
  1. In the Library > Materials and Textures > Material Types, select the material type for which you want to set the lights.
For example, select the VertexPhong material type.
You can use this approach only for the Kanzi default VertexPhong, FragmentPhong, and PhysicallyBased material types. To modify the number of lights for other material types, you must manually edit the material shaders. See [Editing shaders](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/shaders/editing-shaders.html).
![../../_images/vertexphong-in-library.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/vertexphong-in-library.png)
  2. In the Properties, in the Preprocessor Definitions, for each light type set the Value to the number of lights that you want to use:
     * KANZI_SHADER_NUM_DIRECTIONAL_LIGHTS to set the number of directional lights
     * KANZI_SHADER_NUM_POINT_LIGHTS to set the number of point lights
     * KANZI_SHADER_NUM_SPOT_LIGHTS to set the number of spot lights
For example, to set a material to use four spot lights, set the KANZI_SHADER_NUM_SPOT_LIGHTS Value to 4 and press the `Enter` key. Now all the materials that use this material type can render four spot lights. If a scene contains more than four spot lights, only the first four lights in that scene affect the rendering of the nodes which use the material with that material type.
When you press the `Enter` key, Kanzi Studio updates in the Uniforms the uniform arrays for the properties of the light types that you changed.
![../../_images/phong-preprocessor-defines.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/phong-preprocessor-defines.png) ![../../_images/phong-shader-uniforms-with-4-spot-lights.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/phong-shader-uniforms-with-4-spot-lights.png)

content:
## Controlling light uniforms[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/lights/using-lights.html#controlling-light-uniforms "Link to this heading")
In a material type, vertex and fragment shaders define the uniforms and property types that you can use in that material. When rendering 3D nodes with a specific material type, uniform bindings allow Kanzi to write values to the render state and use those values for uniforms and property types.
See [Uniform bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/materials.html#uniform-bindings), [Using material types](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/using-material-types.html), and [Rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html).
Light property types support uniform arrays, which enables you to use multiple lights of the same type. See [Uniform arrays for light property types](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/shaders/editing-shaders.html#uniform-arrays-for-light-property-types).
A uniform binding for a light property type sets the uniform values in a render state based on the values extracted from lights that use that property type. For example, a uniform binding for the `PointLightColor` property type sets the render value based on the individual values of the Point Light Color property in all Point Light nodes in the scene that light those 3D nodes that use the material type which has the binding.
To use bindings to control light uniforms:
  1. In the Node Tree, create 3D content and the Light nodes that you use to light that content.
For example, here three Point Light nodes of different color light a gray Sphere node. Make sure that the material type, which your 3D content uses, supports the number of lights that you want to use. See [Setting the number of lights for a material type](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/lights/using-lights.html#setting-the-number-of-lights-for-a-material-type).
![../../_images/sphere-and-rgb-lights.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/sphere-and-rgb-lights.png) ![../../_images/point-lights-in-preview-default.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/point-lights-in-preview-default.png)
  2. In the Library > Materials and Textures > Material Types, select the material type that your 3D content uses.
For example, select the `VertexPhong` material type.
![../../_images/vertexphong-in-library.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/vertexphong-in-library.png)
  3. In the Properties, in the Bindings > Uniforms, click the binding that sets the render value of the uniform that you want to modify.
For example, click the binding that sets the value of the `PointLightColor` uniform. This binding sets the render value of the uniform based on the individual values of the Point Light Color property in all Point Light nodes in a scene that light those 3D nodes that use the VertexPhong material type.

  4. In the Binding Editor, enter the binding expression that you want to use and click Save.
A uniform binding for a light property type sets the uniform values in a render state based on the values extracted from lights that use that property type. For example, a uniform binding for the `PointLightColor` property type sets the render value based on the individual values of the Point Light Color property in all Point Light nodes in the scene that light those 3D nodes that use the material type which has the binding.
You can use this syntax in the binding expression:
     * To get the range that contains each light node of a specific type used by a Draw Objects render pass or Draw Objects With Material render pass to draw the 3D nodes in a scene, use `{##RenderPass/DrawObjectsRenderPass.[lightType]}`.
Kanzi has these light types: `DirectionalLights`, `PointLights`, and `SpotLights`.
See [Using lights in rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/lights-rendering.html).
     * To get the range that contains the value of a property in each light node of a specific type, in the binding expression enter in curly braces `##RenderPass/DrawObjectsRenderPass.[lightType]`, followed by ellipsis and the name of the property in the light nodes.
     * To create a view over a range of lights, use the [createView](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/reference-for-bindings-expressions.html#createview) function.
     * To perform accumulation operations on a range of lights, use the `...` operator followed by an arithmetic operator.
     * To refer to the result of a temporary variable binding in the same material type, use the `{##Self/[temporaryVariableProperty]}` syntax, where `temporaryVariableProperty` is the target property of the temporary variable binding. See [Temporary variable bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/materials.html#temporary-variable-bindings).
See [Light uniform bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/reference-for-bindings-expressions.html#light-uniform-bindings).
For example:
     * To halve the value of the red and green color channels in the Point Light Color property of each Point Light node, multiply the result of the default binding by `Color4(0.5, 0.5, 1, 1)`:

pointLightsView = createView<OutputSize>({##RenderPass/DrawObjectsRenderPass.PointLights})

     * To dim all Point Light nodes based on the value of the Opacity property in any of those Point Light nodes:

```
# Get the range that contains the value of the Point Light Color property in each
# Point Light node.
rangeA = {##RenderPass/DrawObjectsRenderPass.PointLights ... PointLightColor}
# Get the range that contains the value of the Opacity property in each
# Point Light node.
rangeB = {##RenderPass/DrawObjectsRenderPass.PointLights ... Node.Opacity}
# Multiply the value of the Opacity property in each Point Light node.
totalOpacity = ...* rangeB
# For each Point Light node multiply the value of the Point Light Color property

rangeA * totalOpacity

Use the List Box nodes to arrange items in scrollable lists. For example, use List Box nodes to create contact lists, album lists in a media player, or car settings lists. While the layout control nodes arrange their items in a static layout, the List Box nodes arrange their items in a list where the user can see only a set number of items at a time. To access more items, the user scrolls the list box. See [Layout control nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/layouts.html).

## Setting the size of the visible area[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/list-box-nodes.html#setting-the-size-of-the-visible-area "Link to this heading")
To set the size of the area in which the items in a List Box node are visible, use these properties:
  * Layout Height to set the height of the visible area of a Grid List Box or Trajectory List Box 3D node.
  * Layout Width to set the width of the visible area of a Grid List Box or Trajectory List Box 3D node.
  * Layout Depth to set the depth of the visible area of a Trajectory List Box 3D node.


## Selecting an item and defining its selection behavior[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/list-box-nodes.html#selecting-an-item-and-defining-its-selection-behavior "Link to this heading")
You can set which item in a List Box node is selected and how an item reacts when the user selects it. For example, you can bring the selected item to the center of the list box visible area.
  * To set which item in a list box is selected, use the Selected Item Index property. The indexing starts from 0.
To update the value of the Selected Item Index property with a binding, use a to-source or two-way binding. Kanzi internally overrides any one-way binding that targets the Selected Item Index property. See [Bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/bindings.html).
For example, you can enable the user to select an item in a List Box node either by clicking that item, or by using a slider. See [Creating a two-way binding](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html#creating-a-two-way-binding).
  * To set a list box to bring an item to the center of the list box area when the user selects that item, use the Selection Behavior property. See [Bringing the selected item to the center of a Grid List Box](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#bringing-selected-item-to-center-of-glb) and [Using the Trajectory List Box 3D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html).

content:
## Accessing the number and position of items[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/list-box-nodes.html#accessing-the-number-and-position-of-items "Link to this heading")
To get the number and position of items in a List Box node, use these read-only properties:
  * List Box > Item Count to get the number of items in a list box, including virtual items.
For example, use the Item Count property to set the maximum value of a Slider that the user can use to:
    * Select an item in a List Box node. See [Creating a two-way binding](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html#creating-a-two-way-binding).
    * Scroll a Grid List Box node. See [Scrolling a Grid List Box node with a slider](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#scrolling-glb-node-with-slider).
  * List Box Item Container > Item Index to get the position of an item in a list box. The indexing starts from 0.
For example, use the Item Index property in a binding that sets the appearance of a list box item based on its distance from the selected item. Use the List Box > Selected Item Index property to get the index of the selected item. You can use this approach to decrease the size and opacity of items that are farther from the selected item.
