## Creating the base for a Kanzi Studio window plugin[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/creating-kanzi-studio-window-plugins.html#creating-the-base-for-a-ks-window-plugin "Link to this heading")
Kanzi Studio window plugins are plugins that you use in a Kanzi Studio window and have a user interface. For example, use the window plugins to create an editor or to visualize the content in your project.
Here you create the base for a Kanzi Studio window plugin where you then add functionality that extends the functionality of Kanzi Studio.
To create a Kanzi Studio window plugin:
  1. In Visual Studio select File > New > Project and create a Visual C# Class Library.
![../../_images/create-visual-c-class-library.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-visual-c-class-library.png)
  2. In the Solution Explorer right-click the project name, select Add > Reference, and add references to files:
    1. Select Assemblies > Framework targeting .NET Framework and add the reference to:
       * `System.ComponentModel.Composition`
       * `System.XAML`
    2. Click Browse… and add the reference to the `<KanziInstallation>/Studio/Bin/PluginInterface.dll` file.
![../../_images/plugininterface_dll.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/plugininterface_dll.png)
  3. In the Solution Explorer right-click the project name, select Properties, and:
     * In the Application tab set the Target framework to .NET Framework 4.8.
![../../_images/target-framework.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/target-framework.png)
     * In the Build tab set the Platform target to x64.
![../../_images/platform-target-x64.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/platform-target-x64.png)
  4. In the Solution Explorer right-click the project name, select Add > User Control and add a User Control (WPF) item.
![../../_images/user-control-wpf.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/user-control-wpf.png)
  5. Open the `UserControl1.xaml.cs` file and add the using directive for the Kanzi Studio plugin API:

using Rightware.Kanzi.Studio.PluginInterface;

Kanzi Studio provides the `KanziStudio[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-studio-plugin-api/a02502.html)` object to plugins. The `KanziStudio[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-studio-plugin-api/a02502.html)` object is the root object for data access and provides the current project, available commands, global undo and redo, and events related to project opening and closing.
For example, use this to enable the command only when a Kanzi Studio project is open

```
private KanziStudio studio;
public bool CanExecute(PluginCommandParameter parameter)
{
    return this.studio != null && this.studio.ActiveProject != null;
}

## Using a custom property editor with Kanzi Engine custom property types[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/creating-plugin-property-editors.html#using-a-custom-property-editor-with-kr-custom-property-types "Link to this heading")
To use a custom property editor for a custom property type that you define in a Kanzi Engine plugin, in the Kanzi Engine plugin in the property editor metadata declarations for that property type set `metadata.editor` to the name of the editor that you want to use.
The name of the editor is set in the `Name` property of the class where you define the property editor.
For example, to set the custom File selector editor as a property editor, use:

```
PropertyType<string> VideoView2D::VideoFileNameProperty(kzMakeFixedString("VideoView2D.VideoFileName"), "", 0, false,
                                                     KZ_DECLARE_EDITOR_METADATA
                                                     (
                                                         metadata.editor = "FileSelectorEditor"
                                                         metadata.displayName = "Video Filename";
                                                         metadata.tooltip = "Video file to be played";
                                                         metadata.host = "VideoView2D:freq";
                                                     ));

```

Here you can find an overview of the Kanzi Studio plugin API.
Kanzi Studio plugins extend the functionality of Kanzi Studio and run in Kanzi Studio.
Kanzi Studio command plugins are plugins that you execute as commands and do not have a user interface. For example, use the command plugins to execute a command on the entire or the selected part of the node tree in your project.
See [Kanzi Studio plugins](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/plugins.html) and [Creating Kanzi Studio command plugins](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/creating-kanzi-studio-plugins.html).
After you create the base for a plugin, use this overview and Kanzi Studio plugin API reference to add functionality to your plugin so that it does something useful. See [Creating the base for a Kanzi Studio command plugin](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/creating-kanzi-studio-plugins.html#creating-the-base-for-command-plugin) and [Kanzi Studio plugin API reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-studio-plugin-api/index.html).

## Kanzi Studio data model[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/reference-kanzi-studio-plugin-interface.html#ks-data-model "Link to this heading")
Kanzi Studio project is a hierarchical structure of project nodes. Each node has a set of properties and can have a set of child nodes or items. Different types of project items, such as nodes, models, textures, and animations have their own characteristics. For example, textures specify the image used in the texture and filtering. To change the data in the project Kanzi Studio uses commands. For example, set values to properties, or create new items.
Kanzi Studio provides the `KanziStudio[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-studio-plugin-api/a02502.html)` object to plugins. The `KanziStudio[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-studio-plugin-api/a02502.html)` object is the root object for data access and provides the current project, available commands, global undo and redo, and events related to project opening and closing.
You can access the nodes, resources, and properties in the project using the current project node. Use libraries for different types of nodes and factory for new project nodes and resources. Nodes provide the access to properties, child nodes and items, changes in the current node and descendants, and events.
In all functions replace this line with the code you want to execute:

```
throw new NotImplementedException();

```
Copy to clipboard
Make sure that your plugin handles all its internal exceptions and does not let them reach the Kanzi Studio interface.

## Kanzi Studio[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/reference-kanzi-studio-plugin-interface.html#ks "Link to this heading")
Use the `studio` object to access the Kanzi Studio interface. For example, use it when you want to write a message to the Log window, get input from the user, to undo and redo changes in a project, and so on.
### Getting user input[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/reference-kanzi-studio-plugin-interface.html#getting-user-input "Link to this heading")
Use `KanziStudio.GetUserInput[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-studio-plugin-api/a02502.html#afe5a8f4957cbfd246b9fd9042d304594)` to display a dialog box which prompts the user to provide input. For example, you can use `KanziStudio.GetUserInput[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-studio-plugin-api/a02502.html#afe5a8f4957cbfd246b9fd9042d304594)` to get the path of a node where you want your plugin to start executing its commands.
To display a dialog box which prompts the user to provide input:
  1. In the Visual Studio solution of your plugin open the class library file that implements the `PluginCommand` interface and in the `Execute` function use `KanziStudio.GetUserInput[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-studio-plugin-api/a02502.html#afe5a8f4957cbfd246b9fd9042d304594)` to display a dialog box with a message.

```
public void Execute(PluginCommandParameter parameter)
{
    studio.GetUserInput("Where do you want to create the structure?", "Enter the path where you want to create the structure:");
}

```
Copy to clipboard
  2. When you run the plugin, it prompts the user to provide input.
![../../_images/getuserinput.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/getuserinput.png)


### Writing a message to the Kanzi Studio Log window[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/reference-kanzi-studio-plugin-interface.html#writing-a-message-to-the-ks-log-window "Link to this heading")
To write a message to the Kanzi Studio Log window:
  1. In the Visual Studio solution of your plugin open the class library file that implements the `PluginCommand` interface and in the `Execute` function use `KanziStudio.Log[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-studio-plugin-api/a02502.html#a45cccc8bffcb9718be3b9be6fc7c1ef6)` to write to the Log window.

```
public void Execute(PluginCommandParameter parameter)
{
    studio.Log("Success!");
}

```
Copy to clipboard
  2. When you run the plugin, it prints Success! to the Kanzi Studio Log window.
![../../_images/print-to-log.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/print-to-log.png)

  3. In Visual Studio add the break points where you want to debug your plugin.

## Using the Kanzi Studio Command History[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/debugging-kanzi-studio-plugins.html#using-the-ks-command-history "Link to this heading")
Use the Kanzi Studio Command History to view the commands you have executed in a Kanzi Studio project.
To open the Command History window in the Kanzi Studio main menu select Edit > Command History or press the `Ctrl` `Shift` `U`.
![../../_images/open-command-history.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/open-command-history.png)
In the Command History window:
  * Executed lists the commands you have executed. To undo these commands one at a time, select Edit > Undo or press the `Ctrl` `Z`.
  * Undone lists the commands you have executed and then undone. To redo these commands one at a time, select Edit > Redo or press the `Ctrl` `Y`.

![../../_images/command-history-window.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/command-history-window.png)

# Using node prefabs[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#using-node-prefabs "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use prefabs (prefabricated templates) to structure your application and to create consistent interfaces. Prefabs allow you to create the building blocks of your application and make the application easier to maintain.
Create a prefab for every item in your application that appears more than once, when you want to logically separate a part of your application, or add content to the node tree when your application is already running. For example, use prefabs to:
  * Create content with consistent structure. For example, with prefabs you can create buttons that always have the same structure, but can vary in appearance.
  * Modularize your project and make it easier to maintain.
  * Control the loading and launch times of your Kanzi application.
  * Create different themes for your Kanzi application.
  * Localize your Kanzi application.


When using prefabs keep in mind that:
  * You can duplicate an instance of a prefab like any other node in the node tree.
  * Property values you add to an instance of a prefab override the property values set in the prefab.
  * Use relative paths when you want to reference items inside a prefab (for example, in a message trigger or a property binding). Do not use the prefab itself as a target path for any messages or animations.


You can nest prefabs within prefabs.

content:
## Node prefabs and node prefab instances[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#node-prefabs-and-node-prefab-instances "Link to this heading")
Node prefabs consume memory on the device only when you load them. When you load a node prefab, the prefab consumes the amount of memory based on the number of nodes and properties that prefab contains. When you instantiate a node prefab, Kanzi creates nodes and assigns properties to those nodes. You can calculate how much memory prefab instances consume by multiplying the number of instances with the memory requirements of a single prefab instance.
When you attach a node to the node tree, resources used by the nodes are looked up and requested from the resource manager. Resource manager loads or returns existing resources if they are already loaded.
When you detach a node prefab instance, Kanzi does not release resources used in the nodes you detached. This is a performance optimization, which allows you to change the parent node of the prefab, or move a prefab in the node tree, without having to load again the resources the prefab uses. When you want to release all resources which are no longer in use, call `ResourceManager::purge[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13998.html#ada106a4cfa891d8cbe13f104db826f85)`.
Kanzi assumes that all the nodes that you place in the node tree are going to be used. Kanzi optimizes for the case that all the content put in the node tree is ready for immediate use. If a node is not supposed to be used, remove it from the node tree.

content:
##  Prefab Placeholder and Prefab View nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#prefab-placeholder-and-prefab-view-nodes "Link to this heading")
You can use both Prefab Placeholder and Prefab View nodes to instantiate a node prefab in your project. The difference between these nodes is:
  * When you instantiate a node prefab with a Prefab Placeholder node, Kanzi reads the value of the Prefab Template property once and replaces the Prefab Placeholder node with the prefab to which that property points.
For example, if you use a Prefab Placeholder 2D node to instantiate a node prefab which contains a Button 2D node, when Kanzi instantiates the node prefab, it replaces the Prefab Placeholder 2D node with the root node of the Button 2D prefab.
  * When you instantiate a node prefab with a Prefab View node, Kanzi monitors the value of the Prefab Template property and adds the prefab to which that property points as a child node of the Prefab View node. This allows you to change the prefab that the Prefab View instantiates and to keep your application responsive when it is loading resources. See [Loading node prefab resources asynchronously](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#loading-node-prefab-resources-asynchronously).
For example, if you use a Prefab View 2D node to instantiate a node prefab which contains a Button 2D node, when Kanzi instantiates the prefab, it adds the root node of the Button 2D node as a child node of the Prefab View 2D node.


### When to use a Prefab Placeholder and when a Prefab View node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#when-to-use-a-prefab-placeholder-and-when-a-prefab-view-node "Link to this heading")
Use a Prefab Placeholder node to instantiate a node prefab which you do not intend to change during application runtime.
If you want to dynamically change a prefab, or want to asynchronously load the resources which the prefab uses, use a Prefab View to instantiate a prefab. For example, when you theme your application and want to use different prefabs for different themes, use a Prefab View node to instantiate those prefabs.
Kanzi reads the value of the Prefab Template property of a Prefab Placeholder once, but a Prefab View node monitors for changes the value of the Prefab Template property. When the value of the Prefab Template property in a Prefab View changes, Kanzi replaces its child node with the new child node.

## Creating and using a node prefab[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#creating-and-using-a-node-prefab "Link to this heading")
To create and use a node prefab:
  1. In the Prefabs click ![create-prefab](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-prefab.png) and select the prefab you want to create.
For example, create a Button 2D prefab, and add an Image and a Text Block 2D node to it.
![../../_images/reuse-create-prefab.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reuse-create-prefab.png)
  2. To instantiate the prefab in your application:
     * From the Prefabs drag the prefab you created to the Node Tree and drop it on the node where you want to use that prefab.
Kanzi Studio creates a Prefab Placeholder node which instantiates the prefab in your project.
![../../_images/reuse-instantiate-prefabs.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reuse-instantiate-prefabs.png) ![../../_images/button-prefab-placeholder-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-prefab-placeholder-in-project.png)
To instantiate a different prefab, in the Node Tree select the prefab you want to change, and in the Properties set the Prefab Template property to the prefab you want to instantiate.
![../../_images/reuse-instantiate-prefabs-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reuse-instantiate-prefabs-properties.png)
     * In the Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click the node where you want to instantiate the prefab, select Prefab View, and in the Properties set the Prefab Template property to the prefab you want to instantiate.
![../../_images/reuse-instantiate-prefabs-prefab-view.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reuse-instantiate-prefabs-prefab-view.png) ![../../_images/reuse-instantiate-prefabs-prefab-view-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reuse-instantiate-prefabs-prefab-view-properties.png)

content:
## Customizing instances of a node prefab[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#customizing-instances-of-a-node-prefab "Link to this heading")
A node prefab can contain a tree of nodes, each with their own properties. When you edit the nodes in a prefab or any of its instances in a project, you change those nodes in all instances of that prefab. You can customize each instance of a prefab to have its own property values by overriding the property values of the prefab. For example, when you create a prefab for an address book entry, you want to show a different name, number, and photo for each address book entry.
To customize instances of a node prefab:
  1. In the Prefabs select the node in a prefab that you want to customize in an instance of that prefab.
For example, to use a different texture for each instance of a prefab, select an Image node.
![../../_images/reuse-edit-prefab-structure.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reuse-edit-prefab-structure.png)
  2. In the Properties, next to the property that you want to customize, click ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/enable-editing-of-this-property.png).
Kanzi Studio creates from that property a custom property, adds it to the root node of that prefab, and creates a `##Template` binding to the property in the root node of that prefab.
See [Prefab root bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/reference-for-bindings-expressions.html#prefab-root-bindings).
For example, to customize the texture that you want to show in different instances of that prefab, click ![image1](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/enable-editing-of-this-property.png) next to the Image property. Kanzi Studio creates a custom Image property, adds it to the root node of that node prefab, and creates in the Image node a `##Template` binding to the custom Image property in the root node of that node prefab.
![../../_images/reuse-edit-prefab-publish.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reuse-edit-prefab-publish.png) ![../../_images/reuse-edit-prefab-root-binding.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reuse-edit-prefab-root-binding.png)
  3. In the Node Tree select the root node of the prefab instance that you want to customize.
![../../_images/reuse-edit-prefab-prefab-instance.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reuse-edit-prefab-prefab-instance.png)
  4. In the Properties click ![image2](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-property.png) next to the property that you customized and set the value of the property.
Only this instance of the prefab uses the value that you set.
![../../_images/reuse-edit-prefab-add-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reuse-edit-prefab-add-property.png) ![../../_images/reuse-edit-prefab-property-added.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/reuse-edit-prefab-property-added.png)

content:
## Loading node prefab resources asynchronously[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#loading-node-prefab-resources-asynchronously "Link to this heading")
When you load prefab resources asynchronously, Kanzi uses separate threads to load resources. When Kanzi finishes loading the resources, it deploys them using the main thread. That way your application stays responsive while it loads resources. To load resources asynchronously from several prefabs, see [Tutorial: Load and deploy resources asynchronously](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/loading/loading.html).
Use resource profiling to measure during runtime how long it takes to load and deploy resources and prefabs in your Kanzi application.
Resource profiling data helps you find out which resources to load asynchronously.
See [Measuring the loading and deployment time of resources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/performance-profiling/resource-profiling.html).
To load node prefab resources asynchronously:
  1. Create the content that you want to show while Kanzi loads resources of a node prefab.
For example, to create a loading screen that you replace with the content of a prefab whose resources you load asynchronously, from the Asset Packages > Factory Content drag the Processing Indicator and drop it on the Prefabs window.
![../../_images/processing-indicator-asset.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/processing-indicator-asset.png) ![../../_images/processing-indicator-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/processing-indicator-project.png)
  2. Create a node prefab whose resources you want to load asynchronously.
For example, in the Prefabs create a Stack Layout 2D and add to it several Image nodes each of which points to a different image.
![../../_images/async-load-content.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/async-load-content.png)
  3. In the Node Tree, create a Prefab View node where you want to asynchronously load prefab resources. In the Properties, set the Prefab Template property to the content that you want to show while Kanzi loads the resources of the prefab that you created in the previous step.
For example, set the Prefab Template property to the Processing Indicator prefab.
![../../_images/prefab-view-2d-processing-indicator.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/prefab-view-2d-processing-indicator.png) ![../../_images/prefab-view-2d-displayed-prefab.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/prefab-view-2d-displayed-prefab.png)
  4. In the Node Tree, select the Prefab View node. In the Node Components, press `Alt` and right-click Triggers and select the trigger that you want to use to start loading prefab resources.
For example, add the On Attached trigger to start loading resources when Kanzi attaches the Prefab View node to the screen graph.
![../../_images/add-on-attached.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-on-attached.png)

content:
For example, add the On Attached trigger to start loading resources when Kanzi attaches the Prefab View node to the screen graph.
![../../_images/add-on-attached.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-on-attached.png)
  5. In the Node Components, press `Alt` and right-click the trigger that you added in the previous step, and select Dispatch Message Action > Prefab View > Start Asynchronous Load.
![../../_images/on-attached-trigger-start-async-load-action.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/on-attached-trigger-start-async-load-action.png)
  6. In the Start Asynchronous Load action, set the Prefab Template property to a prefab or a resource ID that points to a prefab whose resources you want to load asynchronously.
![../../_images/start-async-load-action-settings.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/start-async-load-action-settings.png)
  7. To define what happens when Kanzi finishes loading the resources:
    1. In the Node Tree, select the Prefab View node. In the Node Components, press `Alt` and right-click Triggers and select Message Trigger > Prefab View > Asynchronous Load Completed.
![../../_images/prefab-view-2d-processing-indicator.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/prefab-view-2d-processing-indicator.png) ![../../_images/add-asynchronous-load-completed-trigger.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-asynchronous-load-completed-trigger.png)
    2. In the Node Components > Triggers, press `Alt` and right-click the Asynchronous Load Completed trigger and select an action.
For example, select the Dispatch Message Action > Activity Host > Activate Activity action and set:
       * Target Item to the Activity Host node that contains the Activity that you want to activate
       * Activity Activation Path to the Activity that you want to activate when Kanzi finishes loading the resources
![../../_images/asynchronous-load-completed-add-navigate-to-page-action.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/asynchronous-load-completed-add-navigate-to-page-action.png) ![../../_images/navigation-request-for-asynchronous-load-completed.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/navigation-request-for-asynchronous-load-completed.png)
  8. Select File > Export > Export as KZB Player for Windows and open the application exe file in the `<ProjectName>/Tool_project/Application Player` directory.
Because the Kanzi Studio Preview loads all resources in the project when it starts, to see the effect of loading resources asynchronously, either:
     * Export the project as a kzb file Player
     * Export the project kzb file and run the application from the project Visual Studio solution
![../../_images/export-as-kzb-player-for-windows.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/export-as-kzb-player-for-windows.png)

content:
## Replacing the root node of a node prefab[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#replacing-the-root-node-of-a-node-prefab "Link to this heading")
Replace the root node of a prefab when you want to add or change the node that is used as the parent node of a prefab. For example, if you first created a prefab that has a Grid Layout 3D as its root, but now you want to place that Grid Layout 3D into a Stack Layout 3D, you need to replace the root node of that prefab.
To replace the root of a node prefab:
  1. In the Prefabs press `Alt` and right-click the root of the prefab you want to replace and select Empty Node From Items.
Kanzi Studio replaces the current root of the prefab with an Empty Node node and places the entire prefab inside that empty node. For 3D prefabs Kanzi Studio creates an Empty Node 3D node, for 2D prefabs it creates an Empty Node 2D node.
![../../_images/change-root-of-prefab---before.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/change-root-of-prefab---before.png) ![../../_images/change-root-of-prefab---empty-node-root.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/change-root-of-prefab---empty-node-root.png)
  2. In the Prefabs create the node you want to use as the new root node of the prefab.
For example, create a Stack Layout 3D.
![../../_images/change-root-of-prefab---new-root-node.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/change-root-of-prefab---new-root-node.png)
  3. Drag and drop the old prefab from the Empty Node node root to the new root node you created in the previous step.
![../../_images/change-root-of-prefab---after.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/change-root-of-prefab---after.png)


## Using the Prefab View 3D node in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#using-the-prefab-view-3d-node-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
To use a Prefab view 3D node, create a prefab with 3D content and set it using setPrefab():

```
// Create a Prefab view 3D and add it to the scene.
PrefabView3DSharedPtr prefabView3D = PrefabView3D::create(domain, "Prefab view");
scene->addChild(prefabView3D);

// Acquire prefab from resource manager.
PrefabTemplateSharedPtr prefabTemplate = resourceManager->acquireResource<PrefabTemplate>("kzb://my_project/Prefabs/My3DPrefab");

// Use the prefab in the PrefabView3D node.
prefabView3D->setPrefab(prefabTemplate);

```
Copy to clipboard
For details, see the `PrefabView3D[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a18798.html)` class.

Kanzi shows in real-time the changes that you make in your Kanzi Studio project:
  * The Preview window shows the content of the currently open Kanzi application. For example, the Preview in this image shows the Kanzi application you can create by completing the [Tutorial: Create gauges](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/gauges/gauges.html).
![../../_images/start4.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/start4.png)
Note
The Kanzi Studio Preview by default uses the TCP/IP for internal communication with Kanzi Studio. If you have a firewall installed on your computer, allow the `Kanzi Preview` process to go through the firewall.
Tip
When you are working with large content, such as 4K textures, the Preview cannot process the data in-memory and can terminate during startup with an out-of-memory error. To enable the Preview to start, in Edit > User Preferences > Advanced tab enable the Export initial Preview data to hard drive setting.
You can estimate whether enabling this setting is necessary by exporting the kzb file of your project. If the size of the kzb file is larger than 300 MB, enable the setting.
By enabling this setting, the Preview loads the initial data to the hard drive, instead of the memory. Enable this setting only when your are working with Kanzi Studio projects where the memory transfer exceeds the 32-bit memory limit of the Preview. When this setting is enabled, the Preview takes longer time to load your projects and start because a hard drive is slower than memory.
  * The Target Preview enables you to see on a target device the changes that you make in a Kanzi Studio project without exporting and redeploying the application.
These are the impacts of Target Preview on development workflow:
    * It shows your application as it is, including the rendering and latency, and any behavior that you define in platform-specific code. The content that the Target Preview shows is not a video stream.

These are the impacts of Target Preview on development workflow:
    * It shows your application as it is, including the rendering and latency, and any behavior that you define in platform-specific code. The content that the Target Preview shows is not a video stream.
    * The Target Preview enables you to revise your design even in late stages of the development. You can instantly test designs and see how your changes look in a real environment, such as on a display inside a vehicle.
    * When you develop an Android application using the Kanzi Android framework (droidfw), you can see full composited application that consists of both Kanzi and Android UI.
See [Target Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/using-target-preview.html).

When Kanzi Studio loads a project, it shows in the Preview your project as if it was run as an application on a target device. You can control the Preview from the Project menu or use the shortcut keys.
![../../_images/preview-menu-preview-controls.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-menu-preview-controls.png)  
| Shortcut key  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| `F5`  | Start the Preview in paused mode.  |  
| `F6`  | Start playing the Preview.  |  
| `F7`  | Pause the Preview.  |  
| `F8`  | Exit the Preview.  |  
| `F9`  | Stop the Preview.  |  
| `Ctrl` `F5`  |  Start the Preview in play mode. This is the default Preview setting when you open a Kanzi Studio project. To change this setting, go to Edit > User Preferences > Advanced > Preview.  |  
| `Ctrl` `F8`  | Restart the Preview.  |  
## Controlling keyboard input in the Preview[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/controlling-your-application-in-the-preview.html#controlling-keyboard-input-in-the-preview "Link to this heading")
To control how the Preview handles keyboard input, when the Preview has focus and is in the Interact mode ![interact-mode](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/interact.png), in the Preview click ![keyboard-input](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/keyboard-input.png).
For example, to set the Preview to pass to a Text Box node keyboard input also from the keys and key combinations that are reserved as Kanzi Studio shortcuts, enable the Keyboard Input mode.
![../../_images/keyboard-input-enabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/keyboard-input-enabled.png)

## Setting the font engine for the Preview[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/controlling-your-application-in-the-preview.html#setting-the-font-engine-for-the-preview "Link to this heading")
You can set which font engine you want the Kanzi Studio Preview to use to render the text in your application.
To set the font engine for the Preview:
  1. In the main menu select Project > Properties.
![../../_images/project-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties.png)
  2. In the Properties set the Font Engine property:
     * FreeType uses the FreeType rasterizer, HarfBuzz shaper, and ICU bidirectional library, and libunibreak for line breaking. This is the default font engine.
     * iType uses the Monotype iType rasterizer and WorldType® Shaper™ for shaping. See [Installing the iType font engine](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/controlling-your-application-in-the-preview.html#installing-the-itype-font-engine).
     * None to not load a font engine. When you do not load a font engine, the Preview does not render the text in your application.
![../../_images/font-engine.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/font-engine.png)


To learn how to set which font engine to load at application startup, see [FontEngine](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#fontengine).
## Installing the iType font engine[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/controlling-your-application-in-the-preview.html#installing-the-itype-font-engine "Link to this heading")
Submit the request for the Kanzi iType font engine through [support.rightware.com](http://support.rightware.com/).
To install the iType font engine for Kanzi Studio:
  1. Extract the zip file that contains the iType font engine Kanzi Engine plugin.
  2. Copy the dll file for each build configuration to the `<KanziInstallation>/Studio/Bin/EnginePlugins` directory.
For example, copy the `GL_vs<Version>_Release/kzitypeplugin.dll` to the `<KanziInstallation>/Studio/Bin/EnginePlugins/GL_vs<Version>_Release` directory.

## Setting the Graphics API for the Preview[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/controlling-your-application-in-the-preview.html#setting-the-graphics-api-for-the-preview "Link to this heading")
To set the Graphics API used by the Preview:
  1. In the main menu, select Project > Properties.
![../../_images/project-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties.png)
  2. In the Properties, set the Preview Graphics API Configuration property:
     * OpenGL is the default setting.
     * OpenGL ES creates an OpenGL ES context using the regular OpenGL driver. OpenGL ES differs from regular OpenGL in features such as depth mipmaps, color formats, texture compression, and shader language.
     * Vulkan is a newer graphics API that allows efficient usage of graphics card resources.
You can set the default value for all your Kanzi Studio projects in the Edit > User Preferences > Advanced, by setting Preview Graphics API Configuration.
![../../_images/preview-opengl-es.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-opengl-es.png)


## Setting the background color of the Preview[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/controlling-your-application-in-the-preview.html#setting-the-background-color-of-the-preview "Link to this heading")
The background of the Preview is by default black. To make your content stand out from the background when the Preview is in the Interact mode ![interact-mode](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/interact.png), you can set the background color:
  * For all your Kanzi Studio projects.
In the main menu, select Edit > User Preferences. In the Preview tab, set the Background Color property to the desired color.
![../../_images/edit-user-preferences.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/edit-user-preferences.png) ![../../_images/preview-background-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-background-color.png)
  * For a specific Kanzi Studio project.
In the main menu, select Project > Properties. In the Properties > Preview property category, add and set the Preview Background Color property to the desired color.
When you do not set this property, the project uses the color that you set in the User Preferences.
![../../_images/project-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties.png) ![../../_images/properties-project-preview-background-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-project-preview-background-color.png)

![../../_images/preview-with-background-color-set.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-with-background-color-set.png)

## Showing only the content of Page nodes and prefabs in the Preview[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/controlling-your-application-in-the-preview.html#showing-only-the-content-of-page-nodes-and-prefabs-in-the-preview "Link to this heading")
By default the Preview shows your entire Kanzi project as when it is run as an application on a target device. However, you can isolate parts of your application and view each as a separate item in the Preview. This means that you can work on the content of a prefab without instantiating the prefab.
  * To show only the content of a prefab in the Preview, in the Prefabs double-click that prefab.
Kanzi Studio opens the prefab in a new Preview tab and shows the content of that prefab in the Preview.
![../../_images/prefab-composition-open.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/prefab-composition-open.png)
  * To show only the content of a Page node, in the Node Tree or Pages double-click that page.
Kanzi Studio opens the Page node in a new tab and shows the content of that Page node in the Preview.
![../../_images/page-composition-open.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/page-composition-open.png)


When you isolate content in this way, in the Preview, you can control that part of your application in the Preview with the timeline controls you can find in the bottom of Kanzi Studio. To show the timeline, in the Kanzi Studio main menu select Window > Toolbar > Timeline.
![../../_images/timeline.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/timeline.svg)
The Preview shows prefabs in your application either in play or paused mode:
  * In the play mode the prefab functions just as it would as a standalone application: user interface components are interactive and animations are playing.
  * In the paused mode the animations stop, but the user interface components remain active. If components execute animations, these are not played until you enter the playing mode.


When the Preview is in paused mode, you can set the application time in the timeline bar.
You can use these playback modes in the Preview.  
| Playback mode  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/continuous-play.png)  | In the continuous play mode the Preview starts playing at start time you set in the timeline bar, but does not have a set end time.  |  
| ![image1](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/play-range.png)  | In the play range mode the Preview plays in a loop the range between the start and end times you set in the timeline bar.  |  
| ![image2](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/play-range-and-stop.png)  | In the play range and stop mode the Preview plays once the range between the start and end times you set in the timeline bar.  |

To move with the Free Camera, hold down the right mouse button and use these controls:
  * Move the mouse to tilt and rotate the camera angle in any direction.
  * Use `W`, `S`, `A`, and `D` to move the camera position forward, backward, left, and right.
  * Use `E` and `Q` to move the camera position up and down.
  * Scroll the mouse wheel to set the camera speed.
  * Hold down `Shift` to double the speed when moving.
  * Use `F` to bring the camera to the 3D object selected in the Preview

Tip To place:
  * A node to the position of the current view of the Camera in the Preview, in the Node Tree, right-click that node and select Align With View.
  * The Preview view to the location of any node, in the Node Tree, right-click that node and select Align View To Selected.

For example, to place a Camera node to the position of any node in a Scene node:
  1. Right-click the node to whose position you want to place a Camera node and select Align View To Selected.
  2. To store that position to the Camera, right-click the Camera and select Align With View.

## Panning and zooming in the Preview[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/editing-in-the-preview.html#panning-and-zooming-in-the-preview "Link to this heading")
To pan and zoom in the Preview:  
| Action  | Shortcut  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Pan  | Click and drag the middle mouse button.  |  
| Zoom  | 
  * Use the control in the upper right corner of the Preview: ![../../_images/adjust-the-preview-zoom-level.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/adjust-the-preview-zoom-level.png)
  * Scroll the mouse wheel.
  * Press the `Shift` and `Alt` keys, and click and drag the left mouse button.

 |  
## Resetting the view in the Preview[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/editing-in-the-preview.html#resetting-the-view-in-the-preview "Link to this heading")
When you want to return the Preview zoom level to 100% and position your application screen in the center of the Preview, click ![image32](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/zoom.png) or press `Ctrl` `1` to reset the view in the Preview.

## Taking a screenshot of the Preview[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/editing-in-the-preview.html#taking-a-screenshot-of-the-preview "Link to this heading")
Use the the Screenshot button ![image33](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/screenshot-tool.png) to capture the current view of your application as it appears in the Preview. This is useful for product verification, documentation or to use as project thumbnail for example.
In the User Preferences > Advanced tab, set:
  * The Default Screenshot location where screenshots are saved.
  * The Screenshot background options which controls how the background of the image is filled.
    * Without Background takes the screenshot with a transparent background.
    * With Screen Clear Color takes the screenshot with the Screen Clear Color as background.
![../../_images/preview-screenshot-user-preferences.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-screenshot-user-preferences.png)
Note
The Screenshot background options only take effect if the Background Brush and Foreground Brush properties are set to NullBrush and No Brush. If not, the screenshot background will be filled using the Background Brush defined in the Brush property of the node.
  * To take a screenshot of the current view in the Preview window, click the Screenshot ![image33](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/screenshot-tool.png) button.
![../../_images/preview-screenshot-button.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-screenshot-button.png)
A message in the Status Bar indicates that the screenshot was taken successfully. The image is saved in the location you set in the User Preferences, as a `png` file with the project name and date-time stamp as the name.

## Setting anti-aliasing in the Preview[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/editing-in-the-preview.html#setting-anti-aliasing-in-the-preview "Link to this heading")
By default, the Kanzi Studio Preview and the Kanzi Application Player on Windows apply anti-aliasing using 4 samples. For both, you can configure the amount of anti-aliasing that you want to use.
If you have a Kanzi application with a C++ application, to see your content in the Kanzi Studio Preview and Kanzi Application Player the same way as when running your Kanzi application on a target device, you can set anti-aliasing in an `application.cfg` file. See [Applying anti-aliasing to an entire application](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/anti-aliasing.html#applying-anti-aliasing-to-an-entire-application).
To set anti-aliasing in the Kanzi Studio Preview for a Kanzi application without a C++ application:
  1. In the Kanzi Studio main menu, select Project > Properties. In the Properties in the Preview section, set the value of the Preview Working Directory property to the directory where you want to store the `application.cfg` to configure the Preview.
For example, set the Preview Working Directory property to `Application Player`. This way, you can apply the same anti-aliasing setting to the Preview and the Kanzi Application Player on Windows. If the `<ProjectName>/Application Player` directory does not yet exist, select File > Export > Export as KZB Player for Windows. See [Building and deploying Kanzi applications to Windows from Kanzi Studio](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/deploying-applications/deploying-kanzi-applications-for-windows.html#building-and-deploying-kanzi-applications-to-windows-from-kanzi-studio).
![../../_images/project-properties-myproject.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties-myproject.png) ![../../_images/preview-working-dir-application-player.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-working-dir-application-player.png)
  2. In the directory that you set in the previous step, create or open the `application.cfg` file. Add and set the `SurfaceSamplesAntialiasing` parameter to the number of anti-aliasing samples that you want the Preview to use.
For example, to disable anti-aliasing in the Preview, in the `application.cfg`, add:

```
SurfaceSamplesAntialiasing = 0

```
Copy to clipboard
  3. In Kanzi Studio, restart the Preview.
![../../_images/preview-restart-button-gray.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-restart-button-gray.png)

## Performance[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/debugging-in-the-preview.html#performance "Link to this heading")
  * Performance HUD shows the overall performance indicators of your Kanzi application during the last 500 frames including:
    * Frame Duration (ms) shows the time in milliseconds it took to render the last frame, and the average, highest, and lowest times.
The top value in the Frame Duration (ms) graph shows the longest, and the bottom value the average time it took to render a frame during the last 500 frames.
Use this information to identify performance bottlenecks in your Kanzi application. For example, you can use it to find out how to improve the performance of your application by distributing rendering across several frames. See [Distributing rendering across several frames](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/distributing-rendering.html).
    * API shows the rendering API used by Kanzi. For Example, OpenGL ES or Vulkan. It also shows an identifier of the video card and driver version.
![../../_images/frame-duration-graph.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/frame-duration-graph.png)
    * Frames Per Second shows the number of frames rendered per second.
    * Animation Duration (μs) shows the time in microseconds it takes to execute all animations in the application for the last frame, and the average, highest, and lowest times.
    * Draw Count shows how many individual draw calls were executed.
The top value in the Draw Count graph shows the highest number of batches during the last 500 frames, and the bottom value the number of batches in the last frame.
![../../_images/draw-count-graph.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/draw-count-graph.png)
    * Triangle Count shows an estimated total of individual triangles drawn during a frame.
    * Pipeline Count shows how many times a new render pipeline was bound for the last frame. See [Reducing shader switches](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/shaders/reducing-shader-switches.html).
    * Pass Count shows how many render passes were used in the last frame. See [Rendering best practices](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/rendering-best-practices.html).
    * Memory Upload shows how many bytes of rolling staging memory were used on the last frame as well as the total buffer size. Staging memory contains uniform data and temporary storage used for updating GPU resources like vertex buffers or textures. On some platforms unique buffers are used for each type of data.
    * Dispatch Count shows how many compute dispatches were used in the last frame.
    * Kanzi Graphics Objects shows a summary of the created Kanzi Graphics objects. In parenthesis is the number of created and deleted objects in the last frame.
    * View Camera shows the name of the Camera node that is used for displaying the scene in your application.

metadata.title: Analyzing your application in the Preview (Part 4/6)

content:
* Kanzi Graphics Objects shows a summary of the created Kanzi Graphics objects. In parenthesis is the number of created and deleted objects in the last frame.
    * View Camera shows the name of the Camera node that is used for displaying the scene in your application.
    * Resource Memory Use shows an estimated amount of local GPU memory (VRAM) and non-local GPU memory (RAM) that your Kanzi application uses.
The values that the Performance HUD shows in the Kanzi Studio Preview and when you run the Kanzi application on a target device differ because Kanzi Studio loads and keeps in memory all resources in the application.
    * Timers shows the number of registered timer handlers in the `MainLoopScheduler[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13618.html)`. Too many timer handlers can decrease the performance of your application. See [Adding timers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/application-configuration.html#adding-timers).
You can access the number of timer subscriptions in the Kanzi Engine API by calling `MainLoopScheduler::getTimersCount[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13618.html#adb14c61cae8da0bafd9075ce9bbe843c)`.
    * Recurring Tasks shows the total number of tasks that were added to the stages in the main loop scheduler. The Kanzi Engine adds some tasks by default. See [Adding recurring tasks](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/application-configuration.html#adding-recurring-tasks).
You can access the number of recurring tasks in the Kanzi Engine API by calling `MainLoopScheduler::getTasksTotalCount[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13618.html#ad2f01ce01e69e3a92f0046a65ba050ee)`.
    * Animations shows the number of active and all animations in your Kanzi application.
You can access the number of animations in the Kanzi Engine API:
      * To get the number of active animations, use `TimelineClock::getActiveTimelinePlaybackCount[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11342.html#a0e214a8ff26ac6d9f508fcd6ef0f3029)`.
      * To get the number of all animations, use `TimelineClock::getTimelinePlaybackCount[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11342.html#a5bb2a2aec4b32baeb21c134faab6c998)`.
  * Frame time HUD shows these frame time indicators of your Kanzi application during the last 500 frames:
    * Frame Duration (ms) shows the time in milliseconds it took to render the last frame, and the average, highest, and lowest times.
    * Frames Per Second shows the number of frames rendered per second.
    * Animation Duration (μs) shows the time in microseconds it takes to execute all animations in the application for the last frame, and the average, highest, and lowest times.

## The Preview log file[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/debugging-in-the-preview.html#the-preview-log-file "Link to this heading")
Kanzi Studio stores the Preview log messages in the `%USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\Temp\KanziStudioLogs\KanziPreview.log` file.
To set the level of logging detail, in the `<KanziInstallation>\Studio\Bin\KanziPreview.exe.config` file set the value of the `logLevel` key:
  * `NORMAL` sets Kanzi Studio to log the regular Kanzi Studio Preview flow, including errors and exceptions.
  * `VERBOSE` sets Kanzi Studio to log all low-level communication between Kanzi Studio and the Preview at a millisecond-level of precision.
When you set the log level to `VERBOSE`, the large amount of log messages can reduce the performance of Kanzi Studio.
  * `NONE` sets Kanzi Studio to not log any messages to the `KanziPreview.log` file.


For example, to log all communication between Kanzi Studio and the Preview, open the `KanziPreview.exe.config` file in a text editor, and set:

```
<add key="logLevel" value="VERBOSE"/>

```
Copy to clipboard
To apply the changes to the `KanziPreview.exe.config`, save the `KanziPreview.exe.config` file and press `Ctrl` `F8` to restart the Preview. See [Controlling the Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/controlling-your-application-in-the-preview.html).
Every time you restart the Preview, Kanzi Studio overwrites the contents of the `KanziPreview.log` file.

Rulers and guides help you position the elements in your application.
To use rulers and guides, in the Preview:
  1. Select the Node tool ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tool.png).
  2. Click ![image1](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/analyze-off.png) to enter the Analyze mode.
  3. Right-click ![image2](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/analyze-on.png), and select Rulers and guides.

![../../_images/visualize-rulers-and-guides.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/visualize-rulers-and-guides.png)
## Adding a guide[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/using-rulers-and-guides.html#adding-a-guide "Link to this heading")
To add a guide, in the Preview select the Node tool ![image3](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tool.png) and drag a ruler to the preview area. Drag from the horizontal ruler to add a horizontal guide, and from the vertical ruler to add a vertical guide.
Tip
Use the Snap tool to snap an element in your application to a guide. To enable snapping, in the Node Tree select a 2D node, in the Preview select the Node tool ![image4](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tool.png) , and select ![image5](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/toggle-snap.png). When you move 2D node in your application, it snaps to the nearest guide.
![../../_images/add-guide.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-guide.gif) ![../../_images/horizontal-and-vertical-guide.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/horizontal-and-vertical-guide.png)
## Moving a guide[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/using-rulers-and-guides.html#moving-a-guide "Link to this heading")
To move a guide, in the Preview select the Node tool ![image7](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tool.png) and drag the guide you want to move.

The Target Preview enables you to see on a target device the changes that you make in a Kanzi Studio project without exporting and redeploying the application.
These are the impacts of Target Preview on development workflow:
  * It shows your application as it is, including the rendering and latency, and any behavior that you define in platform-specific code. The content that the Target Preview shows is not a video stream.
  * The Target Preview enables you to revise your design even in late stages of the development. You can instantly test designs and see how your changes look in a real environment, such as on a display inside a vehicle.
  * When you develop an Android application using the Kanzi Android framework (droidfw), you can see full composited application that consists of both Kanzi and Android UI.


The Target Preview plugin creates a TCP/IP communication channel so that Kanzi Studio can make changes to an application on a connected device. It does not replace the deployment process, but it improves the workflow by allowing you to see the changes on a target device without redeploying an application.
![../../_images/target-preview-android.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/target-preview-android.gif)
Keep in mind that:
  * If your Kanzi Studio project uses a Kanzi Engine plugin, you must add the same plugin to the Kanzi application and redeploy the application to your target device.
  * The changes that you make in the Target Preview are not saved on the target device. To make the changes permanent, follow the regular application deployment process. See [Deploying Kanzi applications](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/deploying-applications/deploying-kanzi-applications.html).

## Using the Target Preview[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/using-target-preview.html#using-the-target-preview "Link to this heading")
The Target Preview is a Kanzi Engine plugin that is delivered with the Kanzi platform packages.
It is meant to be used only as a tool to help you develop your Kanzi application. To get your application ready for production, remove the link to the Target Preview plugin. This way you remove possible security issues that the plugin can introduce.
To use the Target Preview:
  1. Load the plugin:
     * For dynamically linked plugin, load the plugin by adding it to the `application.cfg`. See [ModuleNames](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#modulenames).

```
ModuleNames="kztargetpreview"

```
Copy to clipboard
     * For statically linked plugin, register the plugin in your application code:

```
#include <kanzi/plugins/targetpreview/targetpreview_plugin.hpp>

void MyApplication::registerMetadataOverride(ObjectFactory& factory) override
{
      TargetPreviewPlugin::registerModule(getDomain());
}

```
Copy to clipboard
  2. For statically linked plugin, and dynamically linked plugin on Android or QNX with the LLVM C++ compiler, link the plugin in the application `CMakeLists.txt`:

```
target_link_libraries(MyApplication Kanzi::kztargetpreview)

```
Copy to clipboard
See [Kanzi Engine plugins](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/plugins-kanzi-engine.html).
  3. (Optional) By default, the Target Preview plugin uses network port `50000`. To set a different port, in the `target_preview_configuration.json` file, set the `port` attribute.

```
{
   "port": 60000
}

```
Copy to clipboard
  4. If you use the Target Preview with an application on Android:
     * Add these network permissions to the `AndroidManifest.xml` file of your application:

```
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.INTERNET" />
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE" />

```
Copy to clipboard
     * For an Android emulator, or device connected through ADB:
       1. Use the 127.0.0.1 address. This address on your computer corresponds to the ADB loopback interface.
       2. Set up port forwarding to the default port or the port that you defined.

```
adb forward tcp:<port> tcp:<port>

```
adb forward tcp:<port> tcp:<port>

```
Copy to clipboard
  5. Before you start using the Target Preview, export the kzb and make sure that on the target device you use the same kzb and set of Kanzi Engine plugins.
  6. In Kanzi Studio, connect to the application on your device:
    1. In the Kanzi Studio Preview, click ![target-preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/target-preview-connect-from-preview.png).
![../../_images/preview-target-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-target-preview.png)
    2. In the Target Preview window, set:
       * Target IP to the IP address of your device
       * Port to the port that you set earlier
The Target Preview uses TCP/IP to communicate with Kanzi Studio. If you use a firewall, allow your Kanzi application to accept incoming network connection at specified port.
![../../_images/target-preview-connection-settings.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/target-preview-connection-settings.png)
    3. Click Connect.
Kanzi Studio prints the connection status in the Log window.
![../../_images/target-preview-log-window.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/target-preview-log-window.png)

Prism graph editor is a visual node tool for creating render graphs. You can add or remove rendering nodes and quickly iterate on visual effects. Graphs provide a clear overview of rendering operations, let you adjust properties, and show results instantly.
Prism simplifies rendering complexities into a handful of basic primitive operations. A typical graph consists of one or more draw operations, shadow rendering operations, and post-processing effect compositions.
A Prism graph consists of nodes such as Draw, Blit, Clear and other more advanced nodes. Nodes are linked together using connections to form a render pipeline, where each operation runs according to the graph structure. Every graph has an output node that displays the final result on screen.
See [Creating Prism graphs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/creating-graphs.html) for a walkthrough on creating a Prism graph.

## Prism graph presets[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#prism-graph-presets "Link to this heading")
Prism offers quick presets to get started when you create a new graph. You can find the available presets when you create a new graph. Go to **Library** > **Prism Graphs** , right-click on **Prism Graphs** , and select **Create** > **Template**.
![../../_images/create-empty-prism-graph.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-empty-prism-graph.png)
### Default Prism Graph[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#default-prism-graph "Link to this heading")
![../../_images/default-graph.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/default-graph.png)
A preset configuration for a render graph similar to Kanzi’s default render pass. The preset draws opaque and transparent objects.
This is a good general starting point to start customizing your rendering.
### Empty Prism Graph[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#empty-prism-graph "Link to this heading")
![../../_images/empty-graph.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/empty-graph.png)
Empty Prism graph only has an output node. By default, this graph doesn’t render anything.
### Offscreen Buffer Prism Graph[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#offscreen-buffer-prism-graph "Link to this heading")
![../../_images/offscreen-framebuffer-graph.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/offscreen-framebuffer-graph.png)
A preset tailored for quickly starting with offscreen or post-processing effects. The graph renders objects to screen and then composites a full-screen shader using blit nodes.
This is a good starting point for building post-processing or offscreen rendering effects where you want to apply a shader to all pixels on screen.
## Navigating the Prism editor[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#navigating-the-prism-editor "Link to this heading")  
| Action  | Shortcut  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Select  | Left-click a node or connection  |  
| Pan  | Middle mouse button  |  
| Zoom  | Mouse wheel  |

## Working with Prism graphs[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#working-with-prism-graphs "Link to this heading")
Here are the most common operations for editing Prism graphs.
### Creating nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#creating-nodes "Link to this heading")
**Right-click** in the graph and select a node type.
![../../_images/creating-prism-nodes.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/creating-prism-nodes.gif)
### Deleting nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#deleting-nodes "Link to this heading")
Select a node and press `Delete`.
Or **right-click** and select **Delete**.
![../../_images/deleting-nodes.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/deleting-nodes.gif)
### Connecting nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#connecting-nodes "Link to this heading")
Drag from a socket with the **left mouse button**. Release on a valid socket to connect.
![../../_images/connecting-prism-nodes.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/connecting-prism-nodes.gif)
### Disconnecting nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#disconnecting-nodes "Link to this heading")
Select a connection and press `Delete`.
Or right-click and select **Delete**.
![../../_images/disconnecting-prism-nodes.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/disconnecting-prism-nodes.gif)
To delete multiple connections, hold `Shift` + `Alt` and draw a line over the connections.
![../../_images/disconnecting-multiple-prism-nodes.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/disconnecting-multiple-prism-nodes.gif)
### Adding properties[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#adding-properties "Link to this heading")
Click the **+** icon on a node and select a property.
![../../_images/adding-properties.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/adding-properties.gif)
You can add multiple properties by clicking a property category.
![../../_images/adding-multiple-properties.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/adding-multiple-properties.gif)
Tip
Each Viewport that shares a Prism graph can override individual material property values independently. Select a property on a Prism node and click the Override value from Viewport button to set a per-Viewport value without affecting other Viewports that use the same graph.
![../../_images/prism-override-property.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/prism-override-property.gif)
### Removing properties[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#removing-properties "Link to this heading")
Right-click a property and select **Delete**.
![../../_images/deleting-properties.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/deleting-properties.gif)

### Removing properties[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#removing-properties "Link to this heading")
Right-click a property and select **Delete**.
![../../_images/deleting-properties.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/deleting-properties.gif)
### Adding and removing properties on a Render Pass node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#adding-and-removing-properties-on-a-render-pass-node "Link to this heading")
On a **Render Pass** node, click ![add-properties-window](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/open-add-properties-window.png) to open the Add Properties window. Use the window to add or remove any property the render pass supports.
### Binding Render Pass node properties[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#binding-render-pass-node-properties "Link to this heading")
You can bind a property on a Render Pass node so its value is driven by another property or by a binding expression. The following types of property bindings are supported:
  * **Resource property bindings.** Drag a binding line directly between two resource properties of the same type.
![Animation of dragging a binding line between two resource properties on different Prism nodes.](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/bind-toplevelas.gif)
  * **Text property bindings.** Right-click a non-resource property row and select Edit binding… to drive the property from a binding expression. The row then shows a binding indicator and a read-only preview of the expression.
![A Prism property row showing a binding indicator on the label and a read-only expression preview in place of the value editor.](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/clear-color-bound-row.gif)


See [Binding Render Pass node properties](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/using-prism-property-bindings.html) for worked examples.
### Minimap[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/prism-graphs.html#minimap "Link to this heading")
![../../_images/minimap.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/minimap.png)
![minimap_icon](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/minimap-toggle.png)
You can enable the minimap from the top-left corner of the Prism editor.
The minimap shows an overview of your graph. A light rectangle shows the visible area in the Prism Editor. Use the minimap to navigate large graphs.  
| Action  | Shortcut  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Resize  | Drag the lower-left corner of the minimap  |  
| Zoom  | Scroll the mouse wheel  |  
| Center view  | Click in the minimap  |  
| Pan  | Drag in the minimap  |

This tutorial guides you through building a basic render graph. You’ll learn how to create render graphs, add nodes, and connect nodes together to create a complete render graph.
## Creating an empty graph[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/creating-graphs.html#creating-an-empty-graph "Link to this heading")
Start by creating a new **Prism graph** :
  1. In the **Library** , find Rendering, right-click on Prism Graphs, and select **Create** > **Empty Prism Graph**.
![../../_images/create-empty-prism-graph.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-empty-prism-graph.png)
A new graph is created. The graph is not used for rendering yet. It has to be connected to a viewport.
  2. Select the viewport you want to render with the graph. In the **Properties** panel, go to Render Pass Prefab and select your graph from the dropdown list.
Your viewport will now stop rendering. **This is normal** because the render graph is currently empty. Rendering will be enabled in the following steps.
![../../_images/viewport-select.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/viewport-select.png) ![../../_images/property-view.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/property-view.png)

content:
## Add and connect nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/creating-graphs.html#add-and-connect-nodes "Link to this heading")
  1. Open your graph by double-clicking it in the **Library** folder.
The initial graph is empty and only contains an output node.
![../../_images/empty-prism-graph.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/empty-prism-graph.png)
Render graph is where you define how Kanzi renders each frame. The graph consists of nodes and connections between them. Nodes can be basic nodes, offscreen nodes, advanced nodes, or render pass nodes.
     * **Basic** nodes are primitive rendering operations: Draw, Clear, and Blit.
     * **Offscreen** nodes are render targets where drawing results are stored and used.
     * **Advanced** nodes are quick shortcuts to common rendering operations, such as adding shadows or rendering post-processing effects.
     * **Render Pass** nodes map directly to engine render pass types, giving you fine-grained control over the rendering pipeline. Examples include Build Acceleration Structure and Compute.
In this tutorial, we’ll cover the basic nodes to learn the fundamentals first.
  2. To add a clear node, right-click anywhere on the graph and select **Add Node** > **Basic Node** > **Clear**.
  3. Similarly, add a draw node by selecting **Add Node** > **Basic Node** > **Draw**.
![../../_images/node-creation.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-creation.gif)
**Clear node** clears the target it is connected to. Often this is a draw node, where the first operation is to clear the previously rendered frame color or depth information.
**Draw node** renders objects to screen or into a render target.
All the required nodes are now there with no errors, but they are not rendering anything on the screen yet. The next step is to make connections to complete the graph.
Tip
Use the **Object Source** property to define which objects to draw.
![../../_images/select-object-source.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-object-source.png)
  4. Connect the clear node to the draw node, and the draw node to the output node by dragging connections from the node output socket.
![../../_images/node-connections.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-connections.gif)
Once the connections are done, your graph is now valid and complete. You should now see 3D objects being rendered in your preview window.

  1. Click the + icon below the clear node and add the **Clear Color 0** property to it.
![../../_images/add-color-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-color-property.png)
  2. Adjust the background color by adjusting the color property.
![../../_images/custom-graph-finished.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/custom-graph-finished.png)


Tip
Each Viewport that shares a Prism graph can override individual material property values independently. Select a property on a Prism node and click the Override value from Viewport button to set a per-Viewport value without affecting other Viewports that use the same graph.

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
These steps guide you through creating a Prism graph with Bloom and tonemap post-processing effects. Learn how to set up a scene with a 3D model, configure lighting for HDR rendering, and build a complete render graph with bloom effects.
## Import and Set Up the Car Model[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/creating-bloom-effect-and-post-processing.html#import-and-set-up-the-car-model "Link to this heading")
  1. Ensure you are working with Linear color flow. Find this setting in **Project** > **Properties** and **Binary Export** settings > **Color Workflow** and set it to **Linear** >
  2. Import your car model into the project:
     * In the **Asset Packages** window, right-click **Asset Toolkit** > **Car** and select **Import Asset Package**.
     * The Car will appear in your **Prefabs** window when the import completes.
![../../_images/assetpackages-import-car.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/assetpackages-import-car.png)
  3. Add the car model to your Scene:
     * Drag the imported model from the **Prefabs** into your Scene hierarchy.
![../../_images/add-car-to-scene.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-car-to-scene.gif)
     * Position the camera node or modify the Car model scaling and position in the **Preview** window.
![../../_images/car-properties.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/car-properties.gif)

metadata.title: Creating Bloom Effect with Prism Graphs (Part 1/6)
metadata.breadcrumb: Working with … > Prism graphs > Creating Bloom Effect with Prism Graphs

content:
## Configure Lighting for HDR[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prism-graphs/creating-bloom-effect-and-post-processing.html#configure-lighting-for-hdr "Link to this heading")
For bloom effects to work properly, your materials should support the Emissive Factor property, which allows producing colors in the HDR range. The Asset Toolkit Car model supports this by default
  1. Select the light materials in your Scene. In the **Library** , expand the **Material Types** and navigate to **PhysicallyBased** > **PBR BrakeLight** for example
  2. Select the **PBR BrakeLight** material and in the **Properties** panel, adjust the **Emissive Factor** property.
![../../_images/adjust-emissive-factor.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/adjust-emissive-factor.gif)
Tip
Emissive Factor Intensity values greater than 0.0 produce HDR colors that will enhance the bloom effect. The higher the value, the stronger the bloom effect.
  3. Set the Emissive Factor Intensity to a grater value (for example, 7.0 ) to create bright areas that will bloom.
  4. Apply a high **Emissive Factor** property value to all of the materials where you want to enhance the bloom effects (for example, the headlights, brake lights and turn signals). In the Car model from the **Asset Toolkit** , the **PhysicallyBased** materials **PBR BrakeLight** , **PBR HeadLight** and **PBR TurnLight** are used.
