Use a State Manager to create different states in your Kanzi application.
For example, you can define the appearance and behavior of a button during different states, such as how the button reacts when a user selects, presses, holds, or releases that button. Kanzi uses its animation system to animate the transitions between states. See [Animation system](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/kanzi-fundamentals/animation-system.html).
Each state manager consists:
  * **State groups.** State groups contain states, define controller properties, and transitions between states in a state group. A typical transition defines a period and interpolation paths between property values of two states. You can define transitions using a general guideline for all properties, using interpolations for each property as specified, or using animation items.
  * **States.** Each state contains a collection of properties that define the appearance and behavior of the node to which you assign the state manager. In each state group only one state can be active at a time. A state can also define interactions either by enabling or disabling controls input using the enabled property, setting the state as a condition for the trigger in trigger settings, or by explicitly defining triggers and actions for each state.
  * **State objects.** State objects define the properties of nodes for a specific state. For example, you can assign a state manager to a Button 2D node which contains a Model node that defines the look of the button. State object sets the properties of the mesh set in the Model node using the Target Object Path property. For example, ./Mesh.

metadata.title: State manager (Part 1/9)
metadata.breadcrumb: Working with … > State manager

content:
For example, a state manager for a button can contain three state groups: button pressed, button released, and hover over button. Each state group contains enabled and disabled states that through state objects define the appearance and behavior of the button when it is in one of the states, and the transition between the states.
You can define the changes between states in these ways:
  * Set a controller property for a state group and a value for that property for each state. These can be implicit properties, such as the Is Down property of the Button nodes. The state changes when the property changes, whether as part of the inherent logic of the node or a specified Set Property action or animation. See [Using a controller property to set states](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-state-managers.html#using-a-controller-property-to-set-states).
  * Using the State Manager actions Go to State, Next State, and Previous State. If you use the State Manager actions and a controller property, note that when the controller property changes, it overrides the previously set state. See [Using state manager actions to set states](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-state-managers.html#using-state-manager-actions-to-set-states).


Learn how to use state managers by completing one of these tutorials:
  * Create a toggle button. See [Tutorial: Creating a toggle button](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/toggle-button/toggle-button.html).
  * Create a button and control its state with the Is Down property. See [Tutorial: Creating a button](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/button/button.html).
  * Create a turn indicator and control it with a custom property. See [Tutorial: Create cluster indicators](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/indicator/indicator.html).

Use states to define the look and behavior of your Kanzi application in different states. For example, you can use states to:
  * Set the size of items in a layout to emphasize when an item is selected.
  * Show or hide parts of a user interface when the application is in a certain state.
  * Enable or disable controls, such as buttons, in your application based on the state of the application.
  * Animate your application.

metadata.title: Using state managers (Part 1/17)

content:
Properties set in states override the default, inherited, and local property values. See [Property precedence](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/kanzi-fundamentals/property-system.html#property-precedence).
Tip
In the Kanzi Studio Node Tree window, an indicator next to a node shows when a State Manager, Binding, Data Source Binding, or an Animation overrides the values of some properties in that node.
![../../_images/node-override-notice.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-override-notice.png)
To navigate to the source of the override in the Kanzi Studio project, right-click the override indicator and select the source you wish to navigate to from the context menu.
You can define the changes between states in these ways:
  * Set a controller property for a state group and a value for that property for each state. These can be implicit properties, such as the Is Down property of the Button nodes. The state changes when the property changes, whether as part of the inherent logic of the node or a specified Set Property action or animation. See [Using a controller property to set states](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-state-managers.html#using-a-controller-property-to-set-states).
  * Using the State Manager actions Go to State, Next State, and Previous State. If you use the State Manager actions and a controller property, note that when the controller property changes, it overrides the previously set state. See [Using state manager actions to set states](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-state-managers.html#using-state-manager-actions-to-set-states).


Learn how to use state managers by completing one of these tutorials:
  * Create a toggle button. See [Tutorial: Creating a toggle button](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/toggle-button/toggle-button.html).
  * Create a button and control its state with the Is Down property. See [Tutorial: Creating a button](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/button/button.html).
  * Create a turn indicator and control it with a custom property. See [Tutorial: Create cluster indicators](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/indicator/indicator.html).

content:
## Creating a state manager[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-state-managers.html#creating-a-state-manager "Link to this heading")
Use state managers in your Kanzi application to control the states of nodes.
For example, a state manager can define the states of a toggle button. The state manager sets how the toggle button looks when it is toggled on and off.
To create a state manager:
  1. In the Node Tree select the Toggle Button 2D node and in the State Tools click Create State Manager.
You can find the State Tools window below the Preview window.
Kanzi Studio creates a new state manager and assigns it to the Toggle Button 2D node.
![../../_images/create-state-manager2.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-state-manager2.png)
  2. In the State Tools, click Create State twice to create two states. Double-click the name of each state and rename the states.
For example, name one state On and the other Off.
The On state defines the state of your application when the toggle button is toggled on, the Off state when the toggle button is toggled off.
To delete a state, right-click the state and select Delete.
![../../_images/rename-states.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/rename-states.png)
  3. Use the State Tools to define in which position the indicator of a toggle button is in the on and off states:
    1. Position the toggle button indicator and in the State Tools click ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/store-current-values.png) below the On state to save the current position of the indicator to that state.
For example, in the Preview use the Node tool to position the indicator.
![../../_images/indicator-positioned.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/indicator-positioned.png) ![../../_images/add-indicator-to-on-state.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-indicator-to-on-state.png)
    2. Repeat the previous step for the Off state and in the State Tools save the current position of the toggle button indicator to that state.
![../../_images/indicatoroff-image.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/indicatoroff-image.png) ![../../_images/add-indicator-to-off-state.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-indicator-to-off-state.png)

Tip
In the Kanzi Studio Properties window, properties with its value is set by a State Manager are marked in blue type, and has the State Manager icon ![statemanager](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/state-manager-override.png) next to it:
![../../_images/state-manager-overrides-property-value.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/state-manager-overrides-property-value.png)
Orange type marks properties with several override sources:
![../../_images/property-value-invalid-override.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/property-value-invalid-override.png)
If a property has multiple override sources, only the one with the highest precedence will take effect. See [Property system](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/kanzi-fundamentals/property-system.html).

content:
## Using a controller property to set states[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-state-managers.html#using-a-controller-property-to-set-states "Link to this heading")
In a state manager, the value of the property that you select as the Controller Property defines the conditions when each state in a state group is active.
Each state group in a state manager can use a different controller property.
You can also use a custom property type as the controller property of a state group. See [Tutorial: Create cluster indicators](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/indicator/indicator.html).
To use a controller property:
  1. Create a state manager and set a node to use that state manager. See [Creating a state manager](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-state-managers.html#creating-a-state-manager).
For example, create a state manager that sets the appearance of a toggle button in two states.
  2. In the State Tools click the <No Controller Property> dropdown menu and select a property. To create a custom controller property, click the <No Controller Property> dropdown menu and select + Create Property Type.
For example, select the Toggle Button > Toggle State property. When you set the Toggle State as the controller property for the state manager that controls the states of a toggle button, the state manager transitions to a state based on the value of that property.
![../../_images/add-controller-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-controller-property.png)
  3. In the State Tools set the value of the controller property for each state.
For example:
     * For the On state set the value to 1.
     * For the Off state leave the value set to 0.
![../../_images/set-controller-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-controller-property.png)
  4. In the State Tools, click Edit State Manager to deactivate the State Tools.
![../../_images/deactivate-state-tools.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/deactivate-state-tools.png)


When you click the toggle button in the Preview you toggle between the On and Off states you defined in the state manager that you created in the Toggle Button 2D node.

## Using state manager actions to set states[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-state-managers.html#using-state-manager-actions-to-set-states "Link to this heading")
Use the State Manager actions to set your Kanzi application to enter different states.
To set the state in a state manager, you can use these actions:
  * Go to State action sets a state manager to the state that you define in the action.
See [Setting a state manager to a specific state](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-state-managers.html#setting-a-state-manager-to-a-specific-state).
  * Next State and Previous State actions set a state manager to the next and previous state in the state group that you define in the action. See [Setting a state manager to the next or previous state](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-state-managers.html#setting-a-state-manager-to-the-next-or-previous-state).

Use the Go to State action to set a state manager to a specific state.
To set a state manager to a specific state:
  1. Create the content the appearance or behavior of which you want to define in different states.
For example, use the Car from the Factory Content.
See [Using the Factory Content assets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/factory-content/using-the-factory-content-assets.html).

For example, create for the CameraRoot node a state manager with three states named Brakes, Roof, and Suspension, that each shows the car from a different angle. See [Using the Camera node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/cameras/creating-and-using-cameras-for-previews.html).

For example, create for the CameraRoot node a state manager with three states named Brakes, Roof, and Suspension, that each shows the car from a different angle. See [Using the Camera node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/cameras/creating-and-using-cameras-for-previews.html).

## Reacting when a node enters or leaves a state[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-state-managers.html#reacting-when-a-node-enters-or-leaves-a-state "Link to this heading")
When a node transitions between states, Kanzi:
  1. Unapplies the state that the node leaves and detaches the triggers of that state.
  2. Sends the `StateManager::LeftStateMessage[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a14522.html#ad310cbfd5b03507ca54a7fcb035a69a8)` message.
  3. Applies the state that the node enters and attaches the triggers of that state.
  4. Sends the `StateManager::EnteredStateMessage[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a14522.html#ad50ab1e7208d1293ea0bb5eccee80290)` message.

[![../../_images/state-manager-triggers.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/state-manager-triggers.svg)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/state-manager-triggers.svg)
To react when a node enters a state, you can use either the Entered State message trigger in the node or the On Attached trigger in the state that the node enters. To react when a node leaves a state, use the Left State message trigger in that node.
To react when a node enters or leaves a state:
  1. In the Node Tree select the node in which you want to react to entering or leaving a state, in the Node Components > Triggers add either:
     * Entered State message trigger to react when the node enters a state
     * Left State message trigger to react when the node leaves a state
For example:
    1. In the Node Tree select a Text Block 3D node which uses a state manager that has two states, State A and State B.
![../../_images/text-block-3d-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-block-3d-in-project.png)
    2. In the Node Components press `Alt` and right-click Triggers, and select Message Trigger > State Manager > Left State.
You use the Left State trigger to react when the Text Block 3D node leaves State A.
![../../_images/add-left-state-trigger.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-left-state-trigger.png)
  2. In the Node Components > Triggers press `Alt` and right-click the trigger that you added in the previous step, and select an action.
For example, select the Write Log action and set Log Text to the message that you want to write to the Log window when the trigger is set off. The Write Log action is useful when you want to verify that the node received the input.
To learn more about the Write Log action, see [Using Write Log action](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/logging/write-log-action.html).
![../../_images/left-state-trigger-add-write-log-action.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/left-state-trigger-add-write-log-action.png) ![../../_images/left-state-write-log-message.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/left-state-write-log-message.png)
  3. In the Node Components > Triggers in the trigger that you created in the first step, right-click Conditions, select Trigger Condition, and set the condition that you want to use for that trigger. See [Creating a condition using a value from a message](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html#creating-a-condition-using-a-value-from-a-message).
For example, for the Left State trigger in the trigger condition set:
     * A
       * Type of A to Message argument
       * Message Argument to State
     * Operation to =
     * B
       * Type of B to Fixed
       * Fixed Value to the name of the state to which you want the trigger to react
For example, set it to State A.

## Using state groups[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-state-managers.html#using-state-groups "Link to this heading")
State groups contain states, define controller properties, and transitions between states in a state group. Use state groups to smoothly control the states and transitions in your application. For example, a state manager for a button can contain three state groups: button pressed, button released, and hover over button. In each state group you create states, which use state objects to define how the button behaves in each state.
To use state groups:
  1. In the State Tools click + Create State Group to create a state group and enter the name for the state group you created.
  2. In the State Tools bring the mouse pointer over a state group to set the properties that this state group records. Set different state groups to record the changes in different property values. Use the All to select or deselect all properties.
To duplicate or remove a state group, hover over the state group and select Duplicate or Remove.
![../../_images/hover-over-state-group.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/hover-over-state-group.png)

For details, see the `StateManager[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a14522.html)` class.

Use state transitions to define how the state manager reacts when the application state changes, such as when the user clicks a button. For example, you can:

  * Define whether the user can interrupt the transition
  * Use a custom animation. See [Using custom easing functions in state transitions](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-transitions.html#using-custom-easing-functions-in-state-transitions).

content:
## Setting transitions between any to any state[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-transitions.html#setting-transitions-between-any-to-any-state "Link to this heading")
When you create states the state manager uses the default transition to transition between states.
To set transitions between any to any state:
  1. Create a node and set the node to use a state manager. See [Using state managers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-state-managers.html) or [Tutorial: Creating a toggle button](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/toggle-button/toggle-button.html).
For example, create a toggle button and a state manager that has one state group with the states On and Off.
  2. In the State Tools click Transition Editor to open the State Transition Editor.
To create a new transition, click + Create Transition under the existing transitions.
![../../_images/open-state-transition-editor1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/open-state-transition-editor1.png)
  3. When you first open the State Transition Editor it shows the transition that is used between all states in that state group. Move your mouse pointer over ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/state-transition-editor-c.png) to see the details of the transition.
![../../_images/set-transition-between-any-to-any-state.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-transition-between-any-to-any-state.png)
  4. In the popup window set:
     * Duration to the length of the transition in milliseconds.
Either click and drag in the Duration area or enter the new value to set the duration of the transition.
     * Allow interrupt or Always full time set how Kanzi handles interruption of the transition:
       * Always full time uses the entire time set in the Duration to transition to the state after the interruption occurs.
       * Allow interrupt uses only the remaining time set in the Duration to transition to the state after the interruption occurs.
     * Configure Animations enables you to further define the details of the transition. In the State Transition Settings window set:
       * Start Time to the time in milliseconds that elapses before the transition starts.
       * Direction to whether the transition applies to the transition from the Start State to the End State, or to the transitions from both states:
         * Unidirectional applies the transition only to the transition from the Start State to the End State.
         * Bidirectional applies the transition to the transition from the Start State to the End State, and from the End State to the Start State.
       * Easing Function sets the easing function that defines the curve of the transition.
Use an easing function to make UI elements more lifelike. Because objects in real life never start or stop immediately, an appropriate easing function can help you create a more pleasant user experience.
Select the most suitable easing function.

## Setting transitions between specific states[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-transitions.html#setting-transitions-between-specific-states "Link to this heading")
You can set custom transitions between specific states. You can add states to the State Transition Editor canvas and configure transition settings between them.
To set transitions between specific states:
  1. In the State Transition Editor right-click, select Add State To Canvas, and select the state for which you want to set the transitions.
To show all states, right-click and select Add All States To Canvas.
![../../_images/add-state-to-canvas.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-state-to-canvas.png)
  2. Click the state to select it and click the Default transitions to set a Custom transition.
![../../_images/state-transition-editor-default-transitions.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/state-transition-editor-default-transitions.png)
  3. Move your mouse pointer over the ![image1](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/state-transition-editor-c.png) transitions to see the details of the transitions.
In the State Tools you see the transitions that you define in the State Transition Editor. To edit the settings for a transition, click that transition.
![../../_images/select-a-transition-in-state-tools.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-a-transition-in-state-tools.png) ![../../_images/click-transition-to-open-editor.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/click-transition-to-open-editor.png)

## Using custom easing functions in state transitions[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-transitions.html#using-custom-easing-functions-in-state-transitions "Link to this heading")
You can use animations to define custom easing functions for transitions between states. For example, define a custom easing function to make a phone call alert blink when you enter that state.
To use custom easing functions in state transitions:
  1. Create or select a node that uses a state manager. See [Using state managers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-state-managers.html) or [Tutorial: Creating a toggle button](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/toggle-button/toggle-button.html).
For example:
    1. Create an Image node that shows the image that alerts the user about an incoming phone call.
![../../_images/incoming-call1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/incoming-call1.png) ![../../_images/image-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/image-in-project.png) ![../../_images/image-incoming-call.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/image-incoming-call.png)
    2. Create for the Image node a state manager that has one state group with the states Default and Incoming Call, and add and set the value of the Opacity property of the Image node for each state:
       * For the Default state set it to 0 This way you hide the incoming call image in the Default state when the phone is not ringing.
       * For the Incoming Call state set it to 1 This way you show the incoming call image in the Incoming Call state when the phone is ringing.
![../../_images/image-state-manager.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/image-state-manager.png)
  2. Create an Animation or Animation Clip resource. You use this animation to change the value of the property that you use in the states which you created in the previous step. See [Creating keyframe animations](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/animations/animating-property-values.html).
For example, in the Library > Animations > Animation Data create an Animation that animates the Opacity property of a node. You use this animation to make the node blink three times when the node enters the Incoming Call state.
![../../_images/animation-data-animation-library.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/animation-data-animation-library.png) ![../../_images/animation-target-property-opacity.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/animation-target-property-opacity.png) ![../../_images/animation-clip-editor-opacity-animation.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/animation-clip-editor-opacity-animation.png)
  3. In the Node Tree select the node that you created in the first step and in the State Tools click Any -> Any to open the State Transition Settings.
![../../_images/state-tools-click-any-to-any.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/state-tools-click-any-to-any.png)

metadata.title: Using state transitions (Part 10/12)

3. In the Node Tree select the node that you created in the first step and in the State Tools click Any -> Any to open the State Transition Settings.
![../../_images/state-tools-click-any-to-any.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/state-tools-click-any-to-any.png)
  4. In the State Transition Settings set:
     * Start State to the state the transition from which you want to animate
For example, set it to Default.
     * End State to the state the transition to which you want to animate
For example, set it to Incoming Call.

     * Property Type to the property that you want to animate
For example, set it to Opacity.
Kanzi Studio shows in the Property Type dropdown menu only the properties with different values in the Start State and End State states.
     * Easing Function to Custom
     * Custom Animation to the animation that you created earlier in this procedure
For example, set it to Animation.

## Configuring easing functions[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-transitions.html#configuring-easing-functions "Link to this heading")
You can configure some of the easing functions in the State Transition Settings to define the values in the function that sets the transition curve.
The easing functions that you can configure in the State Transition Settings are:
  * Back
    * Use the Amplitude property to sets the amplitude or depth of the transition curve.
![../../_images/back-amplitude.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/back-amplitude.png)
  * Elastic
    * Use the Oscillations property to set the amount of oscillations in the transition curve.
    * Use the Springiness property to set the elasticity of the oscillations in the transition curve.
![../../_images/elastic-oscillations.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/elastic-oscillations.png)
  * Exponential
    * Use the Exponent property to set the exponent to the power of which the transition curve multiplies.
![../../_images/exponential-exponent.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/exponential-exponent.png)
  * Power
    * Use the Power property to set the speed by which the transition curve accelerates.
![../../_images/power.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/power.png)


## Crossfading animations between states[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-transitions.html#crossfading-animations-between-states "Link to this heading")
When the states in a state group contain Animation Player node components with the same name, the State Manager automatically crossfades between the outgoing and incoming animations over the transition duration. The crossfade uses a linear blend regardless of the easing function configured on the transition.
See [Blending animations](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/animations/blending-animations.html).

Use styles to set the property values of one or more nodes of a certain type.
In a style you set the values of properties the style applies to a node. For example, use a style to define the font type, size, and color of the text for all Text Block 3D nodes in your project.
To override a property defined in a style, add that property to the node to which the style applies.
Using styles you can:
  * Create a target style that applies to a specific branch of nodes in your Kanzi Studio project. See [Applying a style that applies to a node type in the selected scope](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/styles/using-styles.html#applying-a-style-that-applies-to-a-node-type-in-the-selected-scope).
  * Create a named style that applies to selected instances of a certain node type, or overrides the target styles. See [Applying a style to selected instances of a node type](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/styles/using-styles.html#applying-a-style-to-selected-instances-of-a-node-type).

## Applying a style that applies to a node type in the selected scope[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/styles/using-styles.html#applying-a-style-that-applies-to-a-node-type-in-the-selected-scope "Link to this heading")
Target styles define the look and feel for a selected node type in a specific part of the node tree in a Kanzi Studio project.
For example, to use different font sizes for the text at different levels of navigation, create a style for each navigation level, and add each style to the resource dictionary at each level of navigation.
To apply a style to descendants of a node type:
  1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Styles and select Typed Style.
![../../_images/create-typed-style.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-typed-style.png)
  2. In the Properties set the Target Type property to the node type for which you want to define a style.
For example, set Target Type to Text Block 2D to define a style for Text Block 2D nodes in your project.
![../../_images/set-target-type.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-target-type.png)
  3. In the Properties click ![add-properties](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/open-add-properties-window.png), and add and set the properties you want to define with the style.
For example, to define the color of font for a Text Block 2D node, add the Foreground Brush property, and set it to a brush you want to use to render the text in the Text Block 2D node.
![../../_images/foreground-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/foreground-brush.png)
  4. In the Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click the node to whose descendants you want to apply the style and select Resource Dictionary.
![../../_images/select-resource-dictionary.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-resource-dictionary.png)
  5. In the Dictionaries in the scope of the node to whose descendants you want to apply the style, click + Add Resource, select Add Existing, and select the style you created.
![../../_images/add-existing-typed-style.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-existing-typed-style.png)
  6. If the properties you defined in the style exist in the target nodes, remove them from the target nodes so that the style can take effect.
  7. By default the Text Block 2D nodes use the Text Block 2D Style which sets the Snap to Pixel property.
The Snap to Pixel property rounds the translation and scale of a Text Block 2D or Text Box 2D node to a full pixel, which enables Kanzi to render pixel-perfect text.
To enable the Snap to Pixel property for the Text Block 2D node you created, add the Snap to Pixel property to the Typed Style you created.
![../../_images/typed-style-snap-to-pixel-added.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/typed-style-snap-to-pixel-added.png)

Named styles define the look and feel only for the selected instances of a node type, or override the target styles. For example, if you create a target style for the Text Block 3D, you can override that style with a named style.
To apply a style to only selected instances of a node type:
  1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Styles and select Named Style.
![../../_images/create-named-style.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-named-style.png)
  2. In the Properties set the Target Type property to the node type for which you want to define a style.

  3. In the Properties click ![add-properties](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/open-add-properties-window.png), and add and set the properties you want to define with the style.

Use tags to group, find, and filter nodes in your project. You can assign multiple tags to a single node.
For example, you can use tags to:
  * Find nodes using the quick search in the Node Tree. See [Finding tagged nodes in the Node Tree](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/tags/using-tags.html#finding).
  * Find nodes using the Find Project Item tool. See [Finding tagged nodes using the Find Project Item tool](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/tags/using-tags.html#finding2).
  * Render only specific nodes in your project. See [Using the Tag Filter](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/using-tag-filters.html).


## Tagging a node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/tags/using-tags.html#tagging-a-node "Link to this heading")
You can create a tag and tag a node in the Properties of that node.
To tag a node:
  1. In the Node Tree select the node you want to tag.
  2. In the Properties:
     * In the Tags property enter the name of the tag and press `Enter`.
Kanzi Studio creates the tag and tags the node with the tag.
![../../_images/create-tag-tags-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-tag-tags-property.png)
     * Click the Tags button next to the Tags property and select a tag from the list of existing tags.
Kanzi Studio uses the existing tag to tag the node.
![../../_images/use-exisiting-tag.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/use-exisiting-tag.png)


## Creating a tag without tagging a node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/tags/using-tags.html#creating-a-tag-without-tagging-a-node "Link to this heading")
You can create a tag without tagging a node at the same time.
To create a tag without tagging a node:
  1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Tags and select Tag.
![../../_images/create-tag.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-tag.png)
  2. Name the tag and click OK.
Kanzi Studio creates the tag and lists it in the Library > Tags.
![../../_images/tags-in-library-tags.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/tags-in-library-tags.png)

## Finding tagged nodes in the Node Tree[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/tags/using-tags.html#finding-tagged-nodes-in-the-node-tree "Link to this heading")
To find tagged nodes in the Node Tree:
  1. Create a tag and assign it to nodes. See [Tagging a node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/tags/using-tags.html#tagging-a-node).
  2. In the Node Tree, in the search box, enter the tag name that you are looking for.
The Node Tree shows only the nodes that contain the tag you entered in the search box.


## Finding tagged nodes using the Find Project Item tool[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/tags/using-tags.html#finding-tagged-nodes-using-the-find-project-item-tool "Link to this heading")
To find tagged nodes using the Find Project Item tool:
  1. Create a tag and assign it to nodes. See [Tagging a node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/tags/using-tags.html#tagging-a-node).
  2. Select Edit > Find.
The Find Project Item window opens.
![../../_images/edit-find.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/edit-find.png)
  3. In the Advanced Search tab in the Criteria section click ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-property.png) to add a new criterion and in the criterion:
    1. Select Has Property Value.
    2. Select the Tags property.
    3. Click the Tags button and select the tag you are looking for.
![../../_images/find-tag-criterion.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/find-tag-criterion.png)
  4. Click Search.
The Find Project Item shows all nodes with the tag you selected.
![../../_images/search-tag.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/search-tag.png)


## Using tags in the API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/tags/using-tags.html#using-tags-in-the-api "Link to this heading")
For details, see the `Node[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13774.html)` tag interface. The relevant functions are `Node::acquireTag[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13774.html#acbda97d5353f6eb11c0e5b772860c9cc)`, `Node::hasTag[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13774.html#abad675424d292038276131ceba09060c)`, `Node::setTag[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13774.html#aaf59eb73970df1d7f597391b86057f9f)` and `Node::removeTag[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13774.html#a3b5071a0afeaba1c92f3fe20667fe132)`.

Kanzi has these text nodes:
  * Use the Text Block nodes to show a small amount of text in your application.
See [Using the Text Block nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-blocks.html).
![../../_images/text-blcok-2d-icon.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-blcok-2d-icon.png)
  * Use the Text Box nodes to add single-line text input to your application.
See [Using the Text Box nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html).
![../../_images/text-box-2d-icon.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-2d-icon.png)


## Font type[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/text.html#font-type "Link to this heading")
The default font family in Kanzi is [Fira Sans Regular](https://mozilla.github.io/Fira/). The font file is stored in `<KanziInstallation>/Studio/Asset Library/Fonts`. When you want to use your own font, import it to your Kanzi Studio project.
See [Importing fonts](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing-fonts.html).
You can use these font types in your Kanzi applications:
  * TrueType and OpenType fonts (ttf and otf files)
  * iType linked fonts (ltt files). See [iType linked fonts](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing-fonts.html#itype-linked-fonts).
  * Bitmap fonts (fnt files). See [Using bitmap fonts](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing-fonts.html#using-bitmap-fonts).


Make sure that the font you use includes all the glyphs for the text that you want to include in your Kanzi application.

## Font size[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/text.html#font-size "Link to this heading") Kanzi sets the size of fonts in pixels. When you set the Font Size property, Kanzi passes that value to the Freetype library, which Kanzi uses to render fonts, using the [FT_Set_Char_Size](https://www.freetype.org/freetype2/docs/reference/ft2-base_interface.html#FT_Set_Char_Size) function with the default dpi value of 72. For example, both of these display the letter H of the same size: * Text Block or Text Box nodes with these properties set: * Text to H * Font Family to Arial * Font Size to 36 * HTML markup ```

H

``` Copy to clipboard If you want to control the dpi scaling or set the font size in units other than pixels, you must implement that functionality in your Kanzi application. For example, if you want to automatically select the content that the images and layouts in your project use based on the dpi setting, implement that functionality in your Kanzi application. ## Setting the font engine for the Preview[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/text.html#setting-the-font-engine-for-the-preview "Link to this heading") You can set which font engine you want the Kanzi Studio Preview to use to render the text in your application. To set the font engine for the Preview: 1. In the main menu select Project > Properties. ![../../_images/project-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties.png) 2. In the Properties set the Font Engine property: * FreeType uses the FreeType rasterizer, HarfBuzz shaper, and ICU bidirectional library, and libunibreak for line breaking. This is the default font engine. * iType uses the Monotype iType rasterizer and WorldType® Shaper™ for shaping. See [Installing the iType font engine](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/controlling-your-application-in-the-preview.html#installing-the-itype-font-engine). * None to not load a font engine. When you do not load a font engine, the Preview does not render the text in your application. ![../../_images/font-engine.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/font-engine.png) To learn how to set which font engine to load at application startup, see [FontEngine](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#fontengine).

## Setting font hinting[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/text.html#setting-font-hinting "Link to this heading")
Font hinting provides instructions for rasterization: mapping the outlines of fonts to screen pixels. Font hinting aims to both maintain the design aesthetic of a font and optimize the readability of the font at different sizes.
Text nodes in Kanzi by default use the font hinting data included in a font.
For example, font hinting can affect the height and width of characters, the width of lines, edge contrast, and the space between characters.
To set font hinting for a Text Block or Text Box node, in the Node Tree select that node, in the Properties add the Font Hinting Preference property, and set it to:
  * No hinting to render text without font hinting.
  * Native hinting to render text using the hinting data included in the font. If the font does not contain hinting data, Kanzi uses the hinter of the font engine rasterizer. This is the default value.
  * Auto hinting to render text using the hinter of the font engine rasterizer. See [Setting the font engine for the Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/text.html#setting-font-engine-for-preview).

![../../_images/font-hinting-preference.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/font-hinting-preference.png)
## Font fallback[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/text.html#font-fallback "Link to this heading")
In Kanzi, you can define a Fallback Font Chain for a Font Family. If a character is not available in the current font, Kanzi searches the fallback font chain in order, selecting the first font family that contains the missing character.
If the character is not found in any fallback font family, the glyph with **glyph ID 0** in the current font is used as the missing glyph character.
Use fallback fonts to:
  * Display multiple languages in a single text node.
  * Show special characters like emojis and symbols alongside regular text.


When rendering with a fallback font, Kanzi attempts to select a font file from the fallback family that closely matches the style and weight of the current font.
To optimize performance and memory usage, fallback fonts are only loaded when a character is not found in the current font or any of the earlier fallback fonts in the chain.
To configure the Fallback Font Chain, you can choose from existing font families using the dropdown menu, or add a font family using a kzb URL.
![../../_images/font-fallbacks.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/font-fallbacks.png)

## Color fonts[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/text.html#color-fonts "Link to this heading")
To render emoji and other colored glyphs, import a font file that contains color glyphs. The color font file can be either the primary font of a Font Family or a fallback font.
These color font formats are supported for each Kanzi font engine:  
| Font file type  | FreeType  | iType  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| glyf table (normal non-colored scalable text and icons)  | ✅  | ✅  |  
| CBDT table (non-scalable PNG images)  | ✅  | ✅  |  
| SBIX table (non-scalable PNG images)  | ✅  | ❌  |  
| COLRv0 table (scalable shapes with solid colors)  | ✅  | ✅  |  
| SVG table (SVG images with color gradients)  | ❌  | ❌  |  
| COLRv1 table (scalable shapes with color gradients)  | ❌  | ❌  |  
When you use a font file that contains glyphs in a non-supported font format:
  * If the font file contains glyphs in multiple formats, Kanzi uses non-colored version of the glyphs
  * Kanzi does not render the glyphs


Note
Kanzi renders colored glyphs using a different brush and material than normal text. This material uses only the alpha channel of the Foreground Brush property color (Font Color property for 3D text). This means that you can change the color of text without affecting the emoji colors.
![../../_images/color-fonts.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/color-fonts.png)

## Customizing word wrapping in Thai text with iType font engine[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/text.html#customizing-word-wrapping-in-thai-text-with-itype-font-engine "Link to this heading")
You can customize how Kanzi iType font engine wraps words in Thai text by setting a Thai dictionary that you want to use instead of the one that is built into the iType font engine.
WorldType® SDK comes with:
  * Thai dictionary
  * Python utility that creates a Thai dictionary that your application can use


You can find these resources in the WorldType® SDK in the `wtle/product/tools/language_dictionaries/thai` directory.
To wrap words automatically in Thai text:
  1. Create a Thai dictionary for the iType font engine by passing to `GenerateThaiDictionary.py`:
     * Thai dictionary in plain-text format
     * File where you want to store the generated dictionary

```
py -2 GenerateThaiDictionary.py thai-dictionary.txt thai-dictionary.wtd

```
Copy to clipboard
`GenerateThaiDictionary.py` creates a wtd file that you set in the application configuration of your Kanzi application:

```
Reading lines from file "thai-dictionary.txt"... done.
Extracting, filtering, and normalizing words... done.
Adding words to trie... done.
   number of words: 8
   number of characters: 31
   longest word length: 7
   number of trie nodes: 32
   number of trie edges: 31
Compressing trie into a DAWG (Directed Acyclic Word Graph)... done.
   number of edges in root node: 9
   number of DAWG nodes: 24
   number of DAWG edges: 30
   edges / characters = 96.8 %
   dawgEdges / trieEdges = 96.0 %
   dawgNodes / trieNodes = 75.0 %
   DAWG array elements: 31
Writing DAWG to file "thai-dictionary.wtd"... done.
   file size: 0 k

```
Copy to clipboard
  2. To set your application to use the Thai dictionary that you created, in a text editor set the iType font engine dictionary in the `<ProjectName>/Application/bin/application.cfg` file:

```
# Set additional backend dictionaries.
ITypeDictionaryUrls = file:///usr/share/itype/thai-dictionary.wtd

```
Copy to clipboard
See [Font engine dictionaries](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#font-engine-dictionaries).
  3. (Optional) To set the Kanzi Studio Preview to correctly render Thai text when you use the iType font engine, in Kanzi Studio open your project and in the main menu select Project > Properties. In the Properties set the Preview Working Directory property to the directory that contains the `application.cfg` file that you created in the previous step.
![../../_images/project-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties.png) ![../../_images/properties-preview-working-directory.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-preview-working-directory.png)

A Text Block node uses the font that you select to render the text. Use Text Block 3D to show text in 3D space and Text Block 2D to show text in 2D space.
![../../_images/text-block1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-block1.png)

content:
## Adding text to your application[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-blocks.html#adding-text-to-your-application "Link to this heading")
To add text to your application:
  1. In the Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click the node where you want to show text and select either Text Block 3D, or Text Block 2D.
You can create a 3D node only in a 3D node, such as the Scene node, and a 2D node only in a 2D node.
Tip
In the Preview use the Text Block 2D tool ![text-block-tool](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-block-2d-tool.png) to click and drag to create a Text Block 2D node. To position the Text Block 2D node in a layout, click and drag that Text Block 2D node, press and hold `Ctrl`, and drop the node on top of the cell where you want to place it.
  2. In the Properties in the Text property enter the text that you want to show. To add a new line press `Shift` `Enter`.
Use the Text Block nodes to show a small amount of text in your application.
You can set how Kanzi wraps and truncates text. See [Wrapping and truncating text](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-blocks.html#wrapping-and-truncating-text-in-text-block-node).
![../../_images/text-and-overflow-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-and-overflow-properties.png)
  3. In the Properties set the Font properties to make the text look the way you want it to look. Kanzi applies all the settings that you set in a Text Block node to the entire node.
For example, in the Properties add and set:
     * Font Size to define the size of the text.
![../../_images/set-font-size.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-font-size.png)
     * Font Family to the font family that you want to use.
The default font family in Kanzi is [Fira Sans Regular](https://mozilla.github.io/Fira/). The font file is stored in `<KanziInstallation>/Studio/Asset Library/Fonts`. When you want to use your own font, import it to your Kanzi Studio project.
See [Importing fonts](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing-fonts.html).
     * Fixed Character Width to turn your font into a monospaced font.

content:
## Wrapping and truncating text[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-blocks.html#wrapping-and-truncating-text "Link to this heading")
When you restrict the width of a Text Block node, Kanzi by default clips the text that is longer than the width of that Text Block node. You can:
  * Wrap the text into a new line by adding and enabling the Word Wrap property.
  * Truncate the text by adding either:
    * The Overflow property and setting the characters that indicate truncation
    * The Truncation property and setting the truncation:
      * At character to truncate text character by character
      * At word to truncate text by entire words
      * None to disable truncation
![../../_images/text-block-truncation.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-block-truncation.gif)
Kanzi truncates the text to fit within the vertical and horizontal limits of the Text Block node and adds the characters from the **Overflow** property. If there is not enough vertical space to fit a single line of text, Kanzi truncates all text and does not show the **Overflow** characters.


When you enable truncation, you can set which part of the text to truncate. Add the Truncation Direction property and set it to:
  * Trailing to truncate the end part of the text. Default value.
For multiline text, just like for single-line text, if the Word Wrap property is set to disabled, Kanzi truncates the remaining text that does not fit horizontally.
The value of the Overflow property indicates truncation at the end of the truncated line.
  * Center to truncate the middle part of the text.
If Word Wrap property is set to disabled, Kanzi horizontally clips multiline text. Kanzi completely truncates middle lines of a multiline or word-wrapped text.
The value of the Overflow property indicates truncation at the end of the line that precedes truncated lines.
  * Leading to truncate the beginning part of the text.
If Word Wrap property is set to disabled, Kanzi horizontally clips multiline text. Kanzi completely truncates leading lines of a multiline or word-wrapped text.
The value of the Overflow property indicates truncation at the beginning of the first visible line.

![../../_images/text-block-truncation-direction.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-block-truncation-direction.gif)
This table shows some options that you can use to set text layout.  
| Goal  | Required property values  | Result  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| 
  * The text defines the size of a Text Block node.
  * You cannot wrap or truncate text.

 | Default property values  |  ![../../_images/preview-default-layout.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-default-layout.png)  |  
| 
  * Set the width, but the text sets the height of a Text Block node.
  * Clip the text to fit into the width of a Text Block node.
  * You can wrap or truncate this text with the Word Wrap and Overflow properties.

## Fitting text into a Text Block node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-blocks.html#fitting-text-into-a-text-block-node "Link to this heading")
When you want to make sure that the entire text of a Text Block node fits into the width of that node, use the Horizontal Fit and Horizontal Fit Scale Limits properties.
To fit text into a Text Block node:
  1. In the Node Tree or Prefabs select the Text Block, and in the Properties add and set:
     * Layout Width to the width that you want to use for that Text Block node
     * Horizontal Fit to enabled
When you enable this property and the text does not fit into the width of that Text Block node as set by the Layout Width property, Kanzi automatically scales the glyphs to up to half their size.
![../../_images/properties-horizontal-fit.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-horizontal-fit.png) ![../../_images/preview-horizontal-fit.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-horizontal-fit.png)
  2. (Optional) To adjust the scaling of the glyphs, add the Horizontal Fit Scale Limits property and set its Min and Max property fields to the minimum and maximum scale ranges for the glyphs.
For example:
     * When you set the Min property field to:
       * 1.0, Kanzi does not squeeze the glyphs
![../../_images/properties-horizontal-fit-scale-min-1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-horizontal-fit-scale-min-1.png) ![../../_images/preview-horizontal-fit-scale-min-1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-horizontal-fit-scale-min-1.png)
       * 0.5, Kanzi allows squeezing the glyphs to up to half their size
![../../_images/properties-horizontal-fit-scale-min-05.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-horizontal-fit-scale-min-05.png) ![../../_images/preview-horizontal-fit.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-horizontal-fit.png)
     * When you set the Max property field to:
       * 1.0, Kanzi does not stretch the glyphs
![../../_images/properties-horizontal-fit-scale-min-1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-horizontal-fit-scale-min-1.png) ![../../_images/preview-horizontal-fit-scale-max-1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-horizontal-fit-scale-max-1.png)
       * 2.0, Kanzi allows stretching the glyphs to up to double their size
![../../_images/properties-horizontal-fit-scale-max-2.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-horizontal-fit-scale-max-2.png) ![../../_images/preview-horizontal-fit-scale-max-2.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-horizontal-fit-scale-max-2.png)

## Setting the size and layout of a Text Block 3D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-blocks.html#setting-the-size-and-layout-of-a-text-block-3d-node "Link to this heading")
To render a Text Block 3D node, Kanzi first prepares the text as 2D text using pixels and then projects the prepared text to the 3D space.
To set the size and layout of a Text Block 3D node:
  * Use pixels to set the size and layout of the text in the Text Block 3D node.
For example, set the values of the Font Size, Character Spacing, and Fixed Character Width properties in pixels.
![../../_images/text-block-3d-dip-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-block-3d-dip-properties.png)
  * Use the 2D to 3D Projection Scale property to set the factor that Kanzi uses to scale the text from pixels to 3D units. The default value of the 2D to 3D Projection Scale property is 0.02.
![../../_images/2d-to-3d-projection-scale.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/2d-to-3d-projection-scale.png)
  * Use 3D units to set the size of the Text Block 3D node in the 3D space.
For example, set the values of the Layout Width and Layout Height properties in 3D units.
![../../_images/text-block-3d-layout-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-block-3d-layout-properties.png)


## Setting the color of text in a Text Block 2D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-blocks.html#setting-the-color-of-text-in-a-text-block-2d-node "Link to this heading")
To set the color of text in a Text Block 2D or Text Box 2D node:
  1. In the Node Tree create or select a Text Block 2D or Text Box 2D node.
![../../_images/select-text-block-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-text-block-2d.png)
  2. In the Properties add the Foreground Brush property.
![../../_images/add-foreground-brush-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-foreground-brush-property.png)
  3. Set the Foreground Brush property to an existing Color Brush or select + Color Brush, name the brush, click ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/quick-edit-properties.png) next to the property, and set the color of the Color Brush you created.
![../../_images/select-and-set-color-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-and-set-color-brush.png)
Tip
To quickly edit a brush, in the Properties next to the Background Brush or Foreground Brush property click ![quick-edit-property](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/quick-edit-properties.png) and edit the brush.
![../../_images/background-brush-quick-edit.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/background-brush-quick-edit.png)

## Setting the color of text in a Text Block 3D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-blocks.html#setting-the-color-of-text-in-a-text-block-3d-node "Link to this heading")
To set the color of text in a 3D text node:
  1. In the Node Tree create or select a Text Block 3D or Text Box 3D node.
![../../_images/create-text-block-3d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-text-block-3d.png)
  2. In the Properties add and set the Font Color property.
![../../_images/set-font-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-font-color.png)


## Changing the size of text dynamically[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-blocks.html#changing-the-size-of-text-dynamically "Link to this heading")
To dynamically change the size of text in a Text Block node, use the Scale property field of either Render Transformation or Layout Transformation properties, instead of the Font Size property. For example, use this approach when you want to animate the size of text in a Text Block node. When you use the Font Size property to dynamically scale the text, Kanzi creates multiple textures for different font sizes and does not release them from the memory.
## Rendering pixel-perfect text in a Text Block 2D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-blocks.html#rendering-pixel-perfect-text-in-a-text-block-2d-node "Link to this heading")
When you create a project in Kanzi Studio, the Screen node has in its resource dictionary the Text Block 2D Style which enables the Snap to Pixel property for all Text Block 2D nodes in a Kanzi application.
The Snap to Pixel property rounds the translation and scale of a Text Block 2D or Text Box 2D node to a full pixel, which enables Kanzi to render pixel-perfect text.
![../../_images/dictionaries-text-block-2d-style.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/dictionaries-text-block-2d-style.png)
To disable the Snap to Pixel property, select the Text Block 2D node for which you want to disable that property and in the Properties add and disable the Snap to Pixel property.
![../../_images/properties-snap-to-pixel.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-snap-to-pixel.png)

## Setting the rendering of characters in a Text Block 2D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-blocks.html#setting-the-rendering-of-characters-in-a-text-block-2d-node "Link to this heading")
You can set how Kanzi renders each character in 2D text. In a Text Block 2D node these properties are by default enabled:
  * The Snap Character To Pixel property rounds the translation and scale of each character to a full pixel.
This improves text sharpness, but some characters can shift by a fraction of a pixel.
  * The Fractional Character Width property enables the spacing between characters to vary and be a fraction of a pixel.
In most cases this provides the best text rendering result. Fractional widths can cause characters of small font sizes to run together or have too much space. This can make the text more difficult to read.


This table lists the options you can use to set the rendering of characters in a Text Block 2D node.  
| Goal  | Required property values  | Result  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
|  Best text rendering result for most cases:
  * Round the translation and scale of each character to a full pixel.
  * Allow the spacing between characters to vary and be a fraction of a pixel.

 | Default property values  |  ![../../_images/preview-default-character-rendering.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-default-character-rendering.png)  |  
|  Render characters as the font designer intended. Do not round the translation and scale of each character to a full pixel. Depending on the screen resolution, anti-aliasing, and font size, this can make the text appear more blurry.  |  Snap Character To Pixel disabled ![../../_images/snap-character-to-pixel-disabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/snap-character-to-pixel-disabled.png)  |  ![../../_images/preview-snap-character-to-pixel-disabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-snap-character-to-pixel-disabled.png)  |  
|  Improve the sharpness of small text. Round character widths to the nearest pixel. This prevents characters in small font sizes from running together and can make text appear sharper.  |  Fractional Character Width disabled ![../../_images/fractional-character-width-disabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/fractional-character-width-disabled.png)  |  ![../../_images/preview-fractional-character-width-disabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-fractional-character-width-disabled.png)  |  
| Manually set the space between the characters.  |  Character Spacing to the amount of space you want between the characters ![../../_images/character-spacing.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/character-spacing.png)  |  ![../../_images/preview-character-spacing.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-character-spacing.png)  |

## Setting font hinting for a Text Block node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-blocks.html#setting-font-hinting-for-a-text-block-node "Link to this heading")
Font hinting provides instructions for rasterization: mapping the outlines of fonts to screen pixels. Font hinting aims to both maintain the design aesthetic of a font and optimize the readability of the font at different sizes.
Text nodes in Kanzi by default use the font hinting data included in a font.
For example, font hinting can affect the height and width of characters, the width of lines, edge contrast, and the space between characters.
To set font hinting for a Text Block or Text Box node, in the Node Tree select that node, in the Properties add the Font Hinting Preference property, and set it to:
  * No hinting to render text without font hinting.
  * Native hinting to render text using the hinting data included in the font. If the font does not contain hinting data, Kanzi uses the hinter of the font engine rasterizer. This is the default value.
  * Auto hinting to render text using the hinter of the font engine rasterizer. See [Setting the font engine for the Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/text.html#setting-font-engine-for-preview).

![../../_images/font-hinting-preference.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/font-hinting-preference.png)

content:
## Splitting text into multiple Text Block nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-blocks.html#splitting-text-into-multiple-text-block-nodes "Link to this heading")
You can use bindings to split text into parts and access each part of the text. For example, split runtime data that you get from a data source. See [Using a data source](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/data-sources/using-a-data-source.html).
You can either:
  * Show the parts of text in multiple nodes in the order of those nodes in the Node Tree.
You store the collection of text parts in a property and in each node, where you want to show a part of the text, use a binding to advance the iteration of that collection and show the first element from the iterator.
Because the bindings iterate over the collection of text parts in the order in which Kanzi executes those bindings, the order of the nodes in the Node Tree determines which part of the text each node shows.
When you show the parts of text in this way, if you in Kanzi Studio change any property value in a node that shows a part of the text, the Kanzi Studio Preview re-instantiates the bindings in that node and advances the iteration beyond the end of the text that you split. When this happens, you must restart the Preview to see the correct text.
See [Showing the text parts in multiple nodes in the node tree order](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html#controlling-range-iteration-1).
  * Show the parts of text in multiple nodes in any order.
You store the locations of the text parts in separate properties and in each node, where you want to show a part of the text, use a binding to show the text part from a location stored in a specific property.
See [Showing the text parts in multiple nodes in any order](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html#controlling-range-iteration-2).

![../../_images/duplicated-text-blocks.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/duplicated-text-blocks.png) ![../../_images/my-text-property-set.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/my-text-property-set.png) ![../../_images/preview-all-text.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-all-text.png)

## Formatting display of property values[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-blocks.html#formatting-display-of-property-values "Link to this heading")
Use the `format` binding function to set how a Text Block node displays a property value. See [Formatting display of property values](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html#formatting-display-of-property-values) and the [format](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/reference-for-bindings-expressions.html#format) function reference.
With `format`, you can:
  * Insert values from a node property or data source to a text string.
  * Set the order in which the values that you pass to the function appear in the formatted text. See [Setting text order in a localized string](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/localization/localizing-applications.html#setting-text-order-in-a-localized-string).
![../../_images/format-localized-text-demo.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/format-localized-text-demo.gif)
  * Truncate a floating point value to a specific number of decimal places.
  * Set a minimum width for the formatted text inside a string.
  * When the content takes less space than the minimum width, pad the leftover space with spaces or zeroes. See [Formatting display of property values](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/using-bindings.html#formatting-display-of-property-values).
![../../_images/format-stopwatch-demo.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/format-stopwatch-demo.gif)
  * Align the formatted text to the left or to the right within the available space.


## Rendering text with transparent background[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-blocks.html#rendering-text-with-transparent-background "Link to this heading")
When you want the background of the text block nodes to be transparent, you must render the nodes in the node tree of your Kanzi application in the correct order. See [Rendering partially transparent nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/rendering-transparent-objects.html).

# Using the Text Box nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#using-the-text-box-nodes "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page
Copy this page as Markdown for LLMs.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/markdown.svg) View as Markdown
View this page as Markdown.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Ask Claude
Ask Claude about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/chatgpt.svg) Ask ChatGPT
Ask ChatGPT about this topic.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/vscode.svg) Connect to VS Code
Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use the Text Box nodes to add single-line text input to your application.
Use Text Box 3D to add text input in 3D space and Text Box 2D to add text input in 2D space.
![../../_images/text-box.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box.gif)
The Text Box nodes have the Focusable property enabled and can receive focus by default. By default when a Text Box node has focus, that Text Box node is in the editing state.
When a Text Box node is in the editing state, to move the cursor in that text box, you can use these default keyboard keys:
  * `←` to move the cursor one character backward.
  * `→` to move the cursor one character forward.
  * `Ctrl` `←` to move the cursor to the word boundary that precedes the cursor.
  * `Ctrl` `→` to move the cursor to the word boundary that follows the cursor.
  * `Home` to move the cursor to the beginning of the text content.
  * `End` to move the cursor to the end of the text content.


When a Text Box node is in the editing state, to modify the text selection in that text box, you can use these default keyboard keys:
  * `Shift` `←` to move the active cursor in the text selection one character backward.
  * `Shift` `Ctrl` to move the active cursor in the text selection to the word boundary that precedes the current position.
  * `Shift` `Home` to move the active cursor in the text selection to the beginning of the text content.
  * `Shift` `→` to move the active cursor in the text selection one character forward.
  * `Shift` `Ctrl` `→` to move the active cursor in the text selection to the word boundary that follows the current position.
  * `Shift` `End` to move the active cursor in the text selection to the end of the text content.
  * `Ctrl` `A` to select all text.


Note
The TextBox2D is only implemented for Windows platforms, and to use it you need to include the following snippet to `registerMetadataOverride` in your application code:

```
#if defined WIN32
    WindowsImeBackend::registerModule(getDomain());
#endif

```

## Editing the text in a Text Box node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#editing-the-text-in-a-text-box-node "Link to this heading")
A Text Box node by default:
  * Enters the editing state when focus moves to that Text Box node. This happens when the application user taps the node or sets focus to the node using the focus chain navigation. See [Focus](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/focus/focus.html).
  * Exits the editing state when focus moves from that Text Box node to another node.


See [Controlling manually when a Text Box node is in the editing state](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#controll).
To edit the text in a Text Box node:
  1. In the Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click the node where you want to add single-line text input to your application and select either Text Box 2D, or Text Box 3D.
You can create a 3D node only in a 3D node, such as the Scene node, and a 2D node only in a 2D node.
![../../_images/create-text-box-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-text-box-2d.png) ![../../_images/text-box-2d-in-node-tree.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-2d-in-node-tree.png)
  2. In the Node Tree create a node that you use to add, edit, and remove text in a Text Box node.
For example, create a Button 2D node and add content to it.
![../../_images/text-box-button-in-node-tree.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-button-in-node-tree.png)
  3. In the Node Tree select the node that you created in the previous step and in the Node Components > Triggers section press `Alt` and right-click the trigger that you want to use to add, edit, or remove text, and select one of the Text Box actions. See [Text Box actions](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/reference-for-actions.html#text-box-actions).
For example:
     * Insert Text At Cursor
Inserts text at the cursor position.
In the Insert Text At Cursor action set the value of the Text property to the text that you want to insert.
     * Delete At Cursor
Deletes a character using delete.
     * Backspace At Cursor
Deletes a character using backspace.
     * Move Cursor Backward
Moves the cursor one character backward.
     * Move Cursor Forward
Moves the cursor one character forward.
![../../_images/create-insert-text-at-cursor-action.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-insert-text-at-cursor-action.png) ![../../_images/insert-text-at-cursor.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/insert-text-at-cursor.png)
  4. In the action that you created in the previous step, set the Target Item to the Text Box node where you want to edit the text.
When the trigger, to which you added the action, is set off, Kanzi executes the action that edits the text in the Text Box node.
![../../_images/insert-text-at-cursor-target-item.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/insert-text-at-cursor-target-item.png)

## Controlling manually when a Text Box node is in the editing state[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#controlling-manually-when-a-text-box-node-is-in-the-editing-state "Link to this heading")
The application user can edit the text in a Text Box node when that node is in the editing state. Only one Text Box node can be in the editing state at a time. A Text Box node always leaves the editing state when:
  * Another Text Box node enters the editing state.
  * That Text Box node is disabled. See [Controlling whether a Text Box node is in use](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#text-box-enabled).


A Text Box node by default:
  * Enters the editing state when focus moves to that Text Box node. This happens when the application user taps the node or sets focus to the node using the focus chain navigation. See [Focus](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/focus/focus.html).
  * Exits the editing state when focus moves from that Text Box node to another node.


To manually control when a Text Box node is in the editing state:
  1. In the Node Tree select a Text Box node, in the Properties add the Edit Mode property, and set it to Triggered.
This way you set a Text Box node to:
     * Enter the editing state when a trigger executes the Text Box: Enter Editing State action.
     * Exit the editing state when either:
       * A trigger executes the Text Box: Leave Editing State action.
       * Another Text Box node enters the editing state.
![../../_images/text-box-2d-in-node-tree.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-2d-in-node-tree.png) ![../../_images/text-box-edit-mode.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-edit-mode.png)
  2. Create a trigger that sets the Text Box node to the editing state.
For example, to set the Text Box node to the editing state when the application user clicks a button, in the Node Tree create a Button node, in the Node Components in the Button: Click trigger create a Text Box: Enter Editing State action, and set Target Item to the Text Box node that you want to edit.
![../../_images/text-box-button-in-node-tree.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-button-in-node-tree.png) ![../../_images/enter-editing-state.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/enter-editing-state.png)
  3. Create a trigger that sets the Text Box node to exit the editing state.
For example, to set the Text Box node to exit the editing state when it loses focus, in that Text Box node create a Focus: Focus Lost trigger that executes a Text Box: Leave Editing State action.
![../../_images/text-box-2d-in-node-tree.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-2d-in-node-tree.png) ![../../_images/leave-editing-state.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/leave-editing-state.png)
