## Limiting the length of text in a Text Box node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#limiting-the-length-of-text-in-a-text-box-node "Link to this heading")
In the Text Box nodes you can set:
  * The length of the text that the Text Box node can show. See [Setting the length of text that a Text Box node can show](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-text-length-1).
  * The length of the text that the user can enter in the Text Box node. See [Setting the length of text that the user can enter in a Text Box node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-text-length-2).


### Setting the length of text that a Text Box node can show[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-the-length-of-text-that-a-text-box-node-can-show "Link to this heading")
To set the length of text that a Text Box node can show at a time, in the Node Tree select that node and in the Properties set the value of the Layout Width property.
![../../_images/text-box-2d-layout-width.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-2d-layout-width.png) ![../../_images/text-box-width-300.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-width-300.png)
When the text in a Text Box node is longer than the width of that node, in the editing state the user can scroll the text by moving the cursor in that Text Box node.
![../../_images/text-box-2d-scrolling.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-2d-scrolling.gif)
To let the length of the text in a Text Box node determine the width of that Text Box node, remove the Layout Width property.
### Setting the length of text that the user can enter in a Text Box node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-the-length-of-text-that-the-user-can-enter-in-a-text-box-node "Link to this heading")
To set the length of text that the user can enter in a Text Box node, in the Node Tree select the Text Box node, in the Properties add the Maximum Text Length property, and set it to the number of UTF-8 characters to which you want to limit the text that the user can enter in that Text Box node.
![../../_images/text-box-maximum-text-length.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-maximum-text-length.png)

Tip

![../../_images/background-brush-quick-edit.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/background-brush-quick-edit.png)

## Setting the appearance of the cursor[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-the-appearance-of-the-cursor "Link to this heading")
You can set the appearance of a Text Box cursor. To see the cursor of a Text Box node in the Kanzi Studio Preview click that Text Box node.
![../../_images/text-box-default-cursor.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-default-cursor.png)
To set the appearance of the cursor:
  1. In the Prefabs create a prefab that you want to use as the cursor.
For example, for a Text Box 2D node create an Empty Node 2D node and set its Background Brush, Layout Width, and Layout Height properties.
![../../_images/cursor-prefabs.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/cursor-prefabs.png) ![../../_images/cursor-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/cursor-properties.png) ![../../_images/cursor-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/cursor-preview.png)
  2. In the Node Tree select a Text Box node and in the Properties add and set the Cursor Prefab property to the prefab that you want to use as the cursor.
The Text Box node aligns the top of the cursor with the top of the Text Box node.
If the cursor does not fit in a Text Box 2D node, in the Text Box 2D node set the Horizontal Padding and Vertical Padding properties to adjust the offset of the cursor position.
![../../_images/text-box-cursor-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-cursor-properties.png) ![../../_images/text-box-cursor-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-cursor-preview.png)

## Setting the appearance of the text selection in a Text Box 2D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-the-appearance-of-the-text-selection-in-a-text-box-2d-node "Link to this heading")
In a Text Box node you can set the color of the selected text, its background, and the handles to change the selected text.
To select a word in a Text Box node, double-click that word. To modify the selection, drag the handles in the top-left and bottom-right corners of the selected text.
![../../_images/text-box-selection-preview-default.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-selection-preview-default.png)
To set the appearance of text selection, in the Node Tree select a Text Box 2D node and in the Properties add and set:  
| Selection Background Brush to the brush that you want to use to fill the background of the selected text.  |  ![../../_images/selection-background-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/selection-background-brush.png)  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Selection Foreground Brush to the brush that you want to use to fill the selected text.  |  ![../../_images/selection-foreground-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/selection-foreground-brush.png)  |  
| Selection Start Prefab to the prefab that you want to use for the selection handle at the beginning of the selection.  |  ![../../_images/selection-start-prefab.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/selection-start-prefab.png)  |  
| Selection End Prefab to the prefab that you want to use for the selection handle at the end of the selection.  |  ![../../_images/selection-end-prefab.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/selection-end-prefab.png)  |  
![../../_images/text-box-selection-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-selection-properties.png) ![../../_images/handle-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/handle-properties.png) ![../../_images/handle-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/handle-preview.png) ![../../_images/text-box-selection-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-selection-preview.png)
Tip
If a prefab that you use as a selection handle does not fit in a Text Box 2D node, in the Text Box 2D node set the Horizontal Padding and Vertical Padding properties to at least half of the width and height of the selection handle prefab.

## Setting the appearance of the composition text in a Text Box 2D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-the-appearance-of-the-composition-text-in-a-text-box-2d-node "Link to this heading")
Composition text is an instance of text that the application user produces using an input method editor (IME). An input method editor is an application that enables the user to use their input devices to type characters and symbols that are not natively available on those input devices.
In a Text Box node you can set the color of the composition text and its background.
To set the appearance of the composition text, in the Node Tree select a Text Box 2D node and in the Properties add and set:
  * Composition Text Background Brush to the brush that you want to use to fill the background of the composition text.
  * Composition Text Foreground Brush to the brush that you want to use to fill the composition text.

![../../_images/text-box-2d-composition-appearance.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-2d-composition-appearance.png)

## Showing placeholder content[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#showing-placeholder-content "Link to this heading")
You can set a Text Box node to show placeholder content when the Text Box is empty. For example, you can use this placeholder content to show text that tells the user what they can enter in a Text Box node.
To show placeholder content:
  1. In the Prefabs create a prefab that you want to use as the placeholder content.
For example, create a Text Block node and set its Text property.
![../../_images/hint-prefabs.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/hint-prefabs.png) ![../../_images/hint-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/hint-properties.png) ![../../_images/hint-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/hint-preview.png)
  2. In the Node Tree select a Text Box node and in the Properties add and set:
     * Text Hint Prefab to the prefab that you want to use as the placeholder content
     * (Optional) Hide Text Hint When Editing to enabled to hide the placeholder content whenever that Text Box node is in the editing state. By default Kanzi keeps the placeholder content visible until the user enters some text in the Text Box.
![../../_images/text-box-placeholder-text-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-placeholder-text-properties.png) ![../../_images/text-box-hint-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-hint-preview.png)

## Masking passwords[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#masking-passwords "Link to this heading")
You can set how to mask the password characters that the user enters in a Text Box node.
To set how Kanzi masks passwords in a Text Box node, in the Node Tree select that node, and in the Properties add and set:
  * Echo Mode to Password This way you set Kanzi to show each character for a certain amount of time, and then hide it with a masking character.
  * Password Echo Timeout to the time in milliseconds that you want to show each character before hiding it. By default Kanzi shows each character for one second.
  * Password Masking Character to the UTF-8 character with which you want to hide each password character. By default Kanzi masks each character with a bullet symbol (•).

![../../_images/text-box-password-mode-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/text-box-password-mode-properties.png) ![../../_images/password.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/password.gif)

## Setting truncation in a Text Box[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-truncation-in-a-text-box "Link to this heading")
When a Text Box node is not in the editing state, if the text in the node is longer than the width of that node, Kanzi by default truncates the end part of the text with ellipsis. When a Text Box node is in the editing state, Kanzi does not truncate the text. Instead, the user can scroll the text by moving the cursor.
You can set:
  * Which part of the text to truncate. See [Setting the part to truncate](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-the-part-to-truncate).
  * The type of truncation boundary. See [Setting the truncation boundary](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-the-truncation-boundary).
  * How to indicate truncated text. See [Setting the characters that indicate truncation](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-the-characters-that-indicate-truncation).


### Setting the part to truncate[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#setting-the-part-to-truncate "Link to this heading")
To set which part of the text to truncate, add the Text Concept > Truncation Direction property and set it to:
  * Trailing to truncate the end part of the text. Default value.
![../../_images/properties-truncation-mode-trailing.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-truncation-mode-trailing.png) [![../../_images/preview-truncation-mode-trailing.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-truncation-mode-trailing.png)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-truncation-mode-trailing.png)
  * Center to truncate the middle part of the text.
![../../_images/properties-truncation-mode-middle.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-truncation-mode-middle.png) [![../../_images/preview-truncation-mode-middle.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-truncation-mode-middle.png)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-truncation-mode-middle.png)
  * Leading to truncate the beginning part of the text.
![../../_images/properties-truncation-mode-leading.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-truncation-mode-leading.png) [![../../_images/preview-truncation-mode-leading.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-truncation-mode-leading.png)](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-truncation-mode-leading.png)

## Using a binding to update the text in a Text Box node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#using-a-binding-to-update-the-text-in-a-text-box-node "Link to this heading")
To update the text in a Text Box node with a binding, use a to-source or two-way binding. See [Bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/bindings.html).
For example, use a two-way binding to enable the user to edit a numerical value either by entering text in the Text Box node or by using a slider.
To use a binding to update the text in a Text Box node:
  1. In the Node Tree or Prefabs, create a Text Box node and set its appearance.
![../../_images/node-tree-text-box-in-stack-layout.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-text-box-in-stack-layout.png)
  2. Create a slider and set its lowest and highest value.
The Kanzi Factory Content contains a 2D slider that you can use. See [Using the slider from the Factory Content](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/sliders/using-sliders.html#using-slider-from-fc).
![../../_images/asset-packages-fc-slider.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/asset-packages-fc-slider.png) ![../../_images/node-tree-slider.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-slider.png) ![../../_images/slider-range-properties1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/slider-range-properties1.png)
  3. Select the Text Box node that you created. In the Properties, click + Add Binding and in the Binding Editor, set:
     * Binding Mode to Two way
     * Property to Text Concept > Text
     * Expression to point to the Value property of the slider that you created:

```
{@../Slider/RangeConcept.Value}

```
Copy to clipboard
![../../_images/binding-editor-two-way-text-slider-value.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/binding-editor-two-way-text-slider-value.png)
  4. (Optional) Create another binding and in the Binding Editor, set:
     * Property to Text
     * Expression to

```
int(getCurrentValue())

```
Copy to clipboard
This binding gets the current value of the Text property and converts it to an integer.
![../../_images/binding-editor-text-modifier-binding.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/binding-editor-text-modifier-binding.png)


Now, in the Preview:
  * When you move the slider knob, the text changes.
  * When you edit the text, the slider knob moves.

![../../_images/preview-text-slider-control.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-text-slider-control.gif)

## Controlling whether a Text Box node is in use[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html#controlling-whether-a-text-box-node-is-in-use "Link to this heading")
To control whether a Text Box node is in use, use the Input > Enabled property. A disabled Text Box node does not react to user input. When you disable a Text Box node, that Text Box node leaves the editing state and stays in that state while it is disabled.
When you disable the Enabled property of a node, you effectively disable that node and its descendant nodes in the same overlay focus scope.
To observe whether a node is effectively enabled, use the Input > Effectively Enabled property in a state manager or a binding. For example, to visually indicate to the user whether a node is in use, create a state manager and use the Effectively Enabled property as its controller property.
See [Controlling how a node reacts to input](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#controlling-how-a-node-reacts-to-input).

The default font family in Kanzi is [Fira Sans Regular](https://mozilla.github.io/Fira/). The font file is stored in `<KanziInstallation>/Studio/Asset Library/Fonts`. When you want to use your own font, import it to your Kanzi Studio project.
You can use these font types in your Kanzi applications:
  * TrueType and OpenType fonts (ttf and otf files)
  * iType linked fonts (ltt files). See [iType linked fonts](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing-fonts.html#itype-linked-fonts).
  * Bitmap fonts (fnt files). See [Using bitmap fonts](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing-fonts.html#using-bitmap-fonts).


Make sure that the font you use includes all the glyphs for the text that you want to include in your Kanzi application.
## Importing fonts to a Kanzi Studio project[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing-fonts.html#importing-fonts-to-a-ks-project "Link to this heading")
To import fonts to your project:
  1. Select File > Import > Import Fonts.
The Import Fonts window opens.
![../../_images/file-import-fonts.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/file-import-fonts.png)
  2. In the Fonts column select the font that you want to import and in the Typefaces column double-click the typefaces that you want to select for importing.
When you open the Import Fonts window, Kanzi Studio shows system fonts. To import fonts from a different location, click Browse and select the directory from which you want to import fonts.
![../../_images/import-fonts.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/import-fonts.png)
  3. When you are done selecting the typefaces that you want to import, click Import.
  4. You can see all imported fonts in the Library > Font Families.
![../../_images/font-families-in-library.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/font-families-in-library.png) ![../../_images/font-family-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/font-family-properties.png)

## iType linked fonts[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing-fonts.html#itype-linked-fonts "Link to this heading")
Use the iType linked fonts to link several TrueType or OpenType fonts and use glyphs from all the linked fonts by referring to a single font file. For example, you can link a font with Latin glyphs and a font with Chinese glyphs to render in your Kanzi application the glyphs used in both languages.
### Requirements[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing-fonts.html#requirements "Link to this heading")
To create iType linked font files, you need the Monotype iType FontLinking Kit 6.1.0.1. The linked font files that you create with this version of the FontLinking Kit are compatible with iType 5.3.3.
To use the iType linked font files, you need the Kanzi Engine plugin that adds the iType font engine to Kanzi. Submit the request for the Kanzi iType font engine through [support.rightware.com](http://support.rightware.com/).
### Installing the iType font engine for Kanzi Studio[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing-fonts.html#installing-the-itype-font-engine-for-ks "Link to this heading")
To install the iType font engine for Kanzi Studio:
  1. Extract the zip file that contains the iType font engine Kanzi Engine plugin.
  2. Copy the dll file for each build configuration to the `<KanziInstallation>/Studio/Bin/EnginePlugins` directory.
For example, copy the `GL_vs<Version>_Release/kzitypeplugin.dll` to the `<KanziInstallation>/Studio/Bin/EnginePlugins/GL_vs<Version>_Release` directory.


### Installing the iType font engine for Android[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing-fonts.html#installing-the-itype-font-engine-for-android "Link to this heading")
To install the iType font engine for Android:
  1. Download the `Kanzi-<Version>-android-freetype-itype.zip` file provided by Rightware support. The file contains the iType font engine Kanzi Engine plugin.
  2. Extract the zip file to the `<KanziWorkspace>/Engine` directory. When extracting the archive, you can skip files that already exist.

### Using the iType linked fonts[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing-fonts.html#using-the-itype-linked-fonts "Link to this heading")
To use the iType linked fonts:
  1. In File Explorer copy to the `<ProjectName>/Application/bin` directory the ttf or otf font files that you want to link.
  2. To create an ltt linked font file:
    1. In the iType FontLinking Kit open the FontLinker tool.
    2. In the Edit menu select Modify.
![../../_images/modify-linked-font.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/modify-linked-font.png)
    3. In the Font Link window click Add Font and select the font files that you copied to the `Application/bin` directory.
![../../_images/add-font.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-font.png) ![../../_images/added-fonts.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/added-fonts.png)
    4. In the Font Link window for each font file that you imported in the previous step, select the checkbox and click Apply. After you add all the fonts that you want to link, click OK.
![../../_images/font-checkbox.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/font-checkbox.png) ![../../_images/click-apply.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/click-apply.png)
    5. In the File menu select Save and save the linked font as an ltt file.
![../../_images/save-font.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/save-font.png)
  3. To use the linked font in Kanzi Studio:
    1. In Kanzi Studio import the ltt font you saved in the previous step. See [Importing fonts to a Kanzi Studio project](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing-fonts.html#importing).
In Kanzi Studio, you can see the linked font file in the Library > Font Families.
The linked font file in the `Fonts` directory refers to the font files located in the `<ProjectName>/Application/bin` directory.
![../../_images/linked-font-file-in-library.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/linked-font-file-in-library.png)
    2. In the Node Tree select a Text Block or Text Box node where you want to use a linked font and in the Properties set the Font Family property to that font.
In that Text Block or Text Box node you can now use the glyphs from all font files that you linked in an ltt linked font file.
![../../_images/select-text-block.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-text-block.png) ![../../_images/set-font-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-font-property.png) ![../../_images/linked-font-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/linked-font-in-preview.png)

### Using the iType linked fonts on Android[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing-fonts.html#using-the-itype-linked-fonts-on-android "Link to this heading")
To use the iType linked fonts on Android:
  1. Install the iType font engine for Android. See [Installing the iType font engine for Android](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing-fonts.html#installing-the-itype-font-engine-for-android).
  2. Make sure that the font data you want to use is embedded in the ltt linked font file. See [Using the iType linked fonts](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing-fonts.html#using-the-itype-linked-fonts).
  3. To set your application to load the iType font engine at startup, in `application.cfg` add:

```
FontEngine = IType

```
Copy to clipboard
See [FontEngine](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#fontengine).
  4. To configure the Gradle build to link against the iType font engine Kanzi Engine plugin dll, in the `<ProjectName>/Application/configs/platforms/android_gradle/app/build.gradle` file replace

```
externalNativeBuild {
    cmake {
        arguments "-DKANZI_LINK_FREETYPE=ON"
        arguments "-DKANZI_LINK_ITYPE=OFF"
    }
}

```

with

        arguments "-DKANZI_LINK_FREETYPE=OFF"
        arguments "-DKANZI_LINK_ITYPE=ON"

## Using bitmap fonts[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing-fonts.html#using-bitmap-fonts "Link to this heading")
Use bitmap fonts when you want to use fixed-pixel size text and want to use less resources to render the text. The advantage of bitmap fonts is that rendering bitmap fonts requires less resources than TrueType or linked iType fonts require. The disadvantage of bitmap fonts is that when you scale a bitmap font, the rendered result can be of lower quality.
Kanzi supports the fnt bitmap font format that you can create from a TrueType font using the [AngelCode’s Bitmap Font Generator](http://www.angelcode.com/products/bmfont/). One bitmap font consists of an fnt file and one or more image files.
To use bitmap fonts:
  1. In the AngelCode’s Bitmap Font Generator create a bitmap font file from a TrueType font:
    1. In the **Options** menu select **Font settings** , and in the **Font Settings** window select a TrueType font and glyph rasterization settings that you want to use to create a bitmap font.
![../../_images/bmp-fnt-gen-font-settings.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/bmp-fnt-gen-font-settings.png)
    2. In the main application window select individual characters or character groups for which you want to create a bitmap font.
To keep the size of the bitmap font as small as possible, select only the characters that you want to use in your Kanzi application.
![../../_images/bmp-fnt-gen-char-select.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/bmp-fnt-gen-char-select.png)
    3. In the **Options** menu set the **Export options**.
For example, set:
       * **Width** and **Height** to the dimensions of the font texture so that it is large enough to fit all the glyphs that you selected, but not larger. If you are exporting a large number of glyphs that do not fit on a single texture, the tool creates additional textures. Make sure that you do not create too many textures, because that can decrease the performance of your Kanzi application.
       * **Bit depth** to **8**
       * **Preset** to **White text with alpha**
       * **File format** > **Font descriptor** to **Text**
![../../_images/bmp-fnt-gen-export-options.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/bmp-fnt-gen-export-options.png)
    4. In the **Options** menu select **Save bitmap font as…** , and select a directory and a file name for the bitmap font.
When you save the bitmap font, the application creates a fnt file and exports the selected glyphs to one or more images. This depends on the export settings and the number of glyphs that you selected for that bitmap font.
  2. Use a bitmap font in a Kanzi Studio project:

When you save the bitmap font, the application creates a fnt file and exports the selected glyphs to one or more images. This depends on the export settings and the number of glyphs that you selected for that bitmap font.
  2. Use a bitmap font in a Kanzi Studio project:
    1. In the Kanzi Studio main menu select File > Import > Import Fonts, in the Import Fonts dialog click Browse, select the directory that contains a bitmap font, and import the font. See [Importing fonts to a Kanzi Studio project](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing-fonts.html#importing).

Install Kanzi Documentation MCP server to VS Code.
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use textures to show content in Image nodes, to set the look of textured materials, and to show content in Texture Brush brushes. You can create textures from common image file formats.
See [Images](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/images.html).
In a Kanzi Studio project, image files are located in Library > Resource Files > Images. These image files correspond to files on your hard drive. When you modify a file on the hard drive, Kanzi automatically applies the modifications to the textures generated from that file. If you remove the file from the hard drive, you cannot use the file in your Kanzi project.
![../../_images/resource-files-images-defaulttextureimage.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/resource-files-images-defaulttextureimage.png)
Loading time of images depends on their size and compression:
  * **Image size** defines the time required to load the data into RAM.
  * **Image compression** can reduce the size, but keep in mind that before your application can use the image, it must decompress it, which is often slower than loading the raw data. You can often achieve the fastest start-up times when using Raw image format, where data is loaded into RAM and sent to the GPU memory. See [Image Compression](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/images.html#image-compression).
  * **Texture compression** you can use on devices with GPUs that support the selected compression algorithm. When using compression, the data size is smaller both when loading from kzb file to RAM and when loading from RAM to the GPU memory. Also less GPU memory is reserved. Depending on the target hardware, by using texture compression you can reduce loading times. Before using texture compression, make sure that your target platform supports the texture compression format you selected.
Kanzi supports ASTC, ETC, and BCn compression formats.

metadata.title: Textures (Part 1/7)

content:
Kanzi supports ASTC, ETC, and BCn compression formats.
If your target hardware does not support the selected texture compression algorithm, when you run your Kanzi application on your target device, Kanzi prints a warning message to the log. Kanzi paints black the surfaces where you use compressed texture formats that your target hardware does not support.
See [Compressing textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/compressing-textures.html).

content:
## Texture types[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/textures.html#texture-types "Link to this heading")
These textures are available in Kanzi:  
|  Single textures use a single image for the texture. See [Using single textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-single-textures.html).  |  ![../../_images/single-texture.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/single-texture.png)  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Cubemap textures combine six square-shaped images into one texture to represent reflections of the environment. Each image represents the scenery in one of the six directions along the x, y, and z axes from the viewpoint of the cubemapped object. See [Using cubemap textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-cubemap-textures.html).  |  ![../../_images/cubemap-texture.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/cubemap-texture.png)  |  
|  Volume textures use a single 2D image, made up of many cross-section slices of a 3D shape, to define a 3D volume texture. This technique is often used for effects like smoke, fire, or clouds, where 3D data would be too resource intensive or difficult to generate procedurally. See [Using volume textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-volume-textures.html).  |  ![../../_images/volume-texture.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/volume-texture.png)  |  
|  Use a Render Target Texture to render content to a texture or to apply anti-aliasing to only a part of your application. You can use render target textures like any other texture. For example, you can use it in a Texture Brush or as an image in an Image node. See [Using render target textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-render-target-textures.html) and [Using OpenGL ES 3.0+ in Kanzi](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-opengl-es-30.html).  |  ![../../_images/render-target-texture.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/render-target-texture.png)  |  
|  Use a Cubemap Render Target Texture to render a Cubemap render pass to a cubemap texture. See [Creating cubemap reflections](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/cubemap-render-pass.html).  |  ![../../_images/cubemap-render-target-texture.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/cubemap-render-target-texture.png)  |  
You can use .exr, .dds, and .hdr images with half float and floating point data to bring HDR images to your Kanzi project. See [Setting the color format of textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-opengl-es-30.html#setting-the-color-format-of-textures).

content:
## Setting the image target format[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/textures.html#setting-the-image-target-format "Link to this heading")
When you export your project to a kzb file, Kanzi Studio reads the images in the project using the format of the original image and writes the images to a kzb file in the format you set with the Target Format property for each image.
If the file format of the original image is the same as the format you select in the Target Format property, Kanzi Studio does not modify the image when it writes the image to a kzb file under these conditions:
  * Premultiply Alpha is disabled, or the alpha channel does not need to be premultiplied
To change this setting, in the Project > Properties use the Premultiply Alpha property. You can override this value in the properties of the image file where you want to use a different setting.
![../../_images/premultiply-alpha-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/premultiply-alpha-project.png) ![../../_images/premultiply-alpha-image.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/premultiply-alpha-image.png)
  * Generate Mipmaps is disabled
You can set the value of the Generate Mipmaps property in each image file.
![../../_images/generate-mipmaps-disabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/generate-mipmaps-disabled.png)
  * Round up Image Dimensions to Nearest Power of Two property is disabled
You can set the value of the Round up Image Dimensions to Nearest Power of Two property in the Project > Properties.
When you enable the Round up Image Dimensions to Nearest Power of Two property, Kanzi Studio rounds up the width and height of the images in your project to the nearest power of two during kzb file export. For example, Kanzi Studio exports an image of the size 40 by 30 pixels to the kzb file in the size 64 by 32 pixels.
![../../_images/round-images-to-nearest-power-of-2-disabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/round-images-to-nearest-power-of-2-disabled.png)

metadata.title: Textures (Part 4/7)
metadata.breadcrumb: Working with … > Textures

content:
If your image is in JPEG or PNG format and you do not want Kanzi Studio to modify the image that it exports to a kzb file, in the image Properties enable the Use Original Image property.
![../../_images/use-original-image-enabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/use-original-image-enabled.png)
To set the image target format:
  1. In the Library > Resource Files > Images select the image for which you want to set the target format.
![../../_images/resource-files-images-defaulttextureimage.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/resource-files-images-defaulttextureimage.png)
  2. In the Properties set the Target Format property to the image format you want to use in your Kanzi application.
The format you select is important because this influences the size of the kzb file and the loading time when your Kanzi application loads the image. Make sure that your target device supports the target format you select for the image. See [Images and textures best practices](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/images-and-textures-best-practices.html) and [Compressing textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/compressing-textures.html).
![../../_images/target-format-astc-compression.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/target-format-astc-compression.png)
  3. If the image format you selected in the previous step supports compression, configure the compression scheme you want to use. See [Compressing textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/compressing-textures.html).
![../../_images/astc-block-size.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/astc-block-size.png)
  4. For image formats that support sRGB:
     * If the image contains sRGB color information, set the sRGB Content property to enabled. This is the default setting.
If you disable the sRGB Content property for an image that contains sRGB color information, Kanzi can render the textures that use the image brighter than expected.
     * If the image contains non-color information, such as a normal, roughness, or occlusion map, set the sRGB Content property to disabled.
Textures that contain non-color information are stored in linear format. By disabling the sRGB Content property you set Kanzi to pass the image data to a shader directly, without performing a color space conversion.
![../../_images/srgb-content.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/srgb-content.png)
  5. If you want Kanzi to premultiply the alpha channel in the:
     * Linear color space, set the Linear Premultiply property to enabled.
This is the default value and results in the fewest artifacts in sRGB images.
     * Color space of the image, usually sRGB, set the Linear Premultiply property to disabled.
This can give better results for images created for the standard color workflow.

content:
## Creating a single texture[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-single-textures.html#creating-a-single-texture "Link to this heading")
To create a single texture:
  1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Materials and Textures and select Single Texture.
![../../_images/create-single-texture.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-single-texture.png)
  2. In the Properties set the Image property to the image you want to use for the texture.
Avoid creating mipmaps from .jpeg textures, because the .jpeg image format causes the quality of the mipmaps to degrade.
![../../_images/set-single-texture-image-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-single-texture-image-property.png)
  3. (Optional)
In the Properties set the Texture Settings properties.
Use the Texture Settings properties to control the texture filtering. Start by setting the Mipmap Mode property to the mipmap mode you want to use. Then set the Minification Filter and Magnification Filter properties to Linear. Note that using mipmaps increases the memory use.
Usually the best starting point for setting texture filtering is to set:
     * Minification Filter to Linear
     * Magnification Filter to Linear
     * Mipmap Mode to Nearest. If you are sure that the texture is not minified select Base, otherwise start with Nearest. For example, the default value for a Render Target Texture is Base. With this setting, the texture does not have mipmap levels and the base level is always sampled. See [Using mipmaps](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/using-mipmaps.html).
![../../_images/texture-settings-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-settings-properties.png)
Note that some texture formats are available with OpenGL ES versions higher than 2.0. To set the OpenGL ES version, in the main menu select Project > Properties and in the Properties set the Target Graphics API property.
![../../_images/project-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties.png) ![../../_images/target-graphics-api-opengl-es-30.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/target-graphics-api-opengl-es-30.png)
For example, set the Target Graphics API property to OpenGL ES 3.0, import HDR and floating point images in .dds format, and set the color format of textures. See [Using OpenGL ES 3.0+ in Kanzi](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-opengl-es-30.html).  
| Mipmap Mode  | Nearest sample  | Linear sample  |  
| --- | --- | --- |

metadata.title: Using single textures (Part 2/4)
metadata.breadcrumb: Working with … > Textures > Using single textures

content:
| Mipmap Mode  | Nearest sample  | Linear sample  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Base  |  Number of samples: 1 Uses the nearest pixel in the texture. This combination is equal to point sample. It returns the crudest result of all combinations and can cause aliasing when minified. Use this combination to get a very sharp result when magnifying the texture.  |  Number of samples: 4 Interpolates between four nearest pixels in the texture. Use this combination to magnify gradients. However, do not use it for minification.  |  
| Nearest  |  Number of samples: 1 Helps texture caching and helps reduce aliasing. However, it can produce a sharp transition when the texture is used on a flat surface. Use this combination when you want good performance and cannot afford better quality on your target platform. This combination is usually the fastest.  |  Number of samples: 4 Takes two samples from two mipmap levels and interpolates between these samples. Use this combination as the starting point. This combination is usually the best compromise between quality and performance. If you know there is no minification, you can set Mipmap Mode to Base.  |  
| Linear  |  Number of samples: 2 Takes one sample from two mipmap levels and interpolates between those samples. Use this combination for special effects. For example, to implement the rim light effect.  |  Number of samples: 8 Takes four samples from two mipmap levels and interpolates between these samples. Use this combination when you want the best quality and your platform is powerful enough to effortlessly render the result. This combination has the largest negative impact on performance.  |

# Using cubemap textures[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-cubemap-textures.html#using-cubemap-textures "Link to this heading")

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Cubemap textures combine six square-shaped images into one texture to represent reflections of the environment. Each image represents the scenery in one of the six directions along the x, y, and z axes from the viewpoint of the cubemapped object.
Before you can use a cubemap texture in Kanzi Studio you first have to create the texture images of the six cube faces for the cubemap. You can create the six texture images in the tool where you created the mesh object on which you want to use the cubemap texture, and import the images to Kanzi Studio. See [Importing images](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/importing-images.html).
Make sure that all faces of a cubemap texture use images of the same size and format. When the size and format of the images in a cubemap texture do not match, Kanzi uses the default cubemap texture.
For example, for all faces of a cubemap texture use images that are 256 by 256 pixels large and are 8-bit grayscale.
When the size and format of the images in a cubemap texture do not match, Kanzi Studio uses red type to mark such textures.
![../../_images/cubemap-texture-faces-not-same-size.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/cubemap-texture-faces-not-same-size.png)
## Creating cubemap textures from dds images[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-cubemap-textures.html#creating-cubemap-textures-from-dds-images "Link to this heading")
To create a cubemap texture from a dds image, in the Assets click Import Assets and import a dds image that contains the images for all faces of the cubemap texture.
Kanzi Studio imports the dds image, creates a Cubemap Texture, and sets the faces of the texture to the corresponding images in the dds image.

## Creating cubemap textures[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-cubemap-textures.html#creating-cubemap-textures "Link to this heading")
To create a cubemap texture:
  1. In the Assets, click Import Assets and import images that you want to use as the faces of the cubemap texture. See [Importing images](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/importing-images.html).
![../../_images/assets-import-assets.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/assets-import-assets.png)
  2. In the Library, press `Alt` and right-click Materials and Textures, and select Cubemap Texture.
When you create a cubemap texture, Kanzi Studio marks it with red type because the texture does not yet have textures assigned for each face of the cubemap.
![../../_images/create-a-cubemap-texture.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-a-cubemap-texture.png) ![../../_images/cube-map-texture-red.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/cube-map-texture-red.png)
  3. In the Properties, set the Cubemap Images properties to the images that you want to use for your cubemap texture:
     * NegZ Image to the negative Z-face of the cubemap (the back face)
     * PosZ Image to the positive Z-face of the cubemap (the front face)
     * NegX Image to the negative X-face of the cubemap (the left face)
     * PosX Image to the positive X-face of the cubemap (the right face)
     * NegY Image to the negative Y-face of the cubemap (the bottom face)
     * PosY Image to the positive Y-face of the cubemap (the top face)
Avoid creating mipmaps from JPEG textures, because the JPEG image format causes the quality of the mipmaps to degrade.
![../../_images/cube-map-texture-set-images.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/cube-map-texture-set-images.png)
  4. (Optional)
In the Properties set the Texture Settings properties.
Use the Texture Settings properties to control the texture filtering. Start by setting the Mipmap Mode property to the mipmap mode you want to use. Then set the Minification Filter and Magnification Filter properties to Linear. Note that using mipmaps increases the memory use.
Usually the best starting point for setting texture filtering is to set:
     * Minification Filter to Linear
     * Magnification Filter to Linear
     * Mipmap Mode to Nearest. If you are sure that the texture is not minified select Base, otherwise start with Nearest. For example, the default value for a Render Target Texture is Base. With this setting, the texture does not have mipmap levels and the base level is always sampled. See [Using mipmaps](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/using-mipmaps.html).
![../../_images/texture-settings-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-settings-properties.png)

## Using a cubemap texture as a skybox[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-cubemap-textures.html#using-a-cubemap-texture-as-a-skybox "Link to this heading")
To use a cubemap texture as a skybox:
  1. In the Library > Materials and Textures, press `Alt` and right-click Material Types, and select CubemapSkybox.
Kanzi Studio creates in the Library > Materials and Textures the CubemapSkybox material type and CubemapSkyboxMaterial, which supports showing a cubemap texture as a skybox.
![../../_images/library-create-cubemap-skybox-material-type.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/library-create-cubemap-skybox-material-type.png)
  2. In the Library, select the CubemapSkyboxMaterial material. In the Properties, set the TextureCube property to the cubemap texture that you want to use to render a skybox.
![../../_images/library-cubemap-skybox-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/library-cubemap-skybox-material.png) ![../../_images/properties-cubemap-skybox-my-cubemap-texture.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-cubemap-skybox-my-cubemap-texture.png)
  3. Create a Box or Sphere node that you use to render the skybox. In the Properties, set:
     * Mesh Material to CubemapSkyboxMaterial
     * The size of the node so that it is large enough to fit the content that you want to show inside it:
       * For a Box, set the Width, Height, and Depth properties.
       * For a Sphere, set the Radius property.
     * Generate Mesh Inside Out to enabled
When this property is enabled, Kanzi renders the cubemap texture inside the mesh.
![../../_images/node-tree-box.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-box.png) ![../../_images/properties-box-skybox.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-box-skybox.png)
  4. Position a Camera node inside the node that you created.


When you rotate the camera, in the Preview you can see the cubemap texture rendered as a skybox.
![../../_images/preview-hall-cubemap-texture.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-hall-cubemap-texture.gif)

Volume textures use a single 2D image, made up of many cross-section slices of a 3D shape, to define a 3D volume texture. This technique is often used for effects like smoke, fire, or clouds, where 3D data would be too resource intensive or difficult to generate procedurally.
Before you can create a volume texture in Kanzi Studio you first have to have an image to use in that texture. The image must be made up of vertical slices of the 3D shape, taken at a constant intervals and in stacked in sequence on top of each other. See [Using a volume texture](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-volume-textures.html#using-a-volume-texture).
You can create such a texture image in a third-party tool and import the image to Kanzi Studio. See [Importing images](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/importing-images.html).
## Rendering example using volume textures[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-volume-textures.html#rendering-example-using-volume-textures "Link to this heading")
Below is an example of how volume textures can be used in Kanzi Studio for:
  * Rendering signed distance fields to create a realistic looking surface with accurate ambient occlusion, reflections and soft shadow calculations.
  * Using 3D texture data to raymarch a volume representing density, creating a realistic smoke effect.

Use an environment texture to represent the environment, such as an outdoor scene or an indoor space. You can create an environment texture from an HDR or EXR image:
  * An environment cubemap texture combines six square-shaped images into a texture that represents the environment. See [Using an environment cubemap texture](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-environment-textures.html#using-an-environment-cubemap-texture).
  * An environment lat-long (equirectangular) texture is a single image that represents the environment. See [Using a lat-long environment texture](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-environment-textures.html#using-a-lat-long-environment-texture).

## Using an environment cubemap texture[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-environment-textures.html#using-an-environment-cubemap-texture "Link to this heading")
To use an environment cubemap texture:
  1. Create an environment cubemap texture:
    1. In the Assets click Import Assets and select an HDR or EXR image from which you want to create an environment cubemap texture.
![../../_images/assets-import-assets.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/assets-import-assets.png)
Tip
To create an environment cubemap texture for an HDR or EXR image that you have already imported to your Kanzi Studio project, in the Library > Resource Files > Images press `Alt` and right-click that image and select Environment Cubemap Texture.
![../../_images/create-environment-cubemap-texture-context-menu.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-environment-cubemap-texture-context-menu.png)
    2. In the Create Textures for HDR Images dialog:
      1. Select Environment Cubemap Texture.
![../../_images/create-environment-cubemap-texture-dialog.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-environment-cubemap-texture-dialog.png)
Tip
To create for the image also irradiance and specular cubemap textures that represent the lighting coming from the environment, select Image-Based Lighting Cubemap Textures. See [Using image-based lighting cubemap textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-ibl-textures.html).
      2. (Optional) To manually set the size of the cubemap faces, disable the Automatic setting and set the Cubemap Face Resolution.
For example, to create an environment cubemap texture where the size of each cubemap face is 512 by 512 pixels, set Cubemap Face Resolution to 512.
Kanzi Studio by default creates a cubemap texture where the width and height of each cubemap face is one quarter of the width of the image that you import.
![../../_images/environment-cubemap-face-resolution.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/environment-cubemap-face-resolution.png)
      3. Click Create.
Kanzi Studio imports the image and creates in the Library > Materials and Textures > Textures an environment Cubemap Texture for that image.
Kanzi Studio creates and sets the cubemap face images:
       * NegZ Image to the front face image
       * PosZ Image to the back face image
       * NegX Image to the left face image
       * PosX Image to the right face image
       * NegY Image to the bottom face image
       * PosY Image to the top face image
![../../_images/my-hdr-image-environment.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/my-hdr-image-environment.png) ![../../_images/my-hdr-image-environment-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/my-hdr-image-environment-properties.png) ![../../_images/environment-cubemap-faces.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/environment-cubemap-faces.png)
Tip

content:
Tip
You can restrict the brightness of strongly lit areas in the textures that you create from an HDR image.
To set the maximum brightness level in the cubemap textures that you create from an HDR image:
      1. In the Library > Resource Files > Images, select the image. In the Properties, add the Clamp Pixels property and set it to the value to which you want to restrict the color values in the cubemap face images that you create from that image.
      2. In the Library > Resource Files > Images, press `Alt` and right-click the image and select the cubemap texture that you want to create.
![../../_images/clamp-pixels.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/clamp-pixels.png) ![../../_images/recreate-env-cubemap-textures.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/recreate-env-cubemap-textures.png)
  2. In the Library > Materials and Textures, press `Alt` and right-click Material Types, and select CubemapSkybox.
Kanzi Studio creates in the Library > Materials and Textures the CubemapSkybox material type and CubemapSkyboxMaterial, which supports showing a cubemap texture as a skybox.
![../../_images/library-create-cubemap-skybox-material-type.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/library-create-cubemap-skybox-material-type.png)
  3. In the Library, select the CubemapSkyboxMaterial material. In the Properties, set the TextureCube property to the cubemap texture that you want to use to render a skybox.
![../../_images/library-cubemap-skybox-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/library-cubemap-skybox-material.png) ![../../_images/properties-cubemap-skybox-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-cubemap-skybox-material.png)
  4. Create a Box or Sphere node that you use to render the skybox. In the Properties, set:
     * Mesh Material to CubemapSkyboxMaterial
     * The size of the node so that it is large enough to fit the content that you want to show inside it:
       * For a Box, set the Width, Height, and Depth properties.
       * For a Sphere, set the Radius property.
     * Generate Mesh Inside Out to enabled
When this property is enabled, Kanzi renders the cubemap texture inside the mesh.
![../../_images/node-tree-box.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-box.png) ![../../_images/properties-box-skybox.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-box-skybox.png)
  5. Position a Camera node inside the node that you created.

# Using image-based lighting cubemap textures[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-ibl-textures.html#using-image-based-lighting-cubemap-textures "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)

![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/claude.svg) Connect to Claude
Download and run the Claude mcpb.
Use image-based lighting to light 3D nodes by treating their surrounding environment as a source of lights.
Image-based lighting cubemap textures simulate lighting coming from the environment:
  * **Irradiance cubemap texture** represents the indirect diffuse part of the environment lighting.
A fully diffuse surface is rough and reflects incoming light rays in random directions. For example, rubbery materials have a diffuse surface.
  * **Specular cubemap texture** represents the reflective part of the environment lighting.
A fully reflective surface is smooth and reflects incoming light rays in the same angle as they arrive, like a mirror. For example, metallic materials have a reflective surface.


Each image-based lighting cubemap texture combines six square-shaped images into one texture to represent environment lighting.
Use an environment cubemap texture to render the environment around your 3D content. See [Using environment textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-environment-textures.html).
When you want to create dynamic reflections of the environment on the surface of 3D nodes, use the Cubemap render pass. See [Creating cubemap reflections](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/cubemap-render-pass.html).

metadata.title: Using image-based lighting cubemap textures (Part 1/8)

content:
## Creating image-based lighting cubemap textures[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-ibl-textures.html#creating-image-based-lighting-cubemap-textures "Link to this heading")
To create image-based lighting cubemap textures:
  1. In the Assets, click Import Assets and select an hdr or exr image for which you want to create image-based lighting cubemap textures.
![../../_images/assets-import-assets.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/assets-import-assets.png)
Tip
To create image-based lighting cubemap textures for an hdr or exr image that you have already imported to your Kanzi Studio project, in the Library > Resource Files > Images press `Alt` and right-click that image and select Image-Based Lighting Cubemap Textures.
![../../_images/create-ibl-textures-context-menu.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-ibl-textures-context-menu.png)
  2. In the Create Textures for HDR Images dialog:
    1. Select Image-Based Lighting Cubemap Textures.
![../../_images/create-ibl-textures-dialog.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-ibl-textures-dialog.png)
Tip
To create also an environment cubemap texture for the image, select Environment Cubemap Texture. See [Using environment textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-environment-textures.html).
    2. (Optional) To manually set the size of the cubemap faces, disable the Automatic setting and set the Cubemap Face Resolution.
For example, to create cubemap textures where the size of each cubemap face is 512 by 512 pixels, set Cubemap Face Resolution to 512.
By default, Kanzi Studio creates cubemap textures where the width and height of each cubemap face are 256 pixels, or, if the width of the image that you import is less than 1024 pixels, one quarter of that width.
Increasing the cubemap face resolution increases the cubemap calculation time quadratically.
    3. (Optional) Set the Number of Samples to the number of pixels that you want Kanzi Studio to sample from the image and use to generate the cubemaps.
The more samples, the more accurately the cubemap approximates the environment lighting. Increasing the number of samples increases the cubemap calculation time linearly. The default value of 1024 samples is expected to be enough for most situations. However, for an image that contains very high frequency changes, such as a bright sun, using a higher sample count can reduce the amount of noise in the generated cubemap face images.
    4. Click Create.
Kanzi Studio imports the image and creates in the Library > Materials and Textures > Textures the image-based lighting cubemap textures for that image:
     * <image_name>_irradiance represents the indirect diffuse portion of the environment lighting.
     * <image_name>_specular represents the reflective lighting.

content:
Note
Kanzi Studio stores the generated cubemap faces and roughness mipmaps in cache directories that you typically exclude from version control. When they are missing, such as after a fresh clone or after you import an asset package that does not include them, Kanzi Studio regenerates them from the source image. For this reason, keep the source hdr or exr image in your project and in version control. See [Using version control systems with Kanzi](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/version-control/version-control.html).
Image-based lighting cubemap textures that you created before Kanzi 4.1.0 do not store the information that Kanzi Studio needs to regenerate them. Recreate these textures so that they regenerate correctly.

content:
## Using image-based lighting cubemap textures[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-ibl-textures.html#id1 "Link to this heading")
To use image-based lighting cubemap textures:
  1. In the Library > Materials and Textures, press `Alt` and right-click Material Types and select SmartPhysicallyBased.
Kanzi Studio creates the SmartPhysicallyBased material type and the SmartPhysicallyBasedMaterial material.
This material supports using the features of the Kanzi default physically-based shaders.
![../../_images/library-smart-physically-based-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/library-smart-physically-based-material.png)
  2. Create the 3D content that you want to light by treating their surrounding environment as a source of lights, and set that content to use the SmartPhysicallyBasedMaterial material.
For example, in the Node Tree, create a Sphere node. In the Properties, set the Mesh Material property to SmartPhysicallyBasedMaterial.
![../../_images/sphere-in-node-tree.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/sphere-in-node-tree.png) ![../../_images/sphere-properties-mesh-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/sphere-properties-mesh-material.png)
  3. In the Library > Materials and Textures > Materials, select the SmartPhysicallyBasedMaterial. In the Properties, add the Configuration > Enable Image Based Lighting property and set:
     * Environment Ambient Texture to the irradiance cubemap texture that you want to use for diffuse lighting.
     * Environment Reflection Texture to the specular cubemap texture that you want to use for reflective lighting.
See [Creating image-based lighting cubemap textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-ibl-textures.html#creating-image-based-lighting-cubemap-textures).
![../../_images/properties-add-enable-image-based-lighting.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-add-enable-image-based-lighting.png) ![../../_images/physically-based-material-ibl-textures.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/physically-based-material-ibl-textures.png)
  4. (Optional) In the Properties, add and set:
     * Material > Environment Ambient Factor to set the strength of the irradiance cubemap texture.
     * Material > Environment Reflection Factor to set the strength of the specular cubemap texture.
  5. Use the material properties to control the strength of the reflections on the material surface.
For example, for a metallic-roughness material:
     * Roughness Factor sets the roughness of the material.
When you increase the roughness of a material, the reflections on the material surface get blurrier.
     * Metallic Factor sets the metalness of the material.
When you increase the metalness of a material:
       * Diffuse reflections on the material surface get weaker.
       * Specular reflections on the material surface get stronger.

Use a Render Target Texture to render content to a texture or to apply anti-aliasing to only a part of your application. You can use render target textures like any other texture. For example, you can use it in a Texture Brush or as an image in an Image node.
See [Applying anti-aliasing](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/anti-aliasing.html) and [Textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/textures.html).
For example, if your Kanzi application has more than one scene, you can use render target textures to show the content of other scenes in the current scene.

## Rendering content to a texture[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-render-target-textures.html#rendering-content-to-a-texture "Link to this heading")
To render content to a texture:
  1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Materials and Textures and select Render Target Texture.
![../../_images/create-render-target-texture.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-render-target-texture.png)
  2. In the Node Tree create or select a 2D node the content of which you want to render to a texture.
For example, select a Viewport 2D node that contains the content that you want to render to a texture.
![../../_images/prefab-for-render-target-texture.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/prefab-for-render-target-texture.png)
  3. In the Node Tree select the node that you created or selected in the previous step and in the Properties add and set:
     * Render Target to the Render Target Texture to which you want to render the content of the selected node.
     * Off-Screen Rendering and enable the property.
![../../_images/layer-render-target-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/layer-render-target-property.png)
  4. (Optional) To set Kanzi to render the content to the texture only once, in the Properties add the Caching Mode property and set it to Enabled.
This way you set Kanzi to cache the node, and to keep rendering the node from the cache image. For example, enable caching for a node for which you want Kanzi to create the render target texture only once at application startup. See [Caching 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/caching-2d-nodes.html).
![../../_images/caching-mode-enabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/caching-mode-enabled.png)
  5. Apply the Render Target Texture that you created in the first step to a node where you want to show the content of the node that you created in the second step.
You can use the Render Target Texture in a Texture Brush or as an image in an Image node.
For example:
    1. In the Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click and select Empty Node 2D.
    2. In the Node Tree select the Empty Node 2D node, in the Properties add the Background Brush property, and in the dropdown menu select + Texture Brush.
![../../_images/select-create-texture-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-create-texture-brush.png)
    3. Next to the Background Brush property click ![image0](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/quick-edit-properties.png) and set the Brush Texture property of the Texture Brush to the Render Target Texture you want to show in the Empty Node 2D you created in the first step.
![../../_images/image-property-render-target-texture.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/image-property-render-target-texture.png)

metadata.title: Using render target textures (Part 2/5)
metadata.breadcrumb: Working with … > Textures > Using render target textures

content:
![../../_images/image-property-render-target-texture.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/image-property-render-target-texture.png)
    4. In the Node Tree select the Empty Node 2D, and in the Properties add and set the Layout Width and Layout Height properties to the size in which you want to show the content of the Render Target Texture.
  6. (Optional) In the Library select the Render Target Texture.
In the Properties, you can set the Height and Width of the Render Target, or use the Automatic setting to set the size of the Render Target based on the size of the node where it is used. You cannot yet use this property with a render pass.
![../../_images/render-target-automatic-size.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/render-target-automatic-size.png)
Use the Texture Settings properties to control the texture filtering. Start by setting the Mipmap Mode property to the mipmap mode you want to use. Then set the Minification Filter and Magnification Filter properties to Linear. Note that using mipmaps increases the memory use.
Usually the best starting point for setting texture filtering is to set:
     * Minification Filter to Linear
     * Magnification Filter to Linear
     * Mipmap Mode to Nearest. If you are sure that the texture is not minified select Base, otherwise start with Nearest. For example, the default value for a Render Target Texture is Base. With this setting, the texture does not have mipmap levels and the base level is always sampled. See [Using mipmaps](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/using-mipmaps.html).
![../../_images/texture-settings-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-settings-properties.png)
Note that some texture formats are available with OpenGL ES versions higher than 2.0. To set the OpenGL ES version, in the main menu select Project > Properties and in the Properties set the Target Graphics API property.
![../../_images/project-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/project-properties.png) ![../../_images/target-graphics-api-opengl-es-30.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/target-graphics-api-opengl-es-30.png)
For example, set the Target Graphics API property to OpenGL ES 3.0, import HDR and floating point images in .dds format, and set the color format of textures. See [Using OpenGL ES 3.0+ in Kanzi](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-opengl-es-30.html).  
| Mipmap Mode  | Nearest sample  | Linear sample  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Base  |  Number of samples: 1 Uses the nearest pixel in the texture. This combination is equal to point sample. It returns the crudest result of all combinations and can cause aliasing when minified. Use this combination to get a very sharp result when magnifying the texture.  |  Number of samples: 4 Interpolates between four nearest pixels in the texture. Use this combination to magnify gradients. However, do not use it for minification.  |

metadata.title: Using render target textures (Part 3/5)
metadata.breadcrumb: Working with … > Textures > Using render target textures

content:
| Nearest  |  Number of samples: 1 Helps texture caching and helps reduce aliasing. However, it can produce a sharp transition when the texture is used on a flat surface. Use this combination when you want good performance and cannot afford better quality on your target platform. This combination is usually the fastest.  |  Number of samples: 4 Takes two samples from two mipmap levels and interpolates between these samples. Use this combination as the starting point. This combination is usually the best compromise between quality and performance. If you know there is no minification, you can set Mipmap Mode to Base.  |  
| Linear  |  Number of samples: 2 Takes one sample from two mipmap levels and interpolates between those samples. Use this combination for special effects. For example, to implement the rim light effect.  |  Number of samples: 8 Takes four samples from two mipmap levels and interpolates between these samples. Use this combination when you want the best quality and your platform is powerful enough to effortlessly render the result. This combination has the largest negative impact on performance.  |

Use textured materials to render a texture on a mesh. In Kanzi you can use textured materials with:
  * Single textures use a single image for the texture.
  * Cubemap textures combine six square-shaped images into one texture to represent reflections of the environment. Each image represents the scenery in one of the six directions along the x, y, and z axes from the viewpoint of the cubemapped object.


Physically-based textured materials use multiple textures to define the appearance of the material. See [Creating a physically-based textured material](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/creating-textured-materials.html#creating-a-physically-based-textured-material).

content:
## Creating a textured material[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/creating-textured-materials.html#creating-a-textured-material "Link to this heading")
To create a textured material:
  1. Create a texture. See [Using single textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-single-textures.html).
  2. In the Library > Materials and Textures > Materials, select a material that uses a material type that supports textures. For example, these Kanzi material types support rendering a texture:
     * Textured renders only texture data.
     * ColorTexture renders only colored texture data.
     * SmartVertexPhong is a high-performance material type that uses vertex-based Phong shaders.
     * SmartFragmentPhong is a high-quality, slower-performing material type that uses pixel-based Phong shaders.
     * SmartPhysicallyBased implements physically based rendering (PBR) principles. See [Creating a physically-based textured material](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/creating-textured-materials.html#creating-a-physically-based-textured-material).
See [Using material types](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/using-material-types.html) and [Using smart materials](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/using-smart-materials.html).
For example, use the TexturedMaterial. If your project does not contain that material, in the Library > Materials and Textures press `Alt` and right-click Material Types, and select Textured.
![../../_images/select-textured-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-textured-material.png)
  3. In the Properties, set the Texture property to the texture that you want to use in the material.
![../../_images/set-texture-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-texture-property.png)
  4. In the Node Tree or Prefabs, select the node on which you want to use the textured material. In the Properties, set the Material or Mesh Material property to the textured material.
![../../_images/set-material-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-material-property.png) ![../../_images/preview-textured-material.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-textured-material.png)
  5. (Optional) Set the texture tiling:
    1. In the Library > Materials and Textures > Materials, select the textured material. In the Properties, set the Texture Tiling property X and Y property fields to the number of times that you want to show the texture along the x and y axes.
![../../_images/properties-texture-tiling.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-texture-tiling.png) ![../../_images/preview-texture-tiling-clamp.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-texture-tiling-clamp.png)
    2. If you set the Texture Tiling property fields to values greater than 1, set the texture to repeat along the node that uses the textured material.

metadata.title: Creating textured materials (Part 2/8)
metadata.breadcrumb: Working with … > Textures > Creating textured materials

content:
2. If you set the Texture Tiling property fields to values greater than 1, set the texture to repeat along the node that uses the textured material.
In the Library > Materials and Textures > Textures, select the texture. In the Properties, set the Wrap Mode property to:
       * Repeat to repeat the texture
       * Mirror to repeat the texture, but mirror every other repetition
![../../_images/properties-texture-wrap-mode.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-texture-wrap-mode.png) ![../../_images/preview-texture-tiling-repeat.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-texture-tiling-repeat.png)
  6. (Optional) In the Library > Materials and Textures > Materials, select the textured material. In the Properties, set the Texture Offset property X and Y property fields to the amount by which you want to offset the texture on the surface of the node that uses the textured material.
![../../_images/properties-texture-offset.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/properties-texture-offset.png) ![../../_images/preview-texture-offset.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/preview-texture-offset.png)
