content:
## Adding a resource to a Theme Group manually[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/using-themes.html#adding-a-resource-to-a-theme-group-manually "Link to this heading")
The fastest way to add a resource to a Theme Group is to use in the Node Tree the Add Resources to a Theme Group command. See [Adding resources used in a project to a Theme Group](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/theming-applications.html#adding-resources-used-in-project-to-theme-group).
![../../_images/add-resource-to-theme-group.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-resource-to-theme-group.png)
To add a resource to a Theme Group manually:
  1. In the Library > Themes double-click the Theme Group which contains the Theme to which you want to manually add resources.
Kanzi Studio opens the Theme Group in the Theme Editor.
![../../_images/export-example-library-color.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/export-example-library-color.png)
  2. In the Theme Editor click + Add Resource and select:
     * Create and select the type of resource you want to create.
     * Add Existing and select a resource that already exists in your project.
![../../_images/add-resource.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-resource.png)
  3. Enter a name for the resource ID you want to use for that resource and click OK.
  4. In the Theme Editor in the column of each Theme set resource you want to use for the resource ID you created.
  5. In the Node Tree select the node where you want to use the resource ID you created, in the Properties set the property which points to a resource to < Resource ID >, and enter the resource ID you created in the Theme Editor.


## Deleting resource IDs from a Theme Group[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/using-themes.html#deleting-resource-ids-from-a-theme-group "Link to this heading")
To delete resource IDs from a Theme Group:
  * To delete resource IDs that are not used in the project, click Clean, select the resource IDs you want to delete, and click OK.
![../../_images/delete-unused-resource-ids.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/delete-unused-resource-ids.png)
  * To delete a resource ID, right-click the resource ID and select Delete Resource ID.
  * To delete multiple resource IDs press the `Ctrl` or `Shift` key and select resource IDs you want to delete, and press the `Delete` key.

content:
## Localizing a Theme[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/using-themes.html#localizing-a-theme "Link to this heading")
Kanzi enables you to localize themed applications.
To localize themes:
  1. For each theme the content of which you want to localize, create a prefab from the content that includes the text nodes you want to localize. See [Creating and using a node prefab](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#creating-and-using-a-node-prefab).
![../../_images/table-rpm-gasoline-hybrid-prefabs.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/table-rpm-gasoline-hybrid-prefabs.png)
  2. Localize the text resources:
    1. In the Prefabs select the prefabs you created in the previous step and add their resources to a localization table.
See [Adding resources to a localization table](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/localization/localizing-applications.html#adding-resources-to-a-localization-table).
![../../_images/add-resources-to-localization-table.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-resources-to-localization-table.png) ![../../_images/localization-table-add.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/localization-table-add.png)
    2. In the Library > Localization double-click the localization table you created in the previous step to open it in the Localization Editor, add the locales to which you want to localize themes, and localize the text resources. See [Localizing text resources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/localization/localizing-applications.html#localizing-text-resources).
To add a locale click + Create Locale, enter the name for the locale, and click OK.
![../../_images/localization-editor-with-localized-text.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/localization-editor-with-localized-text.png)
  3. Use Prefab View nodes to show the localized content:
    1. In the Prefabs under the node where you want to show the localized content create a Prefab View node and in the Properties add and set the Prefab Template property to one of the prefabs you created in step 1.
You must use a Prefab View node so that you can dynamically change the prefab that the Prefab View instantiates. See [Prefab Placeholder and Prefab View nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#prefab-placeholder-and-prefab-view-nodes).
![../../_images/table-rpm-prefab-view-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/table-rpm-prefab-view-in-project.png) ![../../_images/displayed-prefab-in-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/displayed-prefab-in-properties.png)
    2. In the Prefabs right-click the Prefab View node you created in the previous step and select Add Resources to a Theme Group.
![../../_images/add-resource-to-theme-group.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-resource-to-theme-group.png)
    3. In the Add Resources to a Theme Group window:

## Using themes in multiple Kanzi Studio projects combined into a Kanzi application[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/using-themes.html#using-themes-in-multiple-ks-projects-combined-into-a-k-application "Link to this heading")
To use themes when you combine multiple Kanzi Studio projects into a Kanzi application, you must make the theme groups accessible to the Screen node of the main project of your application in one of these ways:
  * Define the theme groups in the main project of your application.
  * Merge the theme groups from referenced projects to the main project which contains the Screen node. You can then use resource IDs to access the resources in the theme groups from the referenced projects. See [Merging projects](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/merging-projects.html).
  * Contact the Rightware support team and request the Kanzi Engine plugin which enables you to use theming across multiple Kanzi Studio projects and kzb files. See [Submitting a support request](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/technical-support.html#submitting-a-support-request).

Use trajectories as paths along which Trajectory Layout 3D and Trajectory Layout 2D nodes arrange their child nodes, and along which Trajectory List Box 3D nodes move their items.
Trajectories are paths in 3D space. See [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html) and [Using the Trajectory List Box 3D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html).
Kanzi Studio comes with these trajectory types:
  * Use an Angle Trajectory to create a path where two straight lines form an angle in 3D space.

![../../_images/ellipse.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/ellipse.png)
  * Use a Line Trajectory to create a path with a single straight line in 3D space.
See [Using line trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-line-trajectories.html).
![../../_images/line.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/line.png)

## Creating an angle trajectory[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-angle-trajectories.html#creating-an-angle-trajectory "Link to this heading")
To create an angle trajectory:
  1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Trajectories and select Angle Trajectory.
![../../_images/create-angle-trajectory.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-angle-trajectory.png)
  2. In the Properties set these properties:
     * Normal to set the position of the trajectory in 3D space.
For example:
       * To set the trajectory parallel to the x axis, set X to 1, and Y and Z property fields to 0.
       * To set the trajectory parallel to the y axis, set Y to 1, and X and Z property fields to 0.
       * To set the trajectory diagonally into I and II, and VII and VIII octants, set X to 1, Y to -1, and the Z property field to 0.
       * To set the trajectory diagonally into II and III, and V and VIII octants, set Y and Z to 1, and the X property field to 0.
     * Length to set the length of the trajectory.
     * Angle to set the size of the angle in degrees.
![../../_images/angle-trajectory-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/angle-trajectory-properties.png)
  3. To take the trajectory into use, in the Node Tree select a Trajectory Layout or a Trajectory List Box 3D node and in the Properties set the Trajectory property to the trajectory you want to use. See [Using the Trajectory List Box 3D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html) and [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html).


##  Angle Trajectory property types[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-angle-trajectories.html#angle-trajectory-property-types "Link to this heading")
For a list of the available property types for angle trajectories, see [Angle Trajectory](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/angle-trajectory-reference.html).

## Creating an ellipse trajectory[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-ellipse-trajectories.html#creating-an-ellipse-trajectory "Link to this heading")
To create an ellipse trajectory:
  1. In the Library right-click Trajectories and select Create > Ellipse Trajectory.
![../../_images/create-ellipse-trajectory.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-ellipse-trajectory.png)
  2. In the Properties set these properties:
     * Normal to set the position of the trajectory in 3D space.
For example:
       * To set the trajectory parallel to the x axis, set X to 1, and Y and Z property fields to 0.
       * To set the trajectory parallel to the y axis, set Y to 1, and X and Z property fields to 0.
       * To set the trajectory diagonally into I and II, and VII and VIII octants, set X to 1, Y to -1, and the Z property field to 0.
       * To set the trajectory diagonally into II and III, and V and VIII octants, set Y and Z to 1, and the X property field to 0.
     * Radius A to set the size of the ellipse trajectory on the X axis.
     * Radius B to set the size of the ellipse trajectory on the Y axis.
     * Angle to set the starting point of the ellipse trajectory.
![../../_images/ellipse-trajectory-properties.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/ellipse-trajectory-properties.png)
  3. To take the trajectory into use, in the Node Tree select a Trajectory Layout or a Trajectory List Box 3D node and in the Properties set the Trajectory property to the trajectory you want to use. See [Using the Trajectory List Box 3D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html) and [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html).

## Creating a spiral trajectory[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-spiral-trajectories.html#creating-a-spiral-trajectory "Link to this heading")
To create a spiral trajectory:
  1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Trajectories and select Spiral Trajectory.
![../../_images/create-spiral-trajectory.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-spiral-trajectory.png)
  2. In the Properties set these properties:
     * Normal to set the position of the trajectory in 3D space.
For example:
       * To set the trajectory parallel to the x axis, set X to 1, and Y and Z property fields to 0.
       * To set the trajectory parallel to the y axis, set Y to 1, and X and Z property fields to 0.
       * To set the trajectory diagonally into I and II, and VII and VIII octants, set X to 1, Y to -1, and the Z property field to 0.
       * To set the trajectory diagonally into II and III, and V and VIII octants, set Y and Z to 1, and the X property field to 0.
     * Start Radius to set the radius of the starting point of the spiral.
     * End Radius to set the radius of the endpoint of the spiral.
     * Height to set the height of the spiral.
     * Revolutions to set the amount of revolutions in the spiral.
  3. To take the trajectory into use, in the Node Tree select a Trajectory Layout or a Trajectory List Box 3D node and in the Properties set the Trajectory property to the trajectory you want to use. Use a Spline Trajectory to import a trajectory defined by a set of points and control points in 3D space you created in a third-party tool.
Use trajectories as paths along which Trajectory Layout 3D and Trajectory Layout 2D nodes arrange their child nodes, and along which Trajectory List Box 3D nodes move their items.
You can import and convert curves, including NURBS curves, to Kanzi splines from .fbx files. Make sure that your third-party software exports splines as curves. See [Adjusting a spline created from a NURBS curve](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-spline-trajectories.html#adjusting-a-spline-created-from-a-nurbs-curve).
## Creating a spline trajectory[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-spline-trajectories.html#creating-a-spline-trajectory "Link to this heading")
To create a spline trajectory:
  1. Select File > Import > Import 3D Assets and select the .fbx file containing the spline you want to use for a trajectory.
![../../_images/import-3d-assets.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/import-3d-assets.png)
  2. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Trajectories and select Spline Trajectory.
![../../_images/create-spline-trajectory.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-spline-trajectory.png)
  3. In the Properties set the Spline property to the spline you imported.
  4. To take the trajectory into use, in the Node Tree select a Trajectory Layout or a Trajectory List Box 3D node and in the Properties set the Trajectory property to the trajectory you want to use. See [Using the Trajectory List Box 3D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html) and [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html).

## Adjusting a spline created from a NURBS curve[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-spline-trajectories.html#adjusting-a-spline-created-from-a-nurbs-curve "Link to this heading")
When you use a NURBS curve for a spline trajectory you can adjust the number of subdivisions when importing the NURBS curve to Kanzi Studio. Kanzi uses the value you provide to tesselate the NURBS curve as a Kanzi spline. See [Using the Trajectory List Box 3D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html) and [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html).
To adjust a spline created from a NURBS curve:
  1. In the Library > Resource Files > 3D Assets select the .fbx file that contains the NURBS curve you are using for a spline trajectory.
  2. In the Properties set the Curve Tesselation Detail property to the number of subdivisions in the NURBS curve you want to use.
The default value is 16. Set the property to different values to find the result that suits you best.
  3. In the Library > Resource Files > 3D Assets right-click the .fbx file that contains the NURBS curve and select Clean Import 3D Asset File.
  4. In the Library > Trajectories select the spline trajectory that uses the NURBS curve you imported and in the Properties set the Spline property to the spline you imported.


##  Spline Trajectory property types[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-spline-trajectories.html#spline-trajectory-property-types "Link to this heading")
For a list of the available property types for spline trajectories, see [Spline Trajectory](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/node-and-resource-reference/spline-trajectory-reference.html).

content:
## Creating a Trajectory Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html#creating-a-trajectory-layout-node "Link to this heading")
To create a Trajectory Layout node:
  1. In the Node Tree, press `Alt` and right-click the node where you want to create a Trajectory Layout node and select either Trajectory Layout 3D, or Trajectory Layout 2D.
![../../_images/node-tree-create-trejectory-layout-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-create-trejectory-layout-2d.png)
You can create a 3D node only in a 3D node, such as the Scene node, and a 2D node only in a 2D node.
Tip
To see the trajectory, in the Preview click ![image-analyze-off](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/analyze-off.png) to enter the Analyze mode, right-click ![image-analyze-on](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/analyze-on.png), and select Debug objects.
![../../_images/visualize-mode-debug-objects.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/visualize-mode-debug-objects.png)
  2. In the Node Tree, add child nodes to the layout that you created in the previous step.
For example, if you created a Trajectory Layout 3D node, add several Sphere nodes. If you created a Trajectory Layout 2D node, add several Image nodes.
![../../_images/node-tree-trajectory-layout-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-trajectory-layout-2d.png)
As you add child nodes, the Trajectory Layout node positions them along the trajectory used by the Trajectory Layout node.
![../../_images/trajectory-layout-element-position.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout-element-position.gif)
  3. (Optional)
Kanzi Studio creates and uses a circle trajectory by default. You can use an angle, arc, circle, ellipse, line, rectangle, spiral, spline, or a trapezoid trajectory. See [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html).
![../../_images/trajectory-layout-types.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout-types.gif)


## Stretching the trajectory to fill the layout[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html#stretching-the-trajectory-to-fill-the-layout "Link to this heading")
By default, the size of the trajectory used by a Trajectory Layout node determines the amount of space that the trajectory occupies in the layout. For example, in a Circle Trajectory, the Radius property determines the size of the trajectory.
To stretch the trajectory to fill the layout:
  1. Select a Trajectory Layout node.
  2. In the Properties, add and enable the Trajectory Layout > Stretch property.

![../../_images/trajectory-layout-stretch.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout-stretch.gif)

## Adjusting the distance between items in a Trajectory Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html#adjusting-the-distance-between-items-in-a-trajectory-layout-node "Link to this heading")
A Trajectory Layout node automatically calculates the distance between its child nodes.
To adjust the distance between the child nodes in a Trajectory Layout node:
  1. Select a Trajectory Layout node.
  2. In the Properties, add and set the Trajectory Layout > Override Distance property.

![../../_images/trajectory-layout-override-distance.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout-override-distance.gif)
## Adjusting the position of items in a Trajectory Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html#adjusting-the-position-of-items-in-a-trajectory-layout-node "Link to this heading")
By default, a Trajectory Layout node arranges its child nodes from the start of the trajectory spline.
To adjust the starting position of the Trajectory Layout node child nodes on the trajectory:
  1. Select a Trajectory Layout node.
  2. In the Properties, add and set the Trajectory Layout > Start Offset property.

![../../_images/trajectory-layout-start-offset.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout-start-offset.gif)

To set the appearance of 2D nodes:
  * You can fill 2D nodes with a solid color, a texture, or a material. See [Adjusting the appearance of 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html).
![../../_images/color-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/color-brush.png) ![../../_images/texture-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-brush.png) ![../../_images/material-brush.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/material-brush.png)
  * You can apply a post-processing effect to a 2D node. See [Effects for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/2d-effects.html).
![../../_images/blur-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/blur-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/mask-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/mask-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/outline-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/outline-effect-2d.png) ![../../_images/shadow-effect-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/shadow-effect-2d.png)
  * You can rotate a 2D node around all three axes to create a 3D perspective effect. See [Creating a 3D perspective effect for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/setting-the-perspective.html).
![../../_images/perspective-transformation-visualization.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/perspective-transformation-visualization.png)
  * You can apply custom rendering to 2D nodes to create post-processing effects. See [Applying custom rendering to 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/applying-custom-rendering.html).
![../../_images/texture-grayscale.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/texture-grayscale.png)
  * You can render a 2D node as pixel-perfect. See [Rendering pixel-perfect 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/2d-content/adjusting-the-appearance.html#rendering-pixel-perfect-2d-nodes).

Use the Trajectory List Box 3D node to create scrollable lists of items arranged along a trajectory in 3D space.
![../../_images/trajectory-list-box-3d.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-list-box-3d.gif)
Kanzi Studio comes with several types of trajectories. When you need a different type of trajectory, create a spline trajectory in a third-party tool and import it to your Kanzi Studio project. See [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html).
The items in a Trajectory List Box 3D node appear in the order that you add them to the Trajectory List Box 3D node. To select an item in a Trajectory List Box 3D node, click or tap that item.
The size of the trajectory defines the interactive area for click and drag gestures. If the trajectory is too small, the user is not able to select the items in the Trajectory List Box 3D node. To avoid this, make sure that the trajectory is large enough. See [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html).
The Trajectory List Box 3D nodes that you create in Kanzi Studio are focus scopes and handle the key focus and key input by default. See [Handling the key focus in a List Box node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/list-box-nodes.html#lb-handling-key-focus).
Note

content:
The Trajectory List Box 3D nodes that you create in Kanzi Studio are focus scopes and handle the key focus and key input by default. See [Handling the key focus in a List Box node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/list-box-nodes.html#lb-handling-key-focus).
Note
Items in all list box nodes (Grid List Box nodes and Trajectory List Box 3D node) are not its child nodes, even though in Kanzi Studio it seems so when you add items to a list box. Because list box items are not child nodes of a list box, you cannot refer to these items from outside of a list box using paths or aliases. If you need to refer from a list box item to an object outside of a list box, use bindings and aliases. See [Binding to properties outside of a Grid List Box node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html#binding) and [Navigating to Page nodes from a Trajectory List Box 3D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#navigating).
Trajectory List Box 3D node is an interactive version of the Trajectory Layout 3D node. See [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html).
For an example of how to use the Trajectory List Box 3D node to create an interactive scrollable list of items, see the [Trajectory list box example](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#trajecto).

To create a Trajectory List Box 3D node:
  1. In the Node Tree, press `Alt` and right-click the 3D node where you want to create a Trajectory List Box 3D node and select Trajectory List Box 3D.
For example, create a Trajectory List Box 3D node in the Scene node.

Tip

![../../_images/visualize-mode-debug-objects.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/visualize-mode-debug-objects.png)
  2. In the Node Tree, add items to the Trajectory List Box 3D node.
Use a data source to add items to a List Box node. See [Using a data source](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/data-sources/using-a-data-source.html).
For example, to create an album list, add several nodes that represent the albums in the list. See [Using the List Box Item Container prefabs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/using-list-box-item-containers.html).
As you add items, the Trajectory List Box 3D node arranges them along the trajectory used by the Trajectory List Box 3D node.
To browse the items in a Trajectory List Box 3D node, in the Preview, click and drag the items in the Trajectory List Box 3D node.
![../../_images/trajectory-list-box-3d-add-item.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-list-box-3d-add-item.png) ![../../_images/trajectory-list-box-3d-with-items-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-list-box-3d-with-items-in-project.png) ![../../_images/trajectory-list-box-with-items-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-list-box-with-items-in-preview.png)
  3. (Optional)
Kanzi Studio creates and uses a circle trajectory by default. You can use an angle, arc, circle, ellipse, line, rectangle, spiral, spline, or a trapezoid trajectory. See [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html).

## Fine-tuning the mechanics of a Trajectory List Box 3D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#fine-tuning-the-mechanics-of-a-trajectory-list-box-3d-node "Link to this heading")
You can fine-tune the mechanics of a Trajectory List Box 3D node. You can set the list box to:
  * **Bring the selected item to the center of the list box.**
To set the list box to bring the item to the center of the list box object when the user clicks that item, set the Selection Behavior property to Bring Center. Use the Cursor Offset property to set the direction in which selection moves the items in the list box. Use the Cursor Offset property to set the direction in which selection moves the items in the list box.
![../../_images/selection-behavior.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/selection-behavior.gif)
  * **Show items from the beginning after reaching the last item.**
To start showing the items in a Trajectory List Box 3D from the beginning after reaching the last item, enable the Looping property.
![../../_images/loop-along-x.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/loop-along-x.gif)
  * **Use either x or y axis for scrolling the items in the list box.**
To set the scrolling axis, set the Allowed Scroll Axis property.
For example, to set the list box so that the user can scroll along the y axis to browse the items, set the Allowed Scroll Axis property to Y axis.
  * **Reverse the scrolling direction.**
To reverse the direction in which the list box scrolls when the user clicks and drags the items, add and enable the Reversed Scrolling property.
  * **Change the appearance of the items based on their location on the trajectory.**
To set how the items look at different points on the trajectory, use the Item Area Begin and Item Area End properties. You use the Item Area Begin and Item Area End properties to set the value of the Visible Amount In Parent property, which sets shaders to change the appearance of an item based on the location of that object in the list box.
For example, if you use the Visible Amount In Parent property to gradually change the visibility of an item, set the Item Area Begin property to a larger value and the Item Area End property to a smaller value. This way you limit the area where that item is visible.

## Nesting Trajectory List Box 3D nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#nesting-trajectory-list-box-3d-nodes "Link to this heading")
You can nest Trajectory List Box 3D nodes to create a Trajectory List Box 3D node within a Trajectory List Box 3D node, each of which you can scroll independently. For example, you can create a Trajectory List Box 3D which you use to scroll on a circle trajectory Trajectory Layout 3D nodes which contain sets of albums.
In a Trajectory List Box 3D node, use the Allowed Scroll Axis property to set the axis on which the user can scroll the list.
To nest Trajectory List Box 3D nodes:
  1. Create a Trajectory List Box 3D node. See [Creating a Trajectory List Box 3D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#creating-tlb-3d-node).
For example, use the circle trajectory to create a path in the shape of a circle. See [Using circle trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-circle-trajectories.html).
![../../_images/create-trajectory-list-box-3d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-trajectory-list-box-3d.png) ![../../_images/circle-trajectory-for-nested.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/circle-trajectory-for-nested.png)
  2. Select the Trajectory List Box 3D node that you created in the previous step. In the Properties, set the Allowed Scroll Axis property to the axis on which you want that node to scroll.
For example, to set the Trajectory List Box 3D node to scroll on the x axis, set the Allowed Scroll Axis property to X axis.
![../../_images/use-circle-trajectory.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/use-circle-trajectory.png)
  3. Create the Trajectory List Box 3D node that you want to nest in the Trajectory List Box 3D node that you created in the previous step.
For example, if you want to create several nested Trajectory List Box 3D nodes of albums:
    1. In the Prefabs, create a Trajectory List Box 3D node.
The Trajectory List Box 3D node arranges its items along a circle trajectory by default.
    2. In the Properties, set the Allowed Scroll Axis property to X axis.
![../../_images/trajectory-list-box-prefab.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-list-box-prefab.png) ![../../_images/use-circle-trajectory.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/use-circle-trajectory.png)
  4. In the Node Tree, add items to the Trajectory List Box 3D node.
For example, from the Prefabs, drag several Trajectory List Box 3D prefabs that represent the album lists. In each nested Trajectory List Box 3D node, add items that represent the albums in each list.
You can add items to a Trajectory List Box 3D using a data source. See [Using a data source](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/data-sources/using-a-data-source.html).

## Binding to properties outside of a Trajectory List Box 3D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#binding-to-properties-outside-of-a-trajectory-list-box-3d-node "Link to this heading")
Use an alias when you want to bind a property of a list box item to a property of a node outside of the list box.
For example, if you have a Grid List Box 3D or a Trajectory List Box 3D node with a Text Block 3D node item and want to set the Text property value of the Text Block 3D node to a value of an Empty Node 3D node property that is not in the list box:
![../../_images/binding-outside-a-list-box---structure.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/binding-outside-a-list-box---structure.png)
  1. In the Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click the nodes that contain the property to which you want to bind and select Alias. See [Using aliases](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/aliases/using-aliases.html).
For example, create an alias for the Empty Node 3D node.
  2. In the Dictionaries make sure that the aliases you created are in the resource dictionary that the list box node can access.
For example, place all aliases to the resource dictionary of the Screen node, or create a resource dictionary in the list box node and place the aliases to that resource dictionary. See [Using resource dictionaries](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/resources/using-resource-dictionaries.html).
  3. Create the binding:
    1. In the Node Tree select the node inside the list box node from which you want to bind to a node outside of the list box node.
    2. In the Properties click + Add Binding and create the binding using the alias to bind to the property in a node outside of the list box node.
For example, in the Text Block 3D node create a binding to the Empty Node 3D node using the alias you created in the first step. See [Bindings expressions reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/reference-for-bindings-expressions.html).
For example, use this binding expression:

```
{#Empty Node 3D/TextConcept.Text}

```
Copy to clipboard
The Text property in the Text Block 3D node gets the value of the Text property from the Empty Node 3D node.
    3. Click Save.

## Navigating to Page nodes from a Trajectory List Box 3D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#navigating-to-page-nodes-from-a-trajectory-list-box-3d-node "Link to this heading")
Note
The Page and Page Host nodes are deprecated. Use the Activity and Activity Host nodes to build navigable UIs for your application. See [Activities](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/activities/activities.html).
Use an alias when you want to navigate to a Page node from a node that is inside a list box node. For example, if you use a Grid List Box or a Trajectory List Box 3D node to create an address book and want to show the content of an address book entry in a Page node.
To navigate to Page nodes from a list box node:
  1. In the Node Tree press `Alt` and right-click each Page node to which you want to navigate to and select Alias. Kanzi Studio creates an alias that points to the node from which you created it, and places the alias to the nearest resource dictionary.
![../../_images/create-alias.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-alias.png)
  2. In the Dictionaries make sure that the aliases you created are in the resource dictionary that the list box node can access.
For example, place all aliases to the resource dictionary of the Screen node, or create a resource dictionary in the list box node and place the aliases to that resource dictionary. See [Using resource dictionaries](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/resources/using-resource-dictionaries.html).
![../../_images/aliases-in-context-resources.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/aliases-in-context-resources.png)
  3. Add and set the Navigate to Page action:
    1. In the Node Tree in the list box node select the node that contains the trigger that you want to use to navigate to one of the Page nodes for which you created the alias in the first step.
![../../_images/select-button.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/select-button.png)
    2. In the Node Components > Triggers press `Alt` and right-click the trigger that you want to use to navigate to the Page node, and create a Navigate to Page action.
![../../_images/add-navigate-to-page-action.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-navigate-to-page-action.png)
    3. In the Navigate to Page action set the Target Item property to the alias of the Page node to which you want to navigate.
All aliases start with a # sign.
![../../_images/navigate-to-car-page.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/navigate-to-car-page.png)


In the Preview when you click the node that contains the Navigate to Page action, you activate the Page node selected in the action.

## Reacting when the user interacts with a Trajectory List Box 3D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#reacting-when-the-user-interacts-with-a-trajectory-list-box-3d-node "Link to this heading")
Use the List Box triggers to react when the user interacts with a Trajectory List Box 3D node. For example, you can set the appearance of a Trajectory List Box 3D when the user scrolls that list box.
You can use these List Box triggers with a Trajectory List Box 3D node:  
| Name  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| List Box: Item Loaded  |  List Box: Item Loaded trigger is set off when an item in a list box is created and loaded to the working memory. To set how many items around the visible items you want to keep loaded in the working memory at a time, use the Keep Alive Item Count property.  |  
| List Box: Item Selected  | List Box: Item Selected trigger is set off when the user selects an item in a list box.  |  
| List Box: Item Unloaded  |  List Box: Item Unloaded trigger is set off when an item in a list box is unloaded from the working memory. To set how many items around the visible items you want to keep loaded in the working memory at a time, use the Keep Alive Item Count property.  |  
| List Box: Scroll Finished  | List Box: Scroll Finished trigger is set off when the scrolling of a list box ends.  |  
| List Box: Scroll Started  | List Box: Scroll Started trigger is set off when the scrolling of a list box starts.  |  
| List Box: Scrolled  | List Box: Scrolled trigger is set of whenever a list box scrolls.  |  
| List Box: Target Changed  |  List Box: Target Changed trigger is set off when the scroll target of a list box changes. For example, the scroll target changes when the user selects a list box item and the list box scrolls to bring that item to the center of the list box area.  |  
| List Box: User Scroll Finished  | List Box: User Scroll Finished trigger is set off when the user stops scrolling a list box.  |  
| List Box: User Scroll Started  | List Box: User Scroll Started trigger is set off when the user starts to scroll a list box.  |  
To use the List Box triggers with a Trajectory List Box 3D node:
  1. Create a Trajectory List Box 3D node and add items to it. See [Creating a Trajectory List Box 3D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#creating-tlb-3d-node).
![../../_images/trajectory-list-box-3d-with-items-in-project.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-list-box-3d-with-items-in-project.png) ![../../_images/trajectory-list-box-with-items-in-preview.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-list-box-with-items-in-preview.png)
  2. Define the behavior that you want to set with the List Box triggers.

2. Define the behavior that you want to set with the List Box triggers.
For example, create a state manager where you define the states which set the appearance of the Trajectory List Box 3D node when the List Box: Scroll Started and List Box: Scroll Finished triggers are set off. See [Creating a state manager](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/using-state-managers.html#creating-a-state-manager).

For example, select the State Manager: Go to State action. In the action, set the State property to the state that sets the appearance of the Trajectory List Box 3D node when the List Box: Scroll Started trigger is set off.

## Controlling whether a Trajectory List Box 3D node is in use[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#controlling-whether-a-trajectory-list-box-3d-node-is-in-use "Link to this heading")
To control whether a Trajectory List Box 3D node is in use, use the Input > Enabled property. A disabled Trajectory List Box 3D node does not react to user input. When you disable a Trajectory List Box 3D node, Kanzi stops ongoing gestures and preserves the selected item and scroll position of that Trajectory List Box 3D node.
When you disable the Enabled property of a node, you effectively disable that node and its descendant nodes in the same overlay focus scope.
To observe whether a node is effectively enabled, use the Input > Effectively Enabled property in a state manager or a binding. For example, to visually indicate to the user whether a node is in use, create a state manager and use the Effectively Enabled property as its controller property.
See [Controlling how a node reacts to input](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#controlling-how-a-node-reacts-to-input).
## Enabling the double-click gesture for Trajectory List Box items[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#enabling-the-double-click-gesture-for-trajectory-list-box-items "Link to this heading")
When you add to a List Box node items that support the double-click gesture, you must enable the double-click gesture for those items in the List Box Item Container prefab.
To learn how to enable the double-click gesture for a node, see [Enabling the multi-click gesture for a node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/multi-click-manipulator.html#enabling-the-multi-click-gesture-for-a-node).
To enable the double-click gesture for List Box items:
  1. Create a List Box Item Container prefab and set it as the Item Container Template of the List Box node. See [Creating a List Box Item Container prefab](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/using-list-box-item-containers.html#create-list-box-item-container).
  2. In the Prefabs, select the List Box Item Container prefab. In the Properties, add and enable the Input > Double-Click Enabled property.
When you enable the Double-Click Enabled property, Kanzi installs in the List Box Item Container prefab a multi-click manipulator that generates double-click messages.
![../../_images/double-click-enabled.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/double-click-enabled.png)

## Trajectory list box example[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html#trajectory-list-box-example "Link to this heading")
This example shows the use of the Trajectory List Box 3D node to create an interactive scrollable list of items. The example implements a simple gallery of photos with a selection effect using an animation.
The Trajectory List Box 3D node, its Circle Trajectory, content shown in the Trajectory List Box 3D, and animation that highlights the centered photo are created in Kanzi Studio. The point of time at which a highlight-animation is launched is defined based on the scroll speed and focused item data available from the user input events that the trajectory list box component produces.
The Trajectory List Box 3D node in the example uses these features:
  * Looping. You can clamp the items in the Trajectory List Box 3D node to the defined trajectory start and end or to transition between the start and end positions, as in this example, with the Looping property.
  * Trajectory. To use a trajectory for the Trajectory List Box 3D, you need to create it in the Library > Trajectories. You can create circle and line trajectories in Kanzi Studio. To use a spline trajectory, create a spline in a third-party tool, import it, and add the spline as a Spline Trajectory. See [Using circle trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-circle-trajectories.html), [Using line trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-line-trajectories.html), and [Using spline trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-spline-trajectories.html). You can customize the trajectory by adding and setting trajectory properties such as Item Area Begin, Item Area End, Cursor Offset, and Override Distance.
  * **Selection and target behavior**. Selection and target events are handled separately. The target changed message is generated at the moment the user releases the pointer. It contains the information on the item that is brought to the center with the current trajectory movement. The selection message is generated when a user selects an item by clicking or tapping it. You can select the Bring Center selection behavior in Kanzi Studio. You can define more actions for the target and selection events for any member of the Trajectory List Box 3D, or even the trajectory list box component itself, by setting invoked actions for List Box: Target Changed or List Box: Item Selected triggers.

content:
## Creating a trapezoid trajectory[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trapezoid-trajectories.html#creating-a-trapezoid-trajectory "Link to this heading")
To create a trapezoid trajectory:
  1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Trajectories and select Trapezoid Trajectory.
![../../_images/create-trapezoid-trajectory.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-trapezoid-trajectory.png)
  2. In the Properties set these properties:
     * Normal to set the position of the trajectory in 3D space.
For example:
       * To set the trajectory parallel to the x axis, set X to 1, and Y and Z property fields to 0.
       * To set the trajectory parallel to the y axis, set Y to 1, and X and Z property fields to 0.
       * To set the trajectory diagonally into I and II, and VII and VIII octants, set X to 1, Y to -1, and the Z property field to 0.
       * To set the trajectory diagonally into II and III, and V and VIII octants, set Y and Z to 1, and the X property field to 0.
     * Length to set the length of the base of the trajectory.
     * Back Length to set the length and angle of the non-parallel sides of the trajectory.
     * Depth to set the depth of the trajectory.
     * Smoothness to set the roundness of the angles in the trajectory.
  3. To take the trajectory into use, in the Node Tree select a Trajectory Layout or a Trajectory List Box 3D node and in the Properties set the Trajectory property to the trajectory you want to use. See [Using the Trajectory List Box 3D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html) and [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html).

## Creating a Trajectory Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html#creating-a-trajectory-layout-node "Link to this heading")
To create a Trajectory Layout node:
  1. In the Node Tree, press `Alt` and right-click the node where you want to create a Trajectory Layout node and select either Trajectory Layout 3D, or Trajectory Layout 2D.
![../../_images/node-tree-create-trejectory-layout-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-create-trejectory-layout-2d.png)
You can create a 3D node only in a 3D node, such as the Scene node, and a 2D node only in a 2D node.
Tip
To see the trajectory, in the Preview click ![image-analyze-off](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/analyze-off.png) to enter the Analyze mode, right-click ![image-analyze-on](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/analyze-on.png), and select Debug objects.
![../../_images/visualize-mode-debug-objects.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/visualize-mode-debug-objects.png)
  2. In the Node Tree, add child nodes to the layout that you created in the previous step.
For example, if you created a Trajectory Layout 3D node, add several Sphere nodes. If you created a Trajectory Layout 2D node, add several Image nodes.
![../../_images/node-tree-trajectory-layout-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-trajectory-layout-2d.png)
As you add child nodes, the Trajectory Layout node positions them along the trajectory used by the Trajectory Layout node.
![../../_images/trajectory-layout-element-position.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout-element-position.gif)
  3. (Optional)
Kanzi Studio creates and uses a circle trajectory by default. You can use an angle, arc, circle, ellipse, line, rectangle, spiral, spline, or a trapezoid trajectory. See [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html).
![../../_images/trajectory-layout-types.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout-types.gif)


## Stretching the trajectory to fill the layout[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html#stretching-the-trajectory-to-fill-the-layout "Link to this heading")
By default, the size of the trajectory used by a Trajectory Layout node determines the amount of space that the trajectory occupies in the layout. For example, in a Circle Trajectory, the Radius property determines the size of the trajectory.
To stretch the trajectory to fill the layout:
  1. Select a Trajectory Layout node.
  2. In the Properties, add and enable the Trajectory Layout > Stretch property.

![../../_images/trajectory-layout-stretch.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout-stretch.gif)

A Trajectory Layout node automatically calculates the distance between its child nodes.
To adjust the distance between the child nodes in a Trajectory Layout node:
  1. Select a Trajectory Layout node.
  2. In the Properties, add and set the Trajectory Layout > Override Distance property.

![../../_images/trajectory-layout-override-distance.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout-override-distance.gif)
## Adjusting the position of items in a Trajectory Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html#adjusting-the-position-of-items-in-a-trajectory-layout-node "Link to this heading")
By default, a Trajectory Layout node arranges its child nodes from the start of the trajectory spline.
To adjust the starting position of the Trajectory Layout node child nodes on the trajectory:
  1. Select a Trajectory Layout node.
  2. In the Properties, add and set the Trajectory Layout > Start Offset property.

![../../_images/trajectory-layout-start-offset.gif](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trajectory-layout-start-offset.gif)

Use triggers and actions to create interactions. Use triggers to set off actions, such as setting a property to a certain value or setting the state of an application.
For example, Kanzi generates messages from user input and these messages are handled by nodes according to specified behavior.
Nodes define most of the message handling behavior, such as scrolling in a List Box node. However, to meet the requirements of your application, you can define additional behavior. For example, a Button node sends a click message when a user clicks that button, but you can define what happens after the sent click message. An example action is that a click triggers an animation that highlights the button that the user clicked.
All Kanzi nodes can send and receive messages and you can intercept these messages with triggers. Some nodes by default receive messages from specific user input events. For example, a Button node by default receives click messages and a Scroll View node by default receives scroll messages.
![../../_images/messages-and-triggers.svg](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/messages-and-triggers.svg)
In Kanzi these concepts relate to defining event-driven logic:
  * **Input and hit testing.** Input is first recognized in a hit testing phase, where all nodes that have Hit Testable property enabled participate. If a pointer event (for example, mouse button down) is performed on top of nodes that participate in hit testing, only the topmost component receives the input. If a node has a manipulator that reacts to the received type of input, it can send messages (for example, a click message). See [Defining which node receives input](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#defining-which-node-receives-input), [Using input manipulators](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#using-input-manipulators) and [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html).

metadata.title: Triggers (Part 1/3)
metadata.breadcrumb: Working with … > Triggers

content:
* **Input manipulators.** An input manipulator reacts to a specific type of input gesture, such as pan, click, or long press. In Kanzi Studio you can use nodes that already contain specific types of manipulators, or you can add input manipulators using the Kanzi Engine API. For example, a Scroll View node contains a pan manipulator and a Button node includes a click manipulator. See [Using input manipulators](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#using-input-manipulators).
  * **Messages.** Nodes use messages to communicate. The messages travel between nodes using a process called tunneling and bubbling. The message reaches its target node during tunneling and during bubbling messages travel to ancestor nodes, until a trigger intercepts the message and sets it as handled. This enables you to place triggers in nodes themselves, or their ancestors. For example, you can place a trigger called radioButtonHandler to the parent of multiple buttons. See [Using messages](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-messages.html).
  * **Triggers.** Triggers react to messages, a change in data, or events and apply logic. Kanzi includes the most common action types, such as Set Property or Go to State, but you can use the Kanzi Engine API to define to which messages triggers react. Each trigger includes settings, such as the Set Message Handled property, which prevents the message from bubbling up to other triggers, and conditions which you can use to define conditions under which the trigger sets off. You can add multiple triggers to a single message or event and each can have specific settings and conditions. See [Using triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html) and [Triggers reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/reference-for-triggers.html).
  * **Actions.** An action is an outcome of a trigger. Kanzi includes general actions like Set Property, Write Log, Activate Theme, and actions you can use to control a specific type of item such as, Go to State, Set Scroll Target, or Activate Activity. See [Actions and messages reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/reference-for-actions.html).

Use triggers and actions to create interactions based on user input.
A trigger defines a condition and an action defines what the trigger does when that condition is met. For example, to print a message to the Log window when a node is attached to the node tree, add the On Attached trigger to that node and add the Write Log action to that trigger.
Kanzi Studio has a range of actions which you can add to a trigger. For example, you can add an action to print to the Log window (Write Log), set a property to a certain value (Set Property), activate an a Activity node (Activate Activity), or change application theme (Activate Theme).

content:
## Trigger messages[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html#trigger-messages "Link to this heading")
When a trigger intercepts a message that originates from an action you can set what the trigger does with the message. You can:
  * Intercept the message, act on it, and let it continue traveling up or down the project tree.
  * Intercept the message, act on it, and handle it. When a trigger handles a message it consumes it so that the message stops at the trigger that handles it and no other node can intercept it.


With a trigger you can intercept a message either at the node where the message originates, or in a trigger in any of its ancestor or descendant nodes. You can intercept many different message types in the same node. When a message travels up the project tree, the message bubbles. When a message travels down the project tree, the message tunnels. You can set in the action that creates the message whether the message bubbles, tunnels, or both bubbles and tunnels.
For example, if the action creates a bubbling message, after an action generates a message, the message bubbles from the node that receives the input to its parent node, then to the parent of the parent, and so on until a trigger intercepts the message. If the trigger also handles the message, the message stops bubbling (traveling up the project tree). If none of the ancestors handle the message, the message travels all the way to the root node of the project.
By default all triggers handle their own messages. You can control the handling of trigger messages by setting the Set Message Handled property in the trigger.

content:
## Data Triggers[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html#data-triggers "Link to this heading")
Use a Data Trigger to:
  * Apply a value to a property with an Apply Property Action
  * Activate an Activity with an Apply Activation Action. See [Activating Activities with an Apply Activation Action](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/activities/pah.html#pah-apply-activation-action) and [Tutorial: Control application UI](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/data-trigger/data-trigger.html).


A Data Trigger keeps the change on a node applied for as long as the condition expression in that Data Trigger is met. When the condition in that Data Trigger is no longer met, Kanzi reverts the changes that it applied using that Data Trigger.
You set the condition in a Data Trigger in the form of a binding expression that evaluates to either `True` or `False`. In the condition you can use as an input either a property or a data source.
For example, you can use a Data Trigger to control the logic and activation state of Activities in an Activity Host.
Apply Activation Action and Apply Property Action actions have higher priority than any other actions. For example, if you use an Apply Activation Action that sets the Active Index property and a Set Property action that sets that same property to a different value, the effect of the Set Property action becomes visible only after Kanzi unapplies the Apply Activation Action.
## Getting started[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html#getting-started "Link to this heading")
To get started with triggers, see:
  * [Adding a trigger](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html#adding-a-trigger)
  * [Setting the handling of trigger messages](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html#setting-the-handling-of-trigger-messages)
  * [Adding conditions to a trigger](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html#adding-conditions-to-a-trigger)
    * [Creating a condition using a value from a property](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html#creating-a-condition-using-a-value-from-a-property)
    * [Creating a condition using a value from a message](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html#creating-a-condition-using-a-value-from-a-message)
  * [Removing a trigger](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html#removing-a-trigger)


For a list of all the triggers you can use in Kanzi Studio, see [Triggers reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/reference-for-triggers.html).
For a list of all the actions you can add to a trigger in Kanzi Studio, see [Actions and messages reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/reference-for-actions.html).

## Adding a trigger[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html#adding-a-trigger "Link to this heading")
The most common place to add a triggers is in the node that uses the trigger, but you can add a trigger to any node.
To add a trigger:
  1. In the Node Tree create or select a node to which you want to add a trigger.
For example, create a Button 2D node. When you create the Button 2D node it already has a Button: Click trigger.
![../../_images/button-2d.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/button-2d.png)
  2. In the Node Components right-click Triggers and select a trigger that intercepts the type of message that you want to intercept. See [Triggers reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/reference-for-triggers.html).
For example, add an On Attached trigger. The On Attached trigger is set off when Kanzi attaches the node to the node tree.
![../../_images/add-on-attached-trigger.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-on-attached-trigger.png)
  3. In the Node Components > Triggers press `Alt` and right-click the trigger that you added in the previous step, and select an action.
See [Actions and messages reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/reference-for-actions.html).
For example, select the Write Log action and set Log Text to the message that you want to write to the Log window when the trigger is set off. The Write Log action is useful when you want to verify that the node received the input.
You can add any number of actions. Kanzi carries out the actions in the order beginning from the first action.
![../../_images/add-write-log-action.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/add-write-log-action.png) ![../../_images/log-message.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/log-message.png)
When Kanzi attaches the node, it prints the message you entered as the value of the Log Text property to the Log window.
To learn more about the Write Log action, see [Using Write Log action](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/logging/write-log-action.html).
To open the Log window, in the main menu select Window > Log.
![../../_images/message-in-the-log-window.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/message-in-the-log-window.png)
  4. (Optional) If you want the trigger to be set off only under specific conditions, in the Node Components > Triggers in the trigger for which you want to set a condition, right-click Conditions, and select Trigger Condition. See [Adding conditions to a trigger](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html#adding-conditions-to-a-trigger).
![../../_images/click-add-condition.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/click-add-condition.png)

## Setting the handling of trigger messages[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html#setting-the-handling-of-trigger-messages "Link to this heading")
When a trigger handles a message it consumes it so that the message stops at the trigger that handles it and no other node can intercept it. See [Creating custom messages in Kanzi Studio](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-messages.html#creating-custom-messages).
To set the handling of trigger messages, in the Node Components > Triggers, in the trigger for which you want to set message handling, set:
Set Message Handled property:
  * When you enable the Set Message Handled property, this trigger intercepts and handles the message. The message stops here, and does not continue neither bubbling nor tunneling in the project tree.
  * When you disable the Set Message Handled property, this trigger intercepts the message, but the message continues bubbling or tunneling in the project tree.


Routing Mode property:
  * Bubbling to intercept only bubbling messages.
  * Tunneling to intercept only tunneling messages.
  * Tunneling and bubbling to intercept tunneling and bubbling messages.


Message Source property:
  * To intercept messages from a specific target item, do one of the following:
    * Select the item from the dropdown menu.
    * Select <Relative> and set the path to the item:
      * Separate node names with `/` to build the path.
      * Use `.` to access the current item.
      * Use `..` to access the parent item of the current item.
      * Use `#` to access a node using an alias in the resource dictionary of the current node. See [Using aliases](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/aliases/using-aliases.html).
  * To intercept messages from all sources, select <Any>.

![../../_images/set-message-handled-property.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/set-message-handled-property.png)

## Adding conditions to a trigger[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html#adding-conditions-to-a-trigger "Link to this heading")
Trigger conditions enable you to set which conditions must be met for the trigger to set off. For example, you can define conditions to set off a trigger when the user navigates to a specific Page node or enable the user to scroll a scroll view only when a specific Page node is active.
You create a trigger condition by comparing a value that you define in the A section to the value that you define in the B section using an operator that you set with the Operation property.
![../../_images/trigger-condition-editor-default.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/trigger-condition-editor-default.png)
You can create conditions to set off a trigger when:
  * A value that comes from a property type matches a certain rule. See [Creating a condition using a value from a property](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html#creating-a-condition-using-a-value-from-a-property).
  * A value that comes from a message argument matches a certain rule. See [Creating a condition using a value from a message](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html#creating-a-condition-using-a-value-from-a-message).

### Creating a condition using a value from a property[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html#creating-a-condition-using-a-value-from-a-property "Link to this heading")
You can define a trigger condition to set off a trigger when a property that you select gets a value you set in that condition. For example, you can create a condition that allows the user to scroll a Scroll View node only when a specific Page node is active.
To create a condition using a value from a property:
  1. In the Node Tree select or create a node with a trigger to which you want to add a condition, in the Node Components in that trigger right-click Conditions, and select Trigger Condition. See [Adding a trigger](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html#adding-a-trigger).
For example, create a Scroll View 2D node with a Scroll View: Scrolled trigger, in that trigger right-click Conditions, and select Trigger Condition. See [Using the Scroll View nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/scroll-views/using-scroll-views.html).
![../../_images/create-scroll-view.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/create-scroll-view.png) ![../../_images/scrolled-trigger-add-trigger-condition.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/scrolled-trigger-add-trigger-condition.png)
  2. In the trigger condition that you created set the condition that must be met for the trigger to set off.
You create a trigger condition by comparing a value that you define in the A section to the value that you define in the B section using an operator that you set with the Operation property.
In the trigger condition set:
     * In the A section define the property type and value that you want to use for the condition. To use a value from a property, set:
       * Type of A to Property
       * Item to the node whose property you want to use for the condition
For example, set it to a Page node.
       * Property to the property type that you want to use for the condition
For example, set it to the Activation State property of the Page node you selected in the Item property.
Use the Activation State property to find out whether a Page or Page Host node is active.
![../../_images/value-a.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/value-a.png)
     * Operation to the operator that you want to use to compare the value that you defined in the A section to the value that you define in the B section.
For example, set it to = to create a condition where the trigger sets off only when the value that you defined in the A section is equal to the value that you define in the B section.
![../../_images/operator.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/operator.png)
     * In the B section define the value to which you want to compare the value that you defined in the A section. The Type of B property defines where the value for the B comes from. Set the Type of B property to:

![../../_images/operator.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/operator.png)
     * In the B section define the value to which you want to compare the value that you defined in the A section. The Type of B property defines where the value for the B comes from. Set the Type of B property to:
       * Property to compare to a value from any property from any node in the project
       * Message argument to use a value from a message argument from a trigger in the node that you set in the A section in the Item property
       * Fixed when you want to use the same property from the node that you set in the A section and set a value for that property

## Messages and arguments[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-messages.html#messages-and-arguments "Link to this heading")
`MessageArguments[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13650.html)` is the base class for arguments passed in messages. Kanzi provides built-in message types for different nodes and triggers. For example, the `ButtonConcept::ClickedMessageArguments[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a18102.html)` message for the Button: Click trigger and the `Page::ActivatedMessageArguments[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a18718.html)` message for the Page Activated trigger.
You can extend the `MessageArguments[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13650.html)` class by writing your own message types.
Message type describes:
  * The nature of an event or information
For example, `ClickManipulator::ClickMessage[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13162.html#a5ec459cf339d2a9fa47a77a1e245cb8c)` and `ListBoxConcept::ItemSelectedMessage[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a18226.html#afe24eae641ba656317239668da447a51)`.
  * Arguments to describe the data associated within the message
For example, the `InputManipulator::InputMessageArguments::HitTestPointProperty[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13378.html#a7b997792a899a1893addbe50ebafb2ab)` and `ListBoxConcept::ItemSelectedMessageArguments::SelectedItemIndexProperty[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a18230.html#acd932ae28baf32c0ab7b0ebe898ea993)` properties.


You can describe and access the message arguments with the `PropertyType[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a15386.html)` objects. `MessageArguments::setArgument[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13650.html#a39d1aec9e1fcab6f69388c8d928c9726)` function sets and `MessageArguments::getArgument[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13650.html#ae6bcba423091c4f8dc2c41c423eab7cb)` function retrieves arguments with the underlying storage type for arguments, such as float, boolean, and vector3.

## Creating custom messages in Kanzi Studio[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-messages.html#creating-custom-messages-in-ks "Link to this heading")
To create a custom message in Kanzi Studio:
  1. In the Library press `Alt` and right-click Message Types and select Message Type.
![../../_images/message-type-in-library.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/message-type-in-library.png)
  2. In the Properties set:
     * Category to the category where you want Kanzi Studio to show this message in context menus.
     * Arguments to the arguments accepted by the message type.
     * Routing Mode to the routing mode of the message type.
       * Tunneling mode passes the message through the outermost parent node of the recipient node.
       * Bubbling mode passes the message through the closest parent node of the recipient node.
![../../_images/message-type-arguments.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/message-type-arguments.png)


See [Setting the handling of trigger messages](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-triggers.html#setting-the-handling-of-trigger-messages).

## Using messages in the Kanzi Engine API[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-messages.html#using-messages-in-the-kr-api "Link to this heading")
### Dispatching messages[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-messages.html#dispatching-messages "Link to this heading")
To dispatch messages use `Node::dispatchMessage[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13774.html#abc47048be3c6a3a1934ae8dcd87068cd)`. This function defines the message type and arguments and calls all the handlers and filters which are registered for the node for that message type. `Node::dispatchMessage[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a13774.html#abc47048be3c6a3a1934ae8dcd87068cd)` notifies the handlers and filters immediately before the function call returns, which enables the handlers and filters to react to the message immediately.
When you dispatch a message it travels in two phases: first tunneling, then bubbling. During the tunneling phase the message travels down the node tree from the first child node of the Screen node (the root node) to the node where the message originated. From there the message bubbles back up the node tree to the root node.

## Writing to the Log window[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/logging/write-log-action.html#writing-to-the-log-window "Link to this heading")
When you want to write a message to the Log window, use a Write Log action in any trigger.
To write to the Log window:
  1. In the Node Tree, create or select a node where you want to react to an event as a result of which you want to write a message to the Log window.
For example, in the Node Tree, create a Scroll View 2D node with content that you can scroll. See [Creating a Scroll View node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/scroll-views/using-scroll-views.html#creating-scroll-view-node).
![../../_images/node-tree-scroll-view1.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-tree-scroll-view1.png)
  2. In the Node Components, press `Alt` and right-click Triggers and select a trigger that you want to use to write to the Log window when that trigger is set off. See [Triggers reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/reference-for-triggers.html).
For example, create a Message Trigger > Scroll View > Scroll Ended trigger. Scroll Ended trigger is set off when the scroll position of a scroll view has finished changing.
![../../_images/node-components-create-scroll-ended.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-components-create-scroll-ended.png)
  3. In the Node Components > Triggers, press `Alt` and right-click the trigger that you added in the previous step, and select Write Log action.
![../../_images/node-components-write-log-action.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-components-write-log-action.png)
  4. In the Write Log action, set the Log Text property to the message that you want to write to the Log window when the trigger is set off.
![../../_images/node-components-write-log-action-log-text.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-components-write-log-action-log-text.png)


In the Preview, when you scroll the Scroll View and the scrolling stops, Kanzi prints to the Log window the message that you set in the Log Text property.
![../../_images/log-window-scroll-ended.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/log-window-scroll-ended.png)
Tip
To open the Log window, in the main menu select Window > Log.

content:
## Using Write Log action macros[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/logging/write-log-action.html#using-write-log-action-macros "Link to this heading")
Use a Write Log action macro to add to your log message content that Kanzi replaces with the value of that macro.
To use Write Log action macros:
  1. Create a Write Log action. See [Writing to the Log window](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/logging/write-log-action.html#create-write-log-action).
  2. In the Write Log action, click Enter Operation and select a macro.
For example, instead of manually entering the name of a node, use the <Name> macro.
The <Name> macro inserts the name of the node that contains the Write Log action.
You can combine macros and text.  
| Macro  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| <Name>  | Inserts the name of the node that contains a Write Log action.  |  
| <EventName>  | Inserts the name of the trigger that executes a Write Log action.  |  
| {ValueSourceIndex}  | After you add a property value or a message argument, inserts the value of that item. See [Logging values from properties or message arguments](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/logging/write-log-action.html#logging-values-from-properties-or-message-arguments).  |  
![../../_images/node-components-write-log-action-name-macro.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/node-components-write-log-action-name-macro.png)


In the Preview, when you scroll the Scroll View and the scrolling stops, Kanzi prints to the Log window the message that you set in the Log Text property.
![../../_images/log-window-scroll-ended-macro.png](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_images/log-window-scroll-ended-macro.png)
