Activity Browser[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Activity-Browser "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Activity Browser to create and inspect Activities and Activity Hosts, and to simulate the activation of Activities. The Activity Browser shows all possible UI states of Activities in your application.
See [Using the Activity Browser](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/activities/activity-browser.html). 

Activity node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Activity-node "Link to this term") 
    
An Activity is a part of an application UI that is responsible for a task. For example, a media player application can have Activities, such as radio, music player, and AUX.
See [Activities](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/activities/activities.html). 

Alias[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Alias "Link to this term") 
    
Use an Alias to get consistent access to a Kanzi node. You can use aliases to access nodes both in Kanzi Studio and using the Kanzi Engine API.
See [Using aliases](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/aliases/using-aliases.html). 

Angle Trajectory[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Angle-Trajectory "Link to this term") 
    
Use an Angle Trajectory to create a path where two straight lines form an angle in 3D space.
Use trajectories as paths along which Trajectory Layout 3D and Trajectory Layout 2D nodes arrange their child nodes, and along which Trajectory List Box 3D nodes move their items.
See [Using angle trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-angle-trajectories.html), [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html), and [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html).

metadata.title: Glossary (Part 1/30)
metadata.breadcrumb: References > Glossary

content:
Animation Child Clip[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Animation-Child-Clip "Link to this term") 
    
Use an Animation Child Clip to create hierarchical animations. Animate the target node with an Animation Clip.
See [Creating keyframe animations](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/animations/animating-property-values.html) and [Editing animation clips](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/animations/editing-animation-clips.html). 

Animation Clip[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Animation-Clip "Link to this term") 
    
Use an Animation Clip to combine Animation Data resources into more complex animations. You can reuse the same Animation Data resources in different Animation Clip items. Use an Animation Child Clip to create hierarchical animations.
See [Creating keyframe animations](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/animations/animating-property-values.html) and [Editing animation clips](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/animations/editing-animation-clips.html). 

Animation Data[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Animation-Data "Link to this term") 
    
Use an Animation Data resource to define the keyframes and target property of a keyframe animation. One Animation Data resource can target only one property or property field. Animation Data resources are independent from the nodes they target. This allows you to reuse Animation Data resources to animate different nodes.
See [Creating keyframe animations](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/animations/animating-property-values.html) and [Editing animation clips](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/animations/editing-animation-clips.html). 

Animation Player[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Animation-Player "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Animation Player to play and control the playback of keyframe animations.
See [Using keyframe animations](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/animations/triggering-animations-with-the-play-animation-action.html). 

Arc Trajectory[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Arc-Trajectory "Link to this term") 
    
Use an Arc Trajectory to create a path in the shape of an arc in 3D space.
Use trajectories as paths along which Trajectory Layout 3D and Trajectory Layout 2D nodes arrange their child nodes, and along which Trajectory List Box 3D nodes move their items.
See [Using arc trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-arc-trajectories.html), [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html), and [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html).

metadata.title: Glossary (Part 2/30)
metadata.breadcrumb: References > Glossary

content:
Asset Packages[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Asset-Packages "Link to this term") 
    
Kanzi Studio asset packages are collections of ready-made content that you can import to your Kanzi Studio projects. With asset packages, you can create an asset library with content, such as UI components, materials, brushes, styles, and textures.
See [Asset packages](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/asset-packages/asset-packages.html). 

Bindings[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Bindings "Link to this term") 
    
Use bindings to set the value of a property or property field with the value from another property, property field, or a data source.
Bindings allow nodes, render passes, 2D effects, states, state objects, and styles to automatically update the values of their properties in response to the changing property values, or the occurrence of some external event.
See [Bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/bindings.html). 

Blit render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Blit-render-pass "Link to this term") 
    
Use a Blit render pass to blit one or more textures or render passes on the screen using a specific material.
See [Blit render pass](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#blit-render-pass). 

Blur Effect 2D[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Blur-Effect-2D "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Blur Effect 2D effect to apply a Gaussian blur to a 2D node.
See [Using the Blur Effect 2D effect](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/blur-effect-2d.html). 

Bookmark[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Bookmark "Link to this term") 
    
Use bookmarks to quickly access items in your Kanzi Studio projects.
See [Using bookmarks](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bookmarks/using-bookmarks.html). 

Brushes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Brushes "Link to this term") 
    
Use Brushes to set the appearance of the foreground and background of 2D nodes. For example, with brushes you can define the color of text in a Text Block 2D node, fill a background of a 2D node with an image pattern, or apply a material effect on 2D content.
See [Using brushes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html). 

Button nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Button-nodes "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Button, Toggle Button, and Toggle Button Group nodes to create interactions through clicking, tapping, or pressing a key on the keyboard.
See [Buttons](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/buttons.html).

metadata.title: Glossary (Part 3/30)
metadata.breadcrumb: References > Glossary

content:
Camera node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Camera-node "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Camera node to show the content of a Scene in Kanzi Studio Preview and in your Kanzi application.
See [Camera node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/cameras/cameras.html). 

Circle Trajectory[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Circle-Trajectory "Link to this term") 
    
Use a Circle Trajectory to create a path in the shape of a circle in 3D space.
Use trajectories as paths along which Trajectory Layout 3D and Trajectory Layout 2D nodes arrange their child nodes, and along which Trajectory List Box 3D nodes move their items.
See [Using circle trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-circle-trajectories.html), [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html), and [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html). 

Clear render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Clear-render-pass "Link to this term") 
    
Use a Clear render pass to clear some or all of the color, depth, and stencil buffers of the current render context.
See [Clear render pass](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#clear-render-pass). 

Click Manipulator[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Click-Manipulator "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Click Manipulator to enable users to click nodes in your Kanzi application.
See [Using the Click Manipulator](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/click-manipulator.html) and [Handling user input](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html). 

Code Behind[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Code-Behind "Link to this term") 
    
Code Behind is a workflow where you associate code with an instance of an Activity instead of a type.
See [Programming Activities with Code Behind](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/activities/code-behind.html). 

Color Brush[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Color-Brush "Link to this term") 
    
Use a Color Brush to fill a 2D node with a solid color.
See [Filling 2D nodes with a solid color](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#filling-2d-nodes-with-a-solid-color). 

Color workflow[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Color-workflow "Link to this term") 
    
Use the color workflow to set the color space in which Kanzi operates on color values. In the linear color workflow Kanzi operates on color values in linear color space. In the standard color workflow Kanzi operates on color values in nonlinear gamma color space.
See [Color workflow](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/color/color.html).

metadata.title: Glossary (Part 4/30)
metadata.breadcrumb: References > Glossary

content:
Combine Object Source[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Combine-Object-Source "Link to this term") 
    
Use a Combine Object Source to collect and combine nodes from one or more input sources.
See [Using object sources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/object-sources/using-object-sources.html). 

Compose and Blit Pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Compose-and-Blit-Pass "Link to this term") 
    
Compose and Blit Pass contains the render pass structure that enables you to blit to the screen Composition Target render passes or textures using a specific material.
See [Using Kanzi Studio render pass presets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-render-pass-templates.html) and [Rendering content to composition targets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-to-composition-target.html). 

Composition Target render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Composition-Target-render-pass "Link to this term") 
    
Use a Composition Target render pass to render content to one or more composition targets.
See [Rendering content to composition targets](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-to-composition-target.html). 

Contains Property Filter[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Contains-Property-Filter "Link to this term") 
    
Contains Property Filter collects 3D nodes that contain, or do not contain a specific property.
See [Using the Contains Property Filter](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/using-contains-property-filters.html). 

Content Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Content-Layout-node "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Content Layout nodes to present content in a UI control as a single item.
See [Using the Content Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-content-layouts.html). 

Cubemap render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Cubemap-render-pass "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Cubemap render pass to create dynamic reflections of the environment on the surface of 3D nodes.
See [Creating cubemap reflections](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/cubemap-render-pass.html). 

Cubemap Render Target Texture[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Cubemap-Render-Target-Texture "Link to this term") 
    
Use a Cubemap Render Target Texture to render a Cubemap render pass to a cubemap texture.
See [Creating cubemap reflections](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/cubemap-render-pass.html).

metadata.title: Glossary (Part 5/30)
metadata.breadcrumb: References > Glossary

content:
Cubemap Texture[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Cubemap-Texture "Link to this term") 
    
Cubemap textures combine six square-shaped images into one texture to represent reflections of the environment. Each image represents the scenery in one of the six directions along the x, y, and z axes from the viewpoint of the cubemapped object.
See [Using cubemap textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-cubemap-textures.html). 

Data-Driven Exclusive Activity Host[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Data-Driven-Exclusive-Activity-Host "Link to this term") 
    
You can use a list data source and a Data-Driven Exclusive Activity Host to create parts of UI with Activities from content of data objects. For example, you can define the content of menus in a data source and use a Data-Driven Exclusive Activity Host to create the menus in your application.
See [Data-Driven Exclusive Activity Host](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/activities/ddeah.html). 

Default render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Default-render-pass "Link to this term") 
    
You can use a Default render pass as the starting point for your render pass tree.
Default render pass contains a basic set of render passes that first render opaque nodes and then transparent nodes.
See [Using the Default render pass](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-render-pass-templates.html#using-drp). 

Directional Light node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Directional-Light-node "Link to this term") 
    
Directional Light emits light only in one direction and is suitable for modeling the sunlight.
See [Using the light nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/lights/using-lights.html). 

Dock Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Dock-Layout-node "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Dock Layout nodes to place nodes relative to each other along the sides of a Dock Layout node.
See [Using the Dock Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-dock-layouts.html). 

Drag-And-Drop Manipulator[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Drag-And-Drop-Manipulator "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Drag-And-Drop Manipulator to enable users to drag and drop nodes in your Kanzi application.
See [Using the Drag-And-Drop Manipulator](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/drag-and-drop-manipulator.html) and [Handling user input](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html).

content:
Draw Objects render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Draw-Objects-render-pass "Link to this term") 
    
Use a Draw Objects render pass to render one object source using the camera from the Scene.
See [Draw Objects render pass](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#draw-objects-render-pass). 

Draw Objects With Material render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Draw-Objects-With-Material-render-pass "Link to this term") 
    
Use a Draw Objects With Material render pass to render 3D nodes with a specific material.
See [Setting materials for rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-materials.html). 

Effect Stack 2D[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Effect-Stack-2D "Link to this term") 
    
Use an Effect Stack 2D effect prefab to apply multiple effects to a 2D node.
See [Using multiple effects](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/multiple-effects.html). 

Effects[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Effects "Link to this term") 
    
Use effects to apply post-processing effects to 2D nodes.
See [Effects for 2D nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/2d-effects.html). 

Ellipse Trajectory[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Ellipse-Trajectory "Link to this term") 
    
Use an Ellipse Trajectory to create a path in the shape of an ellipse in 3D space.
Use trajectories as paths along which Trajectory Layout 3D and Trajectory Layout 2D nodes arrange their child nodes, and along which Trajectory List Box 3D nodes move their items.
See [Using ellipse trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-ellipse-trajectories.html), [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html), and [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html). 

Empty Node node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Empty-Node-node "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Empty Node nodes to group nodes and to set property values of their child nodes.
See [Using the Empty Node nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/empty-nodes/using-empty-nodes.html).

metadata.title: Glossary (Part 7/30)
metadata.breadcrumb: References > Glossary

content:
Exclusive Activity Host node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Exclusive-Activity-Host-node "Link to this term") 
    
An Activity Host node defines the rules for when an Activity node is active.
An Exclusive Activity Host can have only one of its child Activities active at a time. When one child Activity of an Exclusive Activity Host is active, all other Activities of that Activity Host are inactive. For example, you can use an Exclusive Activity Host to toggle between views in your application.
See [Exclusive Activity Host](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/activities/eah.html). 

Filters[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Filters "Link to this term") 
    
Filters collect and reorganize 3D nodes in your Kanzi project. You can use filters to determine which 3D nodes to render in different render passes.
See [Filters](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/filters.html). 

Float Value Accumulator[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Float-Value-Accumulator "Link to this term") 
    
Use a Float Value Accumulator to increment a value of a float property type or a property field over time or per frame.
See [Incrementing the value of a property type](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/animations/property-animator.html). 

Flow Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Flow-Layout-node "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Flow Layout nodes to arrange nodes along a line. When a line runs out of space, the Flow Layout node places its child nodes in a new line.
See [Using the Flow Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-flow-layouts.html). 

Font[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Font "Link to this term") 
    
Use a font to render text. The default font in Kanzi is Fira Sans Regular. To use your own font, import it to your Kanzi Studio project.
See [Importing fonts](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/importing/importing-fonts.html). 

Gather Lights render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Gather-Lights-render-pass "Link to this term") 
    
Gather Lights render pass allows you to collect from a list of nodes the light nodes for lighting 3D nodes in a scene.
See [Using lights in rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/lights-rendering.html). 

Grid Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Grid-Layout-node "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Grid Layout nodes to arrange nodes in a grid.
See [Using the Grid Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html).

metadata.title: Glossary (Part 8/30)
metadata.breadcrumb: References > Glossary

content:
Grid Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Grid-Layout-node "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Grid Layout nodes to arrange nodes in a grid.
See [Using the Grid Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-layouts.html). 

Grid List Box node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Grid-List-Box-node "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Grid List Box nodes to create scrollable lists of items arranged in a grid.
See [Using the Grid List Box nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/grids/using-grid-list-boxes.html). 

Group render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Group-render-pass "Link to this term") 
    
Group render pass allows you to collect render passes so that you can refer to a single render pass prefab in your Viewport 2D node.
See [Group render pass](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#group-render-pass) and [Creating and using render passes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-render-pass-prefabs.html#creating-and-using-render-passes). 

Image node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Image-node "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Image node to show a bitmap image.
See [Using the Image node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/using-images.html). 

Input Manipulators[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Input-Manipulators "Link to this term") 
    
Use Input Manipulators components to enable gesture recognition for nodes. You can create Input Manipulators components in the Node Components window.
See [Using input manipulators](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html#using-input-manipulators). 

Instantiator node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Instantiator-node "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Instantiator node to replicate the appearance of a 3D node or a tree of 3D nodes that the Instantiator node targets.
See [Using the Instantiator node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/instantiator-nodes/instantiator-nodes.html). 

Int Value Accumulator[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Int-Value-Accumulator "Link to this term") 
    
Use an Int Value Accumulator to increment a value of an integer property type over time or per frame.
See [Incrementing the value of a property type](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/animations/property-animator.html).

metadata.title: Glossary (Part 9/30)
metadata.breadcrumb: References > Glossary

content:
Kanzi Command Prompt[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Kanzi-Command-Prompt "Link to this term") 
    
The Kanzi Command Prompt opens the Windows Command Prompt with the Kanzi environment variables set for the version of Kanzi for which you open a Kanzi Command Prompt.
Use the Kanzi Command Prompt to access Kanzi utilities and build tools, such as Gradle and CMake, without using absolute paths or setting environment variables.
See [Using the Kanzi Command Prompt](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/using-kanzi-command-prompt.html). 

Key Manipulator[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Key-Manipulator "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Key Manipulator to set the keys that the user can use to navigate your application. For example, you can override the default focus navigation keys and use a specific key to set focus to a node, set a key to open or close a popup-type window, or move focus in the focus chain.
See [Using the Key Manipulator](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/key-manipulator.html) and [Handling user input](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html). 

Layouts[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Layouts "Link to this term") 
    
You can use layout nodes to position nodes in relation to the application screen and other nodes. Layout consists of properties alignment, margins and layout size and that you can define either specific to a node or as a general rule imposed on child nodes by specific layout containers.
See [Layout control nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/layouts.html) and [Layouts](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/kanzi-fundamentals/layouts.html). 

Library window[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Library-window "Link to this term") 
    
You can find all resources in a Kanzi Studio project in the Library window.
The Library window shows, for example, animation clips, brushes, fonts, materials, mesh data, textures, render passes, state managers, themes, and styles.
See [Resources](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/resources/resources.html). 

Light nodes[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Light-nodes "Link to this term") 
    
Use the light nodes to create sources of light for a Scene in your Kanzi application.
Kanzi has Directional Light, Point Light, and Spot Light nodes.
See [Using the light nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/lights/using-lights.html).

metadata.title: Glossary (Part 10/30)
metadata.breadcrumb: References > Glossary

content:
Line trajectory[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Line-trajectory "Link to this term") 
    
Use a Line Trajectory to create a path with a single straight line in 3D space.
Use trajectories as paths along which Trajectory Layout 3D and Trajectory Layout 2D nodes arrange their child nodes, and along which Trajectory List Box 3D nodes move their items.
See [Using line trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-line-trajectories.html), [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html), and [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html). 

List Box Item Container[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-List-Box-Item-Container "Link to this term") 
    
Use the List Box Item Container prefabs to set the appearance and behavior of items in List Box nodes. For example, use a List Box Item Container prefab to add decorative elements to List Box items or change the appearance of the currently selected item.
See [Using the List Box Item Container prefabs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/container-controls/using-list-box-item-containers.html). 

Locale[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Locale "Link to this term") 
    
Kanzi uses locale as an ID to select the resources associated with a language and location.
See [Using locales](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/localization/using-locales.html). 

Localization Table[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Localization-Table "Link to this term") 
    
Kanzi uses localization tables to keep track of locales and localized resources.
See [Localizing applications](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/localization/localizing-applications.html). 

Log window[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Log-window "Link to this term") 
    
In the Log window you can see the state of your application, such as trigger messages, links to the binary files when Kanzi Studio creates an application from your project, shader compiler errors, warnings, and errors.
See [Logging](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/logging/logging.html). 

Long-Press Manipulator[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Long-Press-Manipulator "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Long-Press Manipulator to enable users to long-press nodes in your Kanzi application.
See [Using the Long-Press Manipulator](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/long-press-manipulator.html) and [Handling user input](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html).

metadata.title: Glossary (Part 11/30)
metadata.breadcrumb: References > Glossary

content:
Mask Effect 2D[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Mask-Effect-2D "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Mask Effect 2D effect to apply a mask to a 2D node.
See [Using the Mask Effect 2D effect](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/mask-effect-2d.html). 

Material[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Material "Link to this term") 
    
Use materials to set the appearance of 3D nodes and Material Brush brushes.
See [Using materials](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/using-materials.html). 

Material Brush[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Material-Brush "Link to this term") 
    
Use a Material Brush to fill a 2D node with a material.
See [Filling 2D nodes with a material](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#filling-2d-nodes-with-a-material). 

Material Setup render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Material-Setup-render-pass "Link to this term") 
    
Material Setup render pass allows you to set properties for a material so that all successive rendering with that material uses the property values that you set in this render pass.
See [Setting materials for rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering-materials.html). 

Material Type[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Material-Type "Link to this term") 
    
Material types define the property types of a material. By adjusting material property values defined by a material type, you set the appearance of a material. Each material type has a vertex shader and a fragment shader, which set the type of properties you can use in a material.
See [Using material types](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/using-material-types.html). 

Message[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Message "Link to this term") 
    
Use messages to carry information between Kanzi Engine systems, such as input and animation systems, and nodes in your Kanzi application.
See [Using messages](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/using-messages.html) and [Triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/triggers.html). 

Model node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Model-node "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Model node to show the imported meshes in your Kanzi application.
See [Using meshes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/meshes/meshes.html). 

Modifier binding[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Modifier-binding "Link to this term") 
    
A modifier binding modifies a property value, much like an animation or a state manager.
See [Modifier bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/bindings.html#modifier-bindings).

metadata.title: Glossary (Part 12/30)
metadata.breadcrumb: References > Glossary

content:
Morph[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Morph "Link to this term") 
    
Morphing transforms a shape into another in a seamless transition. Use the Mesh resource containing morph data to morph between shapes.
See [Using Morphs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/morphs/using-morphs.html). 

Multi-Click Manipulator[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Multi-Click-Manipulator "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Multi-Click Manipulator to enable users to multi-click nodes in your Kanzi application.
See [Using the Multi-Click Manipulator](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/multi-click-manipulator.html) and [Handling user input](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html). 

Navigation Manipulator[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Navigation-Manipulator "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Navigation Manipulator to set the keys that the user can use to navigate to different directions in your application.
See [Using the Navigation Manipulator](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/navigation-manipulator.html) and [Handling user input](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html). 

Nine Patch Image node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Nine-Patch-Image-node "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Nine Patch Image node to create a scalable button background that scales with the size of the Nine Patch Image content.
See [Using the Nine Patch Image node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/images/using-nine-patch-images.html). 

Node Components window[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Node-Components-window "Link to this term") 
    
In the Node Components window you can see the triggers and actions, animation players, and input manipulator components for the selected node.
Use node components to add functionality to a node.
For example, add triggers and actions to create interactions, or an Animation Player to play keyframe animations.
See [Node components](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/node-components/node-components.html). 

Node List render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Node-List-render-pass "Link to this term") 
    
Node List render pass allows you to filter and hold a list of nodes that you want to render using other render passes.
See [Collecting nodes for rendering](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/filtering-node-lists.html). 

Node Tree window[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Node-Tree-window "Link to this term") 
    
In the Node Tree window you can see the structure of your Kanzi project, create and organize content, and manage your project.
See [Presentation](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/kanzi-fundamentals/presentation.html).

metadata.title: Glossary (Part 13/30)
metadata.breadcrumb: References > Glossary

content:
Object Type Filter[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Object-Type-Filter "Link to this term") 
    
Use Object Type Filter to collect 3D nodes based on their type.
See [Using the Object Type Filter](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/using-object-type-filters.html). 

Outline Effect 2D[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Outline-Effect-2D "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Outline Effect 2D effect to apply an outline to the content of a 2D node.
See [Using the Outline Effect 2D effect](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/outline-effect-2d.html). 

Page node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Page-node "Link to this term") 
    
Note
The Page and Page Host nodes are deprecated. Use the Activity and Activity Host nodes to build navigable UIs for your application. See [Activities](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/activities/activities.html).
Use a Page node to add structure to your Kanzi application. For example, if your Kanzi application contains several applications, such as a music player, a photo album, and a calendar, create each on its own Page, and then use Page nodes to create the structure for each of these applications.
See [Using the Page and Page Host nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/pages/using-pages.html). 

Page Host node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Page-Host-node "Link to this term") 
    
Note
The Page and Page Host nodes are deprecated. Use the Activity and Activity Host nodes to build navigable UIs for your application. See [Activities](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/activities/activities.html).
Use a Page Host node to handle the navigation and transitions between Page nodes.
See [Using the Page and Page Host nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/pages/using-pages.html). 

Pan Manipulator[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Pan-Manipulator "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Pan Manipulator to enable users to move nodes in your Kanzi application.
See [Using the Pan Manipulator](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/pan-manipulator.html) and [Handling user input](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html).

metadata.title: Glossary (Part 14/30)
metadata.breadcrumb: References > Glossary

content:
Parallel Activity Host node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Parallel-Activity-Host-node "Link to this term") 
    
An Activity Host node defines the rules for when an Activity node is active.
Parallel Activity Host can activate more than one of its child Activities at a time. When you activate an Activity, a Parallel Activity Host brings that Activity to the front.
For example, you can use a Parallel Activity Host to implement the showing of critical messages, such as engine failure, in front of regular notifications, such as a phone call notification.
See [Parallel Activity Host](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/activities/pah.html). 

Pinch Manipulator[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Pinch-Manipulator "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Pinch Manipulator to enable users to zoom and rotate nodes in your Kanzi application.
See [Using the Pinch Manipulator](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/pinch-manipulator.html) and [Handling user input](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/input/handling-input.html). 

Pipeline State render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Pipeline-State-render-pass "Link to this term") 
    
Use a Pipeline State render pass to set depth and stencil testing, transparency, and culling for the child render passes.
See [Pipeline State render pass](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/rendering.html#pipeline-state-render-pass). 

Plane node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Plane-node "Link to this term") 
    
Plane node is a primitive mesh node in the shape of a 2D plane and is centered in the origin.
See [Using meshes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/meshes/meshes.html). 

Plugins[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Plugins "Link to this term") 
    
With Kanzi plugins, you can extend the functionality of Kanzi and customize Kanzi to fit your application development requirements. When you create a Kanzi plugin, you can share the extended functionality with any Kanzi user.
See [Kanzi Engine plugins](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/plugins-kanzi-engine.html) and [Kanzi Studio plugins](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/plugins.html). 

Point Light node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Point-Light-node "Link to this term") 
    
Point Light emits light from a specific location uniformly to all directions (360 degrees).
See [Using the light nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/lights/using-lights.html).

metadata.title: Glossary (Part 15/30)
metadata.breadcrumb: References > Glossary

content:
Prefab Placeholder node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Prefab-Placeholder-node "Link to this term") 
    
Use a Prefab Placeholder node to instantiate a node prefab which you do not intend to change during application runtime.
See [Prefab Placeholder and Prefab View nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#prefab-placeholder-and-prefab-view-nodes). 

Prefab View node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Prefab-View-node "Link to this term") 
    
Use a Prefab View node to dynamically change a prefab, or to asynchronously load the resources which the prefab uses.
See [Prefab Placeholder and Prefab View nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html#prefab-placeholder-and-prefab-view-nodes). 

Prefabs[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Prefabs "Link to this term") 
    
Use prefabs (prefabricated templates) to structure your application and to create consistent interfaces. Prefabs allow you to create the building blocks of your application and make the application easier to maintain.
See [Using node prefabs](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/prefabs/prefabs.html). 

Preview window[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Preview-window "Link to this term") 
    
In the Preview window you can see in real time what the Kanzi project that you are working on looks like. In the Preview window you can directly move, scale, and rotate nodes, and see structural information for your project and individual nodes.
See [Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/preview/preview.html). 

Project[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Project "Link to this term") 
    
You can use one or more Kanzi Studio projects to create your Kanzi application.
See [Projects](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/projects/projects.html). 

Property Driven Animation Player[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Property-Driven-Animation-Player "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Property Driven Animation Player when you want to use a property type instead of time to control a keyframe animation.
See [Creating property-driven animations](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/animations/property-driven-animations.html). 

Property Is Equal Filter[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Property-Is-Equal-Filter "Link to this term") 
    
Property Is Equal Filter collects 3D nodes that contain, or do not contain a specific property the value of which matches a specific value.
See [Using the Property Is Equal Filter](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/using-property-is-equal-filters.html).

metadata.title: Glossary (Part 16/30)
metadata.breadcrumb: References > Glossary

content:
Property Target Easing Interpolator[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Property-Target-Easing-Interpolator "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Property Target Easing Interpolator when you want to dynamically set the target value for a property and want to interpolate the current value to the target value over time using an easing function. Easing functions enable you to create lifelike animations that offer a more pleasant user experience.
See [Interpolating property values using easing functions](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/animations/property-target-easing-interpolator.html). 

Property Target Interpolator[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Property-Target-Interpolator "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Property Target Interpolator when you want to dynamically set the target value for a property and want to interpolate the current value to the target value over time.
See [Interpolating property values](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/animations/property-target-interpolator.html). 

Rectangle Trajectory[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Rectangle-Trajectory "Link to this term") 
    
Use a Rectangle Trajectory to create a path in the shape of a rectangle in 3D space.
Use trajectories as paths along which Trajectory Layout 3D and Trajectory Layout 2D nodes arrange their child nodes, and along which Trajectory List Box 3D nodes move their items.
See [Using rectangle trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-rectangle-trajectories.html), [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html), and [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html). 

Render Target Texture[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Render-Target-Texture "Link to this term") 
    
Use a Render Target Texture to render content to a texture or to apply anti-aliasing to only a part of your application. You can use render target textures like any other texture. For example, you can use it in a Texture Brush or as an image in an Image node.
See [Using render target textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-render-target-textures.html). 

Render to Texture Pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Render-to-Texture-Pass "Link to this term") 
    
Render to Texture Pass creates the render passes and texture you need to render to a texture.
See [Rendering to texture](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/rendering/using-render-pass-templates.html#rendering-to-texture).

metadata.title: Glossary (Part 17/30)
metadata.breadcrumb: References > Glossary

content:
Resource dictionary[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Resource-dictionary "Link to this term") 
    
A resource dictionary is a collection of resource IDs pointing to resources. You can add a resource dictionary to any node.
See [Using resource dictionaries](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/resources/using-resource-dictionaries.html). 

Resource Files[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Resource-Files "Link to this term") 
    
Kanzi Studio lists in the Library > Resource Files references to files in the resource directories of a Kanzi project. Kanzi Studio synchronizes the content of Resource Files with the files in the resource directories.
See [Using resource files](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/resource-files/resource-files.html). 

Scene node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Scene-node "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Scene node to show 3D content in your Kanzi application.
See [Using the Scene node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/scenes/scenes.html). 

Screen node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Screen-node "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Screen node to set the metrics and the content of the screen of the target device on which your Kanzi application is rendered.
See [Setting the Screen node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/screens/screens.html). 

Scroll View node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Scroll-View-node "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Scroll View nodes to define an area where to generate scrolling messages in response to user input and physics-based animation.
See [Using the Scroll View nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/scroll-views/using-scroll-views.html). 

Shaders[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Shaders "Link to this term") 
    
Use Shaders to produce appropriate levels of light and color within an image, to produce special effects, or to do post-processing.
See [Shaders](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/shaders/shaders.html). 

Shadow Effect 2D[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Shadow-Effect-2D "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Shadow Effect 2D effect to apply a shadow to the content of a 2D node.
See [Using the Shadow Effect 2D effect](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/effects/shadow-effect-2d.html). 

Single Texture[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Single-Texture "Link to this term") 
    
Single textures use a single image for the texture.
See [Using single textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-single-textures.html).

metadata.title: Glossary (Part 18/30)
metadata.breadcrumb: References > Glossary

content:
Single Texture[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Single-Texture "Link to this term") 
    
Single textures use a single image for the texture.
See [Using single textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-single-textures.html). 

Slider node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Slider-node "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Slider nodes when you want to allow users to change numerical values using a visual indicator between a minimum and a maximum value.
See [Using the Slider nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/sliders/using-sliders.html). 

Sorting Filter[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Sorting-Filter "Link to this term") 
    
Sorting Filter either orders 3D nodes by their position on the z axis or groups them by their material type.
See [Using the Sorting Filter](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/using-sorting-filters.html). 

Spiral Trajectory[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Spiral-Trajectory "Link to this term") 
    
Use a Spiral Trajectory to create a path in the shape of a spiral in 3D space.
Use trajectories as paths along which Trajectory Layout 3D and Trajectory Layout 2D nodes arrange their child nodes, and along which Trajectory List Box 3D nodes move their items.
See [Using spiral trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-spiral-trajectories.html), [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html), and [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html). 

Spline Trajectory[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Spline-Trajectory "Link to this term") 
    
Use a Spline Trajectory to import a trajectory defined by a set of points and control points in 3D space you created in a third-party tool.
Use trajectories as paths along which Trajectory Layout 3D and Trajectory Layout 2D nodes arrange their child nodes, and along which Trajectory List Box 3D nodes move their items.
See [Using spline trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-spline-trajectories.html), [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html) and [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html). 

Spot Light node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Spot-Light-node "Link to this term") 
    
Spot Light emits light from a specific location towards a specified direction in the shape of a cone.
See [Using the light nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/lights/using-lights.html).

metadata.title: Glossary (Part 19/30)
metadata.breadcrumb: References > Glossary

content:
Stack Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Stack-Layout-node "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Stack Layout nodes to arrange nodes next to each other on the selected axis.
See [Using the Stack Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/layouts/using-stack-layouts.html). 

State Managers[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-State-Managers "Link to this term") 
    
Use a State Manager to create different states in your Kanzi application.
For example, you can define the appearance and behavior of a button during different states, such as how the button reacts when a user selects, presses, holds, or releases the button.
See [State manager](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/state-managers/state-managers.html). 

Styles[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Styles "Link to this term") 
    
Use styles to set the property values of one or more nodes of a certain type.
You can set a Style so that it applies to all nodes of a certain type in the selected scope, or to individual nodes.
See [Using styles](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/styles/using-styles.html). 

Tag Filter[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Tag-Filter "Link to this term") 
    
Tag Filter collects 3D nodes that have a specific tag assigned.
See [Using the Tag Filter](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/filters/using-tag-filters.html). 

Tags[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Tags "Link to this term") 
    
Use tags to group, find, and filter nodes in your project. You can assign multiple tags to a single node.
See [Using tags](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/tags/using-tags.html). 

Text Block node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Text-Block-node "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Text Block nodes to show a small amount of text in your application.
See [Using the Text Block nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-blocks.html). 

Text Box node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Text-Box-node "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Text Box nodes to add single-line text input to your application.
See [Using the Text Box nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/using-text-boxes.html). 

Texture Brush[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Texture-Brush "Link to this term") 
    
Use a Texture Brush to fill a 2D node with a texture.
See [Filling 2D nodes with a texture](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/brushes/using-brushes.html#filling-2d-nodes-with-a-texture). 

Theme Group[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Theme-Group "Link to this term") 
    
Use a Theme Group to define a collection of themes.
See [Using Themes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/using-themes.html).

metadata.title: Glossary (Part 20/30)
metadata.breadcrumb: References > Glossary

content:
Theme Group[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Theme-Group "Link to this term") 
    
Use a Theme Group to define a collection of themes.
See [Using Themes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/using-themes.html). 

Theme[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Theme "Link to this term") 
    
Use a Theme to set the resources which define the look and feel of your application.
Themes enable you to use a single Kanzi Studio project for multiple variants of your product.
See [Tutorial: Theme your application](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/theming/theming.html) and [Using Themes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/themes/using-themes.html). 

Timeline Entry[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Timeline-Entry "Link to this term") 
    
Use a Timeline Entry to manipulate animations, including repetition, scaling, targeting, and blending, and to define the type of animation input: time or property value.
See [Editing timeline sequences](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/animations/editing-timeline-sequences.html). 

Timeline Sequence[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Timeline-Sequence "Link to this term") 
    
Use a Timeline Sequence to combine a set of Timeline Entry resources.
Timeline entries can target specific items inside the scope of a Timeline Sequence.
See [Editing timeline sequences](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/animations/editing-timeline-sequences.html). 

To-source binding[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-To-source-binding "Link to this term") 
    
A to-source binding pushes a property value to a node or another project item, or to a resource used by that item.
See [To-source bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/bindings.html#to-source-bindings). 

Toggle Button Group node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Toggle-Button-Group-node "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Toggle Button Group nodes to allow users to select only one option from a set of options that are mutually exclusive.
See [Using the Toggle Button Group nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-toggle-button-groups.html) and [Buttons](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/buttons.html). 

Toggle Button node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Toggle-Button-node "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Toggle Button nodes to create interactions through buttons that can have multiple toggle states.
See [Using the Toggle Button nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/using-toggle-buttons.html) and [Buttons](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/buttons/buttons.html).

metadata.title: Glossary (Part 21/30)
metadata.breadcrumb: References > Glossary

content:
Trajectory Layout node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Trajectory-Layout-node "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Trajectory Layout nodes to arrange items along a trajectory path.
See [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html) and [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html). 

Trajectory List Box 3D node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Trajectory-List-Box-3D-node "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Trajectory List Box 3D node to create scrollable lists of items arranged along a trajectory in 3D space.
See [Using the Trajectory List Box 3D node](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-list-boxes.html) and [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html). 

Trapezoid Trajectory[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Trapezoid-Trajectory "Link to this term") 
    
Use a Trapezoid Trajectory to create a path in the shape of a trapezoid in 3D space.
Use trajectories as paths along which Trajectory Layout 3D and Trajectory Layout 2D nodes arrange their child nodes, and along which Trajectory List Box 3D nodes move their items.
See [Using trapezoid trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trapezoid-trajectories.html), [Trajectories](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/trajectories.html), and [Using the Trajectory Layout nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/trajectories/using-trajectory-layouts.html). 

Triggers[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Triggers "Link to this term") 
    
Use Triggers to create interactions based on user input. With triggers you can set actions, such as printing to the Log window, setting a property to a certain value, activating an Activity, or playing an animation.
See [Triggers](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/triggers/triggers.html). 

Value source binding[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Value-source-binding "Link to this term") 
    
A value source binding sets the local value of an entire property and provides the value for that property during application runtime.
See [Value source bindings](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/bindings/bindings.html#value-source-bindings). 

Viewport node[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Viewport-node "Link to this term") 
    
Use the Viewport nodes to set the size of a render target surface onto which Kanzi projects content.
See [Viewport nodes](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/viewports/using-viewports.html).

metadata.title: Glossary (Part 22/30)
metadata.breadcrumb: References > Glossary

content:
Volume Texture[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Volume-Texture "Link to this term") 
    
Volume textures use a single 2D image, made up of many cross-section slices of a 3D shape, to define a 3D volume texture. This technique is often used for effects like smoke, fire, or clouds, where 3D data would be too resource intensive or difficult to generate procedurally.
See [Using volume textures](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/textures/using-volume-textures.html).

content:
## Synonyms[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#synonyms "Link to this heading")
This section lists other names for Kanzi terms: names from other tools and from the industry, and names that people use for Kanzi features. 

Anti-aliasing render pass[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Anti-aliasing-render-pass "Link to this term") 
    
See [Multisampling](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/rendering/anti-aliasing.html). 

appendTimer[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-appendTimer "Link to this term") 
    
`MainLoopScheduler::appendTimer` in the Kanzi Engine API. See [Application development](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/application-configuration.html). 

application.cfg configuration[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-application.cfg-configuration "Link to this term") 
    
See [Application configuration](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/application-configuration.html). 

Blend shape[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Blend-shape "Link to this term") 
    
See [Morph](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Morph). 

Blender intensity[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Blender-intensity "Link to this term") 
    
See [Blend Intensity](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/materials/creating-transparent-materials.html). 

C# plugin[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-C-plugin "Link to this term") 
    
See [Kanzi Studio plugin](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/plugins/creating-kanzi-studio-plugins.html). 

contextNode global variable[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-contextNode-global-variable "Link to this term") 
    
`contextNode` in the Kanzi Engine Lua API. See [Using Lua](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/lua/using-lua.html). 

CreateBindingItemCommand[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-CreateBindingItemCommand "Link to this term") 
    
`CreateBindingItem` command in Kanzi Studio. See [Kanzi Studio command reference](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/command-reference.html). 

Custom data object[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Custom-data-object "Link to this term") 
    
See [Data object](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/data-sources/data-sources.html). 

Data source object[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Data-source-object "Link to this term") 
    
See [Data context](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/data-sources/using-a-data-source.html).

metadata.title: Glossary (Part 24/30)
metadata.breadcrumb: References > Glossary

content:
Data source object[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Data-source-object "Link to this term") 
    
See [Data context](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/data-sources/using-a-data-source.html). 

Data source XML file[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Data-source-XML-file "Link to this term") 
    
See [XML data source](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/tutorials/data-sources/data-sources.html). 

Depth write mode[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Depth-write-mode "Link to this term") 
    
See [Depth Write Enabled](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-Pipeline-State-render-pass). 

DLL plugin[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/glossary.html#term-DLL-plugin "Link to this term")

# Application configuration reference[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#application-configuration-reference "Link to this heading")
![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/copy-to-clipboard.svg) Copy page ![](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/_static/arrow-down.svg)

You can configure your Kanzi application:
  * In the C++ application override the `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` function of your application class. Kanzi calls this function as part of application initialization before it reads the `application.cfg` and before it initializes the graphics subsystem. Use this function to configure application properties.
  * In `application.cfg` by setting the parameters for Kanzi Studio projects without recompiling your application or even without a C++ application.


The configuration you specify in `application.cfg` overrides the configuration you specify in `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`.
## Setting which `application.cfg` to use[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#setting-which-application-cfg-to-use "Link to this heading")
When you have more than one Kanzi application executable file in a directory, you can set a separate configuration file for each executable.
To set which `application.cfg` to use when running your Kanzi application from the command line, enter the name of the application executable file followed by the `-config` option, and the name of the configuration file.
For example, to run a Kanzi application named MyApplication with the myConfiguration.cfg file use

```
MyApplication.exe -config=myConfiguration.cfg

```
Copy to clipboard

content:
## Using the `application.cfg`[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#using-the-application-cfg "Link to this heading")
To configure your Kanzi application using `application.cfg`, create an `application.cfg` file that contains the parameter names and their values in:
  * `<ProjectName>/Application Player` if you have a Kanzi Studio project without a C++ application
  * `<ProjectName>/Application/bin` if you have a Kanzi Studio project with a C++ application


When you launch your Kanzi application, the application uses the parameters in the `application.cfg` to configure your application.
## Error handling for `application.cfg`[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#error-handling-for-application-cfg "Link to this heading")
If an `application.cfg` is missing or is corrupted, Kanzi application logs a corresponding error message and continues to run with the default settings.
If you want to implement your own `application.cfg` error handling, you can create a custom logger to detect such errors. See [Creating a custom logger](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/logging/logging.html#creating-a-custom-logger).
## Running an application without reading the `application.cfg`[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#running-an-application-without-reading-the-application-cfg "Link to this heading")
On some embedded platforms reading the `application.cfg` file can have a performance impact.
To run an application without reading the `application.cfg` file, on the command line launch your Kanzi application with the `-config=""` option.
For example, to run a Kanzi application named MyApplication without reading the `application.cfg` file use

```
MyApplication.exe -config=""

```

## Loading[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#loading "Link to this heading")
### BinaryName[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#binaryname "Link to this heading")
You can set which kzb file or kzb configuration file your Kanzi application loads when you launch your Kanzi application.
See [Kzb files](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/kzb-binaries/kzb-files.html).  
| In `application.cfg`  | `BinaryName = "name"`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.binaryName = "name";`  |  
| Value  |   
 | `name`  | Path to a single kzb file, or to the kzb configuration file that lists all the kzb files that your Kanzi application loads.  |  
| --- | --- |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Loads the kzb file named my_application.kzb.
BinaryName = "my_application.kzb"

```
Copy to clipboard 
```
# Loads the kzb configuration file my_application.kzb.cfg that lists
# all the kzb files that your Kanzi application loads.
BinaryName = "my_application.kzb.cfg"

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
| `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` example  |  
```
// Loads the kzb file named my_application.kzb.
configuration.binaryName = "my_application.kzb";

```
Copy to clipboard 
```
// Loads the kzb configuration file my_application.kzb.cfg that lists
// all the kzb files that your Kanzi application loads.
configuration.binaryName = "my_application.kzb.cfg";

```

### FontEngine[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#fontengine "Link to this heading")
You can set which font engine you want to load at application startup to render the text in your application:
  * FreeType uses the FreeType rasterizer, HarfBuzz shaper, and ICU bidirectional library, and libunibreak for line breaking. This is the default font engine.
  * iType uses the Monotype iType rasterizer and WorldType® Shaper™ for shaping.
  * When you do not load a font engine, Kanzi does not render the text in your application.


When loading a font engine, keep in mind that:
  * In a static build, you must statically link to the application the font engine that you want to load.
  * In a dynamic build, Kanzi loads the font engine library.


You can also set which font engine you want the Kanzi Studio Preview to use to render text. See [Setting the font engine for the Preview](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/text/text.html#setting-font-engine-for-preview).  
| In `application.cfg`  | `FontEngine = fontEngine`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.fontEngine = fontEngine;`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `fontEngine`  |  The font engine that Kanzi loads at application startup. To load the iType font engine:
  * In `application.cfg` use `IType`.
  * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `ApplicationProperties::FontEngine::IType`.

To load the FreeType font engine (the default value):
  * In `application.cfg` use `FreeType`. Default value.
  * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `ApplicationProperties::FontEngine::FreeType`. Default value.

To not load a font engine:
  * In `application.cfg` use `None`.
  * In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` use `ApplicationProperties::FontEngine::None`.

When you do not load a font engine, Kanzi does not render the text in your application.  |  
| --- | --- |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Load the iType font engine at application startup.
FontEngine = IType

```

### DeploymentQueueBudget[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#deploymentqueuebudget "Link to this heading")
Kanzi keeps a queue of resources that are deployed on the UI thread. Use `DeploymentQueueBudget` to control the amount of time that Kanzi spends each frame to deploy resources. When many small resources are in the deployment queue, time budget greater than 0 can significantly decrease the time to load application resources.
The time budget does not set a hard limit on the total amount of time spent on resource deployment each frame. A long running deployment task can take longer than the allocated time.
When set to the default value of 0 milliseconds, Kanzi deploys each frame only one resource from the resource deployment queue.
See [Balancing between UI responsiveness and resource loading](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/application-configuration.html#balancing-between-ui-responsiveness-and-resource-loading).  
| In `application.cfg`  | `DeploymentQueueBudget = milliseconds`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.deploymentQueueBudget = milliseconds;`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `milliseconds`  | Maximum number of milliseconds to spend on resource deployment each frame. The default value is 0. For Kanzi Android framework (droidfw) applications, the default value is 5.  |  
| --- | --- |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Each frame Kanzi spends up to 2 milliseconds to deploy resources.
# Kanzi keeps deploying resources until it spends the allocated time budget
# for that frame.
DeploymentQueueBudget = 2

```
Copy to clipboard  |  
| `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` example  |  
```

// for that frame.
configuration.deploymentQueueBudget = 2;

```

### LoadingThreadCount[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#loadingthreadcount "Link to this heading")
When users run your Kanzi application in an environment with a multi-core processor, Kanzi automatically uses multiple CPU cores to load the GPU resources in the kzb files to RAM.
See [Loading resources in parallel](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/loading-resources-in-parallel.html).
GPU resources Kanzi loads in parallel include all types of textures, shaders, and meshes. To deploy these resources from RAM to GPU memory and to load prefab templates, Kanzi always uses the main thread. See [Images and textures best practices](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/images-and-textures/images-and-textures-best-practices.html), [Shaders best practices](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/shaders/shaders-best-practices.html), [Meshes best practices](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/best-practices/meshes/meshes-best-practices.html).  
| In `application.cfg`  | `LoadingThreadCount = threads`  |  
| --- | --- |  
| In `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)`  | `configuration.loadingThreadCount = threads;`  |  
| Values  |   
 | `threads`  | Number of CPU cores used for loading the resources. The default value is 3.  |  
| --- | --- |  
 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Switches off the use of multiple cores for loading your application.
# Loads your application resources using the main thread.
LoadingThreadCount = 0

```

```
# Uses six threads to load your application.
LoadingThreadCount = 5

```

| `Application::onConfigure[](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/reference/kanzi-runtime-api/a11370.html#a3803fce5a93d4211e67cc9be1d14f92c)` example  |  
```

```

### MaxPendingResources[¶](https://docs.kanzi.com/4.1.0/en/working-with/application-configurations/reference-for-application-configuration.html#maxpendingresources "Link to this heading")
You can set the maximum number of resources that the loading threads process at the same time. By increasing the number of resources you can speed up the loading, but at the same time you increase the peak memory use during loading because you can load more resources to the memory before they are deployed to the GPU.

| Values  |   
 | `resources`  | The maximum number of resources processed at the same time by the loading threads. The default value is 0 and sets the maximum number of resources to the number of loading threads +1.  |

 |  
| `application.cfg` example  |  
```
# Sets the maximum number of resources processed by the loading
# threads to the number of loading threads + 1. This is the default value.
MaxPendingResources = 0

```

# threads to 20 resources.
MaxPendingResources = 20

```
